feat: recognize semisimple groups from their Lie algebras (#18070)

This PR proves a Lie-algebra recognition criterion for semisimple affine groups. Eliminate connected smooth solvable normal subgroups when the ambient Lie radical vanishes, deduce semisimplicity from a nondegenerate Killing form over any field, and combine this with the existing converse to obtain an equivalence in characteristic zero.

Advance [ReductiveGroups/README.md, Layer 6, “Reductive and semisimple groups”](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/ReductiveGroups/README.md#layer-6-reductive-and-semisimple-groups), specifically semisimplicity as triviality of the geometric solvable radical, using Layer 2's Lie-algebra dictionary. The concrete consumer is the missing strengthening of `reductiveCommHopfAlgProperty.derived` from reductivity to semisimplicity in characteristic zero: after identifying `Lie(G_der)` with the derived Lie ideal, `TauCeti.isKilling_derivedSeries` supplies the Killing-form calculation and the new `semisimpleCommHopfAlgProperty.of_isKilling` supplies group semisimplicity. Previously only semisimplicity of the group supplied semisimplicity of its Lie algebra. After this PR, Layer 6 still needs the derived subgroup of a reductive group to be proved semisimple and the central-isogeny decomposition by its radical torus and derived group.

Choose this complete recognition step because tangent base change, the containment of a solvable normal subgroup's tangent ideal in the Lie radical, the connected zero-tangent theorem, and the characteristic-zero converse are already on main. Scan all 289 open PRs, 100 recent merges, and an additional merged semisimple/Lie search; none supplies this criterion. The open derived-tangent and central-intersection PRs address different missing steps. Claim `author/ReductiveGroups/semisimple-iff-is-killing-lie-algebra` before implementation; registration returns the documented exit-2 fallback because the fork account cannot write canonical claim refs. No unmerged work is used.

Add `TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Semisimple/Lie.lean` (103 lines), extend `Solvable/Radical/Lie.lean`, and update `Semisimple/LinearlyReductive.lean`: 143 insertions and 39 deletions across three mathematics modules. Move the existing `semisimpleCommHopfAlgProperty.isKilling_lieAlgebra` theorem, with its proof unchanged, into the new canonical Lie module and import it from the representation-theoretic module. No declaration is renamed, no module path is removed, and no compatibility alias is introduced.

The subgroup-elimination lemma works over every field, without smoothness or connectedness assumptions on the ambient group. The sufficient Killing-form criterion explicitly requires smoothness and geometric connectedness, and works in every characteristic. The equivalence assumes characteristic zero and geometric connectedness; smoothness follows from Cartier's theorem. No algebraic-closedness or splitting hypothesis is imposed on the ground field. Introduce three theorems, no definitions, predicates, instances, notation, or chosen data.

Reuse the existing solvable tangent-ideal containment, quotient Lie equivalence, connected zero-tangent theorem, quotient/augmentation identities, tangent Killing-form base-change equivalence, Cartier's theorem, and Mathlib's Killing-form and Cartan criteria. The module documentation cites Humphreys, §13, and Milne, Chapters 10 and 22, and identifies the central formal inputs. No Mathlib infrastructure or external formalization is vendored.

Read the shared protocol and all ten rubrics: scope, correctness, reuse, attribution, api-design, generality, placement, naming, documentation, and proof-quality. Self-review removes an unnecessary characteristic-zero restriction from the sufficient criterion, places the reusable elimination lemma beside the existing solvable tangent containment, moves the converse into the Lie module, updates its former module's documentation, and removes a redundant import. Repeated pinned-Mathlib and Tau Ceti searches find no existing replacement. The public surface contains only the elimination theorem, sufficient recognition theorem, and characteristic-zero equivalence, alongside the relocated existing converse.

Validation: the final targeted foreground build passes for all three changed modules and the downstream `Semisimple.CommutativeImage` module. The scoped axiom audit checks 8 declarations across the three changed modules and finds only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`. All 14 default environment linters pass on those modules with zero violations and zero grandfathered findings; the documentation scan has no definitions to check. The staged whitespace check passes. CI supplies the authoritative repository-wide build.

The prescribed `tauceti-lint-env --changed-since-merge-base origin/main` stops at its freshness guard because its downloaded helper omits Mathlib's new `tacticAlt`. A temporary copy adds only that default, exactly matching current main's approved `LINTERS_TACTIC_ALT`; the freshness guard, changed-module scope, documentation scan, allowlist, and violation checks remain enabled. No repository tooling or linter settings are changed.

An ordinary module importing the public API checks the all-characteristic sufficient criterion, the characteristic-zero equivalence from `HasTrivialRadical`, and a nontrivial `SL₂/ℚ` application from its computed tangent `sl₂`, without importing the existing group-semisimplicity proof or unfolding the new API.

feat: add the Rademacher distribution (#17961)

This PR adds the Rademacher probability measure and its complete scalar-distribution API as the next independent step in the StandardDistributions Layer 9, §9.1 “Finite uniform and categorical” milestone.

The exact roadmap target is `StandardDistributions/README.md`, Layer 9, §9.1: formalize the Rademacher law with equal mass at `-1` and `1`, together with the shared scalar-distribution requirements used by later probability developments. This is the most effective available step because the general finite-uniform and categorical portions are already in flight, while Rademacher remains an unmet named law on the same critical path. After this PR, §9.1 still needs the integer-interval uniform family, plus completion of those in-flight finite-uniform and categorical contributions.

The new `TauCeti.Probability.Distributions.Rademacher` module defines `rademacherMeasure` through Mathlib's `bernoulliMeasure`, proves its Dirac decomposition, probability instance, integration and integrability criteria, atom masses, support, CDF, interior quantiles and endpoint limits, all natural moments, mean and variance, exponential integrability, MGF, CGF, and characteristic function. The proofs reuse Mathlib's Bernoulli integration infrastructure and TauCeti's existing quantile and exponential-integrability foundations; no external formalization or Mathlib infrastructure is vendored.

feat: extend coefficients of measures from the unit ball (#18025)

This PR constructs the extension of coefficients of measures from the unit ball, `AbstractMeasure.extendCoefficients j hj : D(X, O) →+ D(X, K)`. Here `X` is a profinite space, `O` is a topological commutative ring, `K` is a complete ultrametric normed field, and `j : O →+* K` satisfies `‖j a‖ ≤ 1`. On a locally constant function `Σ c_i 1_{U_i}` the extension is `Σ c_i j(μ(1_{U_i}))`. That value does not depend on the clopen partition, it is bounded by the sup norm (ultrametric inequality), and Mathlib's `LinearMap.extendOfNorm` extends it to all of `C(X, K)`.

Roadmap target: `PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras/README.md`, §1.7 "Comparison with the completed group algebra", item **Extension of coefficients from the unit ball**. Its Lean form is `AbstractMeasure.existsUnique_extendCoefficients` in `Suggested.lean`.

This PR provides, under the roadmap's names where it gives them:
- `extendCoefficients`.
- `extendCoefficients_apply_comp`: ι_j(μ)(j ∘ f) = j(μ(f)) for continuous `j`.
- `eq_extendCoefficients_of_apply_comp`: uniqueness.
- `norm_toCLMEquiv_extendCoefficients_le`: ‖ι_j(μ)‖ ≤ 1.
- `extendCoefficients_smul`, `extendCoefficients_dirac`, `extendCoefficients_map` and `extendCoefficients_injective`.
- `finiteProjection_extendCoefficients` (simp): the finite projections of ι_j(μ) are those of μ with `j` applied to the coefficients. This characterises the extension.
- `extendCoefficients_apply_comp_eq_sum`: the cylinder formula.

Together these give every clause of `existsUnique_extendCoefficients`, under weaker hypotheses. Instead of `Isometry j`, the construction needs only the unit-ball bound. Continuity of `j` is needed only for the `j ∘ f` characterisation, and `O` need not be complete or normed. I did not add the bundled ∃! statement, since it would only repackage these lemmas. The module docstring records the roadmap's negative control (the discrete norm on `ℚ_p`), and the file closes with ℤ_p → ℚ_p examples for two of the roadmap checks: the Dirac evaluation, and that δ_x + δ_x and δ_x have different extensions.

After this PR, the rest of this item is: `extendCoefficients_restrictClopen`, multiplicativity and `extendCoefficientsRingHom` for profinite monoids, the comparisons with base change and with `extendIntegralCoefficients` (they need `completedGroupAlgebraBaseChange` and §2.5), and the character evaluations `extendedCharacterRingHom` and `extendedPseudoCharacterEval` (they need §3.1). This PR does not overlap with the open #18017 (`toCompletedGroupAlgebra`) or #17452 (unit coordinates).

Supporting additions:
- `TauCeti/Topology/ContinuousMap/LocallyConstant.lean` (new, 40 lines): `LocallyConstant.denseRange_toContinuousMap`. On a profinite space, locally constant functions are dense in `C(X, V)` for any uniform space `V`. The proof uses Mathlib's `ContinuousMap.exists_finite_approximation_of_mem_nhds_diagonal`. `finiteProjection_ext` and `dense_setOf_comp_unitsToZModPow` currently re-derive this density inline; switching them to this lemma is left to a separate refactor.
- `FiniteProjection.lean`: `fiberIndicator_comp`, `fiberIndicator_eq_zero_of_notMem_range`, `finiteProjection_apply_of_notMem_range` and `finiteProjection_map` (finite projection of a pushforward).
- `TauCeti/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/ExtendCoefficients.lean` (new, 383 lines).

The construction follows Rodrigues Jacinto–Williams, *An introduction to p-adic L-functions*, Proposition 3.16 and Remark 3.28. No Mathlib material is vendored.

feat: add Pareto quantile formula (#18065)

This PR computes the Pareto quantile as `t * (1 - u) ^ (-1 / r)` for positive threshold and shape and every interior level. Prove its one-sided limits in `EReal`: the threshold as the level tends to zero from above, and positive infinity as the level tends to one from below.

Advance [StandardDistributions/README.md, Layer 13, “Quantile formulas and coverage of all families”](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/StandardDistributions/README.md#layer-13-quantile-formulas-and-coverage-of-all-families), specifically the Pareto row and its required support-endpoint limits. This closes that row. After this PR, Layer 13 still needs the remaining scalar, discrete-cast, order-statistic, and named non-scalar quantile specializations listed there.

This is a direct available step because the Pareto cdf and generic quantile adjunction are already on main. Scans of open PRs and recent merges, plus a dedicated Pareto-quantile PR search, find no overlapping target; the open Pareto power-bias work concerns a different identity. The cooperative claim for `author/StandardDistributions/quantile-pareto-measure` returned the permitted exit-2 fallback because the canonical repository denied write access.

Add `TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Pareto/Quantile.lean` (93 lines), exposing exactly three theorems. Reuse Tau Ceti's `cdf_paretoMeasure_eq` and `Measure.quantile_le_iff`, together with Mathlib's negative-power comparison, continuity, asymptotic, and extended-real limit APIs. The module cites Johnson–Kotz–Balakrishnan, *Continuous Univariate Distributions*, vol. 1, Chapter 20. No Mathlib infrastructure or external formalization is vendored.

feat: add finite quadratic-module orthogonal group (#18044)

This PR defines the finite quadratic-module orthogonal group `O(q)` and its canonical equivalence with self-isometries, proves that the group is finite, and records its action on the quadratic map, isotropic and Lagrangian subgroups, and orthogonal complements.

It completes the `O(q)` target in IntegralLattices milestone 1G, “isometries, and the group `O(q)`.” This is the most direct remaining group-theoretic prerequisite for the discriminant-form automorphisms used by Layer 5; after this PR, 1G still needs a normal-form or completeness theorem for the proved Nikulin generator relations.

The implementation specializes `QuadraticMap.orthogonalGroup` and its existing isometry equivalence, so the generic conjugation and transport API remains the single source of truth. The new finite-module results add only the carrier-specific finiteness and subgroup-action interface needed by the roadmap.

feat: compute the tangent exact sequence of abelianization (#18059)

This PR identifies the tangent exact sequence of the affine abelianization and proves `[Lie G, Lie G] ⊆ Lie([G,G])`. Compute the differential’s kernel as the tangent Lie ideal of the scheme-theoretic derived subgroup; for smooth groups, prove smoothness of the projection, surjectivity of its differential, and the canonical equivalence `Lie G / Lie([G,G]) ≃ Lie(G/[G,G])` with forward and inverse simp equations.

Advance [ReductiveGroups/README.md, Layer 6, “Develop the radical, the centre Z(G), the derived group G_der, central isogenies and the simply connected and adjoint forms”](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/ReductiveGroups/README.md#layer-6-reductive-and-semisimple-groups), using Layer 2’s differential and kernel tools. The concrete consumer comparison is `Lie([G,G]) = [Lie G, Lie G]` for reductive groups in characteristic zero: `Reductive/Lie.lean` already constructs the semisimple derived Lie ideal and explicitly leaves comparison with the group-theoretic derived subgroup as a further step. This PR supplies the missing inclusion and the tangent kernel and quotient computations, combining quotient infrastructure already on main. After this PR, the milestone still needs the reverse inclusion in characteristic zero, semisimplicity of the derived group of a reductive group, and the central isogeny from the radical torus times the derived group.

Add `TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Derived/Tangent.lean` (172 lines). The kernel and bracket inclusion assume geometric reducedness and finite type over an arbitrary field, with independent coordinate and coefficient universes. The smoothness and quotient-equivalence results assume only smoothness and finite type, using the common base/coordinate universe required by the existing faithful-flatness theorem and an independent coefficient universe. All characteristics, disconnected groups and nonreduced coefficient algebras are allowed. The quotient is by `Lie([G,G])`; no equality with the abstract derived Lie ideal is asserted.

feat: the Sobolev trace of a function continuous up to the boundary is its restriction (#18060)

This PR proves that the `H¹` traces in Tau Ceti give the classical boundary values when the function is continuous up to the boundary. This holds for the flat trace, the half-space trace, the trace on a Lipschitz graph, and the localized trace in a Lipschitz boundary chart. The traces are defined abstractly, as continuous extensions of restriction from test functions. Until now, nothing identified them with boundary values except on test functions. Evans states this identification as part of the trace theorem (*PDE*, §5.5, Theorem 1: `Tu = u|∂U` for `u ∈ W^{1,p}(U) ∩ C(Ū)`).

Roadmap target: `PDE/README.md`, Lane A, item 6, "Trace, extension, Rellich", the trace operator `W^{1,p}(Ω) → L^p(∂Ω)` with `ker = W^{1,p}_0` on Lipschitz domains. Extension, Rellich–Kondrachov, the local chart traces, the Lipschitz-graph surface-measure comparison and the chart-trace kernel characterization (#17965) are already on `main`. What remains is to assemble the global trace into `L²(frontier Ω, μHE[n−1])` from the chart traces. For that, the traces taken in two overlapping charts must agree on the overlap, so the result does not depend on the partition of unity. That compatibility comes from this PR's `W1p.lipschitzChartTrace_apply_ae_of_continuousOn` combined with density of functions continuous up to the boundary (global extension plus whole-space test-function density, both on `main`). The same theorem gives the global trace its defining property `Tu = u|∂Ω`. After this PR, Lane A.6 still needs the global trace into surface measure. Its kernel identification then follows from #17965.

New file `TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/Trace/Continuous.lean` (252 lines):
- `W1p.hyperplaneTrace_apply_ae_of_continuous`: if `u ∈ H¹(ℝ × E)` has a continuous representative `f`, then its trace on `{a} × E` is `y ↦ f (a, y)` a.e. In the compactly supported case, `W1p.normedBumpL` gives test functions (`W1p.normedBumpL_mem_range_of_ae_eq_zero`) that converge to `u` in `H¹` (`W1p.tendsto_normedBumpL`) and to `f` pointwise (Mathlib's `ContDiffBump.convolution_tendsto_right_of_continuous`). Their traces converge in `L²`, so a subsequence converges a.e. (`TendstoInMeasure.exists_seq_tendsto_ae`), and the two limits agree. The general case reduces to this one with cutoffs and the existing locality lemma `W1p.hyperplaneTrace_contDiffSMul_ae`.
- `W1p.halfSpaceTrace_apply_ae_of_continuousOn`: the same for `u ∈ H¹({a < t})` and `f` continuous on `{a ≤ t}`. The even reflection extension is represented by `f` composed with the continuous fold `(t, y) ↦ (a + |t - a|, y)`.
- `W1p.normalEpigraphTrace_apply_ae_of_continuousOn`: for `φ` Lipschitz and `f` continuous on `{φ y ≤ t}`, the graph trace is `y ↦ f (normalGraphEmbedding φ y)`. This goes through graph flattening.

Additions to existing files:
- `TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/LipschitzDomain/Trace/Basic.lean`: `W1p.lipschitzChartTrace_apply_ae_of_continuousOn`. If `u ∈ H¹(Ω)` agrees a.e. with `f` continuous on `closure Ω`, then the local chart trace is `ψ f` evaluated at `e.symm (normalGraphEmbedding φ y)`.
- `TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/LipschitzDomain/Basic.lean`: `Set.IsLipschitzChart.image_closure_inter_normalCylinder`. Inside a chart cylinder, the closure of `Ω` is the region on or above the graph. It is the closure companion of the existing `image_frontier_inter_normalCylinder`.
- `TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/Haar/InnerProductSpace.lean`: `MeasureTheory.Measure.addHaar_setOf_fst_eq`. The hyperplane `{a} × E` of `ℝ × E` is null for every additive Haar measure (via Mathlib's `Measure.addHaar_affineSubspace`).
- `TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/W1p/Basic.lean`: `W1p.coe_ae_eq_zero_of_value_ae_eq_zero`. A Sobolev function whose value vanishes on an open subset has vanishing jet there. It is the `W1p` analogue of `Wkp.firstOrder_ae_eq_zero_of_value_ae_eq_zero`, which now reuses it.

No Mathlib infrastructure or external formalization is vendored. The new module cites Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, §5.5, Theorem 1, and Brezis, *Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and PDE*, §9.3. I read all ten rubrics (scope, correctness, reuse, attribution, api-design, generality, placement, naming, documentation, proof-quality) and reviewed the diff against api-design, reuse and generality. I found no existing trace-equals-restriction statement for continuous functions in Tau Ceti or pinned Mathlib. As a result of that review, I made the null-hyperplane fact public, stated it for every additive Haar measure, and placed it with the other Haar-measure facts. I replaced a private copy of the whole-space `restrict univ` lemma with the existing simp lemmas `Opens.coe_top` and `Measure.restrict_univ`, keeping only a local Haar instance as in `W1p/Mollification.lean`. One declaration stays private: the compactly supported flat case, which is a special case of the public theorem. Only `H¹` is treated, because the half-space, graph and chart traces exist only for `p = 2`.

feat: the Hopf–Lax formula and its subsolution inequality (#18067)

This PR adds the Hopf–Lax value `hopfLax L φ t x = inf_y (φ y + t L (t⁻¹ (x - y)))` for a Lagrangian `L` and initial datum `φ` on a real vector space (`TauCeti/Analysis/PDE/HopfLax.lean`). Its main result is the subsolution inequality `u (t + h, x + h w) ≤ u (t, x) + h L w` for convex `L`, `t > 0` and `h ≥ 0` (`TauCeti.hopfLax_add_add_smul_le`). The PR also proves the characterising infimum API (`hopfLax_le`, `le_hopfLax`, `le_hopfLax_iff`, `hopfLax_mono`), the two-sided bounds `m + t l ≤ u ≤ φ + t L 0`, monotonicity in time, and joint upper semicontinuity on `t > 0` (so the extended potential is Borel). For the cost `L w = ‖w‖ ^ p` it adds the closed form `inf_y (φ y + ‖x - y‖ ^ p / t ^ (p - 1))` and the `p`-th power subsolution inequality for `1 ≤ p`. That last lemma uses the new `TauCeti.convexOn_norm_rpow` (`‖·‖ ^ q` is convex on any real normed space for `1 ≤ q`), which sits beside its strict counterpart `strictConvexOn_norm_rpow` in `TauCeti/Analysis/Convex/StrictConvexSpace.lean`. Mathlib has `convexOn_norm` and `convexOn_rpow` but not their composite.

Roadmap target: `OptimalTransport/README.md`, Layer 8, item 8, the Eulerian **Benamou–Brenier formula** `W_p(μ₀,μ₁)^p = inf ∫₀¹∫‖v_t‖^p dμ_t dt`. The upper bound (`≤`, via displacement interpolation) is on main in `ContinuityEquation/PlanInterpolation.lean`. The lower bound `W_p^p ≤ ∫∫‖v‖^p` is missing. Its route without ODE flows takes a Kantorovich pair `(φ, ψ)` and the Hopf–Lax potential `u (t, x) = hopfLax (‖·‖ ^ p) φ (t + δ) x`. feat: compressible subspaces induce isomorphisms on singular homology (#18117)

This PR adds `TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/Cubical/Compression/Retraction.lean`. It turns a `SubspaceCubeDeformation A` (a coherent deformation of the singular cubes of `X` into a subspace `A`, merged in #16876) into chain-level data on normalized cubical chains. It then proves that the inclusion `A → X` induces isomorphisms on singular homology.

The end of the deformation of a cube is a cube of `A`. Its retraction `D.retractChainMap R` is a chain map from the normalized cubical chains of `X` to those of `A`. It is a strict left inverse of the inclusion, because the deformation is constant on cubes of `A`. The swept-cube operator satisfies the prism identity `∂P + P∂ = ιρ − id`, so `D.retractHomotopy R` is a chain homotopy `𝟙 ≃ ρ ≫ ι`. Together these give `SubspaceCubeDeformation.normalizedCubicalChainComplexHomotopyEquiv`, a chain homotopy equivalence induced by the inclusion, and hence `quasiIso_normalizedCubicalChainComplex_map`.

Through the natural cubical/simplicial comparison `singularCubicalHomologyIso`, `SubspaceCubeDeformation.isIso_singularHomologyMap` shows that the inclusion is an isomorphism on singular homology with coefficients in any ring. Combined with the compression lemma (`nonempty_subspaceCubeDeformation_of_relHomotopyGroup`), `isIso_singularHomologyMap_subtypeVal_of_relHomotopyGroup` gives the same conclusion whenever every point of `X` is joined to `A` and every relative homotopy set `π_{n+1}(X, A, a)` vanishes.

Roadmap target: `DGFloer/README.md`, Layer 1 item 2 ("Weak equivalences and CW approximation"), statement "A weak homotopy equivalence induces isomorphisms on singular homology with local coefficients" (Hatcher, Proposition 4.21). This PR is the homological half of Hatcher's proof: invariance under the inclusion of a subspace with vanishing relative homotopy. What remains for that statement is to apply it to the bottom of the mapping cylinder of a weak homotopy equivalence (showing that its relative homotopy sets vanish and that the mapping cylinder deformation retracts onto the target), and then to extend from constant coefficients to local coefficients. CW approximation, the other half of the item, is untouched.

The chain-level part follows the existing `Based/Retraction.lean` (the retraction onto based cubes for a `BasedCubeDeformation`) step by step. The two deformation structures are separate on `main`, so the swept-cube lemmas are parallel rather than shared. Factoring them through a common structure would be a refactor of merged code, so it belongs in a separate PR. Sources: Eilenberg, *Singular homology theory* (1944), for deforming singular chains into a subspace; Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Proposition 4.21; Massey, *Singular Homology Theory*, Chapter II, for normalized cubical chains and prism operators. Suppose `σ⁻¹ (h(P) + 4 n r₀ [K : ℚ]) ≤ rᵢ h(βᵢ)` for every `i`. Then `Ind_{β,r}(P) ≤ 2 n σ^(1/2^(n-1))`. feat: the scaling law of Haar measure under integral matrices over a local field (#18147)

This PR proves the scaling law for Haar measure on `ι → K` over a nonarchimedean local field `K`. Let `A` be a square matrix over `𝒪[K]` whose determinant is associated to `ϖ ^ k` for a uniformizer `ϖ`. Then `A` (acting by `mulVec`) multiplies measure by `q ^ (-k)`, where `q = Nat.card 𝓀[K]`. This is the nonarchimedean analogue of Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.Measure.addHaar_image_linearMap`.

Target: `MassFormula/README.md`, Layer 2 ("lattices, index, and the Haar scaling law"), the item **"The scaling law"**: `μ (M '' S) = q^{−k} · μ S`. The README asks for it in two forms, and this PR proves both:
- **Box and balls, with no side condition** (the form Layer 3 consumes). `measure_image_mulVec_univ_pi_integer` covers the integer box `univ.pi fun _ ↦ 𝒪[K]`. `measure_image_mulVec_vadd_smul_univ_pi_integer` covers every ball `x +ᵥ c • univ.pi fun _ ↦ 𝒪[K]` with `c ≠ 0`. Both hold for any `μ.IsAddLeftInvariant`; neither Haar normalisation nor regularity is needed.
- **General sets.** `addHaar_image_mulVec`: for `[μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] [μ.Regular]` and every set `s`, `μ (A '' s) = q^{-k} * μ s`. The constant is read off the box using uniqueness of Haar measure (`isAddLeftInvariant_eq_smul_of_regular`). This is the `μ.Regular` route the README describes. Mathlib has no `SecondCountableTopology` instance for local fields, so the hypothesis cannot be dropped.

Its consumer is the Layer 3 milestone "The integral of the root count" (Serre 1978, Lemmas 2–3). There a ball of the ring of integers of `L` is, in power-basis coordinates, the image lattice of the matrix of multiplication by an element, and the README says "Layer 2 supplies the factor `q^{−d L}`". After this PR, the Layer 2 item "Boxes and balls" still needs its diagonal-box volume `q^{−∑ e i}` (open #17663 also proves this, as `measure_univ_pi_image_maximalIdeal_pow`) and the ball-of-`𝒪_L` volume in power-basis coordinates. Layer 3's root-count integral and Layer 4's Theorem 1 also remain.

New file `TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Group/LocalFieldScaling.lean` (177 lines, three public theorems in `MeasureTheory.Measure`, next to `addHaar_image_linearMap`). It sits in `TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Group/`, as the roadmap suggests. Proof outline:
- **Box.** `μ` is pulled back along the closed embedding `ι → 𝒪[K] ↪ ι → K` of the compact group `ι → 𝒪[K]`. In that group the range of `A.mulVecLin` has index `q ^ k`, by the lattice index `Matrix.card_quotient_range_mulVecLin_eq_pow` that #18122 put on main. Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.AddSubgroup.index_mul_measure` then gives the box identity. This avoids a relative-index measure lemma. Open #17663 adds one, `AddSubgroup.relIndex_mul_measure`; this PR does not duplicate it.
- **Balls.** The box form is applied to the left-invariant measure `T ↦ μ (c • T)`, together with translation invariance.
- **General sets.** As above, via uniqueness of Haar measure.

The hypotheses on `K` are `[Field K] [ValuativeRel K] [TopologicalSpace K] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K]`. No uniform structure is needed, because `IsNonarchimedeanLocalField` takes only a topology. The index type is any `Fintype ι`, not just `Fin n`.

Nothing is vendored. The proof uses Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.AddSubgroup.index_mul_measure` and `isAddLeftInvariant_eq_smul_of_regular`, and is not adapted from the cited 0stellensatz/MassFormula `HaarScaling.lean`, which I did not consult. The module docstring cites Serre, *Une « formule de masse » …*, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 286 (1978), §3.

Before writing any Lean I read the shared protocol and all ten rubrics: scope, correctness, reuse, attribution, api-design, generality, placement, naming, documentation and proof-quality. Self-review changed four things:

feat: monoidality of the pivotal traces (#18105)

This PR proves the monoidality of the pivotal traces from Layer 2 of the `PivotalSpherical` roadmap ("Layer 2: traces, dimensions, and spherical categories", basic theory: *monoidality `leftTrace (f ⊗ₘ g) = leftTrace f ≫ leftTrace g` modulo unitors*, and *multiplicativity on `⊗`* of the left and right dimensions). It computes the traces of `f ⊗ₘ g` in an arbitrary pivotal category. From that it derives multiplicativity whenever the relevant scalar acts on the object the same way from the left and from the right, and unconditionally in a braided pivotal category.

The roadmap states monoidality without hypotheses, but that version is false in a general pivotal category, so this PR states the correct general form instead. In `leftTrace (f ⊗ₘ g)` the loop of `f` sits inside the loop of `g`, so the scalar `leftTrace f` acts on `Y` from the left (`leftTrace_tensorHom`). Moving it out of the loop means crossing the `Y` strand, which turns the left action of the scalar into its right action. Here is a counterexample. Take the strict monoidal category with objects `ℤ/2`, `End(a) = R = k × k`, no morphisms between distinct objects, and `r ⊗ s = r · σᵃ(s)`, where `σ` swaps the factors. It is rigid, with `1ᘁ = 1` and `η = ε = 1`, and the identity is a pivotal structure. For a scalar `t` on the unit, `leftTrace (t ⊗ₘ 𝟙 1) = σ(t)`, whereas `leftTrace t ≫ leftTrace (𝟙 1) = t`. So the multiplicative statements carry the hypothesis that the scalar acts on `Y` the same way from both sides. That hypothesis holds in any braided category (`leftUnitor_inv_scalar_whiskerRight_leftUnitor_hom`). It also holds for scalars of the form `r • 𝟙` in a linear monoidal category, which is the fusion-category situation.

- `TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Pivotal/Tensor.lean` (new):

  - The nested-loop formulas `leftTrace_tensorHom` / `rightTrace_tensorHom`.
  - The scalar-extraction lemmas `leftTrace_comp_whiskerLeft_scalar` / `rightTrace_scalar_whiskerRight_comp`.
  - Multiplicativity under the both-sides hypothesis: `leftTrace_tensorHom_eq_comp`, `rightTrace_tensorHom_eq_comp`, `leftDim_tensor_eq_comp`, `rightDim_tensor_eq_comp`.
  - The braided `@[simp]` corollaries `…_of_braided`.

feat: Dirichlet polygons with cusps from finite half-plane intersections (#18144)

This PR builds Dirichlet polygons with cusps. A finite intersection `K` of closed geodesic half-planes with nonempty interior is the carrier of a `ConvexPolygon`, possibly with ideal vertices, whenever removing finitely many open horodiscs `{z | A i < Im (g i • z)}` (`A i > 0`) leaves a bounded set (`exists_convexPolygon_carrier_eq_iInter_closure_leftHalfPlane`). Each side is the face of `K` along one of the lines, and each ideal vertex is the centre of one of the horodiscs. Applied to Fuchsian groups: if the Dirichlet domain of a discrete `Γ` is bounded after removing finitely many cusp horodiscs, it is a convex polygon whose ideal vertices are cusp points of the data (`Subgroup.exists_convexPolygon_carrier_eq_dirichletDomain_of_isBounded_truncation`). With finitely many cusp orbits, the cusp compactification `Γ.CompactifiedQuotient` is then compact (`Subgroup.compactSpace_compactifiedQuotient_of_isBounded_truncation`).

Roadmap target: `FuchsianOrbifolds/README.md`, Layer 2, item 4: "Construct the finite-sided Dirichlet polygon, its locally finite translates, ideal vertices, side pairings, and cycles before deriving the equivalence with cofiniteness." It also feeds Layer 4, item 2 (compactness of the compactified quotient of a cofinite group from a truncated fundamental polygon). #17737 handled the compact case and #18032 gave the side pairing of any Dirichlet polygon. Both list "the cusped case: assembling the truncated Dirichlet domain of a cofinite group into a `ConvexPolygon` with ideal vertices" as what remains, and this PR does that step. The finite half-plane description of a truncated Dirichlet domain (`exists_finset_dirichletDomain_eq_iInter_closure_leftHalfPlane_of_isBounded_truncation`) was already on main. After this PR, the milestone needs one more thing: Siegel's theorem that a cofinite group's Dirichlet domain has a bounded truncation outside finitely many cusp horodiscs. With that, the new compactness theorem gives `CompactSpace` for every cofinite group, since cofinite groups already have finitely many cusp orbits (`IsCofinite.finite_cuspOrbit`).

How the proof works (`Polygon/HalfPlaneIntersection.lean`). It generalizes the face-following argument of #17737 instead of duplicating it. The compact theorem `exists_compactConvexPolygon_carrier_eq_iInter_closure_leftHalfPlane` keeps its statement and is now a corollary: with no horodiscs the polygon has no ideal vertices. Its downstream use in `UpperHalfPlane/DirichletDomain/Polygon.lean` is unchanged.
- Faces of an irredundant family are now extended geodesic segments. Their start and end are points of `ℍ ∪ ∂ℍ`, defined by the least or greatest parameter, or by the ideal endpoint of the line when the parameters are unbounded. The finite-endpoint lemmas carry over from the compact proof with a point of the face in place of the far endpoint.
- Ideal endpoints are handled by moving them to `∞`. Two lines of an irredundant family never run to the same ideal point, nor from the same ideal point, because each carries a point strictly left of the other. One line may run to the point another runs from, which is how two sides meet at an ideal vertex. If `K` has points arbitrarily high up, every semicircle has `∞` on its left. So each vertical line of the family has all its high points in `K`, since the vertical constraints only depend on the real part and the line meets `K`. If no line ran down from `∞`, `K` would contain everything far to the left. Points of a small fixed height escaping to the left would then avoid every horodisc, which contradicts the bounded truncation. The same kind of escape shows that every ideal vertex is a horodisc centre.
- The carrier of the polygon lies in `K` by a new hull property for convex polygons with ideal vertices, `ConvexPolygon.carrier_subset_closure_leftHalfPlane_of_forall`. It is proved by connectedness and area: otherwise the carrier would contain a whole open half-plane, which has infinite area (`volume_rightHalfPlane`), while a convex polygon has finite area (`volume_carrier_ne_top`).

This PR adds the differential graded category of twisted objects of a DG category, together with its twisted Hom differential. A twisted object `TauCeti.DGTwistedObject R C` is an object `X` of a DG category `C` with a degree-one endomorphism `δ` satisfying the Maurer–Cartan equation. In Mathlib's enriched factor order that equation is `d δ = dgComp δ δ`, and in Keller's order it is `d δ + δ ∘ δ = 0` (`dgDifferential_twist_add_negOnePow_smul_dgComp_eq_zero`). Morphisms, composition and identities are those of `C`. The Hom differential is twisted, `D f = d f + (-1)^n • dgComp f δ_Y - dgComp δ_X f` (`dgHomEquiv_dgDifferential`), which is `d f + δ_Y ∘ f - (-1)^n f ∘ δ_X` in Keller's order. `D² = 0` is derived from the Maurer–Cartan equations of the two twists: after the Leibniz rule and associativity, the remaining terms are `dgComp f (d δ_Y - δ_Y δ_Y) - dgComp (d δ_X - δ_X δ_X) f`. The Leibniz rule for `D` holds by associativity alone. The category is assembled through the existing `DGCategoryData.toDGCategory`. feat: Roth's theorem (#18176)

This PR proves Roth's theorem: if `α` is a real algebraic number and `κ > 2`, only finitely many `ξ ∈ ℚ` satisfy `|ξ - α| ≤ H(ξ)^(-κ)` (`IsAlgebraic.finite_setOfPred_abs_sub_le_mulHeight₁_rpow_neg`). Here `H` is Mathlib's `Height.mulHeight₁`. It also derives three consequences. There is `c > 0` with `c H(ξ)^(-κ) ≤ |ξ - α|` for all `ξ ≠ α`, so for all `ξ` when `α` is irrational (`IsAlgebraic.exists_pos_mul_mulHeight₁_rpow_neg_le_abs_sub`). A real algebraic number is never `LiouvilleWith p` for `p > 2` (`IsAlgebraic.not_liouvilleWith`). So its irrationality exponent is at most two, and exactly two when it is irrational (`IsAlgebraic.irrationalityExponent_le_two`, `IsAlgebraic.irrationalityExponent_eq_two`).

This PR proves Leray's theorem for finite covers: if a sheaf of abelian groups `F` on a topological space `X` has no cohomology in positive degrees on any nonempty finite intersection of members of a finite open cover `U`, then `Ȟⁿ(U, F) ≅ Hⁿ(X, F)` for every `n` (`TauCeti.Topology.nonempty_homology_cechComplex_iso_H`, Hartshorne Exercise III.4.11). Here `Ȟⁿ` is the homology of Mathlib's `cechComplexFunctor U` and `Hⁿ` is Mathlib's `Sheaf.H`. It also specialises the result to schemes: for a quasi-coherent sheaf on a locally Noetherian scheme with affine diagonal (for instance a separated one), Čech cohomology of any finite affine open cover computes `Hⁿ(X, M)` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.nonempty_homology_cechComplex_iso_cohomology`, Hartshorne Theorem III.4.5).

It advances JacobianChallenge/README.md, Layer B, "Coherent sheaves and cohomology `Hⁱ(X, ℱ)`: acyclicity of affines, Čech ≃ derived on a separated scheme, finite-dimensionality for proper `X/k`, …". After this PR the milestone still needs the comparison to be natural in `F`, so that it respects the base-ring module structures on cohomology, and then finite-dimensionality for coherent sheaves on proper schemes. On every finite intersection `V` the sections stay short exact because `H¹(V, F) = 0`, so the Čech complexes form a short exact sequence (`shortExact_map_cechComplexFunctor`). `I` is flasque, so `Č(U, I)` is acyclic (`TopCat.Sheaf.quasiIso_cechAugmentation_of_isFlasque`) and so is its sheaf cohomology. feat: derive parallel-sided end conditions from an inverted coordinate (#18224)

This PR derives the parallel-sided-end condition of the Schwarz--Christoffel formula at a real zero of the continuous inverted coordinate `g = (f - q)⁻¹` of a Riemann map `f` onto an unbounded domain. First, `exists_eventually_mem_of_inverted_coordinate_eq_zero` shows that if far out the domain is covered by pairwise disjoint open ends, then near such a zero `f` takes its values in a single end. Second, `exists_ball_halfStrip_end_of_inverted_coordinate` applies when that end is a half-strip `{ρ < re ((w - c) / b), 0 < im ((w - c) / b) < π}` contained in the image. In that case the half-strip's exponential coordinate `exp ((f - c') / b')` extends to a function `G` on a closed upper half-disc about the zero. `G` is continuous and injective, vanishes at the zero, is real on the diameter and maps the open half-disc into the upper half-plane. That is exactly the `e i = -1` clause of `hvertex` in `eqOn_const_mul_schwarzChristoffelPrimitive_add_of_polygonal_boundary`, and the conclusion is stated in that clause's exact shape so the assembly can use it directly.

Milestone: `ConformalMapping/README.md`, Layers, **L6 — Schwarz–Christoffel: explicit conformal maps onto polygons**, on the "several vertices at infinity" frontier item of `ConformalMapping/STATUS.md` (the existence theorem for polygonal domains with several ends, such as strips). Merged #18058 supplied the finite side and corner conditions away from the zeros of `g`, using `exists_ball_side_of_inverted_coordinate` and `exists_ball_corner_of_inverted_coordinate`. #18000 supplied injectivity away from the zeros, and #17451 the characterization of the zeros as escapes to infinity. The several-ended existence theorem still lacked the end conditions *at* the zeros, and the PR bodies of #18058 and #18000 name "match every zero of the coordinate to a polygonal end, derive the corresponding end condition" as the next step. This PR does that for parallel-sided ends, the end type of a strip. The new theorems will be consumed by the third `hvertex` clause of `eqOn_const_mul_schwarzChristoffelPrimitive_add_of_polygonal_boundary` when the several-ended existence theorem is assembled. After this PR, L6's several-ends path still needs the analogous end conditions at zeros for sector ends (`e ∈ (-3, -1)`) and half-strip-exterior ends (`e = -3`), a proof that distinct zeros correspond to distinct ends, and the assembly of the existence theorem.

A key step is that the zero is isolated on the real axis. With several accesses to infinity, `g` is only injective away from its zeros, so injectivity of `G` across the zero is not automatic. It comes from reflecting `G`, which is real on the diameter, and applying isolated zeros of the reflected holomorphic function. feat: Lᵖ contraction of Schwarz rearrangement (#18229)

This PR proves that Schwarz rearrangement is a contraction for every `Lᵖ` distance with `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`: for a.e.-measurable `f g : E → ℝ≥0∞` on a finite-dimensional real normed space with additive Haar measure, `eLpNorm (fun x ↦ edist (f* x) (g* x)) p μ ≤ eLpNorm (fun x ↦ edist (f x) (g x)) p μ` (`TauCeti.eLpNorm_edist_schwarzRearrangement_le`). The lintegral form for real `1 ≤ p`, the one-sided form `∫⁻ (f* - g*) ^ p ≤ ∫⁻ (f - g) ^ p` for truncated differences, and the pointwise `L^∞` bound `edist (f* x) (g* x) ≤ essSup (edist f g)` are separate theorems. None of them needs a finiteness or integrability hypothesis, and infinite values are allowed.

It advances `Isoperimetry/README.md`, milestone **I2 — Symmetrization, rearrangements, and convex geometry**, specifically the target in the Schwarz-rearrangement paragraph: "Establish equimeasurability, layer cake, all `Lᵖ` norm comparisons that reduce to equimeasurability, order preservation, `Lᵖ` contraction for `1 ≤ p < ∞`, and the Hardy–Littlewood inequality." #18043 said in its description that this `Lᵖ` contraction was the last item of that paragraph still missing; all the other items are on `main`. The roadmap names a direct consumer in I5: "I2's `L¹` contraction gives `u_j* → u*` in `L¹`". After this PR, every item in the I2 Schwarz-rearrangement paragraph is on `main`. The remaining I2 work is Steiner perimeter nonincrease, convergence of iterated Steiner symmetrizations to the ball, and the convex-body surface-area and parallel-volume targets.

The proof follows Lieb–Loss, *Analysis*, Theorem 3.5 (nonexpansivity of rearrangement), which is cited in the module docstring, using the convex-function-as-mixture-of-hinges argument:
- Two rearranged superlevel sets are concentric, so the measure of their set difference is the truncated difference of the original level measures (`addHaar_setOf_lt_schwarzRearrangement_sdiff`, simp). It is at most `μ ({s < f} \ {t < g})`.

+/-!
+# Tangent spaces of the affine abelianization
+
+For a geometrically reduced affine group of finite type over a field, the kernel of the
+differential of the affine abelianization is the Lie algebra of the scheme-theoretic derived
+subgroup. Consequently every bracket of ambient tangent vectors lies in that Lie algebra:
+`[Lie G, Lie G] ⊆ Lie([G,G])`. If the ambient group is smooth, the abelianization projection
+is smooth and its differential is surjective. Thus differentiating the abelianization gives
+an exact sequence of Lie algebras, in every characteristic.

+The containment does not assert equality with the derived Lie ideal. In positive
+characteristic such an equality requires additional care. All tangent results allow values
+in any commutative coefficient algebra, including nonreduced algebras.

+The construction combines the affine abelianization of `Derived.Abelianization`, the exact
+coinvariant-kernel theorem, and the tangent-kernel comparison. Smoothness uses the geometric
+derived-subgroup theorem and the smooth-kernel criterion for faithfully flat homomorphisms.

+          (Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra k (coinvariants (isNormal_derivedDefiningIdeal H)) B) := by
+  letI := (coinvariants (isNormal_derivedDefiningIdeal H)).hopfAlgebra
+  let f := derivationCompLieHom (B := B) (coinvariantsι (isNormal_derivedDefiningIdeal H)).hom
+  let _ : Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced k H := isGeometricallyReduced_of_smooth k H
+  have hker : f.ker = (isNormal_derivedDefiningIdeal H).lieIdeal (B := B) :=
+    ker_derivationCompLieHom_coinvariantsι_derivedDefiningIdeal H
+  exact hker ▸ f.quotKerEquivOfSurjective

+/-- The tangent abelianization equivalence sends a tangent class to its restriction to
+the derived coinvariants, namely the differential of the quotient projection. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem abelianizationLieEquiv_apply_mk [Algebra.Smooth k H]
+    (d : Derivation k H (Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra k H B)) :
+    let := (coinvariants (isNormal_derivedDefiningIdeal H)).hopfAlgebra

+      derivationComp (B := B) (coinvariantsι (isNormal_derivedDefiningIdeal H)).hom d := by
+  let := (coinvariants (isNormal_derivedDefiningIdeal H)).hopfAlgebra
+  let _ : Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced k H := isGeometricallyReduced_of_smooth k H

+  generalize (isNormal_derivedDefiningIdeal H).lieIdeal (B := B) = I at hker ⊢
+  cases hker

+    (derivationCompLieHom_apply _ d)

+vector from its image under the quotient differential. -/
+@[simp]

+    (d : Derivation k H (Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra k H B)) :
+    let := (coinvariants (isNormal_derivedDefiningIdeal H)).hopfAlgebra
+    (abelianizationLieEquiv H).symm
+        (derivationComp (B := B) (coinvariantsι (isNormal_derivedDefiningIdeal H)).hom d) =
+      LieSubmodule.Quotient.mk d := by
+  let := (coinvariants (isNormal_derivedDefiningIdeal H)).hopfAlgebra
+  dsimp only
+  rw [← abelianizationLieEquiv_apply_mk H, LieEquiv.symm_apply_apply]
+
+end CommHopfAlgCat

+# Defining ideals of dynamic subgroups under closed immersions
+
+A closed immersion identifies the dynamic parabolic and unipotent subgroup with the
+scheme-theoretic inverse images of the corresponding ambient subgroups. This file expresses
+that compatibility as equality of defining Hopf ideals. In particular, differentiating these
+equalities allows a faithful matrix representation to compute dynamic tangent spaces.
+
+The comparison retains the infinitesimal structure; no reducedness or smoothness
+assumption is required.

+

+-/
+
+public section
+

+
+namespace BialgHom
+
+universe u v w
+
+variable {R : Type u} {H : Type v} {K : Type w}
+  [CommRing R] [CommRing H] [CommRing K] [HopfAlgebra R H] [HopfAlgebra R K]

+  -- HopfIdeal.eq_of_forall_quotientPointsSubgroup_eq.

+  intro A
+  ext g
+  rw [quotientPointsSubgroup_parabolicDefiningHopfIdeal,
+    mem_parabolic_iff_of_surjective φ hφ l g,

+  rw [CommHopfAlgCat.mem_quotientPointsSubgroup_iff,

+public import TauCeti.Algebra.AlgebraicGroup.Dynamic.LeviDecomposition.Differential

+/-!
+# The Lie algebra of a dynamic parabolic as a semidirect sum
+
+The Lie algebra of a dynamic parabolic is the semidirect sum of its unipotent Lie ideal and
+its Levi Lie subalgebra. The action is the restriction of the adjoint action, so the mixed
+bracket is retained. The underlying map adds the two ambient tangent derivations, and its
+inverse has Levi coordinate equal to the differential of the dynamic limit.
+
+The two factors are realized inside the parabolic Lie algebra: the unipotent ideal is the
+kernel of the limit differential, and the Levi subalgebra is the inverse image of the ambient
+Levi tangent subalgebra. Their membership lemmas identify these descriptions with vanishing
+on the respective defining Hopf ideals. All constructions work over arbitrary commutative
+base rings and coefficient algebras, including nonreduced ones.
+
+This combines the differential and tangent decompositions in `Dynamic.LeviDecomposition`
+with the internal semidirect-sum recognition theorem `LieIdeal.semiDirectSumEquiv`.
+
+## References
+
+* B. Conrad, O. Gabber, G. Prasad, *Pseudo-reductive Groups*, §2.1.
+* J. S. Milne, *Algebraic Groups* (2017), §§10 and 13.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open TauCeti TauCeti.Cocharacter
+
+namespace BialgHom
+
+universe u v
+
+variable {R H : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing H] [HopfAlgebra R H]
+variable {B : Type v} [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
+
+/-- The tangent Lie ideal of the dynamic unipotent subgroup, inside the parabolic Lie algebra.
+It is the kernel of the differential of the dynamic limit. -/
+noncomputable def unipotentLieIdeal (l : H →ₐc[R] LaurentPolynomial R) :
+    LieIdeal B ((parabolicDefiningHopfIdeal l).lieSubalgebra (B := B)) :=
+  (parabolicLimitLieHom (B := B) l).ker
+
+/-- Membership in the unipotent Lie ideal is membership of the ambient tangent vector in
+`Lie U(λ)`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem mem_unipotentLieIdeal (l : H →ₐc[R] LaurentPolynomial R)
+    (d : (parabolicDefiningHopfIdeal l).lieSubalgebra (B := B)) :
+    d ∈ unipotentLieIdeal l ↔ d.val ∈ l.unipotentDefiningHopfIdeal.lieSubalgebra := by
+  rw [unipotentLieIdeal, LieHom.mem_ker, parabolicLimitLieHom_eq_zero_iff]
+
+/-- The tangent Lie subalgebra of the dynamic Levi, inside the parabolic Lie algebra. -/
+noncomputable def leviLieSubalgebra (l : H →ₐc[R] LaurentPolynomial R) :
+    LieSubalgebra B ((parabolicDefiningHopfIdeal l).lieSubalgebra (B := B)) :=
+  ((leviDefiningHopfIdeal l).lieSubalgebra (B := B)).comap
+    ((parabolicDefiningHopfIdeal l).lieSubalgebra (B := B)).incl
+
+/-- Membership in the Levi Lie subalgebra is membership of the ambient tangent vector in
+`Lie Z(λ)`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem mem_leviLieSubalgebra (l : H →ₐc[R] LaurentPolynomial R)
+    (d : (parabolicDefiningHopfIdeal l).lieSubalgebra (B := B)) :
+    d ∈ leviLieSubalgebra l ↔ d.val ∈ (leviDefiningHopfIdeal l).lieSubalgebra := by
+  rfl
+

+theorem isCompl_unipotentLieIdeal_leviLieSubalgebra
+    (l : H →ₐc[R] LaurentPolynomial R) :
+    IsCompl (unipotentLieIdeal (B := B) l).toSubmodule
+      (leviLieSubalgebra (B := B) l).toSubmodule := by
+  constructor
+  · rw [Submodule.disjoint_def]
+    intro d hu hz
+    apply Subtype.ext
+    exact (Submodule.disjoint_def.mp (disjoint_lieSubalgebra_unipotent_levi (B := B) l))
+      d.val ((mem_unipotentLieIdeal l d).mp hu) ((mem_leviLieSubalgebra l d).mp hz)
+  · rw [Submodule.codisjoint_iff_exists_add_eq]
+    intro d
+    obtain ⟨u, hu, z, hz, hd⟩ := exists_add_lieSubalgebra_unipotent_levi l d.property
+    have hsum := sup_lieSubalgebra_unipotent_levi (B := B) l
+    have huP : u ∈ (parabolicDefiningHopfIdeal l).lieSubalgebra := by
+      rw [← LieSubalgebra.mem_toSubmodule, ← hsum]
+      exact Submodule.mem_sup_left hu
+    have hzP : z ∈ (parabolicDefiningHopfIdeal l).lieSubalgebra := by
+      rw [← LieSubalgebra.mem_toSubmodule, ← hsum]
+      exact Submodule.mem_sup_right hz

+      (mem_leviLieSubalgebra l _).mpr hz, Subtype.ext hd.symm⟩

+/-- The Levi Lie algebra acts on the unipotent Lie ideal by the adjoint action. -/
+noncomputable def leviLieAction (l : H →ₐc[R] LaurentPolynomial R) :
+    leviLieSubalgebra (B := B) l →ₗ⁅B⁆

+/-- On ambient derivations the Levi action is the Lie bracket, with the Levi vector first. -/

+/-!
+# Infinitesimal conjugation by a cocharacter
+
+The coefficients of the adjoint action of the generic cocharacter point on a tangent
+vector are obtained by applying that vector to the coefficients of universal conjugation.
+Together with the coefficient criteria for dynamic tangent spaces, this relates their
+defining equations to the infinitesimal conjugation action, without choosing matrices
+or imposing smoothness or finite projectivity on the cotangent module.
+
+The argument uses the tensor contraction formula for the differential of universal
+conjugation in `Tangent.Conjugation`.
+
+## References
+
+* B. Conrad, O. Gabber, G. Prasad, *Pseudo-reductive Groups*, §2.1.
+* J. S. Milne, *Algebraic Groups* (2017), §§10 and 13.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open TauCeti TauCeti.Cocharacter WithConv
+open scoped TensorProduct
+
+namespace Derivation
+
+variable {R H B : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing H] [HopfAlgebra R H]
+  [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
+
+/-- The Laurent coefficients of infinitesimal conjugation are the derivatives of the
+universal conjugation coefficients. This holds with arbitrary coefficient algebras. -/
+theorem coeff_adDerivation_genericPoint
+    (d : Derivation R H (Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra R H B))
+    (l : H →ₐc[R] LaurentPolynomial R) (h : H) (n : ℤ) :
+    (Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra.algEquivSelf R H (LaurentPolynomial B)
+      (adDerivation (LaurentPolynomial B)
+        (pointInCounitAlgebra (LaurentPolynomial B) (genericPoint B l))
+        (mapValue (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R B (LaurentPolynomial B)) d) h)).coeff n =
+      Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra.algEquivSelf R H B
+        (d ((Cocharacter.conjugationAlgHom l h).coeff n)) := by
+  let P := genericPoint H l
+  let Q := Cocharacter.constPoint H (toConv (AlgHom.id R H))
+  have hc := AlgHom.congr_fun (HopfAlgebra.productMap_comp_conjugationAlgHom P Q) h
+  have hfamily : (Algebra.TensorProduct.productMap P.ofConv Q.ofConv)
+      (HopfAlgebra.conjugationAlgHom (R := R) (H := H) h) =
+      Cocharacter.conjugationAlgHom l h := by
+    rw [AlgHom.comp_apply] at hc
+    ext n
+    rw [hc, ← conjugate_apply]
+    simpa only [ofConv_toConv, AlgHom.id_apply] using
+      coeff_conjugate l (toConv (AlgHom.id R H)) h n
+  rw [adDerivation_eq_lift_conjugationAlgHom, ← hfamily]
+  generalize HopfAlgebra.conjugationAlgHom (R := R) (H := H) h = z
+  induction z using TensorProduct.inductionOn with
+  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, AddMonoidAlgebra.coeff_add,
+      Finsupp.add_apply, hx, hy]
+  | tmul a b =>
+    rw [TensorProduct.lift.tmul, LinearMap.compl₁₂_apply, LinearMap.mul_apply', map_mul]
+    have hp : Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra.algEquivSelf R H (LaurentPolynomial B)
+        ((pointInCounitAlgebra (LaurentPolynomial B) (genericPoint B l)).ofConv a) =
+        (genericPoint B l).ofConv a := by
+      rw [pointInCounitAlgebra_apply]
+      exact Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra.algEquivSelf_apply R H (LaurentPolynomial B) _
+    simp only [AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply, Derivation.coeFn_coe]
+    rw [hp, mapValue_apply, Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra.algEquivSelf_map]
+    simp only [Algebra.TensorProduct.productMap_apply_tmul, P, Q,
+      genericPoint_ofConv, constPoint_apply, ofConv_toConv, AlgHom.comp_apply,
+      AlgHom.id_apply, IsScalarTower.coe_toAlgHom']
+    rw [← LaurentPolynomial.C_eq_algebraMap (R := B),
+      ← LaurentPolynomial.C_eq_algebraMap (R := H)]
+    simp only [← LaurentPolynomial.single_eq_C, AddMonoidAlgebra.coeff_mul_single_zero,
+      AddMonoidAlgebra.coeff_mapAlgHom, Algebra.ofId_apply]
+    rw [d.leibniz, d.map_algebraMap, smul_zero, add_zero,

+    simp
+
+end Derivation

+module

+public import TauCeti.Algebra.AlgebraicGroup.Dynamic.Unipotent.Representability
+public import TauCeti.Algebra.AlgebraicGroup.HopfIdeal.Tangent
+
+/-!
+# Coefficient criteria for dynamic tangent spaces
+
+The tangent Lie algebra of a dynamic parabolic consists of the derivations annihilating
+all negative coefficients of universal conjugation. For the dynamic unipotent subgroup,
+the constant coefficient must also be annihilated. These criteria apply over arbitrary
+commutative base rings and coefficient algebras, including nonreduced ones.
+
+They express the infinitesimal extension and zero-limit conditions without choosing a
+faithful matrix representation.
+
+The proofs use the coefficient presentations of the dynamic defining ideals and
+`TauCeti.HopfIdeal.mem_lieSubalgebra_iff_of_toIdeal_eq_span`.
+
+## References
+
+* B. Conrad, O. Gabber, G. Prasad, *Pseudo-reductive Groups*, §2.1.
+* J. S. Milne, *Algebraic Groups* (2017), §§10 and 13.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open TauCeti TauCeti.Cocharacter
+
+namespace BialgHom
+
+universe u v w
+
+variable {R : Type u} {H : Type v} {B : Type w}
+variable [CommRing R] [CommRing H] [HopfAlgebra R H] [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
+
+/-- A tangent vector belongs to the dynamic parabolic exactly when it kills every negative
+Laurent coefficient of universal conjugation. Use this as an explicit rewrite: the general
+`TauCeti.HopfIdeal.mem_lieSubalgebra_iff` already simplifies tangent membership. -/
+theorem mem_lieSubalgebra_parabolicDefiningHopfIdeal_iff
+    (l : H →ₐc[R] LaurentPolynomial R)
+    (d : Derivation R H (Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra R H B)) :
+    d ∈ (parabolicDefiningHopfIdeal l).lieSubalgebra (B := B) ↔
+      ∀ h : H, ∀ n : ℤ, n < 0 → d ((conjugationAlgHom l h).coeff n) = 0 := by
+  rw [HopfIdeal.mem_lieSubalgebra_iff_of_toIdeal_eq_span _
+    (parabolicDefiningHopfIdeal_toIdeal l)]
+  constructor
+  · intro hd h n hn
+    exact hd _ ⟨h, n, hn, rfl⟩
+  · rintro hd x ⟨h, n, hn, rfl⟩
+    exact hd h n hn
+
+/-- A tangent vector belongs to the dynamic unipotent subgroup exactly when it kills every
+nonpositive Laurent coefficient of universal conjugation. Use this as an explicit rewrite: the
+general
+`TauCeti.HopfIdeal.mem_lieSubalgebra_iff` already simplifies tangent membership. -/
+theorem mem_lieSubalgebra_unipotentDefiningHopfIdeal_iff
+    (l : H →ₐc[R] LaurentPolynomial R)
+    (d : Derivation R H (Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra R H B)) :
+    d ∈ l.unipotentDefiningHopfIdeal.lieSubalgebra (B := B) ↔
+      ∀ h : H, ∀ n : ℤ, n ≤ 0 → d ((conjugationAlgHom l h).coeff n) = 0 := by
+  have hspan : (l.unipotentDefiningHopfIdeal).toIdeal =
+      Ideal.span ({x | ∃ h : H, ∃ n : ℤ,
+        n < 0 ∧ (conjugationAlgHom l h).coeff n = x} ∪
+        {x | ∃ h : H, (conjugationAlgHom l h).coeff 0 -
+          algebraMap R H (Coalgebra.counit h) = x}) := by
+    rw [unipotentDefiningHopfIdeal_toIdeal, parabolicDefiningHopfIdeal_toIdeal,
+      Ideal.span_union]
+  rw [HopfIdeal.mem_lieSubalgebra_iff_of_toIdeal_eq_span _ hspan]
+  constructor
+  · intro hd h n hn
+    rcases lt_or_eq_of_le hn with hn | rfl
+    · exact hd _ (Or.inl ⟨h, n, hn, rfl⟩)
+    · have hz := hd _ (Or.inr ⟨h, rfl⟩)
+      simpa only [map_sub, d.map_algebraMap, sub_zero] using hz
+  · intro hd x hx
+    rcases hx with ⟨h, n, hn, rfl⟩ | ⟨h, rfl⟩
+    · exact hd h n hn.le
+    · simpa only [map_sub, d.map_algebraMap, sub_zero] using hd h 0 le_rfl
+
+end BialgHom

+module

+public import TauCeti.Algebra.AlgebraicGroup.Dynamic.Tangent.Adjoint
+public import TauCeti.Algebra.AlgebraicGroup.Tangent.RootSpace
+import Mathlib.Algebra.DirectSum.Decomposition
+
+/-!
+# Adjoint weights of dynamic tangent spaces
+
+For a cocharacter, the Lie algebra of its dynamic parabolic is the sum of the
+nonnegative adjoint weight spaces, and that of its dynamic unipotent subgroup is the
+sum of the strictly positive weight spaces. The coefficient of infinitesimal conjugation
+extracts the corresponding weight component.
+
+These statements use the existing adjoint comodule and its internal weight decomposition.
+They assume finite projectivity of the augmentation cotangent module, but impose no field,
+characteristic, reducedness or smoothness assumption.
+
+## References
+
+* B. Conrad, O. Gabber, G. Prasad, *Pseudo-reductive Groups*, §2.1.
+* J. S. Milne, *Algebraic Groups* (2017), §§10 and 13.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open TauCeti TauCeti.Cocharacter WithConv
+open scoped TensorProduct DirectSum
+
+namespace BialgHom
+
+universe u
+
+variable {R H : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing H] [HopfAlgebra R H]
+variable [Module.Finite R (Bialgebra.CotangentSpace R H)]
+  [Module.Projective R (Bialgebra.CotangentSpace R H)]
+
+attribute [local instance] Derivation.adjointComodule Classical.decEq
+
+private theorem adDerivation_genericPoint_of_mem_adjointWeightSpace
+    (l : H →ₐc[R] LaurentPolynomial R) (m : ℤ)
+    (x : Module.Dual R (Bialgebra.CotangentSpace R H))
+    (hx : x ∈ Derivation.adjointWeightSpace
+      ((AddMonoidAlgebra.toMultiplicativeBialgEquiv R R ℤ).toBialgHom.comp l)
+      (Multiplicative.ofAdd m)) :
+    Derivation.adDerivation (LaurentPolynomial R)
+        (Derivation.pointInCounitAlgebra (LaurentPolynomial R) (genericPoint R l))
+        (Derivation.mapValue (Algebra.ofId R (LaurentPolynomial R))
+          (Derivation.cotangentLinearEquiv (B := R) x)) =
+      (LaurentPolynomial.T m : LaurentPolynomial R) •
+        Derivation.mapValue (Algebra.ofId R (LaurentPolynomial R))
+          (Derivation.cotangentLinearEquiv (B := R) x) := by
+  let e := AddMonoidAlgebra.toMultiplicativeBialgEquiv R R ℤ
+  let π := e.toBialgHom.comp l
+  let f := e.symm.toAlgEquiv.toAlgHom
+  have hp : f.comp π.toAlgHom = (genericPoint R l).ofConv := by
+    ext a : 1
+    simp only [f, π, BialgHom.comp_toAlgHom, AlgHom.comp_apply,
+      AlgEquiv.coe_toAlgHom, genericPoint_ofConv]
+    ext n
+    simp
+  have ht : f (MonoidAlgebra.single (Multiplicative.ofAdd m) (1 : R)) =
+      LaurentPolynomial.T m := by
+    apply e.injective
+    rw [← AddMonoidAlgebra.toMultiplicativeBialgEquiv_single (R := R) (A := R) (M := ℤ) m 1]
+    exact e.apply_symm_apply _
+  have ha := Derivation.endOfPoint_tmul_of_mem_adjointWeightSpace π f 1 hx
+  rw [hp, one_mul, ht] at ha
+  have hd := congrArg (Derivation.tangentScalarExtensionEquiv
+    (R := R) (A := H) (B := LaurentPolynomial R)) ha
+  rw [Derivation.tangentScalarExtensionEquiv_adjointComodule_endOfPoint
+      (CommAlgCat.of R (LaurentPolynomial R)),
+    Derivation.tangentScalarExtensionEquiv_tmul,
+    Derivation.tangentScalarExtensionEquiv_tmul, one_smul] at hd
+  exact hd

+/-- On an adjoint weight vector of weight `m`, differentiation of the `n`th universal
+conjugation coefficient is zero unless `n = m`, when it recovers the vector. -/
+theorem cotangentLinearEquiv_coeff_conjugationAlgHom_of_mem_adjointWeightSpace
+    (l : H →ₐc[R] LaurentPolynomial R) {m : ℤ}
+    {x : Module.Dual R (Bialgebra.CotangentSpace R H)}
+    (hx : x ∈ Derivation.adjointWeightSpace
+      ((AddMonoidAlgebra.toMultiplicativeBialgEquiv R R ℤ).toBialgHom.comp l)
+      (Multiplicative.ofAdd m)) (h : H) (n : ℤ) :
+    Derivation.cotangentLinearEquiv (B := R) x ((Cocharacter.conjugationAlgHom l h).coeff n) =

+  have hc := congrArg (fun D : Derivation R H
+      (Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra R H (LaurentPolynomial R)) =>
+    (Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra.algEquivSelf R H (LaurentPolynomial R) (D h)).coeff n) he
+  have hm : IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R R (LaurentPolynomial R) =
+      Algebra.ofId R (LaurentPolynomial R) := by ext
+  rw [← hm, Derivation.coeff_adDerivation_genericPoint] at hc
+  rw [TauCeti.algEquivSelf_derivation_smul_apply, Derivation.mapValue_apply,
+    Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra.algEquivSelf_map] at hc
+  simp only [hm, Algebra.ofId_apply, ← LaurentPolynomial.C_eq_algebraMap,
+    ← LaurentPolynomial.single_eq_C, AddMonoidAlgebra.coeff_mul_single_zero,
+    LaurentPolynomial.T_apply] at hc

+  simpa only [eq_comm (a := m) (b := n), ite_mul, one_mul, zero_mul,

+private theorem cotangentLinearEquiv_decompose_adjointWeightSpace_apply
+    (l : H →ₐc[R] LaurentPolynomial R)

+      ((AddMonoidAlgebra.toMultiplicativeBialgEquiv R R ℤ).toBialgHom.comp l)
+    let : DirectSum.Decomposition W :=
+      (Derivation.isInternal_adjointWeightSpace _).chooseDecomposition

+        ((Cocharacter.conjugationAlgHom l h).coeff n) =
+      Derivation.cotangentLinearEquiv (B := R)

+  classical
+  let : DecidableEq (Multiplicative ℤ) := Classical.decEq _
+  let π := (AddMonoidAlgebra.toMultiplicativeBialgEquiv R R ℤ).toBialgHom.comp l
+  let W := Derivation.adjointWeightSpace π
+  let : DirectSum.Decomposition W :=
+    (Derivation.isInternal_adjointWeightSpace π).chooseDecomposition
+  have hy : y ∈ ⨆ α, W α := by
+    rw [(Derivation.isInternal_adjointWeightSpace π).submodule_iSup_eq_top]
+    trivial
+  induction hy using Submodule.iSup_induction' with
+  | mem α y hy =>
+    rw [cotangentLinearEquiv_coeff_conjugationAlgHom_of_mem_adjointWeightSpace
+      l (m := α.toAdd) hy]
+    by_cases hα : α = Multiplicative.ofAdd n
+    · subst α
+      rw [DirectSum.decompose_of_mem_same W hy]
+      exact ite_eq_left rfl
+    · rw [DirectSum.decompose_of_mem_ne W hy hα]
+      simp only [map_zero, Derivation.zero_apply, ite_eq_right_iff]
+      intro hn
+      exact (hα (congrArg Multiplicative.ofAdd hn.symm)).elim
+  | zero =>
+    simp only [map_zero, DirectSum.decompose_zero, DirectSum.zero_apply,
+      Submodule.coe_zero, Derivation.zero_apply]
+  | add y z _ _ hy hz =>
+    simpa only [map_add, Derivation.add_apply, DirectSum.decompose_add,
+      DirectSum.add_apply, Submodule.coe_add] using congrArg₂ (· + ·) hy hz
+
+/-- The sum of a set of adjoint weight spaces is characterized by vanishing of the
+infinitesimal conjugation coefficients at all weights outside that set. -/
+theorem mem_iSup_adjointWeightSpace_iff_coeff_conjugationAlgHom
+    (l : H →ₐc[R] LaurentPolynomial R) (s : Set ℤ)
+    (x : Module.Dual R (Bialgebra.CotangentSpace R H)) :
+    x ∈ (⨆ n ∈ s, Derivation.adjointWeightSpace
+      ((AddMonoidAlgebra.toMultiplicativeBialgEquiv R R ℤ).toBialgHom.comp l)
+      (Multiplicative.ofAdd n)) ↔
+      ∀ h : H, ∀ n : ℤ, n ∉ s →
+        Derivation.cotangentLinearEquiv (B := R) x
+          ((Cocharacter.conjugationAlgHom l h).coeff n) = 0 := by

+  let : DecidableEq (Multiplicative ℤ) := Classical.decEq _
+  let π := (AddMonoidAlgebra.toMultiplicativeBialgEquiv R R ℤ).toBialgHom.comp l
+  let W := Derivation.adjointWeightSpace π

+  · intro hx h n hn
+    induction hx using Submodule.iSup_induction' with
+    | mem m y hy =>

+      | mem hm y hy =>
+        rw [cotangentLinearEquiv_coeff_conjugationAlgHom_of_mem_adjointWeightSpace l hy]
+        simp only [ite_eq_right_iff]
+        intro hnm
+        subst m
+        exact (hn hm).elim
+      | zero => simp
+      | add y z _ _ hy hz =>
+          simpa only [map_add, Derivation.add_apply, add_zero] using congrArg₂ (· + ·) hy hz
+    | zero => simp
+    | add y z _ _ hy hz =>
+        simpa only [map_add, Derivation.add_apply, add_zero] using congrArg₂ (· + ·) hy hz
+  · intro hx
+    have hzero (n : ℤ) (hn : n ∉ s) :
+        (DirectSum.decompose W x (Multiplicative.ofAdd n) :
+          Module.Dual R (Bialgebra.CotangentSpace R H)) = 0 := by
+      apply (Derivation.cotangentLinearEquiv (B := R)).injective

+        (Submodule.mem_iSup_of_mem hα (DirectSum.decompose W x α).property)
+    · exact (hzero α.toAdd hα) ▸ Submodule.zero_mem _

+/-- The tangent Lie algebra of the dynamic parabolic is the sum of the nonnegative
+adjoint weight spaces, transported from the cotangent-dual model of the ambient Lie algebra. -/
+theorem lieSubalgebra_parabolicDefiningHopfIdeal_toSubmodule
+    (l : H →ₐc[R] LaurentPolynomial R) :

+/-!
+# Dynamic tangent spaces in a faithful matrix representation
+
+Let a closed subgroup `G` of `GL_N` carry a cocharacter that acts diagonally with integer
+weights `w i` on the ambient representation. Its dynamic parabolic tangent space consists
+exactly of the tangent vectors whose matrix entries have nonnegative weight difference
+`w i - w j`; its dynamic unipotent tangent space consists exactly of those with strictly
+positive weight difference. These are equations on the differential of the given closed
+immersion, with no smoothness, field, or finite-type assumptions.
+
+These criteria also apply to nonreduced subgroups and coefficient algebras.
+
+## References
+
+* B. Conrad, O. Gabber, G. Prasad, *Pseudo-reductive Groups*, §2.1.
+* J. S. Milne, *Algebraic Groups* (2017), §§10 and 13.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open TauCeti.Cocharacter
+
+namespace TauCeti.GeneralLinear.Dynamic
+
+universe u v w
+
+variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {N : ℕ}
+variable {H : Type v} [CommRing H] [HopfAlgebra R H]
+variable {B : Type w} [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
+
+/-- In a faithful representation with diagonal cocharacter, the dynamic parabolic Lie
+algebra is cut out by the negative-weight matrix entries of the differential. -/
+theorem mem_lieSubalgebra_parabolicDefiningHopfIdeal_iff_of_weightCocharacter
+    (w : Fin N → ℤ) (φ : coordinateHopfAlgebra R N →ₐc[R] H)
+    (hφ : Function.Surjective φ) (l : H →ₐc[R] LaurentPolynomial R)
+    (hl : l.comp φ = weightCocharacter (R := R) w)
+    (d : Derivation R H (Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra R H B)) :
+    d ∈ (parabolicDefiningHopfIdeal l).lieSubalgebra (B := B) ↔
+      (tangentMatrix N (derivationCompLieHom (B := B) φ d)).BlockTriangular
+        (OrderDual.toDual ∘ w) := by
+  -- Combine the closed-immersion identities from Dynamic.ClosedImmersion.Ideals
+  -- with the matrix criterion in GeneralLinear.Weight.Parabolic.Tangent.
+  rw [φ.parabolicDefiningHopfIdeal_eq_map_of_surjective hφ l, hl,
+    parabolicDefiningHopfIdeal_weightCocharacter]
+  exact mem_lieSubalgebra_map_weightParabolicDefiningHopfIdeal_iff w φ d
+

+algebra is cut out by the nonpositive-weight matrix entries of the differential. -/

+    (w : Fin N → ℤ) (φ : coordinateHopfAlgebra R N →ₐc[R] H)
+    (hφ : Function.Surjective φ) (l : H →ₐc[R] LaurentPolynomial R)
+    (hl : l.comp φ = weightCocharacter (R := R) w)

+/-!
+# Tangent equations of weight-unipotent subgroups
+
+The Lie algebra of the weight-unipotent subgroup of `GL_N` consists of matrices whose
+`(i,j)` entry vanishes whenever `w i ≤ w j`. Thus only strictly positive weight differences
+occur. The inverse-image criterion applies the same equations to the differential of any
+homomorphism into `GL_N`, over arbitrary commutative base and coefficient rings.
+
+## References
+
+* J. S. Milne, *Algebraic Groups* (2017), §§10 and 13.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+namespace TauCeti.GeneralLinear
+

+
+/-- A tangent vector belongs to the weight-unipotent subgroup exactly when every entry
+of nonpositive weight difference vanishes. -/
+theorem mem_lieSubalgebra_weightUnipotentDefiningHopfIdeal_iff (w : Fin N → ℤ)
+    (d : Derivation R (coordinateHopfAlgebra R N)
+      (Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra R (coordinateHopfAlgebra R N) B)) :
+    d ∈ HopfIdeal.lieSubalgebra (B := B) (weightUnipotentDefiningHopfIdeal R w) ↔
+      ∀ i j, w i ≤ w j → tangentMatrix N d i j = 0 := by
+  -- Use HopfIdeal.mem_lieSubalgebra_iff_of_toIdeal_eq_span and the tangent-matrix map
+  -- of GeneralLinear.Tangent, as in the weight-parabolic calculation.
+  rw [HopfIdeal.mem_lieSubalgebra_iff_of_toIdeal_eq_span _
+    (weightUnipotentDefiningHopfIdeal_toIdeal R w)]
+  have hentry (i j : Fin N) :
+      d ((genericMatrix R N) i j -
+        (1 : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) (coordinateHopfAlgebra R N)) i j) =
+      d ((genericMatrix R N) i j) := by
+    classical
+    simp only [map_sub, Matrix.one_apply]
+    split_ifs <;> simp
+  constructor
+  · intro hd i j hij
+    have hz := hd _ (sub_one_apply_mem_weightUnipotentRelationSet R w hij)
+    rw [hentry] at hz
+    rw [tangentMatrix_apply, ← genericMatrix_apply, hz, map_zero]
+  · intro hd x hx
+    obtain ⟨i, j, hij, rfl⟩ := (mem_weightUnipotentRelationSet_iff R w x).mp hx
+    rw [hentry]
+    apply (Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra.algEquivSelf R (coordinateHopfAlgebra R N) B).injective
+    rw [map_zero, genericMatrix_apply, ← tangentMatrix_apply]
+    exact hd i j hij
+
+/-- The tangent space of the inverse image of a weight-unipotent subgroup is cut out by
+the nonpositive-weight entries of the differential. -/
+theorem mem_lieSubalgebra_map_weightUnipotentDefiningHopfIdeal_iff
+    {H : Type*} [CommRing H] [HopfAlgebra R H]
+    (w : Fin N → ℤ) (f : coordinateHopfAlgebra R N →ₐc[R] H)
+    (d : Derivation R H (Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra R H B)) :
+    d ∈ HopfIdeal.lieSubalgebra (B := B) ((weightUnipotentDefiningHopfIdeal R w).map f) ↔
+      ∀ i j, w i ≤ w j → tangentMatrix N (derivationCompLieHom (B := B) f d) i j = 0 := by
+  rw [HopfIdeal.lieSubalgebra_map, LieSubalgebra.mem_comap]
+  exact mem_lieSubalgebra_weightUnipotentDefiningHopfIdeal_iff w _
+
+end TauCeti.GeneralLinear

+group over a characteristic-zero field is reductive. Coordinate arrows reverse direction:

+connectedness descend along the injective coordinate map; Cartier's theorem supplies
+smoothness. This argument does not establish quotient-image reductivity in positive
+characteristic, where reductivity does not imply linear reductivity.

+/-!
+# Semisimplicity under extension of characteristic-zero fields
+
+Semisimplicity of a finite-type affine group over a field of characteristic zero is preserved
+and reflected by every field extension. Neither field needs to be algebraically closed, the
+extension need not be algebraic, and the group need not split. In particular, one can establish
+semisimplicity on a split model over an extension and descend to the original group.
+
+The Lie-algebra criterion in `Semisimple.Lie` reduces the assertion to invariance of the
+nondegeneracy of the Killing form under scalar extension. Geometric connectedness is also
+preserved and reflected by field extension. Smoothness is automatic by Cartier's theorem.
+
+## Main declarations
+
+* `TauCeti.semisimpleCommHopfAlgProperty.baseChange`: preservation of semisimplicity.
+* `TauCeti.semisimpleCommHopfAlgProperty.of_baseChange`: descent of semisimplicity.
+* `TauCeti.semisimpleCommHopfAlgProperty.baseChange_iff`: the scalar-extension criterion,
+  without a separate connectedness hypothesis.
+
+## References
+
+* J. S. Milne, *Algebraic Groups* (2017), Chapters 10 and 22.
+* J. E. Humphreys, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §13.
+
+The tangent comparison is `TauCeti.isKilling_lie_baseChange_iff`; the group-theoretic
+comparison is `TauCeti.semisimpleCommHopfAlgProperty_iff_isKilling_lieAlgebra`.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open scoped TensorProduct
+
+namespace TauCeti.semisimpleCommHopfAlgProperty
+
+universe u
+
+variable {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [CharZero k]
+variable {H : FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.{u, u} k}
+
+/-- A semisimple affine group in characteristic zero remains semisimple after any extension
+of the ground field, including transcendental extensions. -/
+theorem baseChange (hH : semisimpleCommHopfAlgProperty k H) :
+    semisimpleCommHopfAlgProperty K (FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.baseChange (K := K) H) := by
+  let _ : LieAlgebra.IsKilling K
+      (Derivation K (K ⊗[k] H) (Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra K (K ⊗[k] H) K)) :=
+    (isKilling_lie_baseChange_iff (k := k) (K := K) (H := H)).mpr hH.isKilling_lieAlgebra
+  let _ : Algebra.Smooth k H := hH.smooth
+  exact semisimpleCommHopfAlgProperty.of_isKilling (Algebra.Smooth.baseChange k H K)
+    (geometricallyConnectedCommHopfAlgProperty.baseChange k K H.obj hH.geometricallyConnected)
+
+/-- Semisimplicity descends along any extension of characteristic-zero fields. No smoothness,
+connectedness, or splitting hypothesis on the original group needs to be supplied. -/
+theorem of_baseChange
+    (hH : semisimpleCommHopfAlgProperty K (FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.baseChange (K := K) H)) :
+    semisimpleCommHopfAlgProperty k H := by
+  let _ : CharZero K := charZero_of_injective_algebraMap (algebraMap k K).injective
+  let _ : LieAlgebra.IsKilling k (Derivation k H (Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra k H k)) :=
+    (isKilling_lie_baseChange_iff (k := k) (K := K) (H := H)).mp hH.isKilling_lieAlgebra
+  exact semisimpleCommHopfAlgProperty.of_isKilling
+    ((smoothCommHopfAlgProperty_iff _).mp (smoothCommHopfAlgProperty_of_charZero k H.obj))
+    (geometricallyConnectedCommHopfAlgProperty.of_baseChange k K H.obj hH.geometricallyConnected)
+
+-- The defining simp lemma `semisimpleCommHopfAlgProperty_iff` already expands the left-hand side,
+-- so adding this equivalence to the simp set would violate simpNF.
+/-- In characteristic zero, a finite-type affine group is semisimple exactly when it becomes
+semisimple after a field extension. The extension may be arbitrary. -/
+theorem baseChange_iff (H : FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.{u, u} k) :
+    semisimpleCommHopfAlgProperty K (FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.baseChange (K := K) H) ↔
+      semisimpleCommHopfAlgProperty k H :=
+  ⟨of_baseChange, baseChange⟩
+
+end TauCeti.semisimpleCommHopfAlgProperty

+
+Over a field of characteristic zero, an affine group of finite type is semisimple if and
+only if it is reductive and its scheme-theoretic center is finite. In particular, this
+criterion distinguishes the semisimple part of reductive structure theory from central
+torus factors. No splitting or algebraic-closedness assumption is imposed on the field.
+
+For the converse, the geometric solvable radical of a reductive group is central. If the
+center is finite, the radical is finite as well; being smooth and connected, it is trivial.
+The proof uses the centrality theorem in `Solvable.Radical.Reductive` and the finite connected
+reduced group theorem in `Connected.Finite`. The forward implication is the finite-center
+theorem in `Semisimple.Center.Finite`.

+/-!
+# Special linear groups are scheme-theoretically perfect
+
+Over every field, the scheme-theoretic derived subgroup of `SLₙ` is the whole group.
+Consequently every homomorphism from `SLₙ` to a commutative affine group is trivial,
+and every character is one. These statements include all characteristics and ranks.
+
+Perfectness of the matrix group over an algebraic closure, together with reduced finite-type
+point separation, proves the equality of defining Hopf ideals. It is essential to pass to the
+algebraic closure: `SL₂(𝔽₂)` and `SL₂(𝔽₃)` are not perfect as abstract groups. No assertion
+of perfectness of rational-point groups over the original field is made here.
+
+The proof follows the algebraic-closure point-separation argument of
+`TauCeti.GeneralLinear.derivedDefiningIdeal_eq_specialLinear_definingHopfIdeal`, using
+`Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.commutator_eq_top` in place of the general-linear determinant kernel.
+The universal property of the affine abelianization supplies the statement about commutative
+images.
+
+## References
+
+* J. S. Milne, *Algebraic Groups* (2017), §§6d and 21.
+* W. C. Waterhouse, *Introduction to Affine Group Schemes*, Chapter 10.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open CategoryTheory WithConv
+
+namespace TauCeti.SpecialLinear
+
+universe u
+
+variable (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ)
+
+/-- **The scheme-theoretic derived subgroup of `SLₙ` is `SLₙ` over every field.**
+The zero Hopf ideal defines the whole group, so this retains the full subgroup scheme structure,
+including its points with values in nonreduced algebras. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem derivedDefiningIdeal_eq_bot :
+    CommHopfAlgCat.derivedDefiningIdeal (R := k) (coordinateHopfAlgebra k n) = ⊥ := by
+  classical
+  apply le_bot_iff.mp
+  rw [← HopfIdeal.toIdeal_le_toIdeal, HopfIdeal.bot_toIdeal]
+  intro x hx
+  rw [Ideal.mem_bot]
+  let K := AlgebraicClosure k
+  let _ : IsReduced (coordinateHopfAlgebra k n) := isReduced_of_smooth k _
+  apply eq_of_forall_algHom_apply_eq (k := k) (K := K)
+  intro f
+  rw [map_zero]
+  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := Infinite.exists_notMem_finset ({0, 1, -1} : Finset K)
+  have ha' : a ≠ 0 ∧ a ≠ 1 ∧ a ≠ -1 := by
+    simpa only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, not_or] using ha
+  have hSL : commutator (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin n) K) = ⊤ :=
+    Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.commutator_eq_top ha'.1 (sq_ne_one_iff.mpr ha'.2)
+  let e := pointsMulEquiv (R := k) (A := K) n
+  have hpoints : commutator (WithConv (coordinateHopfAlgebra k n →ₐ[k] K)) = ⊤ := by
+    apply Subgroup.map_injective (f := e.toMonoidHom) e.injective
+    rw [Subgroup.map_commutator_eq_commutator e.surjective, hSL,
+      Subgroup.map_top_of_surjective e.toMonoidHom e.surjective]
+  have hg : toConv f ∈ commutator (WithConv (coordinateHopfAlgebra k n →ₐ[k] K)) := by
+    rw [hpoints]
+    trivial
+  exact (CommHopfAlgCat.mem_quotientPointsSubgroup_iff _ _ _ _).mp
+    (CommHopfAlgCat.commutator_le_quotientPointsSubgroup_of_le_derivedDefiningIdeal
+      (coordinateHopfAlgebra k n) _ le_rfl (CommAlgCat.of k K) hg) x hx
