+/-- Every homomorphism from `SLₙ` to a commutative affine group is trivial, in every
+characteristic. The target need not be of finite type. -/
+theorem hom_eq_unit_comp_counit {C : _root_.CommHopfAlgCat.{u} k}
+    [Coalgebra.IsCocomm k C] (f : C ⟶ coordinateHopfAlgebra k n) :
+    f = _root_.CommHopfAlgCat.ofHom

+  let _ : Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced k (coordinateHopfAlgebra k n) :=

+    (coordinateHopfAlgebra k n)).mp (derivedDefiningIdeal_eq_bot k n) C f

+/-- The special linear group has no nontrivial algebraic characters over any field. -/

+  apply GroupLike.ext
+  have hx := x.sub_one_mem_derivedDefiningIdeal
+  rw [derivedDefiningIdeal_eq_bot, HopfIdeal.mem_bot, sub_eq_zero] at hx
+  exact hx
+
+end TauCeti.SpecialLinear

+/-!
+# Differentiating universal conjugation
+
+Contracting the first factor of the universal conjugation morphism against a point and
+its second factor against a tangent derivation gives the adjoint action of that point.
+This coordinate formula allows one to compute infinitesimal conjugation families without
+choosing a matrix representation.
+
+The calculation uses `Derivation.snd_conjugate_tangentPoint` and
+`TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.productMap_comp_conjugationAlgHom`.
+
+## References
+
+* J. S. Milne, *Algebraic Groups* (2017), §§10 and 14.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open TauCeti WithConv TrivSqZeroExt
+open scoped TensorProduct
+
+namespace Derivation
+
+variable {R H B : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring H] [HopfAlgebra R H]
+  [CommSemiring B] [Algebra R B]
+
+/-- The adjoint action is obtained by evaluating the conjugating coordinate at the point
+and differentiating the acted-on coordinate at the identity. -/
+theorem adDerivation_eq_lift_conjugationAlgHom
+    (d : Derivation R H (Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra R H B))
+    (g : WithConv (H →ₐ[R] Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra R H B)) (h : H) :
+    adDerivation B g d h =
+      TensorProduct.lift ((LinearMap.mul R (Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra R H B)).compl₁₂
+        g.ofConv.toLinearMap d.toLinearMap)
+        (HopfAlgebra.conjugationAlgHom (R := R) (H := H) h) := by
+  let C := Bialgebra.CounitAlgebra R H B
+  let q := AlgHom.mapValue (H := H) (inlAlgHom R C C) g
+  let p := (derivationMulEquivTangentKer R H B (Multiplicative.ofAdd d)).val
+  have hc := AlgHom.congr_fun (HopfAlgebra.productMap_comp_conjugationAlgHom q p) h
+  rw [AlgHom.comp_apply] at hc
+  rw [← snd_conjugate_tangentPoint d g h, ← hc]
+  have hm : (sndHom C C).restrictScalars R ∘ₗ
+      (Algebra.TensorProduct.productMap q.ofConv p.ofConv).toLinearMap =
+      TensorProduct.lift ((LinearMap.mul R C).compl₁₂
+        g.ofConv.toLinearMap d.toLinearMap) := by
+    apply TensorProduct.ext'
+    intro a b
+    have hp : snd (p.ofConv b) = d b :=
+      derivationMulEquivTangentKer_apply_snd (Multiplicative.ofAdd d) b
+    simpa [q] using congrArg (fun x => g.ofConv a * x) hp
+  exact LinearMap.congr_fun hm _
+
+end Derivation

+  rw [iff_multiplicativeType_and_geometricallyConnected_and_geometricallyReduced,

+
+/-!
+# Semisimple endomorphisms of bundled finite comodules
+
+Over a commutative ring, the bundled finitely generated comodule `FGComoduleCat.of N`
+reconstructs its additive group from its module structure. So semisimplicity of an endomorphism
+on the bundled object and on the unbundled comodule `N` use different additive-group instances.
+This file records that the two statements agree, so callers need not rebuild the
+`@`-explicit transport.
+
+## Main declarations
+
+* `TauCeti.isSemisimple_fgComoduleCatOf_iff`: semisimplicity of an endomorphism on
+  `FGComoduleCat.of N` agrees with semisimplicity on `N`.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+universe u v w
+
+/-- Semisimplicity of an endomorphism of a bundled finitely generated comodule agrees with
+semisimplicity on the underlying unbundled comodule. The bundled object reconstructs its additive
+group from its module structure, so the two statements use different additive group instances. -/
+theorem isSemisimple_fgComoduleCatOf_iff {R : Type u} {C : Type v} {N : Type w} [CommRing R]
+    [AddCommMonoid C] [Module R C] [Coalgebra R C] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
+    [Comodule R C N] [Module.Finite R N] (f : Module.End R N) :
+    @Module.End.IsSemisimple R (FGComoduleCat.of (R := R) (C := C) N) _
+        (FGComoduleCat.instAddCommGroupCarrier _) _ f ↔ f.IsSemisimple :=
+  @LinearEquiv.isSemisimple_iff R (FGComoduleCat.of (R := R) (C := C) N) _
+    (FGComoduleCat.instAddCommGroupCarrier _) _ f N _ _ f (LinearEquiv.refl R N) rfl
+
+end TauCeti

+module
+
+public import TauCeti.Algebra.Homology.Curved.Module.Right.Abelian
+public import TauCeti.Algebra.Homology.Curved.Module.Right.Triangulated
+public import TauCeti.CategoryTheory.Triangulated.LocalizingClosure
+
+/-!
+# Totalizations and the acyclic classes of the second kind
+
+Let `A` be a right-convention curved DG algebra. A short exact sequence `0 → K → L → M → 0` in
+the abelian category of curved right `A`-modules with closed morphisms has a **totalization**:
+the total curved module of the three-term sequence, here realized as the iterated cone
+`cone(cone(K → L) → M)` with underlying graded module `K[2] × L[1] × M`. Curved modules have no
+homology, so this totalization replaces the homology of the sequence as the basic acyclic
+object.
+
+Inside the triangulated curved homotopy category this file defines, as closures generated by
+the class of totalizations,
+
+* the **absolutely acyclic** objects: the thick closure `ObjectProperty.triangEnvelope`;
+* the **coacyclic** objects: the localizing closure, closed under small coproducts;
+* the **contraacyclic** objects: the colocalizing closure, closed under small products.
+
+Each of these, and more generally every isomorphism-closed triangulated subcategory containing
+all totalizations, satisfies the two-out-of-three property for short exact sequences: if two
+terms of a short exact sequence of curved modules belong to it, so does the third. In
+particular its preimage in the closed category is extension-closed in the sense of Mathlib's
+`CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderExtensions`.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `TauCeti.CurvedDGRightModuleCat.totalization`: the totalization of a short complex of curved
+  modules.
+* `TauCeti.CurvedDGRightModuleCat.totalizations`: the class of totalizations of short exact
+  sequences in the curved homotopy category.
+* `TauCeti.CurvedDGRightModuleCat.absolutelyAcyclic`,
+  `TauCeti.CurvedDGRightModuleCat.coacyclic`, `TauCeti.CurvedDGRightModuleCat.contraacyclic`:
+  the three acyclic classes of the second kind.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `TauCeti.CurvedDGRightModuleCat.prop_X₂_of_shortExact`,
+  `TauCeti.CurvedDGRightModuleCat.prop_X₃_of_shortExact`,
+  `TauCeti.CurvedDGRightModuleCat.prop_X₁_of_shortExact`: an isomorphism-closed triangulated
+  subcategory containing all totalizations is closed under extensions, cokernels of
+  monomorphisms and kernels of epimorphisms.
+* `TauCeti.CurvedDGRightModuleCat.isClosedUnderExtensions_inverseImage`: the same closure under
+  extensions, as Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderExtensions`; instances
+  record it for the three acyclic classes.
+
+## References
+
+* L. Positselski, *Differential graded Koszul duality: an introductory survey*, Bull. Lond. Math.
+  Soc. **55** (2023), 1553–1640, Section 7.6.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated
+
+namespace TauCeti.CurvedDGRightModuleCat
+
+universe u
+
+-- The closed and homotopy categories keep the original curved module objects.
+attribute [local implicit_reducible] ForgetEnrichment dgClosedToHomotopy
+  DGHomotopyCategory.of DGHomotopyCategory.underlying
+
+variable {R A : Type u} [CommRing R] [Ring A] [Algebra R A]
+  {𝒜 : ℤ → Submodule R A} [GradedAlgebra 𝒜] {d : A →ₗ[R] A} {w : A}
+  {h : IsCurvedDGAlgebra 𝒜 d w}
+
+/-! ### Totalizations -/
+
+section Totalization
+
+variable (S : ShortComplex
+  (ForgetEnrichment (CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (CurvedDGRightModuleCat.{u, u, u} h)))
+
+/-- The **totalization** of a short complex `K ⟶ L ⟶ M` of curved right modules: the iterated
+cone `cone(cone(K ⟶ L) ⟶ M)`, with underlying graded module `K[2] × L[1] × M`. -/
+noncomputable def totalization : CurvedDGRightModuleCat.{u, u, u} h :=
+  cone (coneDesc S.f S.g S.zero)
+
+/-- The totalization is the cone of the map `cone(K ⟶ L) ⟶ M` induced by the second map. -/
+theorem totalization_eq : totalization S = cone (coneDesc S.f S.g S.zero) :=
+  (rfl)
+
+variable (R h) in
+/-- The objects of the curved homotopy category represented by totalizations of short exact
+sequences of curved modules. -/
+def totalizations : ObjectProperty (DGHomotopyCategory R (CurvedDGRightModuleCat.{u, u, u} h)) :=
+  ObjectProperty.ofObj fun S : {S : ShortComplex
+      (ForgetEnrichment (CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (CurvedDGRightModuleCat.{u, u, u} h)) //
+      S.ShortExact} ↦
+    DGHomotopyCategory.of R (totalization S.1)
+
+variable {S} in
+/-- The totalization of a short exact sequence belongs to the class of totalizations. -/
+theorem totalizations_totalization (hS : S.ShortExact) :
+    totalizations R h (DGHomotopyCategory.of R (totalization S)) := by
+  rw [totalizations]
+  exact ObjectProperty.ofObj_apply _ (Subtype.mk S hS)
+
+/-- An object property contains all totalizations exactly when it contains the totalization of
+every short exact sequence. -/
+theorem totalizations_le_iff
+    (Q : ObjectProperty (DGHomotopyCategory R (CurvedDGRightModuleCat.{u, u, u} h))) :
+    totalizations R h ≤ Q ↔
+      ∀ S : ShortComplex
+        (ForgetEnrichment (CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (CurvedDGRightModuleCat.{u, u, u} h)),
+        S.ShortExact → Q (DGHomotopyCategory.of R (totalization S)) := by
+  rw [totalizations, ObjectProperty.ofObj_le_iff]
+  exact ⟨fun H S hS ↦ H ⟨S, hS⟩, fun H S ↦ H S.1 S.2⟩
+
+open ZeroObject in
+instance : (totalizations R h).Nonempty :=
+  ⟨_, totalizations_totalization (ShortComplex.Splitting.ofHasBinaryBiproduct
+    (0 : ForgetEnrichment (CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (CurvedDGRightModuleCat.{u, u, u} h))
+    0).shortExact⟩
+
+end Totalization
+
+section TwoOutOfThree
+
+variable (Q : ObjectProperty (DGHomotopyCategory R (CurvedDGRightModuleCat.{u, u, u} h)))
+  [Q.IsTriangulated] [Q.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms] (hQ : totalizations R h ≤ Q)
+  {S : ShortComplex
+    (ForgetEnrichment (CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (CurvedDGRightModuleCat.{u, u, u} h))}
+  (hS : S.ShortExact)
+
+include hQ hS
+
+/-- In the presence of all totalizations, the cone of the first map of a short exact sequence
+lies in an isomorphism-closed triangulated subcategory exactly when its last term does. -/
+theorem prop_cone_iff_of_shortExact :
+    Q (DGHomotopyCategory.of R (cone S.f)) ↔ Q ((dgClosedToHomotopy R).obj S.X₃) := by
+  have hT := hQ _ (totalizations_totalization hS)
+  exact ⟨fun hC ↦ prop_target_of_prop_cone _ Q hC hT,
+    fun h₃ ↦ prop_source_of_prop_cone _ Q h₃ hT⟩
+
+/-- **Closure under extensions.** An isomorphism-closed triangulated subcategory of the curved
+homotopy category containing all totalizations contains the middle term of a short exact
+sequence whose outer terms it contains. -/
+theorem prop_X₂_of_shortExact (h₁ : Q ((dgClosedToHomotopy R).obj S.X₁))
+    (h₃ : Q ((dgClosedToHomotopy R).obj S.X₃)) : Q ((dgClosedToHomotopy R).obj S.X₂) :=
+  prop_target_of_prop_cone S.f Q h₁ ((prop_cone_iff_of_shortExact Q hQ hS).2 h₃)
+
+/-- **Closure under cokernels of monomorphisms.** An isomorphism-closed triangulated subcategory
+of the curved homotopy category containing all totalizations contains the last term of a short
+exact sequence whose first two terms it contains. -/
+theorem prop_X₃_of_shortExact (h₁ : Q ((dgClosedToHomotopy R).obj S.X₁))
+    (h₂ : Q ((dgClosedToHomotopy R).obj S.X₂)) : Q ((dgClosedToHomotopy R).obj S.X₃) :=
+  (prop_cone_iff_of_shortExact Q hQ hS).1 (prop_cone S.f Q h₁ h₂)
+
+/-- **Closure under kernels of epimorphisms.** An isomorphism-closed triangulated subcategory
+of the curved homotopy category containing all totalizations contains the first term of a short
+exact sequence whose last two terms it contains. -/
+theorem prop_X₁_of_shortExact (h₂ : Q ((dgClosedToHomotopy R).obj S.X₂))
+    (h₃ : Q ((dgClosedToHomotopy R).obj S.X₃)) : Q ((dgClosedToHomotopy R).obj S.X₁) :=
+  prop_source_of_prop_cone S.f Q h₂ ((prop_cone_iff_of_shortExact Q hQ hS).2 h₃)
+
+end TwoOutOfThree
+
+/-- An isomorphism-closed triangulated subcategory of the curved homotopy category containing all
+totalizations pulls back to an extension-closed class of curved modules. -/
+theorem isClosedUnderExtensions_inverseImage
+    (Q : ObjectProperty (DGHomotopyCategory R (CurvedDGRightModuleCat.{u, u, u} h)))
+    [Q.IsTriangulated] [Q.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms] (hQ : totalizations R h ≤ Q) :
+    (Q.inverseImage (dgClosedToHomotopy R)).IsClosedUnderExtensions where
+  prop_X₂_of_shortExact hS h₁ h₃ := prop_X₂_of_shortExact Q hQ hS h₁ h₃
+
+/-! ### The three acyclic classes -/
+
+variable (R h) in
+/-- The **absolutely acyclic** curved right modules: the smallest thick triangulated subcategory
+of the curved homotopy category containing all totalizations of short exact sequences. -/
+def absolutelyAcyclic :
+    ObjectProperty (DGHomotopyCategory R (CurvedDGRightModuleCat.{u, u, u} h)) :=
+  (totalizations R h).triangEnvelope
+
+variable (R h) in
+/-- The **coacyclic** curved right modules: the smallest isomorphism-closed triangulated
+subcategory of the curved homotopy category containing all totalizations of short exact
+sequences and closed under coproducts indexed by `Type u`. -/
+def coacyclic : ObjectProperty (DGHomotopyCategory R (CurvedDGRightModuleCat.{u, u, u} h)) :=
+  (totalizations R h).localizingClosure
+
+variable (R h) in
+/-- The **contraacyclic** curved right modules: the smallest isomorphism-closed triangulated
+subcategory of the curved homotopy category containing all totalizations of short exact
+sequences and closed under products indexed by `Type u`. -/
+def contraacyclic : ObjectProperty (DGHomotopyCategory R (CurvedDGRightModuleCat.{u, u, u} h)) :=
+  (totalizations R h).colocalizingClosure
+
+instance : (absolutelyAcyclic R h).IsTriangulated :=
+  inferInstanceAs (totalizations R h).triangEnvelope.IsTriangulated
+
+instance : (absolutelyAcyclic R h).IsStableUnderRetracts :=
+  inferInstanceAs (totalizations R h).triangEnvelope.IsStableUnderRetracts
+
+instance : (absolutelyAcyclic R h).IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms :=
+  inferInstanceAs (totalizations R h).triangEnvelope.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms
+
+instance : (coacyclic R h).IsTriangulated :=
+  inferInstanceAs (totalizations R h).localizingClosure.IsTriangulated
+
+instance : (coacyclic R h).IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms :=
+  inferInstanceAs (totalizations R h).localizingClosure.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms
+
+instance (J : Type u) : (coacyclic R h).IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape (Discrete J) :=
+  inferInstanceAs ((totalizations R h).localizingClosure.IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape (Discrete J))
+
+instance : (contraacyclic R h).IsTriangulated :=
+  inferInstanceAs (totalizations R h).colocalizingClosure.IsTriangulated
+
+instance : (contraacyclic R h).IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms :=
+  inferInstanceAs (totalizations R h).colocalizingClosure.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms
+
+instance (J : Type u) :
+    (contraacyclic R h).IsClosedUnderLimitsOfShape (Discrete J) :=
+  inferInstanceAs ((totalizations R h).colocalizingClosure.IsClosedUnderLimitsOfShape (Discrete J))
+
+variable (R h) in
+/-- Totalizations of short exact sequences are absolutely acyclic. -/
+theorem totalizations_le_absolutelyAcyclic :
+    totalizations R h ≤ absolutelyAcyclic R h :=
+  (totalizations R h).le_triangEnvelope
+
+variable (R h) in
+/-- Totalizations of short exact sequences are coacyclic. -/
+theorem totalizations_le_coacyclic : totalizations R h ≤ coacyclic R h :=
+  (totalizations R h).le_localizingClosure
+
+variable (R h) in
+/-- Totalizations of short exact sequences are contraacyclic. -/
+theorem totalizations_le_contraacyclic : totalizations R h ≤ contraacyclic R h :=
+  (totalizations R h).le_colocalizingClosure
+
+/-- The universal property of the absolutely acyclic class: it is contained in every thick
+triangulated subcategory of the curved homotopy category containing all totalizations. -/
+theorem absolutelyAcyclic_le_iff
+    {Q : ObjectProperty (DGHomotopyCategory R (CurvedDGRightModuleCat.{u, u, u} h))}
+    [Q.IsTriangulated] [Q.IsStableUnderRetracts] :
+    absolutelyAcyclic R h ≤ Q ↔ totalizations R h ≤ Q :=
+  (totalizations R h).triangEnvelope_le_iff
+
+/-- The universal property of the coacyclic class: it is contained in every isomorphism-closed
+triangulated subcategory of the curved homotopy category containing all totalizations and closed
+under coproducts indexed by `Type u`. -/
+theorem coacyclic_le_iff
+    {Q : ObjectProperty (DGHomotopyCategory R (CurvedDGRightModuleCat.{u, u, u} h))}
+    [Q.IsTriangulated] [Q.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms]
+    [∀ J : Type u, Q.IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape (Discrete J)] :
+    coacyclic R h ≤ Q ↔ totalizations R h ≤ Q :=
+  (totalizations R h).localizingClosure_le_iff
+
+/-- The universal property of the contraacyclic class: it is contained in every

+module
+
+public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Linear.FunctorCategory
+public import TauCeti.Algebra.Homology.DG.Bimodule.InternalHom.Basic
+public import TauCeti.Algebra.Homology.DG.Bimodule.Category
+
+/-!
+# Functoriality of the internal Hom of DG modules
+
+For a DG `(A, B)`-bimodule `M` and a right DG `B`-module `N`, the internal Hom
+`Hom_B(M, N)` is a right DG `A`-module. Precomposition with a bimodule morphism and
+postcomposition with a right-module morphism give the map `f ↦ v ∘ f ∘ u`.
+These maps preserve degrees, the right `A`-action, and the graded-commutator differential.
+
+`DGRightModule.InternalHom.map` supplies this map, with evaluation, identity, and composition
+lemmas. `DGBimoduleCat.internalHomFunctor` packages it as a bifunctor, contravariant in the
+bimodule and covariant in the right module. Both variables act linearly. This is the internal-Hom
+functor used in the tensor–Hom adjunction; no claim of derived functoriality is made here.
+
+## References
+
+* B. Keller, *Deriving DG categories*, Sections 2 and 6.1.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open CategoryTheory MulOpposite
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+universe uR uA uB uM uN
+
+variable {R : Type uR} {A : Type uA} {B : Type uB}
+  [CommRing R] [Ring A] [Ring B] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B]
+  {𝒜 : ℤ → Submodule R A} {ℬ : ℤ → Submodule R B}
+  [GradedAlgebra 𝒜] [GradedAlgebra ℬ]
+  {dA : A →ₗ[R] A} {dB : B →ₗ[R] B}
+  {hA : IsDGAlgebra 𝒜 dA} {hB : IsDGAlgebra ℬ dB}
+
+/-- The internal Hom from a DG `(A, B)`-bimodule to a right DG `B`-module, bundled as a
+right DG `A`-module. The abbreviation keeps its carrier available for evaluation. -/
+noncomputable abbrev DGBimoduleCat.internalHomObj
+    (M : DGBimoduleCat.{uR, uA, uB, uM} hA hB) (N : DGRightModuleCat.{uR, uB, uN} hB) :
+    DGRightModuleCat.{uR, uA, max uM uN} hA :=
+  DGRightModuleCat.of (M.isDGBimodule.internalHom N.isDGRightModule)
+
+namespace DGRightModule.InternalHom
+
+variable {M M' M'' : DGBimoduleCat.{uR, uA, uB, uM} hA hB}
+  {N N' N'' : DGRightModuleCat.{uR, uB, uN} hB}
+
+private theorem comp_mem_cochains (u : M' ⟶ M) (v : N ⟶ N') {p : ℤ}
+    {f : M →ₗ[Bᵐᵒᵖ] N}
+    (hf : f ∈ dgRightModuleCochains (R := R) (ℳ := M.grading) (ℳN := N.grading) p) :
+    v.toLinearMap ∘ₗ f ∘ₗ u.val.toLinearMap ∈
+      dgRightModuleCochains (R := R) (ℳ := M'.grading) (ℳN := N'.grading) p := by
+  let u₀ := (dgRightModuleHomEquivZeroCocycles M'.isDGRightModule M.isDGRightModule u.val).1
+  let v₀ := (dgRightModuleHomEquivZeroCocycles N.isDGRightModule N'.isDGRightModule v).1
+  let c := dgRightModuleCochains.comp v₀
+    (dgRightModuleCochains.comp ⟨f, hf⟩ u₀ (add_zero p)) (zero_add p)
+  convert c.2 using 1
+  ext x
+  simp only [c, dgRightModuleCochains.comp_apply, LinearMap.comp_apply,
+    u₀, v₀, dgRightModuleHomEquivZeroCocycles_apply, DGRightModuleHom.coe_toLinearMap]
+
+private def mapLinearMap (u : M' ⟶ M) (v : N ⟶ N') :
+    InternalHom 𝒜 B M.grading N.grading →ₗ[Aᵐᵒᵖ] InternalHom 𝒜 B M'.grading N'.grading where
+  toFun f := ⟨⟨v.toLinearMap ∘ₗ coeLM f ∘ₗ u.val.toLinearMap, by
+    induction f using DirectSum.Decomposition.inductionOn (grading 𝒜 B M.grading N.grading) with
+    | zero => simp
+    | @homogeneous p f =>
+      exact Submodule.mem_iSup_of_mem p (comp_mem_cochains u v (mem_grading_iff.1 f.2))
+    | add f g hf hg =>
+      simpa only [map_add, LinearMap.add_comp, LinearMap.comp_add] using add_mem hf hg⟩⟩
+  map_add' f g := ext fun x ↦ by simp
+  map_smul' a f := ext fun x ↦ by simp
+
+private theorem mapLinearMap_apply (u : M' ⟶ M) (v : N ⟶ N')
+    (f : InternalHom 𝒜 B M.grading N.grading) (x : M') :
+    mapLinearMap u v f x = v (f (u x)) := by
+  simp [mapLinearMap]
+
+private theorem mapLinearMap_mem (u : M' ⟶ M) (v : N ⟶ N') {p : ℤ}
+    {f : InternalHom 𝒜 B M.grading N.grading} (hf : f ∈ grading 𝒜 B M.grading N.grading p) :
+    mapLinearMap u v f ∈ grading 𝒜 B M'.grading N'.grading p := by
+  rw [mem_grading_iff]
+  convert comp_mem_cochains u v (mem_grading_iff.1 hf) using 1
+  ext x
+  simp [mapLinearMap_apply]
+
+/-- Precompose with a DG bimodule morphism and postcompose with a DG right-module morphism.
+The resulting map of internal Homs is a morphism of DG right `A`-modules. -/
+noncomputable def map (u : M' ⟶ M) (v : N ⟶ N') :
+    M.internalHomObj N ⟶ M'.internalHomObj N' where
+  toLinearMap := mapLinearMap u v
+  map_mem' := mapLinearMap_mem u v
+  map_d' f := by
+    induction f using DirectSum.Decomposition.inductionOn (grading 𝒜 B M.grading N.grading) with
+    | zero => simp
+    | @homogeneous p f =>
+      apply ext
+      intro x
+      simp only [differential_apply_of_mem _ _ (mapLinearMap_mem u v f.2),
+        mapLinearMap_apply, differential_apply_of_mem _ _ f.2, map_sub, map_zsmul_unit,
+        DGBimoduleCat.map_d, DGRightModuleCat.map_d]
+    | add f g hf hg => simp only [map_add, hf, hg]
+
+/-- The induced map sends `f` to `v ∘ f ∘ u`, with no extra sign since `u` and `v` have
+ degree zero. -/
+@[simp↓]
+theorem map_apply (u : M' ⟶ M) (v : N ⟶ N')
+    (f : M.internalHomObj N) (x : M') :
+    map u v f x = v (f (u x)) := mapLinearMap_apply u v f x
+
+/-- Identity morphisms induce the identity on the internal Hom. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem map_id_id (M : DGBimoduleCat.{uR, uA, uB, uM} hA hB)
+    (N : DGRightModuleCat.{uR, uB, uN} hB) :
+    map (𝟙 M) (𝟙 N) = 𝟙 (M.internalHomObj N) := by
+  ext f x
+  rw [DGRightModuleCat.id_apply (M.internalHomObj N) f, map_apply]
+  simp
+
+/-- Internal Hom is contravariant in the bimodule and covariant in the right module. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem map_comp (u : M' ⟶ M) (u' : M'' ⟶ M') (v : N ⟶ N') (v' : N' ⟶ N'') :
+    map u v ≫ map u' v' = map (u' ≫ u) (v ≫ v') := by
+  ext f x
+  rw [DGRightModuleCat.comp_apply, map_apply, map_apply, map_apply]
+  simp
+
+/-- The induced map is additive in its contravariant argument. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem map_add_left (u u' : M' ⟶ M) (v : N ⟶ N') :
+    map (u + u') v = map u v + map u' v := by
+  ext f x
+  rw [map_apply, DGRightModuleCat.add_apply, add_apply, map_apply, map_apply]
+  simp
+
+/-- The induced map is additive in its covariant argument. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem map_add_right (u : M' ⟶ M) (v v' : N ⟶ N') :
+    map u (v + v') = map u v + map u v' := by
+  ext f x
+  rw [DGRightModuleCat.add_apply (map u v) (map u v') f, add_apply, map_apply, map_apply,
+    map_apply]
+  simp
+
+/-- The induced map is linear in its contravariant argument over the ground ring. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem map_smul_left (r : R) (u : M' ⟶ M) (v : N ⟶ N') :
+    map (r • u) v = r • map u v := by
+  ext f x
+  rw [map_apply, DGRightModuleCat.smul_apply, smul_apply, map_apply, DGBimoduleCat.smul_apply]
+  exact congrArg v ((coeLM f).map_smul_of_tower r (u x)) |>.trans
+    (v.toLinearMap.map_smul_of_tower r (f (u x)))
+
+/-- The induced map is linear in its covariant argument over the ground ring. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem map_smul_right (r : R) (u : M' ⟶ M) (v : N ⟶ N') :
+    map u (r • v) = r • map u v := by
+  ext f x
+  rw [DGRightModuleCat.smul_apply r (map u v) f, smul_apply, map_apply, map_apply]
+  simp
+
+@[simp]
+theorem map_zero_left (v : N ⟶ N') : map (0 : M' ⟶ M) v = 0 := by
+  ext f x
+  rw [map_apply, DGRightModuleCat.zero_apply, zero_apply]
+  simp
+
+@[simp]
+theorem map_zero_right (u : M' ⟶ M) : map u (0 : N ⟶ N') = 0 := by
+  ext f x
+  rw [DGRightModuleCat.zero_apply (M := M.internalHomObj N) (N := M'.internalHomObj N') f,
+    zero_apply, map_apply]
+  simp
+
+end DGRightModule.InternalHom
+
+namespace DGBimoduleCat
+
+open DGRightModule
+
+/-- The internal Hom out of a fixed DG bimodule, as a linear functor on DG right modules.
+The carrier lives in the maximum of the bimodule and right-module universes. -/
+-- Keep the object carrier reducible for evaluation of morphisms.
+noncomputable abbrev internalHom (M : DGBimoduleCat.{uR, uA, uB, uM} hA hB) :
+    DGRightModuleCat.{uR, uB, uN} hB ⥤ DGRightModuleCat.{uR, uA, max uM uN} hA where
+  obj N := M.internalHomObj N
+  map v := InternalHom.map (𝟙 M) v
+  map_id N := InternalHom.map_id_id M N
+  map_comp v v' := by
+    simpa only [Category.id_comp] using (InternalHom.map_comp (𝟙 M) (𝟙 M) v v').symm
+
+@[simp]
+theorem internalHom_obj (M : DGBimoduleCat.{uR, uA, uB, uM} hA hB)
+    (N : DGRightModuleCat.{uR, uB, uN} hB) :
+    M.internalHom.obj N = M.internalHomObj N :=
+  (rfl)
+
+@[simp]
+theorem internalHom_map (M : DGBimoduleCat.{uR, uA, uB, uM} hA hB)
+    {N N' : DGRightModuleCat.{uR, uB, uN} hB} (v : N ⟶ N') :
+    M.internalHom.map v = InternalHom.map (𝟙 M) v := (rfl)
+
+/-- The internal-Hom functor acts by postcomposition on elements. -/
+@[simp↓]
+theorem internalHom_map_apply (M : DGBimoduleCat.{uR, uA, uB, uM} hA hB)
+    {N N' : DGRightModuleCat.{uR, uB, uN} hB} (v : N ⟶ N')
+    (f : M.internalHomObj N) (x : M) :
+    M.internalHom.map v f x = v (f x) := by
+  rw [internalHom_map, InternalHom.map_apply]
+  simp
+
+instance (M : DGBimoduleCat.{uR, uA, uB, uM} hA hB) :
+    (internalHom.{uR, uA, uB, uM, uN} M).Additive where
+  map_add := by intros; exact InternalHom.map_add_right _ _ _
+
+instance (M : DGBimoduleCat.{uR, uA, uB, uM} hA hB) :
+    (internalHom.{uR, uA, uB, uM, uN} M).Linear R where
+  map_smul := fun v r ↦ InternalHom.map_smul_right r (𝟙 M) v
+
+/-- Internal Hom as a bifunctor on DG bimodules and DG right modules, contravariant in the
+bimodule. A bimodule morphism acts by precomposition, naturally in the right module. -/
+-- Keep the object and component formulas reducible for evaluation.
+noncomputable abbrev internalHomFunctor :
+    (DGBimoduleCat.{uR, uA, uB, uM} hA hB)ᵒᵖ ⥤
+      DGRightModuleCat.{uR, uB, uN} hB ⥤ DGRightModuleCat.{uR, uA, max uM uN} hA where
+  obj M := M.unop.internalHom
+  map u :=
+    { app N := InternalHom.map u.unop (𝟙 N)
+      naturality := fun _ _ v ↦ by
+        simp only [InternalHom.map_comp, Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp] }
+  map_id M := by
+    apply NatTrans.ext
+    funext N
+    exact InternalHom.map_id_id M.unop N
+  map_comp u u' := by
+    apply NatTrans.ext
+    funext N
+    simp only [NatTrans.comp_app, InternalHom.map_comp, CategoryTheory.unop_comp,
+      Category.id_comp]
+
+@[simp]
+theorem internalHomFunctor_obj (M : (DGBimoduleCat.{uR, uA, uB, uM} hA hB)ᵒᵖ) :
+    internalHomFunctor.obj M = internalHom.{uR, uA, uB, uM, uN} M.unop := (rfl)
+
+@[simp]
+theorem internalHomFunctor_map_app {M M' : DGBimoduleCat.{uR, uA, uB, uM} hA hB}
+    (u : Opposite.op M ⟶ Opposite.op M') (N : DGRightModuleCat.{uR, uB, uN} hB) :
+    (internalHomFunctor.map u).app N = InternalHom.map u.unop (𝟙 N) := (rfl)
+
+/-- The contravariant internal-Hom component acts by precomposition on elements. -/
+@[simp↓]
+theorem internalHomFunctor_map_app_apply {M M' : DGBimoduleCat.{uR, uA, uB, uM} hA hB}
+    (u : Opposite.op M ⟶ Opposite.op M') (N : DGRightModuleCat.{uR, uB, uN} hB)
+    (f : M.internalHomObj N) (x : M') :
+    (internalHomFunctor.map u).app N f x = f (u.unop x) := by
+  rw [internalHomFunctor_map_app, InternalHom.map_apply]
+  simp
+
+instance : (internalHomFunctor.{uR, uA, uB, uM, uN} (hA := hA) (hB := hB)).Additive where
+  map_add := by
+    intros
+    apply NatTrans.ext
+    funext N
+    exact InternalHom.map_add_left _ _ (𝟙 N)
+
+instance : (internalHomFunctor.{uR, uA, uB, uM, uN} (hA := hA) (hB := hB)).Linear R where
+  map_smul := by
+    intros
+    apply NatTrans.ext
+    funext N
+    exact InternalHom.map_smul_left _ _ (𝟙 N)
+
+end DGBimoduleCat

+
+public import TauCeti.Algebra.Lie.E6.Minuscule.Generated.Positive.Basic
+public import TauCeti.Algebra.Lie.E6.Minuscule.StandardComodule
+public import TauCeti.Algebra.Coalgebra.Subcomodule.Coordinate

+/-!
+# Invariant subspaces of the positive E₆ minuscule subgroup
+
+The subcomodules of the positive subgroup's 27-dimensional representation over a field
+are precisely the coordinate spans closed under the six raising operators. The weight torus
+separates the coordinate lines, while a raising operator sends a weight vector at a negative
+simple-root coordinate to its reflected weight vector. This classification is the flag
+input for testing maximality of the positive subgroup among connected solvable subgroups.
+
+The coordinate-span criterion works over every nontrivial commutative ring. The assertion
+that every invariant subspace is a coordinate span uses a field. No algebraic closure or
+restriction on the characteristic is needed.
+
+## References
+
+* J. C. Jantzen, *Representations of Algebraic Groups*, I.2.
+* J. E. Humphreys, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §§21 and 27.
+
+Weight extraction uses `Subcomodule.toSubmodule_eq_span_of_corestrict_eq_ofWeights`;
+the standard-comodule and root-point constructions follow the full generated E₆ carrier.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open CategoryTheory WithConv
+open scoped Matrix
+
+namespace TauCeti.E6Minuscule.Generated.Positive
+
+open DynkinType
+
+universe u
+
+noncomputable section
+
+variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
+
+/-- The standard representation of the positive subgroup generated over `R`. -/
+@[instance_reducible]
+def standardComodule : Comodule R (coordinateHopfAlgebra R) (Fin 27 → R) :=
+  GeneralLinear.corestrictStandardComodule R 27
+    (CommHopfAlgCat.mkQuotient _ (definingIdeal R)).hom
+
+attribute [local instance] standardComodule
+
+/-- The coefficient matrix is the ambient generic matrix modulo the positive subgroup's ideal. -/
+theorem coefficientMatrix_basisFun :
+    Comodule.coefficientMatrix (C := coordinateHopfAlgebra R) (Pi.basisFun R (Fin 27)) =
+      (GeneralLinear.genericMatrix R 27).map
+        (CommHopfAlgCat.mkQuotient _ (definingIdeal R)).hom := by
+  let _ := GeneralLinear.standardComodule R 27
+  rw [Comodule.coefficientMatrix_corestrict, GeneralLinear.coefficientMatrix_basisFun]
+  ext a b
+  simp only [Matrix.map_apply, BialgHom.toCoalgHom_apply]
+
+/-- Restriction to the weight torus splits the standard representation into its minuscule lines. -/
+theorem torusCorestrict_eq_ofWeights :
+    Comodule.Corestrict (CommHopfAlgCat.commonKernelLift (generator R) (.inr ())).hom.toCoalgHom =
+      Comodule.ofWeights (Pi.basisFun R (Fin 27)) minusculeCharacter := by
+  apply GeneralLinear.corestrict_corestrict_standardComodule_eq_ofWeights
+    (CommHopfAlgCat.mkQuotient _ (definingIdeal R)).hom
+    (CommHopfAlgCat.commonKernelLift (generator R) (.inr ())).hom e6MinusculeWeight
+  rw [← CommHopfAlgCat.hom_comp, CommHopfAlgCat.mkQuotient_comp_commonKernelLift,
+    generator_inr, generatorCoordinateMap_inr,
+    GeneralLinear.hom_weightTorusBaseChangeCoordinateMap, weightTable_weight]
+
+private theorem rootPoint_matrix (i : Fin 6) (A : CommAlgCat.{u} R)
+    (q : HopfAlgebra.points (R := R) (H := AdditiveGroup.coordinateHopfAlgebra R) A) :
+    GeneralLinear.pointToGeneralLinear 27
+        (toConv (q.ofConv.comp (generator R (.inl i)).hom.toAlgHom)) =
+      (rootSubgroupPoints (.inl i) A (AdditiveGroup.gaPointsMulEquiv q) :
+        Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin 27) A) := by
+  rw [generator_inl, generatorCoordinateMap_inl,
+    ← coordinateMap_comp_rootSubgroupToBaseChangeCoordinateMap]
+  simpa only [BialgHom.mapDomain_apply, CommHopfAlgCat.hom_comp, BialgHom.comp_toAlgHom,
+    AlgHom.comp_assoc] using
+    pointToGeneralLinear_mapDomain_rootSubgroupToBaseChangeCoordinateMap_eq_rootSubgroupPoints
+      R (.inl i) A q
+
+/-- Every positive subcomodule is stable under each raising-root point. -/
+theorem rootSubgroupPoints_mulVec_mem
+    (N : Subcomodule R (coordinateHopfAlgebra R) (Fin 27 → R))
+    (i : Fin 6) (t : Multiplicative R) {v : Fin 27 → R} (hv : v ∈ N) :
+    ((rootSubgroupPoints (.inl i) R t : Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin 27) R) :
+      Matrix (Fin 27) (Fin 27) R) *ᵥ v ∈ N := by
+  let q := (AdditiveGroup.gaPointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := R)).symm t
+  let f := CommHopfAlgCat.commonKernelLift (generator R) (.inl i)
+  have h := GeneralLinear.corestrictStandardComodule_mulVec_mem R 27
+    (CommHopfAlgCat.mkQuotient _ (definingIdeal R)).hom N
+    (toConv (q.ofConv.comp f.hom.toAlgHom)) hv
+  have hcomp : BialgHom.mapDomain (CommHopfAlgCat.mkQuotient _ (definingIdeal R)).hom
+      (toConv (q.ofConv.comp f.hom.toAlgHom)) =
+      toConv (q.ofConv.comp (generator R (.inl i)).hom.toAlgHom) := by
+    apply WithConv.ext
+    ext x
+    simp only [BialgHom.mapDomain_apply_apply, AlgHom.comp_apply]
+    exact congrArg (fun g ↦ q.ofConv (g.hom x))
+      (CommHopfAlgCat.mkQuotient_comp_commonKernelLift (generator R) (.inl i))
+  rw [hcomp, rootPoint_matrix R i (CommAlgCat.of R R) q, MulEquiv.apply_symm_apply] at h
+  exact h
+
+/-- A subcomodule containing a weight vector contains every vector obtained by one raising step. -/
+theorem single_reflection_mem
+    (N : Subcomodule R (coordinateHopfAlgebra R) (Fin 27 → R))
+    (i : Fin 6) (a : Fin 27) (ha : e6MinusculeWeight a i = -1)
+    (hv : Pi.single a (1 : R) ∈ N) :
+    Pi.single (e6MinusculeReflection i a) (1 : R) ∈ N := by
+  have h := rootSubgroupPoints_mulVec_mem R N i (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1) hv
+  rw [coe_rootSubgroupPoints_inl, toAdd_ofAdd, one_smul, Matrix.add_mulVec,
+    Matrix.one_mulVec, Matrix.mulVec_single_one, weightTable.raisingMatrix_map_col] at h
+  rw [← Subcomodule.mem_toSubmodule]
+  simpa only [weightTable_weight, weightTable_reflection, ha, ↓reduceIte,
+    add_sub_cancel_left] using N.toSubmodule.sub_mem h hv
+
+variable {R}
+
+private theorem stable_of_raising_closed (s : Set (Fin 27))
+    (hs : ∀ i a, a ∈ s → e6MinusculeWeight a i = -1 → e6MinusculeReflection i a ∈ s) :
+    (Pi.basisFun R (Fin 27)).coordinateSpanIsStable (C := coordinateHopfAlgebra R) s := by
+  classical
+  let w : Fin 27 → ℤ := fun a ↦ if a ∈ s then 1 else 0
+  have hle : GeneralLinear.weightParabolicDefiningHopfIdeal R w ≤ definingIdeal R := by
+    rw [le_definingIdeal_iff]
+    constructor
+    · intro i
+      apply GeneralLinear.weightParabolicDefiningHopfIdeal_toIdeal_le_ker
+      intro a b hab
+      have ha : a ∉ s := by
+        intro ha
+        by_cases hb : b ∈ s <;> simp [w, ha, hb] at hab
+      have hb : b ∈ s := by
+        by_contra hb
+        simp [w, ha, hb] at hab
+      let A := CommAlgCat.of R (AdditiveGroup.coordinateHopfAlgebra R)
+      let q : HopfAlgebra.points (R := R) (H := AdditiveGroup.coordinateHopfAlgebra R) A :=
+        toConv (AlgHom.id R _)
+      have hm := congrArg (fun g : Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin 27) A ↦
+        (g : Matrix (Fin 27) (Fin 27) A) a b) (rootPoint_matrix R i A q)
+      rw [← GeneralLinear.map_genericMatrix_eq_coe_pointToGeneralLinear] at hm
+      simp only [Matrix.map_apply, GeneralLinear.genericMatrix_apply, q,
+        AlgHom.id_comp, generator_inl] at hm
+      rw [hm, coe_rootSubgroupPoints_inl]
+      have hab' : a ≠ b := fun h ↦ ha (h ▸ hb)
+      have hedge : ¬(e6MinusculeWeight b i = -1 ∧ a = e6MinusculeReflection i b) := by
+        rintro ⟨hbi, rfl⟩
+        exact ha (hs i b hb hbi)
+      simp [Matrix.add_apply, hab', Matrix.smul_apply, Matrix.map_apply, hedge]
+    · apply GeneralLinear.weightParabolicDefiningHopfIdeal_toIdeal_le_ker
+      intro a b hab
+      have hab' : a ≠ b := by intro h; simp [h] at hab
+      rw [generatorCoordinateMap_inr, GeneralLinear.hom_weightTorusBaseChangeCoordinateMap]
+      simpa only [hab', ↓reduceIte, BialgHom.coe_toAlgHom] using
+        GeneralLinear.weightTorusCoordinateBialgHom_X (S := R) weightTable.weight a b
+  rw [Module.Basis.coordinateSpanIsStable_iff]
+  intro a ha b hb
+  rw [coefficientMatrix_basisFun, Matrix.map_apply, GeneralLinear.genericMatrix_apply]
+  apply (CommHopfAlgCat.mkQuotient_eq_zero_iff _ (definingIdeal R) _).mpr
+  apply hle
+  rw [← HopfIdeal.mem_toIdeal, GeneralLinear.weightParabolicDefiningHopfIdeal_toIdeal]
+  exact Ideal.subset_span (GeneralLinear.X_mem_weightParabolicRelationSet R w
+    (by simp [w, ha, hb]))
+
+/-- A coordinate span is invariant exactly when its weight indices are closed under raising.
+This criterion uses the universal coaction, rather than just the action of rational points. -/
+theorem coordinateSpanIsStable_iff [Nontrivial R] (s : Set (Fin 27)) :
+    (Pi.basisFun R (Fin 27)).coordinateSpanIsStable (C := coordinateHopfAlgebra R) s ↔
+      ∀ i a, a ∈ s → e6MinusculeWeight a i = -1 → e6MinusculeReflection i a ∈ s := by
+  classical
+  refine ⟨fun h i a ha hia ↦ ?_, stable_of_raising_closed s⟩
+  let N := (Pi.basisFun R (Fin 27)).coordinateSpanSubcomodule s h
+  have hv : Pi.single a (1 : R) ∈ N := by
+    rw [Module.Basis.mem_coordinateSpanSubcomodule]
+    exact Submodule.subset_span ⟨a, ha, Pi.basisFun_apply R (Fin 27) a⟩
+  have hr := single_reflection_mem R N i a hia hv
+  rw [Module.Basis.mem_coordinateSpanSubcomodule] at hr
+  exact (Pi.basisFun R (Fin 27)).mem_span_image.mp hr (by simp)
+
+variable (k : Type u) [Field k]
+
+/-- Every invariant subspace is the span of exactly those minuscule coordinate lines it contains. -/
+theorem toSubmodule_eq_span
+    (N : Subcomodule k (coordinateHopfAlgebra k) (Fin 27 → k)) :
+    N.toSubmodule = Submodule.span k ((Pi.basisFun k (Fin 27)) ''
+      {a | Pi.single a (1 : k) ∈ N}) := by
+  apply Subcomodule.toSubmodule_eq_span_of_corestrict_eq_ofWeights
+    (CommHopfAlgCat.commonKernelLift (generator k) (.inr ())).hom.toCoalgHom
+    minusculeCharacter minusculeCharacter_injective (torusCorestrict_eq_ofWeights k) N
+
+/-- **Invariant-subspace classification for the positive E₆ minuscule subgroup.** A subspace
+is a subcomodule precisely when it is a coordinate span closed under all six raising operators. -/
+theorem exists_subcomodule_iff (W : Submodule k (Fin 27 → k)) :
+    (∃ N : Subcomodule k (coordinateHopfAlgebra k) (Fin 27 → k), N.toSubmodule = W) ↔
+      ∃ s : Set (Fin 27),
+        (∀ i a, a ∈ s → e6MinusculeWeight a i = -1 → e6MinusculeReflection i a ∈ s) ∧
+        W = Submodule.span k ((Pi.basisFun k (Fin 27)) '' s) := by
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨N, hN⟩
+    refine ⟨{a | Pi.single a (1 : k) ∈ N}, ?_, ?_⟩
+    · intro i a ha hia
+      exact single_reflection_mem k N i a hia ha
+    · exact hN.symm.trans (toSubmodule_eq_span k N)
+  · rintro ⟨s, hs, rfl⟩
+    exact (Module.Basis.exists_subcomodule_toSubmodule_eq_span_iff_coordinateSpanIsStable
+      (Pi.basisFun k (Fin 27)) s).mpr ((coordinateSpanIsStable_iff s).mpr hs)
+
+end
+
+end TauCeti.E6Minuscule.Generated.Positive

+/-!
+# Sums of rapidly decreasing finite sequences
+
+A nonnegative finite sequence in which every term is at most half of the previous one sums to at
+most twice its first term. In Roth's lemma this bounds the sum of the weights `rᵢ` by `2 r₀`.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Fin.sum_le_two_mul_of_two_mul_succ_le`: if `0 ≤ rᵢ` and `2 rᵢ₊₁ ≤ rᵢ`, then
+  `∑ᵢ rᵢ ≤ 2 r₀`.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+namespace Fin
+
+/-- A nonnegative sequence whose terms at least halve at each step sums to at most twice its
+first term. -/
+theorem sum_le_two_mul_of_two_mul_succ_le {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [PartialOrder R]
+    [IsOrderedRing R] {n : ℕ} {r : Fin (n + 1) → R} (hr : ∀ i, 0 ≤ r i)
+    (h : ∀ i : Fin n, 2 * r i.succ ≤ r i.castSucc) : ∑ i, r i ≤ 2 * r 0 := by
+  induction n with
+  | zero =>
+    rw [sum_univ_one, two_mul]
+    exact le_add_of_nonneg_right (hr 0)
+  | succ n ih =>
+    have hs := ih (r := fun i ↦ r i.succ) (fun i ↦ hr _) fun i ↦ by
+      rw [succ_castSucc]
+      exact h i.succ
+    have h0 := h 0
+    rw [castSucc_zero] at h0
+    rw [sum_univ_succ, two_mul]
+    gcongr
+    exact hs.trans h0
+
+end Fin

+/-!
+# Skew derivations from triangular matrix representations
+
+For an algebra endomorphism `σ` of `R`, a linear map `δ : R → R` satisfies the skew Leibniz rule
+`δ (a b) = σ a δ b + δ a b` exactly when `r ↦ !![σ r, δ r; 0, r]` is multiplicative: the
+upper-right entry of a product of two such matrices is `σ a δ b + δ a b`. Consequently the
+upper-right corner of any algebra map `R → Mat₂(R)` whose diagonal entries are `σ r` and `r` is
+a `σ`-derivation.
+
+This is the standard way to extend a skew derivation that is prescribed only on generators: the
+matrix-valued algebra map is produced by a universal property, and checking its shape on
+generators replaces checking the Leibniz rule on all of `R`. Iterated Ore presentations, such as
+the presentation of the quantized enveloping algebra of `sl₂` by adjoining `F` and then `E` to
+the Laurent polynomials in `K`, construct their second skew derivation this way.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `TauCeti.SigmaDerivation.ofMatrix`: the `σ`-derivation in the upper-right corner of an algebra
+  map `R →ₐ[k] Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) R` with diagonal entries `σ r` and `r`.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+namespace TauCeti.SigmaDerivation
+
+variable {k R : Type*} [CommSemiring k] [Semiring R] [Algebra k R] {σ : R →ₐ[k] R}
+
+/-- The upper-right corner of an algebra map `Φ : R → Mat₂(R)` whose diagonal entries are
+`σ r` and `r` is a `σ`-derivation: `Φ r = !![σ r, δ r; *, r]` forces the skew Leibniz rule
+`δ (a b) = σ a δ b + δ a b`. -/
+def ofMatrix (Φ : R →ₐ[k] Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) R) (h₀₀ : ∀ r, Φ r 0 0 = σ r)
+    (h₁₁ : ∀ r, Φ r 1 1 = r) : SigmaDerivation σ where
+  toLinearMap := Matrix.entryLinearMap k R 0 1 ∘ₗ Φ.toLinearMap
+  leibniz' a b := by
+    simp [Matrix.mul_apply, Fin.sum_univ_two, h₀₀, h₁₁]
+  map_one' := by simp
+
+/-- The value of `ofMatrix` is the upper-right entry of the matrix. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem ofMatrix_apply (Φ : R →ₐ[k] Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) R) (h₀₀ : ∀ r, Φ r 0 0 = σ r)
+    (h₁₁ : ∀ r, Φ r 1 1 = r) (r : R) : ofMatrix Φ h₀₀ h₁₁ r = Φ r 0 1 := (rfl)
+
+end TauCeti.SigmaDerivation

+/-!
+# Lower bounds for cross evaluations at rational points
+
+For integer polynomials `P, Q` of degree at most `N`, a nonzero value
+`P(x) - y Q(x)` at rational points cannot be smaller than
+`(den(x)^N den(y))⁻¹`. This is the arithmetic lower bound used when auxiliary
+polynomials give a small rational linear form in two approximants.
+
+The proof applies Mathlib's `one_le_pow_mul_abs_eval_div` to
+`den(y) P - num(y) Q`; it does not require either polynomial to be nonzero.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+open Polynomial
+
+/-- For a nonzero cross evaluation of integer polynomials of degree at most `N`,
+`1 ≤ den(x)^N den(y) |P(x) - y Q(x)|`. -/
+theorem one_le_den_pow_mul_abs_aeval_sub_mul {P Q : ℤ[X]} {N : ℕ}
+    (hP : P.natDegree ≤ N) (hQ : Q.natDegree ≤ N) {x y : ℚ}
+    (hne : aeval x P - y * aeval x Q ≠ 0) :
+    (1 : ℚ) ≤ (x.den : ℚ) ^ N * y.den * |aeval x P - y * aeval x Q| := by
+  let F : ℤ[X] := C (y.den : ℤ) * P - C y.num * Q
+  have hF : F.natDegree ≤ N :=
+    (natDegree_sub_le _ _).trans (max_le
+      ((natDegree_C_mul_le _ _).trans hP) ((natDegree_C_mul_le _ _).trans hQ))
+  have heval : aeval x F = (y.den : ℚ) * (aeval x P - y * aeval x Q) := by
+    simp [F, mul_sub, ← mul_assoc, Rat.den_mul_eq_num]
+  have heval' : (F.map (algebraMap ℤ ℚ)).eval ((x.num : ℚ) / (x.den : ℤ)) =

+/-!
+# Thom encodings of the roots of a polynomial
+
+A root of a nonzero polynomial over an ordered field with polynomial Rolle is determined by its
+Thom encoding, the signs of its derivatives of orders `1, …, natDegree p`
+(`Polynomial.thomEncoding_injOn`). This file turns that injectivity into an API for the finite
+set of encodings realized by roots.
+
+* `Polynomial.thomEncodings p` is the finite set of Thom encodings of the distinct roots of `p`.
+  Its cardinality is the number of distinct roots (`Polynomial.card_thomEncodings`).
+* `Polynomial.thomEncodingEquiv` identifies the distinct roots with their encodings, so that
+  `(thomEncodingEquiv hrolle p).symm` reconstructs a root from its encoding
+  (`Polynomial.existsUnique_eval_eq_zero_thomEncoding_eq` is the underlying uniqueness).
+* `Polynomial.ThomLT` is the comparison of two sign words read off at the last coordinate where
+  they differ. It is decidable and refers to no point of `R`. The order of two points with
+  distinct encodings is this comparison of their encodings (`Polynomial.lt_iff_thomLT`), so the
+  order of the roots of `p` is recovered from their encodings alone
+  (`Polynomial.thomEncodingEquiv_lt_iff`).
+
+## References
+
+S. Basu, R. Pollack, and M.-F. Roy,
+[Algorithms in Real Algebraic Geometry](https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-33099-2),
+second edition, Proposition 2.28 (Thom encodings and the ordering of roots) and Chapter 10
+(Thom encodings of real roots).
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open TauCeti (PolynomialRolle)
+
+namespace Polynomial
+
+section Comparison
+
+variable {d : ℕ}
+
+/-- The Thom comparison of sign words: `ThomLT σ τ` holds when `σ` and `τ` first differ, reading
+from the top, at coordinate `i`, the next coordinate `i + 1` exists, and either `σ (i + 1) = 1`
+and `σ i < τ i`, or `σ (i + 1) = -1` and `τ i < σ i`. For Thom encodings of two points this
+compares the points (`Polynomial.lt_iff_thomLT`). -/
+def ThomLT (σ τ : Fin d → SignType) : Prop :=
+  ∃ i : Fin d, σ i ≠ τ i ∧ (∀ j, i < j → σ j = τ j) ∧ ∃ h : i.val + 1 < d,
+    (σ ⟨i.val + 1, h⟩ = 1 ∧ σ i < τ i) ∨ (σ ⟨i.val + 1, h⟩ = -1 ∧ τ i < σ i)
+
+/-- `ThomLT`, unfolded. -/
+theorem thomLT_iff {σ τ : Fin d → SignType} :
+    ThomLT σ τ ↔ ∃ i : Fin d, σ i ≠ τ i ∧ (∀ j, i < j → σ j = τ j) ∧ ∃ h : i.val + 1 < d,

+  Iff.rfl

+/-- At the last coordinate of disagreement, `ThomLT` is read off from the two differing signs and

+  · rw [h1] at h2; cases h2
+  · rw [h1] at h2; cases h2

+    · rw [h1] at h2; cases h2
+    · exact ⟨i, (hlt'.trans hlt).ne', htail, hd, Or.inr ⟨h1, hlt'.trans hlt⟩⟩

+    rwa [← hk' i hik]
+

+  exact thomEncoding_injOn p hrolle hp ha hb h
+
+/-- **Reconstruction.** A realized Thom encoding is the encoding of exactly one root. -/
+theorem existsUnique_eval_eq_zero_thomEncoding_eq (hrolle : PolynomialRolle R) {p : R[X]}
+    {σ : Fin p.natDegree → SignType} (hσ : σ ∈ p.thomEncodings) :
+    ∃! x, p.eval x = 0 ∧ thomEncoding p x = σ := by
+  obtain ⟨hp, x, hx, rfl⟩ := mem_thomEncodings.1 hσ
+  exact ⟨x, ⟨hx, rfl⟩, fun y hy ↦ thomEncoding_injOn p hrolle hp hy.1 hx hy.2⟩
+
+/-- The distinct roots of `p` correspond to their Thom encodings. The inverse reconstructs a root
+from its encoding. -/
+noncomputable def thomEncodingEquiv (hrolle : PolynomialRolle R) (p : R[X]) :
+    p.roots.toFinset ≃ p.thomEncodings :=
+  Equiv.ofBijective
+    (fun x ↦ ⟨thomEncoding p x, Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ x.2⟩)
+    ⟨fun a b h ↦ by
+      have hp : p ≠ 0 := fun hp ↦ by simpa [hp] using a.2
+      have ha := a.2
+      have hb := b.2
+      simp only [Multiset.mem_toFinset, mem_roots hp, IsRoot.def] at ha hb
+      exact Subtype.ext (thomEncoding_injOn p hrolle hp ha hb (congrArg Subtype.val h)),
+    fun σ ↦ by
+      obtain ⟨x, hx, h⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 σ.2
+      exact ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, Subtype.ext h⟩⟩
+
+/-- The correspondence sends a root to its Thom encoding. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem coe_thomEncodingEquiv_apply (hrolle : PolynomialRolle R) (p : R[X])
+    (x : p.roots.toFinset) : (thomEncodingEquiv hrolle p x : Fin p.natDegree → SignType) =
+      thomEncoding p x :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- The reconstructed point is a root. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem eval_thomEncodingEquiv_symm (hrolle : PolynomialRolle R) (p : R[X])
+    (σ : p.thomEncodings) : p.eval ((thomEncodingEquiv hrolle p).symm σ : R) = 0 := by
+  have h := ((thomEncodingEquiv hrolle p).symm σ).2
+  have hp : p ≠ 0 := fun hp ↦ by simp [hp] at h
+  simpa only [Multiset.mem_toFinset, mem_roots hp, IsRoot.def] using h
+
+/-- The reconstructed root has the prescribed Thom encoding. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem thomEncoding_thomEncodingEquiv_symm (hrolle : PolynomialRolle R) (p : R[X])
+    (σ : p.thomEncodings) :
+    thomEncoding p ((thomEncodingEquiv hrolle p).symm σ : R) = σ := by
+  simpa only [coe_thomEncodingEquiv_apply] using
+    congrArg Subtype.val ((thomEncodingEquiv hrolle p).apply_symm_apply σ)
+
+/-- **Comparison.** Two points with different Thom encodings are ordered as their encodings are
+by `ThomLT`. -/
+theorem lt_iff_thomLT (p : R[X]) (hrolle : PolynomialRolle R) {a b : R}
+    (hne : thomEncoding p a ≠ thomEncoding p b) :
+    a < b ↔ ThomLT (thomEncoding p a) (thomEncoding p b) := by
+  obtain ⟨i, hi, ht⟩ := exists_thomEncoding_ne p hne
+  rw [lt_iff_thomEncoding p hrolle i hi ht, thomLT_iff_of_ne hi ht]
+  exact ⟨fun h ↦ ⟨_, h⟩, fun ⟨_, h⟩ ↦ h⟩
+
+/-- Two roots of a nonzero polynomial are ordered as their Thom encodings are by `ThomLT`. -/
+theorem lt_iff_thomLT_of_eval_eq_zero (hrolle : PolynomialRolle R) {p : R[X]} (hp : p ≠ 0)
+    {a b : R} (ha : p.eval a = 0) (hb : p.eval b = 0) :
+    a < b ↔ ThomLT (thomEncoding p a) (thomEncoding p b) := by
+  rcases eq_or_ne a b with rfl | hab
+  · simp [thomLT_irrefl]
+  · exact lt_iff_thomLT p hrolle fun h ↦ hab (thomEncoding_injOn p hrolle hp ha hb h)
+
+/-- The correspondence between roots and their Thom encodings carries the order of the roots to
+`ThomLT`. -/
+theorem thomEncodingEquiv_lt_iff (hrolle : PolynomialRolle R) (p : R[X])
+    (x y : p.roots.toFinset) :
+    ThomLT (thomEncodingEquiv hrolle p x : Fin p.natDegree → SignType)
+        (thomEncodingEquiv hrolle p y) ↔ (x : R) < y := by
+  have hp : p ≠ 0 := fun hp ↦ by simpa [hp] using x.2
+  have hx := x.2
+  have hy := y.2
+  simp only [Multiset.mem_toFinset, mem_roots hp, IsRoot.def] at hx hy
+  rw [coe_thomEncodingEquiv_apply, coe_thomEncodingEquiv_apply,
+    lt_iff_thomLT_of_eval_eq_zero hrolle hp hx hy]
+
+/-- Distinct realized Thom encodings are comparable by `ThomLT`. -/
+theorem thomLT_or_thomLT_of_mem_thomEncodings (hrolle : PolynomialRolle R) {p : R[X]}
+    {σ τ : Fin p.natDegree → SignType} (hσ : σ ∈ p.thomEncodings) (hτ : τ ∈ p.thomEncodings)
+    (hne : σ ≠ τ) : ThomLT σ τ ∨ ThomLT τ σ := by
+  obtain ⟨hp, a, ha, rfl⟩ := mem_thomEncodings.1 hσ
+  obtain ⟨-, b, hb, rfl⟩ := mem_thomEncodings.1 hτ
+  rw [← lt_iff_thomLT p hrolle hne, ← lt_iff_thomLT p hrolle hne.symm]
+  exact lt_or_gt_of_ne fun h ↦ hne (h ▸ rfl)
+
+end Polynomial

+/-!
+# Čech cohomology of quasi-coherent sheaves for affine covers
+
+Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme with affine diagonal, for instance a separated Noetherian
+scheme, and let `M` be a quasi-coherent sheaf of modules on `X`. Finite intersections of affine
+opens of `X` are then affine, and `M` has no cohomology in positive degrees on them. So every
+finite affine open cover `U` of `X` is a Leray cover for `M`, and by Leray's theorem
+(`TauCeti.Topology.nonempty_homology_cechComplex_iso_H`) the Čech cohomology `Hⁿ(U, M)` of the
+underlying abelian sheaf of `M` is isomorphic to the cohomology `Hⁿ(X, M)`, so that `Hⁿ(X, M)` can
+be computed, as an abelian group, from the Čech complex of any finite affine open cover. The
+isomorphism is one of abelian groups, and is not claimed to be natural in `M`.
+
+## Main declarations
+
+* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.nonempty_homology_cechComplex_iso_cohomology`: for a finite
+  affine open cover `U` of `X`, `Hⁿ(U, M) ≅ Hⁿ(X, M)` for every `n`.
+
+## References
+
+* R. Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*, Theorem III.4.5.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace AlgebraicGeometry
+
+universe u
+
+namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules
+
+open TauCeti TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules
+
+variable {X : Scheme.{u}} (M : X.Modules)
+
+/-- **Čech cohomology computes the cohomology of a quasi-coherent sheaf.** Let `X` be a locally
+Noetherian scheme with affine diagonal (for instance a separated one), `M` a quasi-coherent sheaf
+of modules on `X`, and `U` a finite family of affine opens covering `X`. Then the Čech cohomology
+`Hⁿ(U, M)` of the underlying abelian sheaf of `M` is isomorphic to `Hⁿ(X, M)`, for every `n`. -/
+theorem nonempty_homology_cechComplex_iso_cohomology [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
+    [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal (terminal.from X))] [M.IsQuasicoherent] {ι : Type u}
+    [Finite ι] (U : ι → X.Opens) (hU : ∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) (hcover : ⨆ i, U i = ⊤)
+    (n : ℕ) :
+    Nonempty (((cechComplexFunctor U).obj
+        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf X.ringCatSheaf).obj M).obj).homology n ≅
+      AddCommGrpCat.of (Cohomology M n)) := by
+  refine TauCeti.Topology.nonempty_homology_cechComplex_iso_H U hcover _ (fun s hs k ↦ ?_) n
+  -- a nonempty finite intersection of affine opens is affine, with Noetherian ring of sections
+  have hW : IsAffineOpen (s.inf U) := by
+    rw [Finset.inf_eq_iInf]
+    exact IsAffineOpen.biInf _ s.finite_toSet hs fun j _ ↦ hU j
+  have : IsNoetherianRing Γ(X, s.inf U) := IsLocallyNoetherian.component_noetherian ⟨_, hW⟩
+  exact subsingleton_cohomologyOn_succ_of_isAffineOpen M hW k
+
+end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules

+/-

+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: The Tau Ceti contributors
+-/
+module
+
+public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Acyclic
+import Mathlib.Tactic.FinCases
+import Mathlib.Tactic.IntervalCases
+import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
+
+/-!
+# Dual graphs of nodal curves
+
+The **dual graph** of a proper nodal curve `X` over an algebraically closed field records how
+the curve is assembled from smooth pieces. Its vertices are the irreducible components of the
+normalization of `X`, its edges are the nodes of `X`, and the two endpoints of an edge are the
+components carrying the two branches of the node; when both branches lie on one component the
+edge is a loop. Each vertex is labelled by the genus of its normalized component, and each
+marking of a pointed curve is attached to the component on which it lies.
+
+This file introduces that combinatorial structure, `TauCeti.DualGraph`, together with the
+numerical invariants through which the geometry of the curve is read off from it:
+
+* the **valence** of a vertex, the number of branches of nodes on the component, so that a loop
+  counts twice;
+* the **first Betti number** `b₁ = #edges - #vertices + 1` of the connected graph and the
+  **arithmetic genus** `pₐ = ∑ᵥ gᵥ + b₁` encoded by the graph;
+* the **log-canonical degree** `2gᵥ - 2 + val(v) + n(v)` of a vertex carrying `n(v)` markings,
+  which is the degree of `ω_X(s₁ + ⋯ + sₙ)` on the corresponding component.
+
+A pointed nodal curve is stable exactly when every component has positive log-canonical degree,
+and semistable when none has negative degree; `TauCeti.DualGraph.IsStable` and
+`TauCeti.DualGraph.IsSemistable` are these conditions on the graph.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `TauCeti.DualGraph.sum_valence`: the handshake identity `∑ᵥ val(v) = 2 · #edges`.
+* `TauCeti.DualGraph.card_vertex_le_card_edge_add_one`: a connected graph has at most one more
+  vertex than it has edges, so the first Betti number is computed without truncation
+  (`TauCeti.DualGraph.firstBetti_add_card_vertex`).
+* `TauCeti.DualGraph.sum_logCanonicalDegree`: the log-canonical degrees add up to
+  `2pₐ - 2 + n`, the total degree of `ω_X(s₁ + ⋯ + sₙ)`.
+* `TauCeti.DualGraph.IsStable.card_vertex_le` and `TauCeti.DualGraph.IsStable.card_edge_le`:
+  a stable graph of genus `g` with `n` markings has at most `2g - 2 + n` vertices and at most
+  `3g - 3 + n` edges.
+* `TauCeti.DualGraph.isSemistable_iff_forall_not_isRationalTail`: an unmarked graph of
+  arithmetic genus at least one is semistable exactly when it has no rational tails, and
+  `TauCeti.DualGraph.isStable_iff_forall_not_isRationalTail_and_not_isRationalBridge`: an
+  unmarked graph of arithmetic genus at least two is stable exactly when it has neither rational
+  tails nor rational bridges.
+
+## Implementation notes
+
+An edge carries an ordered pair of endpoints, so the two branches of a node are always two
+distinct half-edges, even for a loop. Valence counts half-edges, which is what makes a loop
+contribute two, matching the two points of the normalization lying over a self-node.
+
+Rational tails and rational bridges are defined without reference to markings, as in the
+unpointed theory of the Stacks Project; the characterizations of stability through them are
+stated for unmarked graphs.
+
+## References
+
+* [Stacks, Tag 0E6X](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0E6X) (semistable curves) and
+  [Stacks, Tag 0E73](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0E73) (stable curves).
+* E. Arbarello, M. Cornalba and P. A. Griffiths, *Geometry of Algebraic Curves, Volume II*,
+  Chapter X, for dual graphs of pointed nodal curves.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+open Finset
+
+universe u v
+
+/-- The dual graph of a proper nodal curve over an algebraically closed field, with markings
+indexed by `ι`.
+
+`Vertex` is the finite nonempty set of irreducible components of the normalization, `Edge` is the
+finite set of nodes, `endpoint e 0` and `endpoint e 1` are the components carrying the two
+branches of the node `e`, `genus v` is the genus of the normalized component `v`, and `marking i`
+is the component carrying the `i`-th marking. The curve is connected, so the graph is. -/
+structure DualGraph (ι : Type v) where
+  /-- The finite nonempty type of vertices: the components of the normalization. -/
+  Vertex : Type u
+  /-- The vertices form a finite type. -/
+  [vertexFintype : Fintype Vertex]
+  /-- Equality of vertices is decidable. -/
+  [vertexDecidableEq : DecidableEq Vertex]
+  /-- There is at least one vertex. -/
+  [vertexNonempty : Nonempty Vertex]
+  /-- The finite type of edges: the nodes. -/
+  Edge : Type u
+  /-- The edges form a finite type. -/
+  [edgeFintype : Fintype Edge]
+  /-- Equality of edges is decidable. -/
+  [edgeDecidableEq : DecidableEq Edge]
+  /-- The components carrying the two branches of a node. -/
+  endpoint : Edge → Fin 2 → Vertex
+  /-- The genus of a normalized component. -/
+  genus : Vertex → ℕ
+  /-- The component carrying a marking. -/
+  marking : ι → Vertex
+  /-- Any two vertices are joined by a chain of edges. -/
+  connected : ∀ v w, Relation.ReflTransGen
+    (fun v w ↦ ∃ e, (endpoint e 0 = v ∧ endpoint e 1 = w) ∨
+      (endpoint e 0 = w ∧ endpoint e 1 = v)) v w
+
+namespace DualGraph
+
+variable {ι : Type v} (G : DualGraph ι)
+
+instance : Fintype G.Vertex := G.vertexFintype
+instance : DecidableEq G.Vertex := G.vertexDecidableEq
+instance : Nonempty G.Vertex := G.vertexNonempty
+instance : Fintype G.Edge := G.edgeFintype
+instance : DecidableEq G.Edge := G.edgeDecidableEq
+
+/-! ### Adjacency and connectedness -/
+
+/-- Two vertices are adjacent when they are the two endpoints of some edge, in either order.
+A vertex carrying a loop is adjacent to itself. -/
+def Adj (v w : G.Vertex) : Prop :=
+  ∃ e, (G.endpoint e 0 = v ∧ G.endpoint e 1 = w) ∨ (G.endpoint e 0 = w ∧ G.endpoint e 1 = v)
+
+variable {G} in
+lemma adj_iff {v w : G.Vertex} : G.Adj v w ↔
+    ∃ e, (G.endpoint e 0 = v ∧ G.endpoint e 1 = w) ∨
+      (G.endpoint e 0 = w ∧ G.endpoint e 1 = v) :=
+  Iff.rfl
+
+variable {G} in
+lemma Adj.symm {v w : G.Vertex} (h : G.Adj v w) : G.Adj w v := by
+  obtain ⟨e, h | h⟩ := h
+  exacts [⟨e, Or.inr h⟩, ⟨e, Or.inl h⟩]
+
+/-- Any two vertices are joined by a chain of adjacencies. -/
+lemma reflTransGen_adj (v w : G.Vertex) : Relation.ReflTransGen G.Adj v w :=
+  G.connected v w
+
+/-- The simple graph on the vertices joining two distinct vertices when some edge does. -/
+def toSimpleGraph : SimpleGraph G.Vertex :=
+  SimpleGraph.fromRel G.Adj
+
+@[simp]
+lemma toSimpleGraph_adj {v w : G.Vertex} : G.toSimpleGraph.Adj v w ↔ v ≠ w ∧ G.Adj v w := by
+  rw [toSimpleGraph, SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj]
+  exact and_congr_right fun _ ↦ ⟨fun h ↦ h.elim id Adj.symm, Or.inl⟩
+
+/-- The simple graph underlying a dual graph is connected. -/
+theorem toSimpleGraph_connected : G.toSimpleGraph.Connected := by
+  obtain ⟨v⟩ := G.vertexNonempty
+  rw [SimpleGraph.connected_iff_exists_forall_reachable]
+  refine ⟨v, fun w ↦ ?_⟩
+  rw [SimpleGraph.reachable_iff_reflTransGen]
+  induction G.reflTransGen_adj v w with
+  | refl => exact .refl
+  | @tail b c _ hbc ih =>
+    by_cases hb : b = c
+    · exact hb ▸ ih
+    · exact ih.tail (G.toSimpleGraph_adj.mpr ⟨hb, hbc⟩)
+
+/-- If every edge at `v` is a loop, then `v` is the only vertex: no edge leaves it, and the graph
+is connected. -/
+theorem eq_of_forall_endpoint_zero_eq_iff {v : G.Vertex}
+    (h : ∀ e, G.endpoint e 0 = v ↔ G.endpoint e 1 = v) (w : G.Vertex) : w = v := by
+  induction G.reflTransGen_adj v w with
+  | refl => rfl
+  | @tail b c _ hbc ih =>
+    subst ih
+    obtain ⟨e, ⟨he₀, he₁⟩ | ⟨he₀, he₁⟩⟩ := hbc
+    · rw [← he₁, ← h, he₀]
+    · rw [← he₀, h, he₁]
+
+/-- A connected graph has at most one more vertex than it has edges. -/
+theorem card_vertex_le_card_edge_add_one :
+    Fintype.card G.Vertex ≤ Fintype.card G.Edge + 1 := by
+  have hconn := G.toSimpleGraph_connected.card_vert_le_card_edgeSet_add_one
+  rw [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card] at hconn
+  refine hconn.trans (Nat.add_le_add_right ?_ 1)
+  -- Every edge of the underlying simple graph is the pair of endpoints of an edge of `G`.
+  let f : G.Edge → Sym2 G.Vertex := fun e ↦ s(G.endpoint e 0, G.endpoint e 1)
+  have hsub : G.toSimpleGraph.edgeSet ⊆ Set.range f := by
+    intro s hs
+    induction s using Sym2.ind with
+    | h v w =>
+      obtain ⟨-, e, ⟨he₀, he₁⟩ | ⟨he₀, he₁⟩⟩ :=
+        G.toSimpleGraph_adj.mp (SimpleGraph.mem_edgeSet _ |>.mp hs)
+      · exact ⟨e, by simp [f, he₀, he₁]⟩
+      · exact ⟨e, by simp [f, he₀, he₁, Sym2.eq_swap]⟩
+  calc Nat.card G.toSimpleGraph.edgeSet
+      ≤ Nat.card (Set.range f) := Nat.card_mono (Set.toFinite _) hsub
+    _ ≤ Nat.card G.Edge := Finite.card_range_le f
+    _ = Fintype.card G.Edge := Nat.card_eq_fintype_card
+
+/-! ### Valence and markings -/
+
+/-- The valence of a vertex: the number of branches of nodes lying on the component, that is, the
+number of half-edges at the vertex. A loop counts twice. -/
+def valence (v : G.Vertex) : ℕ :=
+  #{h : G.Edge × Fin 2 | G.endpoint h.1 h.2 = v}
+
+lemma valence_def (v : G.Vertex) :
+    G.valence v = #{h : G.Edge × Fin 2 | G.endpoint h.1 h.2 = v} :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- The handshake identity: the valences add up to twice the number of edges. -/
+theorem sum_valence : ∑ v, G.valence v = 2 * Fintype.card G.Edge := by
+  have := card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise (s := (univ : Finset (G.Edge × Fin 2))) (t := univ)
+    (f := fun h ↦ G.endpoint h.1 h.2) fun _ _ ↦ mem_univ _
+  simp only [valence, ← this, card_univ, Fintype.card_prod, Fintype.card_fin, mul_comm]
+
+lemma valence_eq_zero_iff {v : G.Vertex} : G.valence v = 0 ↔ ∀ e i, G.endpoint e i ≠ v := by
+  simp [valence, filter_eq_empty_iff]
+
+/-- The number of markings carried by a vertex. -/
+def numMarkings [Fintype ι] (v : G.Vertex) : ℕ :=
+  #{i : ι | G.marking i = v}
+
+lemma numMarkings_def [Fintype ι] (v : G.Vertex) : G.numMarkings v = #{i : ι | G.marking i = v} :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- Every marking lies on exactly one component. -/
+theorem sum_numMarkings [Fintype ι] : ∑ v, G.numMarkings v = Fintype.card ι := by
+  have := card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise (s := (univ : Finset ι)) (t := univ) (f := G.marking)
+    fun _ _ ↦ mem_univ _
+  simp only [numMarkings, ← this, card_univ]
+
+@[simp]
+lemma numMarkings_of_isEmpty [Fintype ι] [IsEmpty ι] (v : G.Vertex) : G.numMarkings v = 0 := by
+  simp [numMarkings]
+
+/-! ### Betti number and arithmetic genus -/
+
+/-- The first Betti number `#edges - #vertices + 1` of the connected graph. -/
+def firstBetti : ℕ :=
+  Fintype.card G.Edge + 1 - Fintype.card G.Vertex
+
+lemma firstBetti_def : G.firstBetti = Fintype.card G.Edge + 1 - Fintype.card G.Vertex :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- The first Betti number is computed without truncation. -/
+theorem firstBetti_add_card_vertex :
+    G.firstBetti + Fintype.card G.Vertex = Fintype.card G.Edge + 1 := by
+  have := G.card_vertex_le_card_edge_add_one
+  rw [firstBetti]
+  omega
+
+/-- The arithmetic genus encoded by the graph: the sum of the genera of the components and the
+first Betti number. -/
+def arithmeticGenus : ℕ :=
+  ∑ v, G.genus v + G.firstBetti
+
+lemma arithmeticGenus_def : G.arithmeticGenus = ∑ v, G.genus v + G.firstBetti :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- The arithmetic genus in terms of the numbers of vertices and edges. -/
+theorem arithmeticGenus_add_card_vertex :
+    G.arithmeticGenus + Fintype.card G.Vertex = ∑ v, G.genus v + Fintype.card G.Edge + 1 := by
+  have := G.firstBetti_add_card_vertex
+  rw [arithmeticGenus]
+  omega
+
+/-- If every edge at `v` is a loop, the graph has the single vertex `v`, and twice its arithmetic
+genus is `2 g(v) + val(v)`. -/
+theorem two_mul_arithmeticGenus_of_forall_endpoint_zero_eq_iff {v : G.Vertex}
+    (h : ∀ e, G.endpoint e 0 = v ↔ G.endpoint e 1 = v) :
+    2 * G.arithmeticGenus = 2 * G.genus v + G.valence v := by
+  have hv := G.eq_of_forall_endpoint_zero_eq_iff h
+  have huniv : (univ : Finset G.Vertex) = {v} := eq_singleton_iff_unique_mem.mpr
+    ⟨mem_univ v, fun w _ ↦ hv w⟩
+  have hcard : Fintype.card G.Vertex = 1 := by rw [← card_univ, huniv, card_singleton]
+  have hval := G.sum_valence
+  have hgenus := G.arithmeticGenus_add_card_vertex
+  rw [huniv, sum_singleton] at hval hgenus
+  omega
+
+/-! ### Log-canonical degree and stability -/
+
+/-- The log-canonical degree `2 g(v) - 2 + val(v) + n(v)` of a vertex carrying `n(v)` markings.
+This is the numerical value that the degree of `ω_X(s₁ + ⋯ + sₙ)` takes on the corresponding
+component of a pointed nodal curve. -/
+def logCanonicalDegree [Fintype ι] (v : G.Vertex) : ℤ :=
+  2 * G.genus v - 2 + G.valence v + G.numMarkings v
+
+lemma logCanonicalDegree_def [Fintype ι] (v : G.Vertex) :
+    G.logCanonicalDegree v = 2 * G.genus v - 2 + G.valence v + G.numMarkings v :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- The log-canonical degrees add up to `2pₐ - 2 + n`. -/
+theorem sum_logCanonicalDegree [Fintype ι] :
+    ∑ v, G.logCanonicalDegree v = 2 * G.arithmeticGenus - 2 + Fintype.card ι := by
+  have hval : (∑ v, G.valence v : ℤ) = 2 * Fintype.card G.Edge := by
+    exact_mod_cast G.sum_valence
+  have hmark : (∑ v, G.numMarkings v : ℤ) = Fintype.card ι := by
+    exact_mod_cast G.sum_numMarkings
+  have hgenus : (G.arithmeticGenus + Fintype.card G.Vertex : ℤ) =
+      ∑ v, (G.genus v : ℤ) + Fintype.card G.Edge + 1 := by
+    exact_mod_cast G.arithmeticGenus_add_card_vertex
+  simp only [logCanonicalDegree, sum_add_distrib, sum_sub_distrib, ← mul_sum, sum_const,
+    card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul]
+  linarith
+
+/-- A vertex has nonpositive log-canonical degree exactly when it is a rational component with at
+most two special points, or a component of genus one with none. -/
+theorem logCanonicalDegree_nonpos_iff [Fintype ι] {v : G.Vertex} :
+    G.logCanonicalDegree v ≤ 0 ↔
+      (G.genus v = 0 ∧ G.valence v + G.numMarkings v ≤ 2) ∨
+        (G.genus v = 1 ∧ G.valence v = 0 ∧ G.numMarkings v = 0) := by
+  rw [logCanonicalDegree]
+  omega
+
+/-- A vertex has negative log-canonical degree exactly when it is a rational component with at
+most one special point. -/
+theorem logCanonicalDegree_neg_iff [Fintype ι] {v : G.Vertex} :
+    G.logCanonicalDegree v < 0 ↔ G.genus v = 0 ∧ G.valence v + G.numMarkings v ≤ 1 := by
+  rw [logCanonicalDegree]
+  omega
+
+/-- A graph is stable when every vertex has positive log-canonical degree. -/
+def IsStable [Fintype ι] : Prop :=
+  ∀ v, 0 < G.logCanonicalDegree v
+
+lemma isStable_iff [Fintype ι] : G.IsStable ↔ ∀ v, 0 < G.logCanonicalDegree v :=
+  Iff.rfl
+
+/-- A graph is semistable when no vertex has negative log-canonical degree. -/
+def IsSemistable [Fintype ι] : Prop :=
+  ∀ v, 0 ≤ G.logCanonicalDegree v
+
+lemma isSemistable_iff [Fintype ι] : G.IsSemistable ↔ ∀ v, 0 ≤ G.logCanonicalDegree v :=
+  Iff.rfl
+
+variable {G}
+
+lemma IsStable.isSemistable [Fintype ι] (hG : G.IsStable) : G.IsSemistable :=
+  fun v ↦ (hG v).le
+
+/-- A stable graph of genus `g` with `n` markings has at most `2g - 2 + n` vertices. -/
+theorem IsStable.card_vertex_le [Fintype ι] (hG : G.IsStable) :
+    (Fintype.card G.Vertex : ℤ) ≤ 2 * G.arithmeticGenus - 2 + Fintype.card ι := by
+  rw [← G.sum_logCanonicalDegree]
+  have : ∑ _v : G.Vertex, (1 : ℤ) ≤ ∑ v, G.logCanonicalDegree v :=
+    sum_le_sum fun v _ ↦ by have := hG v; omega
+  simpa using this
+
+/-- A stable graph of genus `g` with `n` markings has at most `3g - 3 + n` edges. -/
+theorem IsStable.card_edge_le [Fintype ι] (hG : G.IsStable) :
+    (Fintype.card G.Edge : ℤ) ≤ 3 * G.arithmeticGenus - 3 + Fintype.card ι := by
+  have hV := hG.card_vertex_le
+  have hgenus : (G.arithmeticGenus + Fintype.card G.Vertex : ℤ) =
+      ∑ v, (G.genus v : ℤ) + Fintype.card G.Edge + 1 := by
+    exact_mod_cast G.arithmeticGenus_add_card_vertex
+  have hpos : (0 : ℤ) ≤ ∑ v, (G.genus v : ℤ) := sum_nonneg fun _ _ ↦ Int.natCast_nonneg _
+  linarith
+
+/-- The stable range: a stable graph of genus `g` with `n` markings has `2g - 2 + n > 0`. -/
+theorem IsStable.two_mul_arithmeticGenus_sub_two_add_card_pos [Fintype ι] (hG : G.IsStable) :
+    0 < 2 * (G.arithmeticGenus : ℤ) - 2 + Fintype.card ι := by
+  have := hG.card_vertex_le
+  have : 0 < Fintype.card G.Vertex := Fintype.card_pos
+  omega
+
+/-! ### Rational tails and rational bridges -/
+
+variable (G)
+
+/-- A rational tail: a rational component meeting the rest of the curve in a single point. -/
+def IsRationalTail (v : G.Vertex) : Prop :=
+  G.genus v = 0 ∧ G.valence v = 1
+
+lemma isRationalTail_iff {v : G.Vertex} : G.IsRationalTail v ↔ G.genus v = 0 ∧ G.valence v = 1 :=
+  Iff.rfl
+
+/-- A rational bridge: a smooth rational component meeting the rest of the curve in exactly two
+points, so a rational component of valence two carrying no loop. -/
+def IsRationalBridge (v : G.Vertex) : Prop :=
+  G.genus v = 0 ∧ G.valence v = 2 ∧ ∀ e, G.endpoint e 0 = v → G.endpoint e 1 ≠ v
+
+lemma isRationalBridge_iff {v : G.Vertex} : G.IsRationalBridge v ↔
+    G.genus v = 0 ∧ G.valence v = 2 ∧ ∀ e, G.endpoint e 0 = v → G.endpoint e 1 ≠ v :=
+  Iff.rfl
+
+variable {G}
+
+/-- A rational tail has log-canonical degree `-1 + n(v)`. -/
+lemma IsRationalTail.logCanonicalDegree_eq [Fintype ι] {v : G.Vertex}
+    (hv : G.IsRationalTail v) : G.logCanonicalDegree v = -1 + G.numMarkings v := by
+  rw [logCanonicalDegree, hv.1, hv.2]
+  omega
+
+/-- A rational bridge has log-canonical degree `n(v)`. -/
+lemma IsRationalBridge.logCanonicalDegree_eq [Fintype ι] {v : G.Vertex}
+    (hv : G.IsRationalBridge v) : G.logCanonicalDegree v = G.numMarkings v := by
+  rw [logCanonicalDegree, hv.1, hv.2.1]
+  omega
+
+/-- If a vertex carries no half-edge at all, twice the arithmetic genus is twice its genus. -/
+private lemma two_mul_arithmeticGenus_of_valence_eq_zero {v : G.Vertex} (hv : G.valence v = 0) :
+    2 * G.arithmeticGenus = 2 * G.genus v := by
+  have h : ∀ e, G.endpoint e 0 = v ↔ G.endpoint e 1 = v := fun e ↦
+    iff_of_false (G.valence_eq_zero_iff.mp hv e 0) (G.valence_eq_zero_iff.mp hv e 1)
+  rw [G.two_mul_arithmeticGenus_of_forall_endpoint_zero_eq_iff h, hv, add_zero]
+
+/-- If a vertex of valence two carries a loop, that loop is the only edge, and twice the
+arithmetic genus is `2 g(v) + 2`. -/
+private lemma two_mul_arithmeticGenus_of_valence_eq_two_of_loop {v : G.Vertex}
+    (hv : G.valence v = 2) {e : G.Edge} (he₀ : G.endpoint e 0 = v) (he₁ : G.endpoint e 1 = v) :
+    2 * G.arithmeticGenus = 2 * G.genus v + 2 := by
+  -- The loop accounts for both half-edges at `v`.
+  have hsub : ({(e, 0), (e, 1)} : Finset (G.Edge × Fin 2)) ⊆
+      univ.filter fun h ↦ G.endpoint h.1 h.2 = v := by
+    intro x hx
+    simp only [mem_insert, mem_singleton] at hx
+    rcases hx with rfl | rfl <;> simpa
+  have hpair := eq_of_subset_of_card_le hsub (by rw [card_pair (by simp)]; exact hv.le)
+  have hloop (e' : G.Edge) (i : Fin 2) : G.endpoint e' i = v ↔ e' = e := by
+    have hmem : (e', i) ∈ univ.filter (fun h : G.Edge × Fin 2 ↦ G.endpoint h.1 h.2 = v) ↔
+        G.endpoint e' i = v := by simp
+    rw [← hmem, ← hpair]
+    fin_cases i <;> simp
+  rw [G.two_mul_arithmeticGenus_of_forall_endpoint_zero_eq_iff fun e' ↦ by rw [hloop, hloop], hv]
+
+/-- An unmarked graph of arithmetic genus at least one is semistable exactly when it has no
+rational tails. -/
+theorem isSemistable_iff_forall_not_isRationalTail [Fintype ι] [IsEmpty ι]
+    (hg : 1 ≤ G.arithmeticGenus) : G.IsSemistable ↔ ∀ v, ¬ G.IsRationalTail v := by
+  refine ⟨fun hG v hv ↦ ?_, fun hG v ↦ ?_⟩
+  · have := hG v
+    rw [hv.logCanonicalDegree_eq, numMarkings_of_isEmpty] at this
+    omega
+  · by_contra hneg
+    obtain ⟨hgv, hval⟩ := G.logCanonicalDegree_neg_iff.mp (not_le.mp hneg)
+    rw [numMarkings_of_isEmpty, add_zero] at hval
+    obtain hval | hval := Nat.le_one_iff_eq_zero_or_eq_one.mp hval
+    · have := two_mul_arithmeticGenus_of_valence_eq_zero hval
+      omega
+    · exact hG v ⟨hgv, hval⟩
+
+/-- An unmarked graph of arithmetic genus at least two is stable exactly when it has neither
+rational tails nor rational bridges. -/
+theorem isStable_iff_forall_not_isRationalTail_and_not_isRationalBridge [Fintype ι] [IsEmpty ι]
+    (hg : 2 ≤ G.arithmeticGenus) :
+    G.IsStable ↔ ∀ v, ¬ G.IsRationalTail v ∧ ¬ G.IsRationalBridge v := by
+  refine ⟨fun hG v ↦ ⟨fun hv ↦ ?_, fun hv ↦ ?_⟩, fun hG v ↦ ?_⟩
+  · have := hG v
+    rw [hv.logCanonicalDegree_eq, numMarkings_of_isEmpty] at this
+    omega
+  · have := hG v
+    rw [hv.logCanonicalDegree_eq, numMarkings_of_isEmpty] at this
+    omega
+  · by_contra hnonpos
+    rcases G.logCanonicalDegree_nonpos_iff.mp (not_lt.mp hnonpos) with ⟨hgv, hval⟩ | ⟨hgv, hval, -⟩
+    · rw [numMarkings_of_isEmpty, add_zero] at hval
+      interval_cases h : G.valence v
+      · have := two_mul_arithmeticGenus_of_valence_eq_zero h
+        omega
+      · exact (hG v).1 ⟨hgv, h⟩
+      · by_cases hloop : ∃ e, G.endpoint e 0 = v ∧ G.endpoint e 1 = v
+        · obtain ⟨e, he₀, he₁⟩ := hloop
+          have := two_mul_arithmeticGenus_of_valence_eq_two_of_loop h he₀ he₁
+          omega
+        · exact (hG v).2 ⟨hgv, h, fun e he₀ he₁ ↦ hloop ⟨e, he₀, he₁⟩⟩
+    · have := two_mul_arithmeticGenus_of_valence_eq_zero hval
+      omega
+
+end DualGraph
+
+end TauCeti

+module
+
+public import Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Defs
+public import TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Curves.DualGraph.Basic
+import Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Basic
+import Mathlib.Tactic.FinCases
+
+/-!
+# The dual graph of a cycle of rational curves
+
+For `r ≥ 1`, glue `r` smooth rational curves in a ring, each one meeting the next in a node and
+the last meeting the first. The dual graph of the resulting curve is `TauCeti.DualGraph.cycle r`:
+its vertices and edges are both indexed by `ZMod r`, and the edge `e` joins the vertices `e` and
+`e + 1`. For `r = 1` it is the dual graph of the irreducible rational curve with one node, whose
+single edge is a loop. These are the configurations of Kodaira type `Iᵣ`.
+
+Every vertex has genus zero and valence two, so the graph has arithmetic genus one and every
+log-canonical degree vanishes: the cycle is semistable but not stable, the standard example
+separating the two notions.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+namespace DualGraph
+
+open Finset
+
+variable (r : ℕ) [NeZero r]
+
+/-- The dual graph of a cycle of `r` smooth rational curves, the edge `e` joining the vertices `e`
+and `e + 1` of `ZMod r`; for `r = 1` its single edge is a loop. -/
+abbrev cycle : DualGraph.{0, 0} Empty where
+  Vertex := ZMod r
+  Edge := ZMod r
+  endpoint e i := if i = 0 then e else e + 1
+  genus _ := 0
+  marking := Empty.elim
+  connected v w := by
+    -- Walk from `v` along the edges `v, v + 1, …` until reaching `w = v + (w - v)`.
+    obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ : ∃ k : ℕ, w = v + (k : ZMod r) := ⟨(w - v).val, by simp⟩
+    induction k with
+    | zero =>
+      -- after rewriting, `rw` closes the goal `ReflTransGen _ v v` by reflexivity
+      rw [Nat.cast_zero, add_zero]
+    | succ k ih =>
+      rw [Nat.cast_add_one, ← add_assoc]
+      exact ih.tail ⟨v + k, Or.inl ⟨by simp, by simp⟩⟩
+
+variable {r}
+
+/-- Every vertex of a cycle has valence two: it carries one branch of the edge before it and one
+of the edge after it, or both branches of the loop when `r = 1`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem valence_cycle (v : ZMod r) : (cycle r).valence v = 2 := by
+  rw [valence_def, card_eq_two]
+  refine ⟨(v, 0), (v - 1, 1), by simp, ?_⟩
+  ext ⟨e, i⟩
+  fin_cases i <;> simp [eq_sub_iff_add_eq]
+
+/-- A cycle of rational curves has arithmetic genus one. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem arithmeticGenus_cycle : (cycle r).arithmeticGenus = 1 := by
+  have h := (cycle r).arithmeticGenus_add_card_vertex
+  simp only [sum_const_zero, zero_add] at h
+  have hcard : Fintype.card (cycle r).Vertex = Fintype.card (cycle r).Edge := rfl
+  omega
+
+/-- Every vertex of a cycle has log-canonical degree zero. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem logCanonicalDegree_cycle (v : ZMod r) : (cycle r).logCanonicalDegree v = 0 := by
+  simp [logCanonicalDegree_def, valence_cycle]
+
+/-- A cycle of rational curves is semistable. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem isSemistable_cycle : (cycle r).IsSemistable :=
+  (cycle r).isSemistable_iff.mpr fun v ↦ (logCanonicalDegree_cycle v).ge
+
+/-- A cycle of rational curves is not stable. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem not_isStable_cycle : ¬ (cycle r).IsStable :=
+  fun h ↦ ((cycle r).isStable_iff.mp h 0).ne' (logCanonicalDegree_cycle 0)
+
+end DualGraph
+
+end TauCeti

+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 The Tau Ceti contributors. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: The Tau Ceti contributors
+-/
+module
+
+public import Mathlib.FieldTheory.Finite.Basic
+public import TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Frobenius.Basic
+
+/-!
+# Iterated absolute Frobenius
+
+The `n`-fold absolute Frobenius of a scheme in characteristic `p` is the endomorphism obtained by
+composing its absolute Frobenius `n` times.  It fixes the underlying topological space and raises
+sections to their `p ^ n`-th powers.  These iterates are the absolute maps underlying relative
+Frobenius twists and finite-field Frobenius morphisms.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.iterateFrobenius`: the `n`-fold absolute Frobenius of a scheme.

+## Main results
+
+* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.iterateFrobenius_zero`, `_succ`, and `_add`: the iteration laws.
+* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.iterateFrobenius_naturality`: every morphism of characteristic-`p`
+  schemes commutes with every iterate.

+  their `p ^ n`-th powers.
+* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.qPowerFrobenius`: the absolute `q`-power map of a scheme over a finite
+  field of cardinality `q`.

+
