+
+open CategoryTheory
+
+universe u
+
+namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
+
+variable {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
+
+/-- The `n`-fold absolute Frobenius of a scheme in which the prime `p` vanishes. -/
+noncomputable def iterateFrobenius (X : Scheme.{u}) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
+    (hX : (p : Γ(X, ⊤)) = 0) : ℕ → (X ⟶ X)
+  | 0 => 𝟙 X
+  | n + 1 => X.iterateFrobenius p hX n ≫ X.frobenius p hX
+
+/-- The zeroth absolute Frobenius iterate is the identity. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem iterateFrobenius_zero (hX : (p : Γ(X, ⊤)) = 0) :
+    X.iterateFrobenius p hX 0 = 𝟙 X :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- A successor absolute Frobenius iterate is obtained by composing with one Frobenius. -/
+theorem iterateFrobenius_succ (hX : (p : Γ(X, ⊤)) = 0) (n : ℕ) :
+    X.iterateFrobenius p hX (n + 1) =
+      X.iterateFrobenius p hX n ≫ X.frobenius p hX :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- The first absolute Frobenius iterate is the absolute Frobenius. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem iterateFrobenius_one (hX : (p : Γ(X, ⊤)) = 0) :
+    X.iterateFrobenius p hX 1 = X.frobenius p hX := by
+  simp [iterateFrobenius_succ]
+
+/-- Adding iteration exponents corresponds to composition of absolute Frobenius iterates. -/
+theorem iterateFrobenius_add (hX : (p : Γ(X, ⊤)) = 0) (m n : ℕ) :
+    X.iterateFrobenius p hX (m + n) =
+      X.iterateFrobenius p hX m ≫ X.iterateFrobenius p hX n := by
+  induction n with
+  | zero => simp
+  | succ n ih =>
+    rw [Nat.add_succ, iterateFrobenius_succ, ih, iterateFrobenius_succ, Category.assoc]
+
+/-- Every absolute Frobenius iterate fixes the underlying point of the scheme. -/
+theorem iterateFrobenius_apply (hX : (p : Γ(X, ⊤)) = 0) (n : ℕ) (x : X) :
+    X.iterateFrobenius p hX n x = x := by
+  induction n with
+  | zero => rfl
+  | succ n ih => simp [iterateFrobenius_succ, ih]
+
+/-- Every absolute Frobenius iterate has the identity map on the underlying space. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem iterateFrobenius_base (hX : (p : Γ(X, ⊤)) = 0) (n : ℕ) :
+    (X.iterateFrobenius p hX n).base = 𝟙 _ := by
+  induction n with
+  | zero => rfl
+  | succ n ih => simp [iterateFrobenius_succ, ih]
+
+/-- The `n`-fold absolute Frobenius raises global sections to their `p ^ n`-th powers. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem iterateFrobenius_appTop_apply (hX : (p : Γ(X, ⊤)) = 0) (n : ℕ)
+    (s : Γ(X, ⊤)) :

+  induction n generalizing s with
+  | zero => simp
+  | succ n ih =>
+    rw [iterateFrobenius_succ, Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop, CommRingCat.comp_apply,
+      frobenius_appTop_apply, ih, Nat.pow_succ', pow_mul]
+
+omit [Fact p.Prime] in
+/-- The prime `p` vanishes on the global sections of the spectrum of a ring of
+characteristic `p`. -/
+theorem natCast_spec_eq_zero (R : CommRingCat.{u}) [CharP R p] :
+    (p : Γ(Spec R, ⊤)) = 0 := by
+  have hR : (p : R) = 0 := CharP.cast_eq_zero R p
+  simpa only [map_natCast, map_zero] using congr((ΓSpecIso R).inv $hR)
+
+/-- On an affine scheme, iterated absolute Frobenius is induced by the corresponding iterated
+Frobenius of the coordinate ring. -/
+theorem Spec_map_iterateFrobenius (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [CharP R p] (n : ℕ) :
+    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (_root_.iterateFrobenius R p n)) =
+      (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).iterateFrobenius p
+        (natCast_spec_eq_zero (CommRingCat.of R)) n := by
+  induction n with
+  | zero =>
+    simpa only [_root_.iterateFrobenius_zero, CommRingCat.ofHom_id,
+      iterateFrobenius_zero] using Spec.map_id (CommRingCat.of R)
+  | succ n ih =>
+    rw [iterateFrobenius_succ]
+    rw [← ih, ← Spec_map_powRingHom (CommRingCat.of R) (CharP.cast_eq_zero R p),
+      ← Spec.map_comp]
+    congr 1
+    rw [← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp,
+      TauCeti.powRingHom_eq_frobenius (CharP.cast_eq_zero R p)]
+    simpa only [_root_.iterateFrobenius_one] using
+      congrArg CommRingCat.ofHom (_root_.iterateFrobenius_add R p n 1)
+
+/-- Every morphism of schemes in characteristic `p` commutes with every absolute Frobenius
+iterate. -/
+@[reassoc]
+theorem iterateFrobenius_naturality (hX : (p : Γ(X, ⊤)) = 0)
+    (hY : (p : Γ(Y, ⊤)) = 0) (f : X ⟶ Y) (n : ℕ) :
+    X.iterateFrobenius p hX n ≫ f = f ≫ Y.iterateFrobenius p hY n := by
+  induction n with
+  | zero => simp
+  | succ n ih =>
+    rw [iterateFrobenius_succ, iterateFrobenius_succ, Category.assoc,
+      frobenius_naturality hX hY f, ← Category.assoc, ih, Category.assoc]
+
+/-- The absolute `q`-power Frobenius of a scheme over a finite field `k`, where
+`q = Nat.card k = p ^ a`. -/
+noncomputable def qPowerFrobenius (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharP k p]
+    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (a : ℕ) (_ha : Nat.card k = p ^ a) :
+    X ⟶ X :=
+  X.iterateFrobenius p
+    (natCast_eq_zero_of_hom f (natCast_spec_eq_zero (CommRingCat.of k))) a
+
+/-- The finite-field `q`-power Frobenius is the specified absolute Frobenius iterate. -/
+theorem qPowerFrobenius_eq_iterated (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharP k p]
+    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (a : ℕ)
+    (ha : Nat.card k = p ^ a) :
+    qPowerFrobenius k f a ha =
+      X.iterateFrobenius p
+        (natCast_eq_zero_of_hom f (natCast_spec_eq_zero (CommRingCat.of k))) a :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- The finite-field `q`-power Frobenius raises global sections to their `q`-th powers. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem qPowerFrobenius_appTop_apply (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharP k p]
+    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (a : ℕ)
+    (ha : Nat.card k = p ^ a) (s : Γ(X, ⊤)) :
+    (qPowerFrobenius k f a ha).appTop s = s ^ Nat.card k := by
+  rw [qPowerFrobenius_eq_iterated, iterateFrobenius_appTop_apply, ha]
+
+/-- Every morphism between schemes over the same finite field commutes with their `q`-power
+Frobenius maps. -/
+@[reassoc]
+theorem qPowerFrobenius_naturality (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharP k p]
+    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (fX : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
+    (fY : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (g : X ⟶ Y) (a : ℕ)
+    (ha : Nat.card k = p ^ a) :
+    qPowerFrobenius k fX a ha ≫ g = g ≫ qPowerFrobenius k fY a ha := by
+  exact iterateFrobenius_naturality
+    (natCast_eq_zero_of_hom fX (natCast_spec_eq_zero (CommRingCat.of k)))
+    (natCast_eq_zero_of_hom fY (natCast_spec_eq_zero (CommRingCat.of k))) g a
+
+/-- The finite-field `q`-power Frobenius is a morphism over the given finite field. -/
+@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
+theorem qPowerFrobenius_over (k : Type u) [Field k] [Finite k] [CharP k p]
+    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (a : ℕ)
+    (ha : Nat.card k = p ^ a) :
+    qPowerFrobenius k f a ha ≫ f = f := by
+  rw [qPowerFrobenius_eq_iterated,
+    iterateFrobenius_naturality
+      (natCast_eq_zero_of_hom f (natCast_spec_eq_zero (CommRingCat.of k)))
+      (natCast_spec_eq_zero (CommRingCat.of k)) f a]
+  suffices (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).iterateFrobenius p
+      (natCast_spec_eq_zero (CommRingCat.of k)) a = 𝟙 _ by
+    rw [this, Category.comp_id]
+  rw [← Spec_map_iterateFrobenius]
+  let _ : Fintype k := Fintype.ofFinite k
+  have ha' : Fintype.card k = p ^ a := by simpa using ha
+  rw [_root_.iterateFrobenius_eq_pow, FiniteField.frobenius_pow ha']
+  exact Spec.map_id _
+
+end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

+/-!
+# The circle is the classifying space of `ℤ`
+
+Milnor's classifying space `classifyingSpace (Multiplicative ℤ)` is homotopy equivalent to the
+circle, by a homotopy equivalence that induces the identity of `ℤ` under the identifications of
+both fundamental groups with `ℤ`.
+
+The equivalence is the map `circleToClassifyingSpace`, which wraps the circle once around a loop
+at the base point of the classifying space representing the generator `ofAdd 1` of `ℤ`. Under the
+isomorphisms `Circle.fundamentalGroupMulEquiv`, the degree of a loop in the circle, and
+`classifyingSpaceFundamentalGroupMulEquiv`, the map induces the identity of `ℤ`
+(`classifyingSpaceFundamentalGroupMulEquiv_mapOfEq_circleToClassifyingSpace`): both sides are
+homomorphisms out of `ℤ` that agree on the counterclockwise loop. Both spaces are aspherical, so
+the map is a weak homotopy equivalence (`TauCeti.IsAspherical.isWeakHomotopyEquivalence_iff`), and
+both are CW complexes, so Whitehead's theorem makes it a homotopy equivalence.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `TauCeti.circleToClassifyingSpace`: the based map from the circle to the classifying space of
+  `ℤ` around a loop representing the generator.
+* `TauCeti.circleHomotopyEquivClassifyingSpace`: the homotopy equivalence
+  `Circle ≃ₕ classifyingSpace (Multiplicative ℤ)` whose forward map is
+  `circleToClassifyingSpace`.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `TauCeti.classifyingSpaceFundamentalGroupMulEquiv_mapOfEq_circleToClassifyingSpace`: the map
+  induces the identity of `ℤ` on fundamental groups.
+* `TauCeti.isWeakHomotopyEquivalence_circleToClassifyingSpace`: it is a weak homotopy equivalence.
+
+## References
+
+* A. Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Cambridge University Press, 2002, Section 1.B, Theorem 1B.8.
+* J. Milnor, *Construction of universal bundles, II*, Ann. of Math. 63 (1956), 430--436.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+noncomputable section
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+open scoped Topology Topology.Homotopy
+
+/-- The based map from the circle to the classifying space of `ℤ` that goes once around a loop at
+the base point representing the generator `ofAdd 1` of `ℤ`. The point `exp (2πit)` goes to the
+value of the loop at `t`. -/
+def circleToClassifyingSpace : C(Circle, classifyingSpace (Multiplicative ℤ)) :=
+  (Quotient.out (FundamentalGroup.toPath
+    ((classifyingSpaceFundamentalGroupMulEquiv (Multiplicative ℤ)).symm
+      (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1)))).toCircle
+
+/-- The map from the circle preserves the base points. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem circleToClassifyingSpace_one :
+    circleToClassifyingSpace 1 = classifyingSpaceBasepoint (Multiplicative ℤ) :=
+  Path.toCircle_one _
+
+/-- **The map from the circle induces the identity of `ℤ` on fundamental groups**, under the
+identification `Circle.fundamentalGroupMulEquiv` of `π₁(S¹)` with `ℤ` by the degree, and the
+identification `classifyingSpaceFundamentalGroupMulEquiv` of the fundamental group of the
+classifying space with `ℤ`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem classifyingSpaceFundamentalGroupMulEquiv_mapOfEq_circleToClassifyingSpace
+    (γ : FundamentalGroup Circle 1) :
+    classifyingSpaceFundamentalGroupMulEquiv (Multiplicative ℤ)
+        (FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq circleToClassifyingSpace circleToClassifyingSpace_one γ) =
+      Circle.fundamentalGroupMulEquiv 1 γ := by
+  -- Both sides are homomorphisms out of `π₁(S¹) ≅ ℤ`, so it suffices to compare them on the
+  -- counterclockwise loop, which the circle identification sends to the generator.
+  suffices h : ((classifyingSpaceFundamentalGroupMulEquiv (Multiplicative ℤ)).toMonoidHom.comp
+        (FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq circleToClassifyingSpace circleToClassifyingSpace_one)).comp
+          (Circle.fundamentalGroupMulEquiv 1).symm.toMonoidHom = MonoidHom.id _ by
+    simpa using congrArg (· (Circle.fundamentalGroupMulEquiv 1 γ)) h
+  refine MonoidHom.ext_mint ?_
+  have hgen : (Circle.fundamentalGroupMulEquiv 1).symm (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1) =
+      FundamentalGroup.fromPath (Path.Homotopic.Quotient.mk Circle.expLoop) := by
+    rw [MulEquiv.symm_apply_eq, Circle.fundamentalGroupMulEquiv_expLoop]
+  simp only [MonoidHom.coe_comp, MulEquiv.coe_toMonoidHom, Function.comp_apply, hgen,
+    MonoidHom.id_apply]
+  -- The loop wrapped around is a representative of the class sent to the generator.
+  refine (congrArg (classifyingSpaceFundamentalGroupMulEquiv _)
+    ((Circle.mapOfEq_toCircle_expLoop _).trans
+      (congrArg CategoryTheory.End.of (Quotient.out_eq _)))).trans ?_
+  exact MulEquiv.apply_symm_apply _ _
+
+/-- **The map from the circle to the classifying space of `ℤ` is a weak homotopy equivalence.**
+Both spaces are aspherical and the map induces an isomorphism of fundamental groups. -/
+theorem isWeakHomotopyEquivalence_circleToClassifyingSpace :
+    circleToClassifyingSpace.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence := by
+  refine ((IsAspherical.mk inferInstance fun _ ↦ inferInstance).isWeakHomotopyEquivalence_iff
+    (isEilenbergMacLaneSpaceOne_classifyingSpace (Multiplicative ℤ)).isAspherical
+    circleToClassifyingSpace_one).2 ?_
+  have h : ⇑(FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq circleToClassifyingSpace circleToClassifyingSpace_one) =
+      (classifyingSpaceFundamentalGroupMulEquiv (Multiplicative ℤ)).symm ∘
+        Circle.fundamentalGroupMulEquiv 1 := by
+    funext γ
+    rw [Function.comp_apply, MulEquiv.eq_symm_apply,
+      classifyingSpaceFundamentalGroupMulEquiv_mapOfEq_circleToClassifyingSpace]
+  rw [h]
+  exact (MulEquiv.bijective _).comp (MulEquiv.bijective _)
+
+/-- **The circle is homotopy equivalent to the classifying space of `ℤ`**, by Whitehead's
+theorem applied to `circleToClassifyingSpace`. Its forward map induces the identity of `ℤ` on
+fundamental groups
+(`classifyingSpaceFundamentalGroupMulEquiv_mapOfEq_circleToClassifyingSpace`). -/
+def circleHomotopyEquivClassifyingSpace :
+    ContinuousMap.HomotopyEquiv Circle (classifyingSpace (Multiplicative ℤ)) :=
+  isWeakHomotopyEquivalence_circleToClassifyingSpace.homotopyEquiv
+
+/-- The forward map of the homotopy equivalence is `circleToClassifyingSpace`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem circleHomotopyEquivClassifyingSpace_toFun :
+    circleHomotopyEquivClassifyingSpace.toFun = circleToClassifyingSpace :=
+  isWeakHomotopyEquivalence_circleToClassifyingSpace.homotopyEquiv_toFun
+
+end TauCeti

+/-!
+# Weak homotopy equivalences between aspherical spaces
+
+An aspherical space is path-connected and its homotopy groups vanish in every dimension except
+one, so the only homotopy invariant a map between aspherical spaces can fail to preserve is the
+fundamental group. Accordingly, a map between aspherical spaces is a weak homotopy equivalence
+exactly when it induces an isomorphism of fundamental groups at one base point
+(`TauCeti.IsAspherical.isWeakHomotopyEquivalence_iff`).
+
+Combined with Whitehead's theorem `ContinuousMap.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence.homotopyEquiv`, this is
+the last step in the uniqueness of `K(G, 1)` spaces: a map between two `K(G, 1)` spaces of CW type
+that induces an isomorphism of fundamental groups is a homotopy equivalence. The hypothesis on
+both spaces cannot be dropped, because the Warsaw circle and a point are both aspherical with
+trivial fundamental group, but they are not homotopy equivalent.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `TauCeti.IsAspherical.isWeakHomotopyEquivalence_iff`: a map between aspherical spaces is a weak
+  homotopy equivalence exactly when it induces a bijection of fundamental groups.
+
+## References
+
+* A. Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Cambridge University Press, 2002, Section 1.B, Theorem 1B.8,
+  and Section 4.1, Theorem 4.5.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+open scoped Topology Topology.Homotopy
+
+namespace IsAspherical
+
+variable {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] {x : X} {y : Y} {f : C(X, Y)}
+
+/-- **A map between aspherical spaces is a weak homotopy equivalence exactly when it induces an
+isomorphism of fundamental groups.** Bijectivity at the single base point `x` suffices. -/
+theorem isWeakHomotopyEquivalence_iff (hX : IsAspherical X x) (hY : IsAspherical Y y)
+    (hxy : f x = y) :
+    f.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence ↔ Function.Bijective (FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq f hxy) := by
+  refine ⟨fun hf ↦ hf.mapOfEq_bijective hxy, fun h ↦ ?_⟩
+  subst hxy
+  have := hX.pathConnectedSpace
+  have := hY.pathConnectedSpace
+  refine (ContinuousMap.isWeakHomotopyEquivalence_iff_forall_bijective x).2 fun n ↦ ?_
+  match n with
+  | 0 =>
+    -- Both `π_0` are the sets of path components, which are singletons.
+    have : Subsingleton (π_ 0 X x) := HomotopyGroup.pi0EquivZerothHomotopy.subsingleton
+    have : Subsingleton (π_ 0 Y (f x)) := HomotopyGroup.pi0EquivZerothHomotopy.subsingleton
+    exact Function.bijective_of_subsingleton' _
+  | 1 => exact (HomotopyGroup.bijective_map_iff_bijective_mapOfEq f rfl).2 h
+  | n + 2 =>
+    have := hX.subsingleton_homotopyGroup n
+    have := hY.subsingleton_homotopyGroup n
+    exact Function.bijective_of_subsingleton' _
+
+end IsAspherical
+
+end TauCeti

+/-!
+# Attaching cells: homotopy groups below their dimension, and killing `π_n`
+
+Let `Y` be obtained from a Hausdorff space `X` by attaching `(n + 1)`-cells along maps of their
+boundary spheres `Sⁿ → X`, and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be the inclusion. Then `f` induces a bijection
+`π_k(X, x) → π_k(Y, f x)` for `k < n` and a surjection for `k = n`, at every base point `x`
+(`HomotopicalAlgebra.AttachCells.bijective_homotopyGroupMap`,
+`HomotopicalAlgebra.AttachCells.surjective_homotopyGroupMap`). For the space
+`TauCeti.cellAttachment φ` obtained by attaching cells along a family `φ` of maps from spheres,
+these are `TauCeti.bijective_homotopyGroupMap_cellAttachmentIncl` and
+`TauCeti.surjective_homotopyGroupMap_cellAttachmentIncl`.
+
+This is Hatcher's Corollary 4.12 for the pair `(Y, X)`, all of whose cells outside `X` have
+dimension `n + 1`. Attaching the cells is a relative CW complex
+(`HomotopicalAlgebra.AttachCells.toRelativeCWComplex`), whose classical skeleton
+`skeletonLT Y (n + 1)` is the range of `f`, so the statements for the inclusion of a skeleton
+(`TauCeti.surjective_homotopyGroupMap_skeletonLT`, `TauCeti.injective_homotopyGroupMap_skeletonLT`)
+apply; `f` is a closed embedding, which identifies `X` with its range.
+
+When `n ≥ 1`, attaching cells kills chosen classes of `π_n(X, x)`. A generalized loop `p`
+representing a class gives the attaching map `GenLoop.diskBoundaryMap p`, the
+corresponding pointed map `Sⁿ → X`. It becomes null-homotopic in `Y`
+(`TauCeti.cellAttachment_attachingMap_nullhomotopic`), so the class of `p` maps to the identity
+(`TauCeti.map_cellAttachmentIncl_mk_eq_one`). If the classes of the attaching loops generate
+`π_n(X, x)` as a normal subgroup, the surjection on `π_n` then makes `π_n(Y, f x)` trivial
+(`TauCeti.subsingleton_homotopyGroup_cellAttachment`).

+
+* `HomotopicalAlgebra.AttachCells.surjective_homotopyGroupMap`: attaching `(n + 1)`-cells is
+  surjective on `π_k` for `k ≤ n`.
+* `HomotopicalAlgebra.AttachCells.bijective_homotopyGroupMap`: attaching `(n + 1)`-cells is
+  bijective on `π_k` for `k < n`.

+  generators of `π_n(X, x)` kills `π_n`.

+* A. Hatcher, [*Algebraic Topology*](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf),
+  Section 4.1, Corollary 4.12, and the same section for attaching cells to kill homotopy

+public section
+

+
+universe u v
+
+open CategoryTheory Topology Set TauCeti

+namespace HomotopicalAlgebra.AttachCells

+variable {X Y : TopCat.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} {N : Type v} [T2Space X] [Finite N] {n : ℕ}

+/-- **Attaching `(n + 1)`-cells is surjective on `π_k` for `k ≤ n`** (Hatcher, Corollary 4.12).

+induces a surjection `π_k(X, x) → π_k(Y, f x)`, where `k = Nat.card N ≤ n`. -/

+    Function.Surjective (HomotopyGroup.map (N := N) (x := x) f.hom rfl) := by
+  let := c.toRelativeCWComplex.toRelCWComplex
+  have := c.toRelativeCWComplex.t2Space

+    c.toRelativeCWComplex.isClosedEmbedding.isEmbedding x]

+    (c.skeletonLT_toRelCWComplex le_rfl) (subset_univ _) _).comp (Equiv.surjective _))

+If `Y` is obtained from a Hausdorff space `X` by attaching `(n + 1)`-disks along `f`, then `f`
+induces a bijection `π_k(X, x) → π_k(Y, f x)`, where `k = Nat.card N < n`. -/
+theorem bijective_homotopyGroupMap (hN : Nat.card N < n) (x : X) :
+    Function.Bijective (HomotopyGroup.map (N := N) (x := x) f.hom rfl) := by
+  refine ⟨?_, c.surjective_homotopyGroupMap hN.le x⟩
+  let := c.toRelativeCWComplex.toRelCWComplex
+  have := c.toRelativeCWComplex.t2Space
+  rw [HomotopyGroup.map_eq_comp_of_isEmbedding
+    c.toRelativeCWComplex.isClosedEmbedding.isEmbedding x]
+  exact (Equiv.injective _).comp ((injective_homotopyGroupMap_skeletonLT hN
+    (c.skeletonLT_toRelCWComplex le_rfl) (subset_univ _) _).comp (Equiv.injective _))
+
+end HomotopicalAlgebra.AttachCells
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+variable {X : TopCat.{u}} [T2Space X] {ι : Type u} {n : ℕ}
+  (φ : ι → (TopCat.diskBoundary (n + 1) ⟶ X)) {N : Type v} [Finite N]
+
+/-- Attaching `(n + 1)`-cells to a Hausdorff space `X` along any family of maps `Sⁿ → X` induces
+a surjection `π_k(X, x) → π_k(X ∪ eⁿ⁺¹, x)` for `k = Nat.card N ≤ n`. -/
+theorem surjective_homotopyGroupMap_cellAttachmentIncl (hN : Nat.card N ≤ n) (x : X) :
+    Function.Surjective (HomotopyGroup.map (N := N) (x := x) (cellAttachmentIncl φ).hom rfl) :=
+  (cellAttachmentAttachCells φ).surjective_homotopyGroupMap hN x

+/-- Attaching `(n + 1)`-cells to a Hausdorff space `X` along any family of maps `Sⁿ → X` induces

+theorem bijective_homotopyGroupMap_cellAttachmentIncl (hN : Nat.card N < n) (x : X) :
+    Function.Bijective (HomotopyGroup.map (N := N) (x := x) (cellAttachmentIncl φ).hom rfl) :=
+  (cellAttachmentAttachCells φ).bijective_homotopyGroupMap hN x
+

+  rw [GenLoop.toSphere_map]

+  -- `GenLoop.toSphere (p i)` is the attaching map precomposed with `ULift.up`
+  have h : (GenLoop.toSphere (p i)) =

+    ext s
+    exact (GenLoop.diskBoundaryMap_apply (p i) ⟨s⟩).symm

+    Subsingleton (HomotopyGroup (Fin n) (cellAttachment fun i ↦ GenLoop.diskBoundaryMap (p i))
+      (cellAttachmentIncl (fun i ↦ GenLoop.diskBoundaryMap (p i)) x)) := by

+    rw [← hp]
+    refine Subgroup.normalClosure_le_normal ?_
+    rintro _ ⟨i, rfl⟩
+    exact map_cellAttachmentIncl_mk_eq_one p i

+    (fun i ↦ GenLoop.diskBoundaryMap (p i)) (N := Fin n) (by simp) x b
+  exact f.mem_ker.1 (hker (Subgroup.mem_top a))
+
+end TauCeti

+# Mod-two vanishing and the first possible homotopy group
+
+For an `(n + 1)`-connected space, vanishing of mod-two homology in degrees `n + 2` and
+`n + 3` implies unique two-divisibility of `πₙ₊₂`. In particular this homotopy group is a
+module over `ℤ[1/2]`, and its tensor product with `ℤ/2` vanishes. Only the two adjacent
+homology groups are needed; no finite-generation assumption is imposed.
+
+This is the first step in constructing connected covers of a simply connected mod-two
+acyclic space. The Hurewicz equivalence identifies the first possible homotopy group with
+integral homology, on which the coefficient exact sequence makes multiplication by two
+bijective. Both adjacent vanishing hypotheses matter: the lower one gives surjectivity,
+and the higher one rules out two-torsion.
+
+## References
+
+* A. Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Sections 3.A and 4.2.
+* J.-P. Serre, *Groupes d'homotopie et classes de groupes abéliens*, Ann. of Math. 58 (1953).
+-/
+
+public noncomputable section
+
+open CategoryTheory AlgebraicTopology
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+variable {X : Type} [TopologicalSpace X] {x : X} {n : ℕ}
+
+/-- If all lower homotopy groups vanish, vanishing of mod-two homology in two adjacent
+higher degrees makes the first possible nonzero homotopy group uniquely two-divisible.
+The group is written additively to use its canonical integer action. -/

+    (hX : ∀ k < n + 2, Subsingleton (HomotopyGroup (Fin k) X x))
+    (hn : Limits.IsZero (((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{0} ℤ) (n + 2)).obj
+      (ModuleCat.of ℤ (ZMod 2))).obj (TopCat.of X)))
+    (hn' : Limits.IsZero (((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{0} ℤ) (n + 3)).obj
+      (ModuleCat.of ℤ (ZMod 2))).obj (TopCat.of X))) :
+    IsUniquelyTwoDivisible (Additive (HomotopyGroup (Fin (n + 2)) X x)) := by
+  -- The coefficient exact sequence uses lifted coefficients; transport the two zero objects.
+  have liftZero (k : ℕ)
+      (hk : Limits.IsZero (((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{0} ℤ) k).obj
+        (ModuleCat.of ℤ (ZMod 2))).obj (TopCat.of X))) :
+      Limits.IsZero (((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{0} ℤ) k).obj
+        (ModuleCat.of ℤ (ULift.{0} (ZMod 2)))).obj (TopCat.of X)) :=
+    hk.of_iso (((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{0} ℤ) k).mapIso
+      (ULift.moduleEquiv : ULift.{0} (ZMod 2) ≃ₗ[ℤ] ZMod 2).toModuleIso).app (TopCat.of X))
+  have h := (TopCat.of X).isUniquelyTwoDivisible_singularHomology_of_isZero_mod_two
+    (n + 2) (liftZero _ hn) (liftZero _ hn')
+  let e : (((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{0} ℤ) (n + 2)).obj
+      (ModuleCat.of ℤ (ULift.{0} ℤ))).obj (TopCat.of X)) ≃+
+      ((singularChains ℤ).obj (TopCat.of X)).homology (n + 2) :=
+    (((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{0} ℤ) (n + 2)).mapIso
+      (ULift.moduleEquiv : ULift ℤ ≃ₗ[ℤ] ℤ).toModuleIso).app
+        (TopCat.of X)).toLinearEquiv.toAddEquiv
+  exact (h.of_addEquiv e).of_addEquiv
+    (HomotopyGroup.cubicalHurewiczSingularHomologyAddEquiv hX).symm
+
+end TauCeti

+/-!
+# Attaching no cells
+
+An isomorphism `f : X₁ ⟶ X₂` is obtained by attaching an empty family of cells
+(`HomotopicalAlgebra.AttachCells.ofIsIso`): the pushout of the identity of an initial object along
+any morphism is an isomorphism. This fills the stages of a relative cell complex at which nothing
+is attached, for instance when all cells are attached at a single stage.
+
+## References
+
+* R. Fritsch and R. Piccinini, *Cellular Structures in Topology*, Cambridge University Press,
+  1990.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open CategoryTheory Limits
+
+universe w v u
+
+namespace HomotopicalAlgebra.AttachCells
+
+variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasColimitsOfShape (Discrete PEmpty.{w + 1}) C]
+  {α : Type*} {A B : α → C} (g : ∀ a, A a ⟶ B a) {X₁ X₂ : C} (f : X₁ ⟶ X₂) [IsIso f]
+
+/-- An isomorphism is obtained by attaching no cells. -/
+noncomputable def ofIsIso : AttachCells.{w} g f where
+  ι := PEmpty.{w + 1}
+  π := PEmpty.elim
+  cofan₁ := Cofan.mk _ (Sigma.ι fun i : PEmpty.{w + 1} ↦ A i.elim)
+  cofan₂ := Cofan.mk _ (Sigma.ι fun i : PEmpty.{w + 1} ↦ B i.elim)
+  isColimit₁ := coproductIsCoproduct _
+  isColimit₂ := coproductIsCoproduct _
+  m := Sigma.desc fun i ↦ i.elim
+  hm i := i.elim
+  g₁ := Sigma.desc fun i ↦ i.elim
+  g₂ := Sigma.desc fun i ↦ i.elim
+  isPushout := by
+    -- Both coproducts are empty, so the left vertical map is an isomorphism, as is `f`.
+    refine @IsPushout.of_vert_isIso _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ ?_ _ ⟨Sigma.hom_ext _ _ fun i ↦ i.elim⟩
+    exact ⟨Sigma.desc fun i ↦ i.elim, Sigma.hom_ext _ _ fun i ↦ i.elim,
+      Sigma.hom_ext _ _ fun i ↦ i.elim⟩
+
+/-- No cells are attached in `AttachCells.ofIsIso`. -/
+instance : IsEmpty (ofIsIso.{w} g f).ι :=
+  ⟨fun i ↦ i.elim⟩
+
+end HomotopicalAlgebra.AttachCells

+module
+
+public import TauCeti.Algebra.Homology.Homotopy
+public import TauCeti.AlgebraicTopology.Singular.Cubical.Compression.Deformation
+public import TauCeti.AlgebraicTopology.Singular.Cubical.Comparison.Basic
+public import TauCeti.AlgebraicTopology.Singular.Cubical.Prism
+
+/-!
+# The retraction of cubical chains onto the chains of a compressible subspace
+
+Let `D` be a `TauCeti.SubspaceCubeDeformation A`: a homotopy of every singular cube `c` of `X` to a
+cube with values in `A ⊆ X`, compatible with faces and degeneracies and constant on the cubes that
+already have values in `A`. This file turns `D` into chain-level data on Massey's normalized cubical
+chains and shows that **the inclusion `A → X` induces a chain homotopy equivalence of normalized
+cubical chains**.
+
+* The end of the homotopy of `c` is a cube `D.retract c` of `A`. It commutes with faces and
+  preserves degeneracies, so it induces a chain map `D.retractChainMap R` from the normalized
+  cubical chains of `X` to those of `A`. As the homotopy of a cube of `A` is constant, this chain
+  map is a left inverse of the chain map induced by the inclusion, on the nose.
+* The homotopy of `c`, with time as the first coordinate, sweeps out the cube `D.sweep c` of one
+  dimension more. Its first two faces are `c` and the cube `D.retract c` read in `X`, and its other
+  faces are the swept faces of `c`. The negative swept-cube operator `D.prismChain R` therefore
+  satisfies `∂ P + P ∂ = ι ρ - id`, so the swept-cube operator `-D.prismChain R` is a chain homotopy
+  `D.retractHomotopy R` from the identity to the composite of the retraction and the inclusion.
+
+Through the comparison of cubical and simplicial singular chains, the inclusion of `A` then induces
+isomorphisms on singular homology with coefficients in any ring
+(`TauCeti.SubspaceCubeDeformation.isIso_singularHomologyMap`). By the compression lemma this
+applies as soon as every point of `X` is joined by a path to `A` and all relative homotopy sets
+`π_{n+1}(X, A, a)` vanish
+(`TauCeti.isIso_singularHomologyMap_subtypeVal_of_relHomotopyGroup`). For the inclusion of the
+bottom of the mapping cylinder of a weak homotopy equivalence, this gives the invariance of
+singular homology under weak homotopy equivalences (Hatcher, Proposition 4.21), proved as
+`ContinuousMap.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence.isIso_singularHomologyMap`.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `TauCeti.SubspaceCubeDeformation.retract`, `TauCeti.SubspaceCubeDeformation.cubeHomotopy`,
+  `TauCeti.SubspaceCubeDeformation.sweep`: the end of the deformation of a cube as a cube of `A`,
+  the deformation as a homotopy, and the cube it sweeps out (its `SingularCube.prism`).
+* `TauCeti.SubspaceCubeDeformation.retractChain`, `TauCeti.SubspaceCubeDeformation.prismChain`: the
+  induced operators on normalized cubical chains.
+* `TauCeti.SubspaceCubeDeformation.retractChainMap`,
+  `TauCeti.SubspaceCubeDeformation.retractHomotopy`: the retraction as a chain map onto the
+  normalized cubical chains of `A`, and the chain homotopy from the identity to its composite with
+  the inclusion.
+* `TauCeti.SubspaceCubeDeformation.normalizedCubicalChainComplexHomotopyEquiv`: the chain homotopy
+  equivalence between the normalized cubical chains of `A` and of `X` induced by the inclusion.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `TauCeti.SubspaceCubeDeformation.retractChain_map_subtypeVal`: the retraction is a left inverse
+  of the inclusion.
+* `TauCeti.SubspaceCubeDeformation.boundary_prismChain_add_prismChain_boundary`: the prism identity
+  `∂ P + P ∂ = ι ρ - id`.
+* `TauCeti.SubspaceCubeDeformation.quasiIso_normalizedCubicalChainComplex_map`,
+  `TauCeti.SubspaceCubeDeformation.isIso_singularHomologyMap`: the inclusion of `A` induces a
+  quasi-isomorphism of normalized cubical chains and isomorphisms on singular homology.
+* `TauCeti.isIso_singularHomologyMap_subtypeVal_of_relHomotopyGroup`: the same conclusion from the
+  vanishing of the relative homotopy sets.
+
+## References
+
+* The chain-level construction follows the parallel formalization in
+  `TauCeti.AlgebraicTopology.Singular.Cubical.Based.Retraction`, adapted so that the retraction
+  lands in the chains of the subspace rather than defining an endomorphism.
+* S. Eilenberg, *Singular homology theory*, Ann. of Math. (2) 45 (1944), 407–447, for the
+  deformation of singular chains into the subcomplex of a subspace.
+* A. Hatcher, [*Algebraic Topology*](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf),
+  Section 4.1, Proposition 4.21 (a weak homotopy equivalence induces isomorphisms on homology).
+* W. S. Massey, *Singular Homology Theory*, GTM 70, Springer, 1980, Chapter II, for normalized
+  cubical chains and their prism operators.

+noncomputable section

+namespace TauCeti
+
+section Cubes
+
+variable {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] {A : Set X}
+
+namespace SubspaceCubeDeformation

+variable (D : SubspaceCubeDeformation A)

+/-! ### The end of the deformation and the swept cube -/
+
+/-- The cube of `A` at the end of the deformation of the singular cube `c` of `X`. -/
+def retract {m : ℕ} (c : SingularCube X m) : SingularCube A m where
+  toFun y := ⟨D.homotopy c (1, y), D.homotopy_one_mem c y⟩
+  continuous_toFun := by fun_prop
+
+@[simp]
+theorem coe_retract_apply {m : ℕ} (c : SingularCube X m) (y : Fin m → I) :
+    (D.retract c y : X) = D.homotopy c (1, y) :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- Read in `X`, the cube `D.retract c` is the end of the deformation of `c`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem subtypeVal_comp_retract {m : ℕ} (c : SingularCube X m) :
+    (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal A).comp (D.retract c) = (D.homotopy c).curry 1 :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- The deformation fixes the cubes of `A`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem retract_subtypeVal_comp {m : ℕ} (c : SingularCube A m) :
+    D.retract ((ContinuousMap.subtypeVal A).comp c) = c := by
+  have hc : range ((ContinuousMap.subtypeVal A).comp c) ⊆ A := by
+    rintro _ ⟨y, rfl⟩
+    exact (c y).2
+  ext y
+  simp [D.homotopy_of_range_subset hc]
+
+/-- The end of the deformation commutes with the faces at the endpoints of the interval. -/
+theorem face_retract {m : ℕ} (c : SingularCube X (m + 1)) (i : Fin (m + 1)) {t : I}
+    (ht : t = 0 ∨ t = 1) :
+    SingularCube.face i t (D.retract c) = D.retract (SingularCube.face i t c) := by
+  ext y
+  simp [D.homotopy_insertNth c i ht]
+
+/-- If `c` does not depend on its coordinate `i`, then neither does the end of its
+deformation. -/
+theorem isDegenerateAt_retract {m : ℕ} {c : SingularCube X m} {i : Fin m}
+    (hc : c.IsDegenerateAt i) : (D.retract c).IsDegenerateAt i := by
+  rw [← SingularCube.isDegenerateAt_comp_iff_of_injective (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal A)
+    Subtype.val_injective, subtypeVal_comp_retract]
+  exact D.isDegenerateAt_curry hc 1
+
+/-- The end of the deformation of a degenerate cube is degenerate. -/
+theorem isDegenerate_retract {m : ℕ} {c : SingularCube X m} (hc : c.IsDegenerate) :
+    (D.retract c).IsDegenerate :=
+  (SingularCube.isDegenerate_iff.1 hc).elim fun _ hi ↦ (D.isDegenerateAt_retract hi).isDegenerate
+
+/-- The deformation of the singular cube `c`, as a homotopy from `c` to the cube `D.retract c`
+read in `X`. -/
+def cubeHomotopy {m : ℕ} (c : SingularCube X m) :
+    ContinuousMap.Homotopy c ((ContinuousMap.subtypeVal A).comp (D.retract c)) where
+  toContinuousMap := D.homotopy c
+  map_zero_left := D.homotopy_zero c
+  map_one_left _ := rfl
+
+@[simp]
+theorem cubeHomotopy_apply {m : ℕ} (c : SingularCube X m) (p : I × (Fin m → I)) :
+    D.cubeHomotopy c p = D.homotopy c p :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- The cube swept out by the deformation of the singular cube `c`, with time as the first
+coordinate. -/
+def sweep {m : ℕ} (c : SingularCube X m) : SingularCube X (m + 1) :=
+  SingularCube.prism (D.cubeHomotopy c) (ContinuousMap.id _)
+
+@[simp]
+theorem sweep_apply {m : ℕ} (c : SingularCube X m) (y : Fin (m + 1) → I) :
+    D.sweep c y = D.homotopy c (y 0, Fin.tail y) := by
+  simp [sweep]
+
+/-- The swept cube starts at `c`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem face_zero_zero_sweep {m : ℕ} (c : SingularCube X m) :
+    SingularCube.face 0 0 (D.sweep c) = c := by
+  simp [sweep]
+
+/-- The swept cube ends at the retraction of `c`, read in `X`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem face_zero_one_sweep {m : ℕ} (c : SingularCube X m) :
+    SingularCube.face 0 1 (D.sweep c) = (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal A).comp (D.retract c) := by
+  simp [sweep]
+
+/-- The faces of the swept cube in the spatial coordinates are the swept faces. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem face_succ_sweep {m : ℕ} (c : SingularCube X (m + 1)) (i : Fin (m + 1)) {t : I}
+    (ht : t = 0 ∨ t = 1) :
+    SingularCube.face i.succ t (D.sweep c) = D.sweep (SingularCube.face i t c) := by
+  ext y
+  rw [SingularCube.face_apply, sweep_apply, sweep_apply, ← Fin.cons_self_tail y,
+    Fin.insertNth_succ_cons]
+  simp [D.homotopy_insertNth c i ht]
+
+/-- If `c` does not depend on its coordinate `i`, then its swept cube does not depend on the
+coordinate `i.succ`. -/
+theorem isDegenerateAt_sweep {m : ℕ} {c : SingularCube X m} {i : Fin m}
+    (hc : c.IsDegenerateAt i) : (D.sweep c).IsDegenerateAt i.succ := by
+  rw [SingularCube.isDegenerateAt_iff]
+  intro y t
+  have h := SingularCube.isDegenerateAt_iff.1 (D.isDegenerateAt_curry hc (y 0)) (Fin.tail y) t
+  simpa [Fin.tail_update_succ, Function.update_of_ne (Fin.succ_ne_zero i).symm] using h
+
+/-- The cube swept out by the deformation of a degenerate cube is degenerate. -/
+theorem isDegenerate_sweep {m : ℕ} {c : SingularCube X m} (hc : c.IsDegenerate) :
+    (D.sweep c).IsDegenerate :=
+  (SingularCube.isDegenerate_iff.1 hc).elim fun _ hi ↦ (D.isDegenerateAt_sweep hi).isDegenerate
+
+/-! ### The operators on normalized chains -/
+
+variable (R : Type*) [Ring R]
+
+/-- The retraction onto the cubes of `A`, on normalized cubical chains. -/
+def retractChain (m : ℕ) : NormalizedCubicalChain X R m →ₗ[R] NormalizedCubicalChain A R m :=
+  Submodule.mapQ _ _ (lmapDomain R R D.retract) fun _ hg ↦
+    CubicalChain.lmapDomain_mem_degenerate R (fun _ ↦ D.isDegenerate_retract) hg
+
+/-- The negative swept-cube operator on normalized cubical chains. -/
+def prismChain (m : ℕ) : NormalizedCubicalChain X R m →ₗ[R] NormalizedCubicalChain X R (m + 1) :=
+  -Submodule.mapQ _ _ (lmapDomain R R D.sweep) fun _ hg ↦
+    CubicalChain.lmapDomain_mem_degenerate R (fun _ ↦ D.isDegenerate_sweep) hg
+
+@[simp]
+theorem retractChain_ofCube {m : ℕ} (c : SingularCube X m) :
+    D.retractChain R m (NormalizedCubicalChain.ofCube X R c) =
+      NormalizedCubicalChain.ofCube A R (D.retract c) := by
+  simp [retractChain, NormalizedCubicalChain.ofCube_def, lmapDomain_apply]
+
+@[simp]
+theorem prismChain_ofCube {m : ℕ} (c : SingularCube X m) :
+    D.prismChain R m (NormalizedCubicalChain.ofCube X R c) =
+      -NormalizedCubicalChain.ofCube X R (D.sweep c) := by
+  simp [prismChain, NormalizedCubicalChain.ofCube_def, lmapDomain_apply]
+
+/-- **The retraction is a left inverse of the inclusion** on normalized cubical chains, since the
+deformation fixes the cubes of `A`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem retractChain_map_subtypeVal {m : ℕ} (g : NormalizedCubicalChain A R m) :
+    D.retractChain R m (NormalizedCubicalChain.map R (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal A) m g) = g := by
+  induction g using NormalizedCubicalChain.induction_on with
+  | zero => simp
+  | add a b ha hb => simp [ha, hb]
+  | smul r a ha => simp [ha]
+  | ofCube c => simp
+
+/-- The retraction commutes with the boundary. -/
+theorem boundary_retractChain (m : ℕ) (g : NormalizedCubicalChain X R (m + 1)) :
+    NormalizedCubicalChain.boundary A R m (D.retractChain R (m + 1) g) =
+      D.retractChain R m (NormalizedCubicalChain.boundary X R m g) := by
+  induction g using NormalizedCubicalChain.induction_on with
+  | zero => simp
+  | add a b ha hb => simp [ha, hb]
+  | smul r a ha => simp [ha]
+  | ofCube c => simp [D.face_retract c _ (Or.inl rfl), D.face_retract c _ (Or.inr rfl)]
+
+/-- **The prism identity** `∂ P + P ∂ = ι ρ - id` in positive degrees, for the swept-cube operator
+`P`, the retraction `ρ` and the inclusion `ι` of `A`. -/
+theorem boundary_prismChain_add_prismChain_boundary (m : ℕ)
+    (g : NormalizedCubicalChain X R (m + 1)) :
+    NormalizedCubicalChain.boundary X R (m + 1) (D.prismChain R (m + 1) g) +
+        D.prismChain R m (NormalizedCubicalChain.boundary X R m g) =
+      NormalizedCubicalChain.map R (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal A) (m + 1)
+        (D.retractChain R (m + 1) g) - g := by
+  induction g using NormalizedCubicalChain.induction_on with
+  | zero => simp
+  | add a b ha hb =>
+    simp only [map_add]
+    rw [add_add_add_comm, ha, hb]
+    abel
+  | smul r a ha => simp only [map_smul, ← smul_add, ha, smul_sub]
+  | ofCube c =>
+    simp only [prismChain_ofCube, retractChain_ofCube, NormalizedCubicalChain.map_ofCube, map_neg,
+      NormalizedCubicalChain.boundary_ofCube, map_sum, map_smul, map_sub]
+    rw [Fin.sum_univ_succ]
+    simp only [face_zero_zero_sweep, face_zero_one_sweep, D.face_succ_sweep c _ (Or.inl rfl),
+      D.face_succ_sweep c _ (Or.inr rfl), Fin.val_zero, pow_zero, one_smul, Fin.val_succ, pow_succ,
+      mul_neg_one, neg_smul, smul_neg, smul_sub]
+    abel
+
+/-- The prism identity `∂ P = ι ρ - id` in degree zero. -/
+theorem boundary_prismChain_zero (g : NormalizedCubicalChain X R 0) :
+    NormalizedCubicalChain.boundary X R 0 (D.prismChain R 0 g) =
+      NormalizedCubicalChain.map R (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal A) 0 (D.retractChain R 0 g) - g := by
+  induction g using NormalizedCubicalChain.induction_on with
+  | zero => simp
+  | add a b ha hb =>
+    simp only [map_add, ha, hb]
+    abel
+  | smul r a ha => simp [ha, smul_sub]
+  | ofCube c => simp
+
+end SubspaceCubeDeformation
+
+end Cubes

+/-! ### The chain homotopy equivalence of normalized cubical chain complexes -/
+
+universe u
+
+namespace SubspaceCubeDeformation
+
+variable {X : TopCat.{u}} {A : Set X} (D : SubspaceCubeDeformation A) (R : Type u) [Ring R]
+
+/-- The retraction onto the cubes of `A`, as a chain map from the normalized cubical chains of `X`
+to those of `A`. -/
+def retractChainMap :
+    (normalizedCubicalChainComplex R).obj X ⟶ (normalizedCubicalChainComplex R).obj (TopCat.of A) :=
+  ChainComplex.ofHom (fun m ↦ ModuleCat.ofHom (D.retractChain R m)) fun m ↦ by
+    ext g
+    exact (normalizedCubicalChainComplex_obj_d_apply (TopCat.of A) m _).trans
+      ((D.boundary_retractChain R m g).trans
+        (congrArg _ (normalizedCubicalChainComplex_obj_d_apply X m g).symm))
+
+@[simp]
+theorem retractChainMap_f_apply (m : ℕ) (g : NormalizedCubicalChain X R m) :
+    (D.retractChainMap R).f m g = D.retractChain R m g :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- The retraction chain map is a left inverse of the chain map induced by the inclusion of
+`A`. -/
+@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
+theorem normalizedCubicalChainComplex_map_comp_retractChainMap :
+    (normalizedCubicalChainComplex R).map (TopCat.ofHom (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal A)) ≫
+      D.retractChainMap R = 𝟙 _ := by
+  ext m g
+  -- In degree `m` both chain maps act by their concrete linear maps, and the terms of the
+  -- normalized cubical chain complex are the modules of normalized chains by definition
+  -- (`normalizedCubicalChainComplex_obj_X`), so the goal is the chain-level statement.
+  exact D.retractChain_map_subtypeVal R g
+
+/-- The negative swept-cube operator, as a morphism between the terms of the normalized cubical
+chain complex. -/
+private def prismHom (m : ℕ) :
+    ((normalizedCubicalChainComplex R).obj X).X m ⟶
+      ((normalizedCubicalChainComplex R).obj X).X (m + 1) :=
+  ModuleCat.ofHom (D.prismChain R m)
+
+/-- **The chain homotopy from the identity to the composite of the retraction and the inclusion of
+`A`**, given in degree `m` by the swept-cube operator `-D.prismChain R m`. -/
+def retractHomotopy :
+    Homotopy (𝟙 _) (D.retractChainMap R ≫
+      (normalizedCubicalChainComplex R).map (TopCat.ofHom (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal A))) :=
+  (Homotopy.equivSubZero.symm
+    (Homotopy.mkChainComplex (D.retractChainMap R ≫
+        (normalizedCubicalChainComplex R).map (TopCat.ofHom (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal A)) - 𝟙 _)
+      (D.prismHom R)
+      (by
+        ext g
+        simp only [HomologicalComplex.sub_f_apply, HomologicalComplex.comp_f,
+          HomologicalComplex.id_f, ModuleCat.hom_sub, ModuleCat.hom_id, ModuleCat.hom_comp,
+          LinearMap.sub_apply, LinearMap.id_apply, LinearMap.comp_apply,
+          normalizedCubicalChainComplex_map_f]
+        exact (D.boundary_prismChain_zero R g).symm)
+      (fun m ↦ by
+        ext g
+        -- The differentials of `ChainComplex.of` are the boundaries only after `ChainComplex.of_d`.
+        have h₁ := normalizedCubicalChainComplex_obj_d_apply (R := R) X m g
+        have h₂ := normalizedCubicalChainComplex_obj_d_apply (R := R) X (m + 1) (D.prismHom R _ g)
+        simp only [HomologicalComplex.sub_f_apply, HomologicalComplex.comp_f,
+          HomologicalComplex.id_f, ModuleCat.hom_sub, ModuleCat.hom_id, ModuleCat.hom_add,
+          ModuleCat.hom_comp, LinearMap.sub_apply, LinearMap.id_apply, LinearMap.add_apply,
+          LinearMap.comp_apply, normalizedCubicalChainComplex_map_f]
+        rw [h₁, h₂]
+        exact (D.boundary_prismChain_add_prismChain_boundary R m g).symm.trans (add_comm _ _))))
+    |>.symm
+
+@[simp]
+theorem retractHomotopy_hom_succ (m : ℕ) (g : NormalizedCubicalChain X R m) :
+    (D.retractHomotopy R).hom m (m + 1) g = -D.prismChain R m g := by
+  simp only [retractHomotopy, Homotopy.symm_hom, Homotopy.equivSubZero, Equiv.coe_fn_symm_mk]
+  rw [Homotopy.mkChainComplex_hom_succ]
+  -- `prismHom` is `prismChain` viewed as a morphism of modules, so this holds by definition.
+  rfl
+
+/-- **The inclusion of `A` induces a chain homotopy equivalence of normalized cubical chains**,
+with the retraction as homotopy inverse. -/
+def normalizedCubicalChainComplexHomotopyEquiv :
+    HomotopyEquiv ((normalizedCubicalChainComplex R).obj (TopCat.of A))
+      ((normalizedCubicalChainComplex R).obj X) where
+  hom := (normalizedCubicalChainComplex R).map (TopCat.ofHom (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal A))
+  inv := D.retractChainMap R
+  homotopyHomInvId := Homotopy.ofEq (D.normalizedCubicalChainComplex_map_comp_retractChainMap R)
+  homotopyInvHomId := (D.retractHomotopy R).symm
+
+@[simp]
+theorem normalizedCubicalChainComplexHomotopyEquiv_hom :
+    (D.normalizedCubicalChainComplexHomotopyEquiv R).hom =
+      (normalizedCubicalChainComplex R).map (TopCat.ofHom (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal A)) :=
+  (rfl)
+
+@[simp]
+theorem normalizedCubicalChainComplexHomotopyEquiv_inv :
+    (D.normalizedCubicalChainComplexHomotopyEquiv R).inv = D.retractChainMap R :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- **The inclusion of `A` induces a quasi-isomorphism of normalized cubical chains.** -/
+theorem quasiIso_normalizedCubicalChainComplex_map (D : SubspaceCubeDeformation A) :
+    QuasiIso ((normalizedCubicalChainComplex R).map (TopCat.ofHom (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal A))) :=
+  inferInstanceAs (QuasiIso (D.normalizedCubicalChainComplexHomotopyEquiv R).hom)
+
+/-- **The inclusion of `A` induces isomorphisms on singular homology**, with coefficients in any
+ring, when the singular cubes of `X` deform into `A`. -/
+theorem isIso_singularHomologyMap (D : SubspaceCubeDeformation A) (n : ℕ) :
+    IsIso (((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) n).obj (ModuleCat.of R R)).map
+      (TopCat.ofHom (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal A))) := by
+  have := D.quasiIso_normalizedCubicalChainComplex_map R
+  exact TopCat.isIso_singularHomologyMap_of_quasiIso _ n

+end SubspaceCubeDeformation
+
+/-- **The inclusion of a subspace with vanishing relative homotopy sets induces isomorphisms on
+singular homology.** If every point of `X` is joined by a path to a point of `A`, and the relative
+homotopy set `π_{n+1}(X, A, a)` is trivial for every `n` and every `a ∈ A`, then the inclusion of
+`A` into `X` induces isomorphisms `H_n(A; R) ≅ H_n(X; R)` for every `n` and every coefficient
+ring `R`. -/
+theorem isIso_singularHomologyMap_subtypeVal_of_relHomotopyGroup {X : TopCat.{u}} {A : Set X}
+    (h₀ : ∀ x : X, ∃ a ∈ A, Joined x a)
+    (h : ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : A), Subsingleton (RelHomotopyGroup (Fin n) ⟨TopPair.ofSubset A, a⟩))
+    (R : Type u) [Ring R] (n : ℕ) :
+    IsIso (((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) n).obj (ModuleCat.of R R)).map
+      (TopCat.ofHom (ContinuousMap.subtypeVal A))) :=
+  (nonempty_subspaceCubeDeformation_of_relHomotopyGroup h₀ h).some.isIso_singularHomologyMap R n
+
+end TauCeti

+/-!
+# Weak homotopy equivalences induce isomorphisms on singular homology
+
+A weak homotopy equivalence `f : X → Y` induces a quasi-isomorphism of normalized cubical singular
+chains, and hence isomorphisms `H_n(X; R) ≅ H_n(Y; R)` on singular homology with coefficients in
+any ring `R` (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Proposition 4.21). No CW structure on `X` or `Y` is
+needed.
+
+The proof factors `f` through its mapping cylinder `M_f` as
+
+  `X ≃ₜ (bottom face of M_f) ↪ M_f → Y`.
+
+* The first map is a homeomorphism (`TauCeti.MappingCylinder.inclHomeomorph`).
+* The last map, the projection, is a homotopy equivalence
+  (`TauCeti.MappingCylinder.homotopyEquiv`), so it induces a chain homotopy equivalence of
+  cubical chains.
+* For the inclusion of the bottom face, every point of `M_f` is joined by a path to the bottom
+  face, and the relative homotopy sets of the pair vanish because `f` is a weak homotopy
+  equivalence
+  (`ContinuousMap.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence.subsingleton_relHomotopyGroup_mappingCylinder`). So
+  the singular cubes of `M_f` deform into the bottom face, and the inclusion induces a chain
+  homotopy equivalence of cubical chains
+  (`TauCeti.isIso_singularHomologyMap_subtypeVal_of_relHomotopyGroup` and the cubical statement
+  behind it).
+
+The singular homology statement is then read off through the comparison of cubical and simplicial
+singular chains.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `ContinuousMap.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence.quasiIso_normalizedCubicalChainComplex_map`: a weak
+  homotopy equivalence induces a quasi-isomorphism of normalized cubical chains.
+* `ContinuousMap.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence.isIso_singularHomologyMap`: a weak homotopy
+  equivalence induces isomorphisms on singular homology.
+
+## References
+
+* A. Hatcher, [*Algebraic Topology*](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf),
+  Section 4.1, Proposition 4.21.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+noncomputable section
+
+open CategoryTheory AlgebraicTopology TauCeti
+
+universe u
+
+namespace ContinuousMap.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence
+
+variable {X Y : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] {f : C(X, Y)}
+  (k : Type u) [Ring k]
+
+/-- **A weak homotopy equivalence induces a quasi-isomorphism of normalized cubical singular
+chains.** -/
+theorem quasiIso_normalizedCubicalChainComplex_map (hf : f.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence) :
+    QuasiIso ((normalizedCubicalChainComplex k).map (TopCat.ofHom f)) := by
+  open MappingCylinder in
+  let A : Set (TopCat.of (MappingCylinder f)) := Set.range (incl f)
+  let ψ : X ≃ₜ A := inclHomeomorph f
+  -- The three factors induce quasi-isomorphisms. The singular cubes of the mapping cylinder
+  -- deform into the bottom face, and the other two factors are homotopy equivalences, whose
+  -- forward maps are `ψ` (by definition) and `proj f`.
+  have D := (nonempty_subspaceCubeDeformation_of_relHomotopyGroup
+    (X := TopCat.of (MappingCylinder f)) (A := A)
+    (exists_mem_range_incl_joined hf.exists_joined)
+    fun n ↦ hf.subsingleton_relHomotopyGroup_mappingCylinder (Fin n)).some
+  have := D.quasiIso_normalizedCubicalChainComplex_map k
+  have : QuasiIso ((normalizedCubicalChainComplex k).map (TopCat.ofHom (ψ : C(X, A)))) :=
+    ψ.toHomotopyEquiv.quasiIso_normalizedCubicalChainComplex_map
+  have : QuasiIso ((normalizedCubicalChainComplex k).map (TopCat.ofHom (proj f))) := by
+    rw [← MappingCylinder.homotopyEquiv_toFun]
+    exact (MappingCylinder.homotopyEquiv f).quasiIso_normalizedCubicalChainComplex_map

+public import TauCeti.AlgebraicTopology.Singular.LocalHomology.Orientation.Basic
+public import TauCeti.Geometry.Manifold.Orientation.Basic

+/-!
+# Local homology generators from oriented charts
+
+An orientation of a positive-dimensional real inner product space canonically selects the
+generator of the reduced homology of its unit sphere: choose any orthonormal basis with that
+orientation and use the basis-dependent sphere computation. The result is independent of the
+choice of basis, is natural under orientation-preserving linear isometries, and changes sign when
+the orientation is reversed.
+
+Composing this generator with the chart computation of local homology gives the local orientation
+selected by an oriented chart. This connects tangent-space orientations with the local homology
+orientations used to construct fundamental classes.
+
+The local generator is the one associated to an oriented coordinate chart in Hatcher's
+*Algebraic Topology*, Section 3.3.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+noncomputable section
+
+open CategoryTheory Limits Metric Module
+open scoped Manifold
+
+universe w v u
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasCoproducts.{w} C] [Abelian C] (R : C)
+
+section Sphere
+
+variable {E : Type w} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
+
+/-- The top-dimensional reduced homology generator of a unit sphere selected by an orientation of
+the ambient inner product space. -/
+def reducedSingularHomologySphereIsoOfOrientation {n : ℕ}
+    (o : Orientation ℝ E (Fin (n + 1))) (hE : finrank ℝ E = n + 1) :
+    (reducedSingularHomologyFunctor R n).obj (TopCat.of (sphere (0 : E) 1)) ≅ R :=
+  reducedSingularHomologySphereIso R (o.finOrthonormalBasis (Nat.succ_pos n) hE)
+
+/-- Any orthonormal basis compatible with `o` computes the sphere generator selected by `o`. -/
+theorem reducedSingularHomologySphereIsoOfOrientation_eq {n : ℕ}
+    (o : Orientation ℝ E (Fin (n + 1))) (hE : finrank ℝ E = n + 1)
+    (b : OrthonormalBasis (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ E) (hb : b.toBasis.orientation = o) :
+    reducedSingularHomologySphereIsoOfOrientation R o hE =
+      reducedSingularHomologySphereIso R b := by
+  apply reducedSingularHomologySphereIso_eq_of_orientation_eq R
+  simpa only [Orientation.finOrthonormalBasis_orientation] using hb.symm
+
+/-- An orientation-preserving linear isometry carries the sphere generator selected by the source
+orientation to the sphere generator selected by the target orientation. -/
+@[reassoc]
+theorem reducedSingularHomologySphereIsoOfOrientation_hom_naturality {F : Type w}
+    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace ℝ F] {n : ℕ}
+    (oE : Orientation ℝ E (Fin (n + 1))) (oF : Orientation ℝ F (Fin (n + 1)))
+    (f : E ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] F) (hf : Orientation.map (Fin (n + 1)) f.toLinearEquiv oE = oF)
+    (hE : finrank ℝ E = n + 1) :
+    let hF : finrank ℝ F = n + 1 := (LinearEquiv.finrank_eq f.toLinearEquiv).symm.trans hE
+    (reducedSingularHomologyFunctor R n).map
+          (TopCat.ofHom ⟨f.toLinearIsometry.unitSphereMap,
+            f.toLinearIsometry.continuous_unitSphereMap⟩) ≫
+        (reducedSingularHomologySphereIsoOfOrientation R oF hF).hom =
+      (reducedSingularHomologySphereIsoOfOrientation R oE hE).hom := by
+  dsimp only
+  let b := oE.finOrthonormalBasis (Nat.succ_pos n) hE
+  let c := b.map f
+  have hc : c.toBasis.orientation = oF := by
+    rw [OrthonormalBasis.toBasis_map, Basis.orientation_map,
+      Orientation.finOrthonormalBasis_orientation, hf]
+  rw [reducedSingularHomologySphereIsoOfOrientation_eq R oE hE b
+      (Orientation.finOrthonormalBasis_orientation _ _ _),
+    reducedSingularHomologySphereIsoOfOrientation_eq R oF
+      ((LinearEquiv.finrank_eq f.toLinearEquiv).symm.trans hE) c hc]
+  exact reducedSingularHomologySphereIso_hom_naturality R b c f.toLinearIsometry (by simp [c])
+
+/-- Reversing the ambient orientation negates the selected sphere generator. -/
+theorem reducedSingularHomologySphereIsoOfOrientation_neg_hom {n : ℕ}
+    (o : Orientation ℝ E (Fin (n + 1))) (hE : finrank ℝ E = n + 1) :
+    (reducedSingularHomologySphereIsoOfOrientation R (-o) hE).hom =
+      -(reducedSingularHomologySphereIsoOfOrientation R o hE).hom := by
+  apply reducedSingularHomologySphereIso_hom_eq_neg_of_orientation_ne R
+  simp only [Orientation.finOrthonormalBasis_orientation]
+  exact Module.Ray.ne_neg_self o
+
+end Sphere
+
+section Chart
+
+variable {M E : Type w} [TopologicalSpace M] [T2Space M]
+  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
+
+/-- The top-degree local homology isomorphism selected by an orientation of the chart model. -/
+def singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation (φ : OpenPartialHomeomorph M E)
+    {x : M} (hx : x ∈ φ.source) {n : ℕ} (o : Orientation ℝ E (Fin (n + 1)))
+    (hE : finrank ℝ E = n + 1) :
+    (TopPair.ofSubset ({x}ᶜ : Set (TopCat.of M))).singularHomology R (n + 1) ≅ R :=
+  singularHomologyComplSingletonIso R φ hx n ≪≫
+    reducedSingularHomologySphereIsoOfOrientation R o hE
+
+/-- The oriented local homology isomorphism is the chart isomorphism followed by the sphere
+generator selected by the chart-model orientation. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation_hom
+    (φ : OpenPartialHomeomorph M E) {x : M} (hx : x ∈ φ.source) {n : ℕ}
+    (o : Orientation ℝ E (Fin (n + 1))) (hE : finrank ℝ E = n + 1) :
+    (singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation R φ hx o hE).hom =
+      (singularHomologyComplSingletonIso R φ hx n).hom ≫
+        (reducedSingularHomologySphereIsoOfOrientation R o hE).hom := by
+  simp only [singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation, Iso.trans_hom]
+
+/-- The inverse oriented local homology isomorphism first selects the oriented sphere generator
+and then carries it into the chart. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation_inv
+    (φ : OpenPartialHomeomorph M E) {x : M} (hx : x ∈ φ.source) {n : ℕ}
+    (o : Orientation ℝ E (Fin (n + 1))) (hE : finrank ℝ E = n + 1) :
+    (singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation R φ hx o hE).inv =
+      (reducedSingularHomologySphereIsoOfOrientation R o hE).inv ≫
+        (singularHomologyComplSingletonIso R φ hx n).inv := by
+  simp only [singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation, Iso.trans_inv]
+
+/-- Reversing the chart-model orientation negates the local homology coordinate map. -/
+theorem singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation_neg_hom
+    (φ : OpenPartialHomeomorph M E) {x : M} (hx : x ∈ φ.source) {n : ℕ}
+    (o : Orientation ℝ E (Fin (n + 1))) (hE : finrank ℝ E = n + 1) :
+    (singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation R φ hx (-o) hE).hom =
+      -(singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation R φ hx o hE).hom := by
+  simp only [singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation, Iso.trans_hom,
+    reducedSingularHomologySphereIsoOfOrientation_neg_hom, Preadditive.comp_neg]
+
+/-- Reversing the chart-model orientation negates the inverse of the local homology coordinate
+map. -/
+theorem singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation_neg_inv
+    (φ : OpenPartialHomeomorph M E) {x : M} (hx : x ∈ φ.source) {n : ℕ}
+    (o : Orientation ℝ E (Fin (n + 1))) (hE : finrank ℝ E = n + 1) :
+    (singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation R φ hx (-o) hE).inv =
+      -(singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation R φ hx o hE).inv := by
+  rw [← cancel_mono (singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation R φ hx o hE).hom]
+  calc
+    (singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation R φ hx (-o) hE).inv ≫
+          (singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation R φ hx o hE).hom =
+        (singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation R φ hx (-o) hE).inv ≫
+          (-(singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation R φ hx (-o) hE).hom) := by
+      rw [singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation_neg_hom, neg_neg]
+    _ = -𝟙 R := by rw [Preadditive.comp_neg, Iso.inv_hom_id]
+    _ = (-(singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation R φ hx o hE).inv) ≫
+          (singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation R φ hx o hE).hom := by
+      rw [Preadditive.neg_comp, Iso.inv_hom_id]
+
+end Chart

+section Integral
+
+variable {M E : Type w} [TopologicalSpace M] [T2Space M]
+  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
+
+/-- The local orientation selected by an oriented chart. -/
+def _root_.OpenPartialHomeomorph.localOrientationOfOrientedChart
+    (φ : OpenPartialHomeomorph M E) {x : M}
+    (hx : x ∈ φ.source) {n : ℕ} (o : Orientation ℝ E (Fin (n + 1)))
+    (hE : finrank ℝ E = n + 1) : LocalOrientation M x (n + 1) :=
+  ⟨(singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation (ModuleCat.of ℤ (ULift.{w} ℤ))
+      φ hx o hE).inv 1,
+    isLocalOrientation_inv_one _⟩
+
+/-- Reversing the chart-model orientation reverses the selected local orientation. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem _root_.OpenPartialHomeomorph.localOrientationOfOrientedChart_neg
+    (φ : OpenPartialHomeomorph M E) {x : M}
+    (hx : x ∈ φ.source) {n : ℕ} (o : Orientation ℝ E (Fin (n + 1)))
+    (hE : finrank ℝ E = n + 1) :
+    φ.localOrientationOfOrientedChart hx (-o) hE =
+      -φ.localOrientationOfOrientedChart hx o hE := by
+  apply Subtype.ext
+  rw [LocalOrientation.coe_neg]
+  exact congrArg (fun f ↦ f 1) (singularHomologyComplSingletonIsoOfOrientation_neg_inv
+    (ModuleCat.of ℤ (ULift.{w} ℤ)) φ hx o hE)
+
+end Integral
+
+section Manifold
+
+variable {M E : Type w} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
+  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [TopologicalSpace M] [T2Space M] [ChartedSpace E M]
+  [IsManifold 𝓘(ℝ, E) 1 M]
+
+/-- The local homology orientation at a point selected by an orientation of a boundaryless
+manifold. The quotient presentation of manifold orientations causes no ambiguity: simultaneously
+reversing the model orientation and every chart sign preserves the signed model orientation in
+the preferred chart. -/
+def localOrientationOfManifoldOrientation {n : ℕ}
+    (o : Manifold.Orientation 𝓘(ℝ, E) M (Fin (n + 1)))
+    (hE : finrank ℝ E = n + 1) (x : M) : LocalOrientation M x (n + 1) :=
+  o.lift
+    (fun l ↦ (chartAt E x).localOrientationOfOrientedChart (mem_chart_source E x)
+      (l.chartOrientation x ⟨x, mem_chart_source E x⟩) hE)
+    (fun l ↦ by
+      have hchart : l.flip.chartOrientation x ⟨x, mem_chart_source E x⟩ =
+          l.chartOrientation x ⟨x, mem_chart_source E x⟩ := by
+        rw [← l.flip.orientationAt_eq x, l.orientationAt_flip, l.orientationAt_eq x]
+      rw [hchart])
+
+/-- The local orientation selected by a represented manifold orientation is the oriented-chart
+generator for its signed model orientation in the preferred chart. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem localOrientationOfManifoldOrientation_mk {n : ℕ}
+    (l : Manifold.OrientationLift 𝓘(ℝ, E) M (Fin (n + 1)))
+    (hE : finrank ℝ E = n + 1) (x : M) :
+    localOrientationOfManifoldOrientation (Manifold.Orientation.mk l) hE x =
+      (chartAt E x).localOrientationOfOrientedChart (mem_chart_source E x)
+        (l.chartOrientation x ⟨x, mem_chart_source E x⟩) hE := by
+  simp only [localOrientationOfManifoldOrientation, Manifold.Orientation.lift_mk]
+
+/-- Reversing a manifold orientation reverses every local homology orientation it selects. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem localOrientationOfManifoldOrientation_neg {n : ℕ}
+    (o : Manifold.Orientation 𝓘(ℝ, E) M (Fin (n + 1)))
+    (hE : finrank ℝ E = n + 1) (x : M) :
+    localOrientationOfManifoldOrientation (-o) hE x =
+      -localOrientationOfManifoldOrientation o hE x := by
+  induction o using Manifold.Orientation.inductionOn with
+  | _ l =>
+      simp only [localOrientationOfManifoldOrientation, Manifold.Orientation.neg_mk,
+        Manifold.Orientation.lift_mk]
+      have hchart : (-l).chartOrientation x ⟨x, mem_chart_source E x⟩ =
+          -l.chartOrientation x ⟨x, mem_chart_source E x⟩ := by
+        rw [← (-l).orientationAt_eq x, l.orientationAt_neg, l.orientationAt_eq x]
+        congr
+      rw [hchart, OpenPartialHomeomorph.localOrientationOfOrientedChart_neg]
+
+end Manifold
+
+end TauCeti

+module

+public import TauCeti.Analysis.Calculus.Morse.Index
+import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.MeanValue
+import TauCeti.Analysis.Calculus.ApproximatesLinearOn
+import TauCeti.Analysis.Matrix.HermitianSignature.Continuity

+/-!
+# Persistence of nondegenerate critical points under small `C²` perturbations
+
+A nondegenerate critical point `x` of `f` survives every sufficiently small `C²` perturbation:
+on each sufficiently small closed ball around `x` there is a threshold `δ > 0` such that every
+function `g` which is `C²` on the ball, whose differential at `x` has norm at most `δ`, and whose
+second derivative stays within `δ` of that of `f` on the ball, has exactly one critical point in
+the ball. That critical point is nondegenerate, its distance to `x` is linearly controlled by
+`‖fderiv ℝ g x‖`, and its critical value differs from `g x` by a quadratic amount in
+`‖fderiv ℝ g x‖`. In finite dimensions its Morse index is that of `x`.
+
+Unlike the continuation theorem
+`TauCeti.IsNondegenerateCriticalPoint.exists_contDiffAt_criticalPoint_continuation`, no
+parametrised family is involved: the perturbation is an arbitrary function, and the size of the
+admissible perturbation is uniform on the chosen ball. A perturbation that is `C²`-close to `f`
+on the ball satisfies the hypotheses, since the differential of `f` vanishes at `x`.
+
+The existence and uniqueness of the perturbed critical point follow from Mathlib's quantitative
+inverse function theorem: on the ball the differential of `g` approximates the invertible Hessian
+of `f` at `x`, so it is injective there and its image contains an explicit ball around
+`fderiv ℝ g x`. The Morse index is preserved because the negative index of a nondegenerate
+symmetric bilinear form is locally constant.
+
+## Main declarations
+
+* `TauCeti.IsNondegenerateCriticalPoint.exists_criticalPoint_perturbation`: in a Banach space, a
+  small perturbation has a unique critical point near `x`; it is nondegenerate, with controlled
+  location and critical value.
+* `TauCeti.IsNondegenerateCriticalPoint.exists_pos_forall_morseIndex_eq`: in finite dimensions,
+  a `C²` function whose Hessian at a point is close to the Hessian of `f` at `x` has the same Morse
+  index there.
+* `TauCeti.IsNondegenerateCriticalPoint.exists_criticalPoint_perturbation_morseIndex_eq`: in
+  finite dimensions the perturbed critical point moreover has the Morse index of `x`.
+
+## References
+
+* M. Audin and M. Damian, *Morse Theory and Floer Homology*, Springer Universitext, 2014,
+  Chapter 1.
+* J. Milnor, *Lectures on the h-cobordism theorem*, Princeton University Press, 1965, §2.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open Filter Metric Set
+open scoped NNReal Topology
+
+namespace TauCeti.IsNondegenerateCriticalPoint
+
+variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] {f : E → ℝ} {x : E}
+
+/-- **Persistence of a nondegenerate critical point under small `C²` perturbations.**
+
+Let `x` be a nondegenerate critical point of `f` on a Banach space. For every sufficiently small
+radius `r` there is `δ > 0` with the following property. If `g` is `C²` at every point of the
+closed ball of radius `r` around `x`, the differential of `g` at `x` has norm at most `δ`, and the
+second derivatives of `g` and `f` differ by at most `δ` on that ball, then `g` has a critical point
+`y` in the ball, and it is the only one there. It is nondegenerate, lies within
+`K * ‖fderiv ℝ g x‖` of `x`, and its critical value differs from `g x` by at most
+`K * ‖fderiv ℝ g x‖ ^ 2`, for a constant `K` depending only on `f` and `x`. -/
+theorem exists_criticalPoint_perturbation [CompleteSpace E]
+    (h : IsNondegenerateCriticalPoint f x) :
+    ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ᶠ r in 𝓝[>] 0, ∃ δ > 0, ∀ g : E → ℝ,
+      (∀ y ∈ closedBall x r, ContDiffAt ℝ 2 g y) →
+      ‖fderiv ℝ g x‖ ≤ δ →
+      (∀ y ∈ closedBall x r,
+        ‖fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ g) y - fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) y‖ ≤ δ) →
+      ∃ y ∈ closedBall x r, IsNondegenerateCriticalPoint g y ∧
+        dist y x ≤ K * ‖fderiv ℝ g x‖ ∧ |g y - g x| ≤ K * ‖fderiv ℝ g x‖ ^ 2 ∧
+        ∀ z ∈ closedBall x r, fderiv ℝ g z = 0 → z = y := by
+  -- On a small ball, `fderiv ℝ g` approximates the invertible Hessian `L` of `f` at `x`, so it
+  -- has a unique zero there; the remaining estimates are read off on the smaller ball of radius
+  -- `2 * C * ‖fderiv ℝ g x‖` containing that zero.
+  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ := h.isInvertible
+  -- `C` bounds the inverse of the Hessian `L` and is positive even on the zero space.
+  let C : ℝ := ‖(L.symm : (E →L[ℝ] ℝ) →L[ℝ] E)‖ + 1
+  have hC : 0 < C := by positivity
+  have hLsymm : ‖(L.symm : (E →L[ℝ] ℝ) →L[ℝ] E)‖ ≤ C := le_add_of_nonneg_right zero_le_one
+  obtain ⟨ε₀, hε₀, hinv⟩ := Metric.eventually_nhds_iff.1 h.isInvertible.eventually_nhds
+  -- `κ` is the admissible distance from the Hessian `L` on the ball.
+  let κ : ℝ := min (2 * C)⁻¹ (ε₀ / 2)
+  have hκ : 0 < κ := by positivity
+  have hκC : 2 * C * κ ≤ 1 :=
+    calc 2 * C * κ ≤ 2 * C * (2 * C)⁻¹ := by gcongr; exact min_le_left _ _
+      _ = 1 := mul_inv_cancel₀ (by positivity)
+  have hκε₀ : κ < ε₀ := (min_le_right _ _).trans_lt (half_lt_self hε₀)
+  have hcont : ContinuousAt (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f)) x :=
+    (h.contDiffAt.fderiv_right (m := 1) (by norm_num)).continuousAt_fderiv (by norm_num)
+  obtain ⟨ρ, hρ, hρf⟩ := Metric.eventually_nhds_iff.1
+    (hcont.eventually_mem (Metric.ball_mem_nhds (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x) (half_pos hκ)))
+  let K : ℝ := 2 * C + 8 * (‖(L : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ)‖ + κ) * C ^ 2
+  refine ⟨K, ?_⟩
+  filter_upwards [Ioo_mem_nhdsGT hρ] with r hr
+  refine ⟨min (κ / 2) (r / (2 * C)), by have := hr.1; positivity, fun g hg hgx hgf ↦ ?_⟩
+  have hdiff : ∀ y ∈ closedBall x r, DifferentiableAt ℝ (fderiv ℝ g) y := fun y hy ↦
+    ((hg y hy).fderiv_right (m := 1) (by norm_num)).differentiableAt (by norm_num)
+  -- On the ball the second derivative of `g` stays within `κ` of `L`.
+  have hclose : ∀ y ∈ closedBall x r,
+      ‖fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ g) y - (L : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ)‖ ≤ κ := fun y hy ↦ by
+    have hfy : ‖fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) y - (L : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ)‖ < κ / 2 := by
+      rw [hL]
+      exact (mem_ball_iff_norm (E := E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ)).1 <|
+        hρf (lt_of_le_of_lt (mem_closedBall.1 hy) hr.2)
+    calc ‖fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ g) y - (L : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ)‖
+        ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ g) y - fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) y‖ +
+            ‖fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) y - (L : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ)‖ :=
+          norm_sub_le_norm_sub_add_norm_sub (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ g) y)
+            (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) y) (L : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ)
+      _ ≤ κ / 2 + κ / 2 := add_le_add ((hgf y hy).trans (min_le_left _ _)) hfy.le
+      _ = κ := add_halves _
+  have happrox : ApproximatesLinearOn (fderiv ℝ g) (L : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ)
+      (closedBall x r) ⟨κ, hκ.le⟩ := fun y hy z hz ↦
+    (convex_closedBall x r).norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le' hdiff hclose hz hy
+  set n := ‖fderiv ℝ g x‖
+  have hεr : 2 * C * n ≤ r := by
+    have : n ≤ r / (2 * C) := hgx.trans (min_le_right _ _)
+    rwa [le_div_iff₀ (by positivity), mul_comm] at this
+  obtain ⟨y, hyε, hy0, huniq⟩ := happrox.exists_eq_zero_of_two_mul_norm_le hC hLsymm hκC hεr
+  have hsub : closedBall x (2 * C * n) ⊆ closedBall x r := closedBall_subset_closedBall hεr
+  have hKC : 2 * C ≤ K := by
+    have : 0 ≤ 8 * (‖(L : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ)‖ + κ) * C ^ 2 := by positivity
+    linarith
+  refine ⟨y, hsub hyε, ⟨hg y (hsub hyε), hy0, hinv ?_⟩, ?_, ?_, huniq⟩
+  · -- Nondegeneracy: the Hessian of `g` at `y` is within `κ < ε₀` of `L`.
+    rw [← hL]
+    exact (dist_eq_norm (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ g) y) (L : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ)).trans_lt
+      ((hclose y (hsub hyε)).trans_lt hκε₀)
+  · calc dist y x ≤ 2 * C * n := mem_closedBall.1 hyε
+      _ ≤ K * n := by gcongr
+  · -- Value: near `y` the differential of `g` is bounded by `(‖L‖ + κ)` times the distance to `y`.
+    let M : ℝ := ‖(L : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ)‖ + κ
+    have hbound : ∀ w ∈ closedBall x (2 * C * n), ‖fderiv ℝ g w‖ ≤ M * (2 * (2 * C * n)) :=
+      fun w hw ↦ by
+        have hlip := happrox.lipschitzWith.dist_le_mul ⟨w, hsub hw⟩ ⟨y, hsub hyε⟩
+        simp only [domRestrict_apply, hy0, dist_zero_right, Subtype.dist_eq] at hlip
+        calc ‖fderiv ℝ g w‖ ≤ M * dist w y := hlip
+          _ ≤ M * (2 * (2 * C * n)) := by
+            gcongr
+            linarith [dist_triangle_right w y x, mem_closedBall.1 hw, mem_closedBall.1 hyε]
+    have hval := (convex_closedBall x (2 * C * n)).norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le
+      (fun w hw ↦ ((hg w (hsub hw)).differentiableAt (by norm_num))) hbound
+      (mem_closedBall_self (by positivity)) hyε
+    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, ← dist_eq_norm] at hval
+    calc |g y - g x| ≤ M * (2 * (2 * C * n)) * dist y x := hval
+      _ ≤ M * (2 * (2 * C * n)) * (2 * C * n) := by gcongr; exact mem_closedBall.1 hyε
+      _ = (8 * M * C ^ 2) * n ^ 2 := by ring
+      _ ≤ K * n ^ 2 := by gcongr; linarith
+
+/-- **The Morse index is stable under small changes of the Hessian.**
+
+In finite dimensions, there is `ε > 0` such that every function `g` which is `C²` at a point `y`
+and whose Hessian at `y` is within `ε` of the Hessian of `f` at the nondegenerate critical point
+`x` has the Morse index of `f` at `x`. The point `y` need not be critical. -/
+theorem exists_pos_forall_morseIndex_eq [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
+    (h : IsNondegenerateCriticalPoint f x) :
+    ∃ ε > 0, ∀ ⦃g : E → ℝ⦄ ⦃y : E⦄, ContDiffAt ℝ 2 g y →
+      ‖fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ g) y - fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x‖ < ε →
+        morseIndex g y = morseIndex f x := by
+  have hsymm {g : E → ℝ} {y : E} (hg : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 g y) :
+      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ g) y).toBilinForm.IsSymm :=
+    ⟨hg.isSymmSndFDerivAt (by simp)⟩
+  have hmorse (g : E → ℝ) (y : E) :
+      morseIndex g y = sigNeg (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ g) y).toBilinForm.toQuadraticMap := by
+    rw [morseIndex_def]
+    congr 1
+    ext v
+    rw [LinearMap.BilinMap.toQuadraticMap_apply, hessianQuadraticForm_apply,
+      ContinuousLinearMap.toBilinForm_apply]
+  -- The negative index is locally constant on the space of symmetric forms.
+  let a : {B : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ // B.toBilinForm.IsSymm} :=
+    ⟨fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x, hsymm h.contDiffAt⟩
+  have hnd : a.1.toBilinForm.Nondegenerate :=
+    LinearMap.BilinForm.Nondegenerate.ofSeparatingLeft h.separatingLeft
+  obtain ⟨ε, hε, hball⟩ := Metric.eventually_nhds_iff
+    (α := {B : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ // B.toBilinForm.IsSymm}) |>.1
+    (ContinuousLinearMap.eventually_sigNeg_toBilinForm_eq_of_continuousAt (V := Subtype.val)
+      (Eventually.of_forall fun B ↦ B.2) continuous_subtype_val.continuousAt hnd)
+  refine ⟨ε, hε, fun g y hg hlt ↦ ?_⟩
+  rw [hmorse, hmorse f x]
+  refine hball (y := ⟨_, hsymm hg⟩) ?_
+  rw [Subtype.dist_eq]
+  exact (dist_eq_norm (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ g) y) (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x)).trans_lt hlt
+
+/-- **Persistence of a nondegenerate critical point with its Morse index.**
+
+In finite dimensions, the unique critical point of a small `C²` perturbation provided by
+`exists_criticalPoint_perturbation` moreover has the Morse index of `f` at `x`. -/
+theorem exists_criticalPoint_perturbation_morseIndex_eq [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
+    (h : IsNondegenerateCriticalPoint f x) :
+    ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ᶠ r in 𝓝[>] 0, ∃ δ > 0, ∀ g : E → ℝ,
+      (∀ y ∈ closedBall x r, ContDiffAt ℝ 2 g y) →
+      ‖fderiv ℝ g x‖ ≤ δ →
+      (∀ y ∈ closedBall x r,
+        ‖fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ g) y - fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) y‖ ≤ δ) →
+      ∃ y ∈ closedBall x r, IsNondegenerateCriticalPoint g y ∧
+        morseIndex g y = morseIndex f x ∧
+        dist y x ≤ K * ‖fderiv ℝ g x‖ ∧ |g y - g x| ≤ K * ‖fderiv ℝ g x‖ ^ 2 ∧
+        ∀ z ∈ closedBall x r, fderiv ℝ g z = 0 → z = y := by
+  obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ := h.exists_criticalPoint_perturbation
+  obtain ⟨ε, hε, hindex⟩ := h.exists_pos_forall_morseIndex_eq
+  have hcont : ContinuousAt (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f)) x :=
+    (h.contDiffAt.fderiv_right (m := 1) (by norm_num)).continuousAt_fderiv (by norm_num)
+  obtain ⟨ρ, hρ, hρf⟩ := Metric.eventually_nhds_iff.1
+    (hcont.eventually_mem (Metric.ball_mem_nhds (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x) (half_pos hε)))
+  refine ⟨K, ?_⟩
+  filter_upwards [hK, Ioo_mem_nhdsGT hρ] with r ⟨δ, hδ, hr⟩ hrρ
+  refine ⟨min δ (ε / 2), by positivity, fun g hg hgx hgf ↦ ?_⟩
+  obtain ⟨y, hy, hnd, hdist, hval, huniq⟩ := hr g hg (hgx.trans (min_le_left _ _))
+    fun y hy ↦ (hgf y hy).trans (min_le_left _ _)
+  refine ⟨y, hy, hnd, hindex (hg y hy) ?_, hdist, hval, huniq⟩
+  have hfy : ‖fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) y - fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x‖ < ε / 2 := by
+    exact (mem_ball_iff_norm (E := E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ)).1 <|
+      hρf (lt_of_le_of_lt (mem_closedBall.1 hy) hrρ.2)
+  calc ‖fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ g) y - fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x‖
+      ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ g) y - fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) y‖ +
+          ‖fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) y - fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x‖ :=
+        norm_sub_le_norm_sub_add_norm_sub (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ g) y) (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) y)
+          (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x)
+    _ < ε / 2 + ε / 2 := add_lt_add_of_le_of_lt ((hgf y hy).trans (min_le_right _ _)) hfy
+    _ = ε := add_halves _
+
+end TauCeti.IsNondegenerateCriticalPoint

+module
+
+public import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Defs
+public import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.UpperHalfPlane.Basic
+public import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Basic
+
+import TauCeti.Analysis.Complex.Conformal.Jordan.Unbounded.BoundaryPrevertex
+import TauCeti.Analysis.Complex.Conformal.LocalFrontier
+import TauCeti.Analysis.Complex.Conformal.Reflection.Principle
+import TauCeti.Analysis.Complex.UpperHalfPlane.Topology
+
+/-!
+# Ends at infinity of an inverted coordinate
+
+Let `f` be a conformal map of the upper half-plane onto an unbounded domain with several accesses
+to infinity, and let `g = (f - q)⁻¹` be its inverted coordinate, continuous on the closed upper
+half-plane.  The real zeros of `g` are the boundary parameters at which `f` tends to infinity.
+
+This file describes the boundary behaviour of `f` at such a zero `x`.  First, if far out the domain
+is covered by pairwise disjoint open ends, then `f` maps a whole upper half-disc about `x` into a
+single one of them.  Second, if that end is an open half-strip contained in the domain, between
+two parallel sides, then the exponential coordinate `exp ((f - c) / b)` of the half-strip, for
+suitable constants `c` and `b`, extends continuously and injectively across `x` with value `0`
+there, has real boundary values, and carries the upper half-disc into the upper half-plane.  These
+are the local conditions at a vertex at infinity of opening `0` in the Schwarz--Christoffel formula
+`TauCeti.eqOn_const_mul_schwarzChristoffelPrimitive_add_of_polygonal_boundary`, so they apply to
+polygonal domains, such as strips, with several parallel-sided ends.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `TauCeti.exists_eventually_mem_of_inverted_coordinate_eq_zero`: near a zero of the inverted
+  coordinate, `f` takes values in a single end.
+* `TauCeti.exists_ball_halfStrip_end_of_inverted_coordinate`: at a zero of the inverted coordinate
+  whose end is a half-strip, the exponential coordinate of that half-strip satisfies the local
+  conditions at a parallel-sided vertex at infinity.
+
+## References
+
+* C. Carathéodory, Über die gegenseitige Beziehung der Ränder bei der konformen Abbildung,
+  Math. Ann. 73 (1913).
+* Ch. Pommerenke, *Boundary Behaviour of Conformal Maps*, Springer, 1992, Ch. 2.
+* T. Driscoll and L. Trefethen, *Schwarz--Christoffel Mapping*, Ch. 2.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open Bornology Complex Filter Function Metric Set Topology UpperHalfPlane
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+variable {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {q : ℂ}
+
+/-- On the upper half-plane the map is recovered from its inverted coordinate. -/
+private theorem eq_add_inv_of_inverted_coordinate
+    (hgf : EqOn g (fun z => (f z - q)⁻¹) upperHalfPlaneSet) {z : ℂ}
+    (hz : z ∈ upperHalfPlaneSet) : f z = q + (g z)⁻¹ := by
+  rw [hgf hz, inv_inv, add_sub_cancel]
+
+/-- **Each access to infinity lies in one end.**  Let `g = (f - q)⁻¹` be the inverted coordinate
+of a map `f` of the upper half-plane into `U`, continuous on the closed upper half-plane and
+nonzero in its interior, and let `x` be a real zero of `g`.  If far out `U` is covered by pairwise
+disjoint open sets `E i`, then near `x` the map `f` takes its values in the upper half-plane in a
+single one of them. -/
+theorem exists_eventually_mem_of_inverted_coordinate_eq_zero {ι : Type*} {U : Set ℂ}
+    {E : ι → Set ℂ} {x R : ℝ} (hgc : ContinuousOn g {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ z.im})
+    (hgf : EqOn g (fun z => (f z - q)⁻¹) upperHalfPlaneSet)
+    (hgne : ∀ z ∈ upperHalfPlaneSet, g z ≠ 0) (hx : g x = 0) (hfU : MapsTo f upperHalfPlaneSet U)
+    (hEo : ∀ i, IsOpen (E i)) (hEd : Pairwise (Disjoint on E))
+    (hE : ∀ w ∈ U, R < ‖w‖ → ∃ i, w ∈ E i) :
+    ∃ i, ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[upperHalfPlaneSet] (x : ℂ), f z ∈ E i := by
+  -- near `x` the map is far out, on a preconnected upper half-disc
+  have hf : Tendsto f (𝓝[upperHalfPlaneSet] (x : ℂ)) (cobounded ℂ) :=
+    tendsto_cobounded_of_inverted_boundary_eq_zero (hgc _ (by simp)) hgf hgne hx
+  obtain ⟨r, hr, hfar⟩ := Metric.mem_nhdsWithin_iff.mp
+    ((tendsto_norm_cobounded_atTop.comp hf).eventually_gt_atTop R)
+  set A := ball (x : ℂ) r ∩ upperHalfPlaneSet
+  have hfc : ContinuousOn f upperHalfPlaneSet :=
+    (continuousOn_const.add ((hgc.mono (ofPred_subset_ofPred.mpr fun _ => le_of_lt)).inv₀
+      hgne)).congr fun z hz => eq_add_inv_of_inverted_coordinate hgf hz
+  have hA : IsPreconnected (f '' A) :=
+    ((convex_ball _ _).inter (convex_halfSpace_im_gt 0)).isPreconnected.image _
+      (hfc.mono inter_subset_right)
+  have hcover (z : ℂ) (hz : z ∈ A) : ∃ i, f z ∈ E i :=
