+/-!
+# Dirichlet polygons of Fuchsian groups with cusps
+
+Let `Γ ≤ PSL(2, ℝ)` be discrete. If the Dirichlet domain of `Γ` centred at `p` becomes bounded
+after removing finitely many cusp horodiscs, then it is the carrier of a convex polygon, possibly
+with ideal vertices, and every ideal vertex is the point of one of the cusp data
+(`Subgroup.exists_convexPolygon_carrier_eq_dirichletDomain_of_isBounded_truncation`). The sides of
+such a polygon are Dirichlet faces, by `ConvexPolygon.exists_side_eq_dirichletFace`, and for a
+centre with trivial stabilizer it has a unique side pairing by elements of `Γ`, by
+`ConvexPolygon.existsUnique_sidePairing_of_carrier_eq_dirichletDomain`.
+
+Since a Dirichlet domain meets every orbit, the cusp compactification of `Γ` is then compact as
+soon as `Γ` has finitely many cusp orbits
+(`Subgroup.compactSpace_compactifiedQuotient_of_isBounded_truncation`).
+
+## References
+
+* Alan Beardon, *The Geometry of Discrete Groups*, §9.4.
+* Svetlana Katok, *Fuchsian Groups*, §§3.2 and 4.2.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open Set UpperHalfPlane TauCeti TauCeti.UpperHalfPlane MulAction
+open scoped MatrixGroups OnePoint

+namespace Subgroup
+
+variable (Γ : Subgroup PSL(2, ℝ)) [DiscreteTopology Γ] {ι : Type*} [Finite ι]
+
+/-- **Dirichlet polygons with cusps.** If the Dirichlet domain of a discrete subgroup `Γ` centred
+at `p` is bounded after removing finitely many cusp horodiscs of positive heights, it is the
+carrier of a convex polygon, possibly with ideal vertices. Each ideal vertex is the cusp point of
+one of the cusp data. -/
+theorem exists_convexPolygon_carrier_eq_dirichletDomain_of_isBounded_truncation (p : ℍ)
+    (D : ι → Γ.CuspDatum) {A : ι → ℝ} (hA : ∀ i, 0 < A i)
+    (hb : Bornology.IsBounded (dirichletDomain Γ p \ ⋃ i, (D i).horodisc (A i))) :
+    ∃ (n : ℕ) (_ : NeZero n) (P : ConvexPolygon n), P.carrier = dirichletDomain Γ p ∧
+      ∀ i c, P.vertex i = .inr c → ∃ j, (D j).cusp = c := by
+  obtain ⟨s, hmove, hD⟩ :=
+    Γ.exists_finset_dirichletDomain_eq_iInter_closure_leftHalfPlane_of_isBounded_truncation
+      p D hA hb
+  -- the centre lies strictly inside every bisector half-plane
+  have hint :
+      (interior (⋂ g ∈ s, _root_.closure (leftHalfPlane (perpBisector p (g • p))))).Nonempty := by
+    refine ⟨p, ?_⟩
+    simp only [Finset.interior_iInter, interior_closure_leftHalfPlane, mem_iInter₂]
+    intro g hg
+    rw [mem_leftHalfPlane_perpBisector_iff (hmove g hg), dist_self]
+    exact dist_pos.2 (hmove g hg)
+  have hH (i : ι) : (D i).horodisc (A i) = {z : ℍ | A i < ((D i).scaling • z).im} :=
+    Set.ext fun _ ↦ TauCeti.Subgroup.CuspDatum.mem_horodisc _
+  simp_rw [hH, hD] at hb
+  obtain ⟨n, _, P, hP, -, hcusp⟩ := exists_convexPolygon_carrier_eq_iInter_closure_leftHalfPlane
+    s (fun g ↦ perpBisector p (g • p)) hint (fun i ↦ (D i).scaling) hA hb
+  refine ⟨n, inferInstance, P, hP.trans hD.symm, fun i c hi ↦ ?_⟩
+  obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hcusp i c hi

+/-- **Compactness from a Dirichlet domain with a bounded cusp truncation.** If a discrete
+subgroup `Γ` has finitely many cusp orbits, and some Dirichlet domain of `Γ` is bounded after
+removing finitely many cusp horodiscs of positive heights, then the quotient `Γ \ ℍ` with its cusp
+orbits adjoined is compact. -/

+    (D : ι → Γ.CuspDatum) {A : ι → ℝ} (hA : ∀ i, 0 < A i)
+    (hb : Bornology.IsBounded (dirichletDomain Γ p \ ⋃ i, (D i).horodisc (A i))) :
+    CompactSpace Γ.CompactifiedQuotient := by
+  obtain ⟨n, _, P, hP, hcusp⟩ :=
+    Γ.exists_convexPolygon_carrier_eq_dirichletDomain_of_isBounded_truncation p D hA hb
+  refine P.compactSpace_compactifiedQuotient (fun q ↦ ?_) fun i c hi ↦ ?_
+  · obtain ⟨z, rfl⟩ := Quotient.mk_surjective q
+    obtain ⟨γ, hγ⟩ := exists_smul_mem_dirichletDomain (G := Γ) p z
+    exact ⟨γ • z, hP ▸ hγ, Quotient.sound ⟨γ, rfl⟩⟩
+  · obtain ⟨j, rfl⟩ := hcusp i c hi
+    exact (D j).isCuspPoint
+
+end Subgroup

+private theorem faceStart_eq_inr (h : ¬BddBelow (geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K)) :
+    faceStart g K = .inr (g • ((0 : ℝ) : OnePoint ℝ)) :=
+  ite_eq_right h
+
+private theorem faceEnd_eq_inr (h : ¬BddAbove (geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K)) :
+    faceEnd g K = .inr (g • (∞ : OnePoint ℝ)) :=
+  ite_eq_right h
+
+private theorem exists_of_faceStart_eq_inl (hS : IsClosed (geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K))
+    (hne : (geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K).Nonempty) {z : ℍ} (h : faceStart g K = .inl z) :
+    ∃ a, geodesicLine g a ∈ K ∧ geodesicLine g a = z ∧ ∀ σ, geodesicLine g σ ∈ K → a ≤ σ := by
+  by_cases hb : BddBelow (geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K)
+  · rw [faceStart, ite_eq_left hb, Sum.inl.injEq] at h
+    exact ⟨_, hS.csInf_mem hne hb, h, fun σ hσ ↦ csInf_le hb hσ⟩
+  · rw [faceStart_eq_inr hb] at h
+    exact absurd h Sum.inr_ne_inl
+
+private theorem exists_of_faceEnd_eq_inl (hS : IsClosed (geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K))
+    (hne : (geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K).Nonempty) {w : ℍ} (h : faceEnd g K = .inl w) :
+    ∃ b, geodesicLine g b ∈ K ∧ geodesicLine g b = w ∧ ∀ σ, geodesicLine g σ ∈ K → σ ≤ b := by
+  by_cases hb : BddAbove (geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K)
+  · rw [faceEnd, ite_eq_left hb, Sum.inl.injEq] at h
+    exact ⟨_, hS.csSup_mem hne hb, h, fun σ hσ ↦ le_csSup hb hσ⟩
+  · rw [faceEnd_eq_inr hb] at h
+    exact absurd h Sum.inr_ne_inl
+
+private theorem of_faceStart_eq_inr {ξ : OnePoint ℝ} (h : faceStart g K = .inr ξ) :
+    g • ((0 : ℝ) : OnePoint ℝ) = ξ ∧ ¬BddBelow (geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K) := by
+  by_cases hb : BddBelow (geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K)
+  · rw [faceStart, ite_eq_left hb] at h
+    exact absurd h Sum.inl_ne_inr
+  · rw [faceStart_eq_inr hb, Sum.inr.injEq] at h
+    exact ⟨h, hb⟩
+
+private theorem of_faceEnd_eq_inr {η : OnePoint ℝ} (h : faceEnd g K = .inr η) :
+    g • (∞ : OnePoint ℝ) = η ∧ ¬BddAbove (geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K) := by
+  by_cases hb : BddAbove (geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K)
+  · rw [faceEnd, ite_eq_left hb] at h
+    exact absurd h Sum.inl_ne_inr
+  · rw [faceEnd_eq_inr hb, Sum.inr.injEq] at h
+    exact ⟨h, hb⟩
+
+/-- A point of a face is its start, its end, or lies strictly between two other points of it. -/
+private theorem faceStart_eq_or_faceEnd_eq_or_exists {τ : ℝ} (hτ : geodesicLine g τ ∈ K) :
+    faceStart g K = .inl (geodesicLine g τ) ∨ faceEnd g K = .inl (geodesicLine g τ) ∨
+      ∃ σ₁ σ₂, σ₁ < τ ∧ τ < σ₂ ∧ geodesicLine g σ₁ ∈ K ∧ geodesicLine g σ₂ ∈ K := by
+  by_cases h₁ : ∃ σ₁, σ₁ < τ ∧ geodesicLine g σ₁ ∈ K
+  · by_cases h₂ : ∃ σ₂, τ < σ₂ ∧ geodesicLine g σ₂ ∈ K
+    · obtain ⟨σ₁, hσ₁, h₁⟩ := h₁
+      obtain ⟨σ₂, hσ₂, h₂⟩ := h₂
+      exact Or.inr (Or.inr ⟨σ₁, σ₂, hσ₁, hσ₂, h₁, h₂⟩)
+    · push Not at h₂
+      exact Or.inr (Or.inl (faceEnd_eq_inl hτ fun σ hσ ↦ le_of_not_gt fun h ↦ h₂ σ h hσ))
+  · push Not at h₁
+    exact Or.inl (faceStart_eq_inl hτ fun σ hσ ↦ le_of_not_gt fun h ↦ h₁ σ h hσ)
+
+/-- A face with two distinct points runs from its start to its end. -/
+private theorem isGeodesicFromTo_faceStart_faceEnd {σ₁ σ₂ : ℝ} (h₁ : geodesicLine g σ₁ ∈ K)
+    (h₂ : geodesicLine g σ₂ ∈ K) (h₁₂ : σ₁ < σ₂) :
+    IsGeodesicFromTo g (faceStart g K) (faceEnd g K) := by
+  by_cases hb : BddBelow (geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K) <;> by_cases hb' : BddAbove (geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K)
+  · rw [faceStart, ite_eq_left hb, faceEnd, ite_eq_left hb']
+    exact isGeodesicFromTo_inl_inl.2
+      ⟨_, _, ((csInf_le hb h₁).trans_lt h₁₂).trans_le (le_csSup hb' h₂), rfl, rfl⟩
+  · rw [faceStart, ite_eq_left hb, faceEnd_eq_inr hb']
+    exact isGeodesicFromTo_inl_inr.2 ⟨mem_range_self _, rfl⟩
+  · rw [faceStart_eq_inr hb, faceEnd, ite_eq_left hb']
+    exact isGeodesicFromTo_inr_inl.2 ⟨rfl, mem_range_self _⟩
+  · rw [faceStart_eq_inr hb, faceEnd_eq_inr hb']
+    exact isGeodesicFromTo_inr_inr.2 ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
+
+/-- A nonempty face with closed order-connected parameters is the extended geodesic segment from
+its start to its end. -/
+private theorem inter_range_eq_extGeodesicSegment (hS : IsClosed (geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K))
+    (hoc : (geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K).OrdConnected) (hne : (geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K).Nonempty) :
+    K ∩ range (geodesicLine g) = extGeodesicSegment (faceStart g K) (faceEnd g K) := by
+  rw [← image_preimage_eq_inter_range]
+  by_cases hb : BddBelow (geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K) ∧ BddAbove (geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K)
+  · obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hne
+    rw [faceStart, ite_eq_left hb.1, faceEnd, ite_eq_left hb.2, extGeodesicSegment_inl_inl,
+      geodesicSegment_geodesicLine, uIcc_of_le ((csInf_le hb.1 ha).trans (le_csSup hb.2 ha))]
+    congr 1
+    exact Subset.antisymm (fun σ hσ ↦ ⟨csInf_le hb.1 hσ, le_csSup hb.2 hσ⟩)
+      (hoc.out (hS.csInf_mem ⟨a, ha⟩ hb.1) (hS.csSup_mem ⟨a, ha⟩ hb.2))
+  rcases hoc.eq_Ici_or_eq_Iic_or_eq_univ hne hS hb with ⟨a, h⟩ | ⟨b, h⟩ | h
+  · rw [faceStart, faceEnd, h, ite_eq_left bddBelow_Ici, ite_eq_right (not_bddAbove_Ici a),
+      csInf_Ici, geodesicLine_image_Ici]
+  · rw [faceStart, faceEnd, h, ite_eq_right (not_bddBelow_Iic b), ite_eq_left bddAbove_Iic,
+      csSup_Iic, geodesicLine_image_Iic]
+  · rw [faceStart, faceEnd, h, ite_eq_right not_bddBelow_univ, ite_eq_right not_bddAbove_univ,
+      image_univ, range_geodesicLine_eq_extGeodesicSegment]
+
+private theorem faceStart_mul_smul (h : PSL(2, ℝ)) :
+    faceStart (h * g) (h • K) = h • faceStart g K := by
+  have hS : geodesicLine (h * g) ⁻¹' (h • K) = geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K := by
+    ext t
+    rw [mem_preimage, mem_preimage, ← smul_geodesicLine, smul_mem_smul_set_iff]
+  by_cases hb : BddBelow (geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K)
+  · rw [faceStart, faceStart, hS, ite_eq_left hb, ite_eq_left hb, Sum.smul_inl,
+      smul_geodesicLine]
+  · rw [faceStart_eq_inr (hS ▸ hb), faceStart_eq_inr hb, Sum.smul_inr, mul_smul]
+
+private theorem faceEnd_mul_smul (h : PSL(2, ℝ)) :
+    faceEnd (h * g) (h • K) = h • faceEnd g K := by
+  have hS : geodesicLine (h * g) ⁻¹' (h • K) = geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K := by
+    ext t
+    rw [mem_preimage, mem_preimage, ← smul_geodesicLine, smul_mem_smul_set_iff]
+  by_cases hb : BddAbove (geodesicLine g ⁻¹' K)
+  · rw [faceEnd, faceEnd, hS, ite_eq_left hb, ite_eq_left hb, Sum.smul_inl, smul_geodesicLine]
+  · rw [faceEnd_eq_inr (hS ▸ hb), faceEnd_eq_inr hb, Sum.smul_inr, mul_smul]
+
+end FaceEndpoints
+
+/-! ### Geodesic lines seen from `∞` -/
+
+section Infinity
+
+/-- Seen from `∞`, a geodesic line is a vertical line running down from `∞` or up to `∞`, or a
+semicircle with `∞` on its left, or a semicircle whose right half-plane contains all sufficiently
+high points. -/
+private theorem smul_eq_infty_or_or_eventually (g : PSL(2, ℝ)) :
+    g • ((0 : ℝ) : OnePoint ℝ) = ∞ ∨ g • (∞ : OnePoint ℝ) = ∞ ∨
+      (∞ : OnePoint ℝ) ∈ boundaryLeftHalfPlane g ∨ ∀ᶠ z in atImInfty, z ∈ rightHalfPlane g := by
+  by_cases h₀ : g • ((0 : ℝ) : OnePoint ℝ) = ∞
+  · exact Or.inl h₀
+  by_cases h₁ : g • (∞ : OnePoint ℝ) = ∞
+  · exact Or.inr (Or.inl h₁)
+  obtain ⟨e₀, he₀⟩ := OnePoint.ne_infty_iff_exists.1 h₀
+  obtain ⟨e₁, he₁⟩ := OnePoint.ne_infty_iff_exists.1 h₁
+  have hne : e₀ ≠ e₁ := fun h ↦ OnePoint.coe_ne_infty (0 : ℝ)
+    (MulAction.injective g (show g • ((0 : ℝ) : OnePoint ℝ) = g • ∞ by rw [← he₀, ← he₁, h]))
+  rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hne with h | h
+  · exact Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl ((infty_mem_boundaryLeftHalfPlane_iff he₀.symm he₁.symm).2 h)))
+  -- reversing the orientation puts `∞` on the left
+  refine Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr ?_))
+  rw [← leftHalfPlane_mul_pslS]
+  refine eventually_mem_leftHalfPlane_of_infty_mem_boundaryLeftHalfPlane
+    ((infty_mem_boundaryLeftHalfPlane_iff (e₀ := e₁) (e₁ := e₀) ?_ ?_).2 h)
+  · rw [mul_smul, pslS_smul_zero, he₁]
+  · rw [mul_smul, pslS_smul_infty, he₀]
+
+/-- A geodesic line running up to `∞` is a vertical line with side form `Re z - e`. -/
+private theorem exists_sideForm_eq_re_sub {g : PSL(2, ℝ)} (hg : g • (∞ : OnePoint ℝ) = ∞) :
+    ∃ e : ℝ, ∀ z : ℂ, sideForm g z = z.re - e := by
+  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := OnePoint.ne_infty_iff_exists.1 fun h₀ : g • ((0 : ℝ) : OnePoint ℝ) = ∞ ↦
+    OnePoint.coe_ne_infty (0 : ℝ) (MulAction.injective g (h₀.trans hg.symm))
+  exact ⟨e, sideForm_eq_of_smul_infty_eq_infty he.symm hg⟩
+
+/-- A geodesic line running down from `∞` is a vertical line with side form `e - Re z`. -/
+private theorem exists_sideForm_eq_sub_re {g : PSL(2, ℝ)}
+    (hg : g • ((0 : ℝ) : OnePoint ℝ) = ∞) : ∃ e : ℝ, ∀ z : ℂ, sideForm g z = e - z.re := by
+  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := OnePoint.ne_infty_iff_exists.1 fun h₁ : g • (∞ : OnePoint ℝ) = ∞ ↦
+    OnePoint.coe_ne_infty (0 : ℝ) (MulAction.injective g (hg.trans h₁.symm))
+  exact ⟨e, sideForm_eq_of_smul_zero_eq_infty hg he.symm⟩
+
+/-- The side form of a vertical geodesic line depends only on the real part. -/
+private theorem sideForm_eq_of_re_eq {g : PSL(2, ℝ)}
+    (hg : g • ((0 : ℝ) : OnePoint ℝ) = ∞ ∨ g • (∞ : OnePoint ℝ) = ∞) {z w : ℂ}
+    (h : z.re = w.re) : sideForm g z = sideForm g w := by
+  rcases hg with h₀ | h₁
+  · obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := exists_sideForm_eq_sub_re h₀
+    rw [he, he, h]
+  · obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := exists_sideForm_eq_re_sub h₁
+    rw [he, he, h]
+
+/-- The points of a vertical geodesic line have the same real part. -/
+private theorem re_eq_of_mem_range {g : PSL(2, ℝ)}
+    (hg : g • ((0 : ℝ) : OnePoint ℝ) = ∞ ∨ g • (∞ : OnePoint ℝ) = ∞) {z w : ℍ}
+    (hz : z ∈ range (geodesicLine g)) (hw : w ∈ range (geodesicLine g)) : z.re = w.re := by
+  rw [mem_range_geodesicLine_iff_sideForm_eq_zero] at hz hw
+  rcases hg with h₀ | h₁
+  · obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := exists_sideForm_eq_sub_re h₀
+    rw [he, coe_re] at hz hw
+    linarith
+  · obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := exists_sideForm_eq_re_sub h₁
+    rw [he, coe_re] at hz hw
+    linarith
+
+variable {κ : Type*} {L : κ → PSL(2, ℝ)} {K : Set ℍ}
+
+/-- If an intersection `K` of closed half-planes has points arbitrarily high up, then every
+sufficiently high point satisfying the constraints of the vertical lines lies in `K`: the
+semicircles all have `∞` on their left. -/
+private theorem eventually_mem_of_frequently [Finite κ]
+    (hK : K = ⋂ j, closure (leftHalfPlane (L j))) (hfreq : ∃ᶠ z in atImInfty, z ∈ K) :
+    ∀ᶠ z : ℍ in atImInfty, (∀ m, (L m • ((0 : ℝ) : OnePoint ℝ) = ∞ ∨
+      L m • (∞ : OnePoint ℝ) = ∞) → sideForm (L m) z ≤ 0) → z ∈ K := by
+  have hm (m : κ) : ∀ᶠ z : ℍ in atImInfty, ((L m • ((0 : ℝ) : OnePoint ℝ) = ∞ ∨
+      L m • (∞ : OnePoint ℝ) = ∞) → sideForm (L m) z ≤ 0) →
+        z ∈ closure (leftHalfPlane (L m)) := by
+    rcases smul_eq_infty_or_or_eventually (L m) with h | h | h | h
+    · exact Eventually.of_forall fun z hz ↦
+        (mem_closure_leftHalfPlane_iff_sideForm_nonpos _ _).2 (hz (Or.inl h))
+    · exact Eventually.of_forall fun z hz ↦
+        (mem_closure_leftHalfPlane_iff_sideForm_nonpos _ _).2 (hz (Or.inr h))
+    · filter_upwards [eventually_mem_leftHalfPlane_of_infty_mem_boundaryLeftHalfPlane h]
+        with z hz _ using subset_closure hz
+    · -- a semicircle with the high points on its right would exclude them from `K`
+      exfalso
+      obtain ⟨z, hzK, hzr⟩ := (hfreq.and_eventually h).exists
+      rw [hK] at hzK
+      exact (disjoint_rightHalfPlane_closure_leftHalfPlane _).le_bot ⟨hzr, mem_iInter.1 hzK m⟩
+  filter_upwards [eventually_all.2 hm] with z hz hv
+  rw [hK, mem_iInter]
+  exact fun m ↦ hz m (hv m)
+
+/-- If `K` has points arbitrarily high up, then a vertical line of one of its half-planes, meeting
+`K`, has all its sufficiently high points in `K`. -/
+private theorem eventually_map_geodesicLine_mem [Finite κ]
+    (hK : K = ⋂ j, closure (leftHalfPlane (L j))) (hfreq : ∃ᶠ z in atImInfty, z ∈ K) {k : κ}
+    (hk : L k • ((0 : ℝ) : OnePoint ℝ) = ∞ ∨ L k • (∞ : OnePoint ℝ) = ∞) {z₀ : ℍ}
+    (hz₀ : z₀ ∈ K) (hz₀k : z₀ ∈ range (geodesicLine (L k))) :
+    ∀ᶠ z in atImInfty, z ∈ range (geodesicLine (L k)) → z ∈ K := by
+  filter_upwards [eventually_mem_of_frequently hK hfreq] with z hz hzk
+  refine hz fun m hm ↦ ?_
+  have hz₀m : z₀ ∈ closure (leftHalfPlane (L m)) := by
+    rw [hK] at hz₀
+    exact mem_iInter.1 hz₀ m
+  rw [mem_closure_leftHalfPlane_iff_sideForm_nonpos] at hz₀m
+  rwa [sideForm_eq_of_re_eq (w := z₀) hm
+    (by rw [coe_re, coe_re]; exact re_eq_of_mem_range hk hzk hz₀k)]
+
+variable {ι : Type*} [Finite ι]
+
+/-- An intersection `K` of closed half-planes with points arbitrarily high up, none of whose lines
+runs down from `∞`, does not stay bounded after removing finitely many horodiscs: it contains
+every point far enough to the left, and the points of a small fixed height escape the horodiscs
+towards the left. -/
+private theorem false_of_forall_smul_zero_ne_infty [Finite κ]
+    (hK : K = ⋂ j, closure (leftHalfPlane (L j))) (hfreq : ∃ᶠ z in atImInfty, z ∈ K)
+    (hdown : ∀ m, L m • ((0 : ℝ) : OnePoint ℝ) ≠ ∞) (g : ι → PSL(2, ℝ)) {A : ι → ℝ}
+    (hA : ∀ i, 0 < A i) (hb : Bornology.IsBounded (K \ ⋃ i, {z : ℍ | A i < (g i • z).im})) :
+    False := by
+  -- every point sufficiently far to the left lies in `K`
+  have hleft (m : κ) : ∀ᶠ x in atBot, ∀ z : ℍ, z.re ≤ x →
+      z ∈ closure (leftHalfPlane (L m)) := by
+    rcases smul_eq_infty_or_or_eventually (L m) with h | h | h | h
+    · exact absurd h (hdown m)
+    · obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := OnePoint.ne_infty_iff_exists.1 (hdown m)
+      filter_upwards [eventually_le_atBot e] with x hx z hz
+      rw [mem_closure_leftHalfPlane_iff_sideForm_nonpos,
+        sideForm_eq_of_smul_infty_eq_infty he.symm h, coe_re]
+      linarith
+    · obtain ⟨c, ρ, κ', hρ, hκ', hform⟩ := exists_sideForm_eq_of_infty_mem_boundaryLeftHalfPlane h
+      filter_upwards [eventually_le_atBot (c - ρ)] with x hx z hz
+      rw [mem_closure_leftHalfPlane_iff_sideForm_nonpos, hform]
+      have hρz : ρ ^ 2 ≤ Complex.normSq ((z : ℂ) - c) := by
+        rw [Complex.normSq_apply, Complex.sub_re, Complex.sub_im, coe_re, Complex.ofReal_re,
+          Complex.ofReal_im]
+        nlinarith [mul_self_nonneg ((z : ℂ).im - 0)]
+      exact mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos hκ'.le (by linarith)
+    · exfalso
+      obtain ⟨z, hzK, hzr⟩ := (hfreq.and_eventually h).exists
+      rw [hK] at hzK
+      exact (disjoint_rightHalfPlane_closure_leftHalfPlane _).le_bot ⟨hzr, mem_iInter.1 hzK m⟩
+  have hcore : ∀ᶠ x in atBot, ∀ z : ℍ, z.re ≤ x → z ∈ K := by
+    filter_upwards [eventually_all.2 hleft] with x hx z hz
+    rw [hK, mem_iInter]
+    exact fun m ↦ hx m z hz
+  -- a common small height at which the points far to the left avoid every horodisc
+  choose b hb₀ hbA using fun i ↦ exists_pos_eventually_im_smul_le (g i) (hA i)
+  obtain ⟨h, hhb, hh⟩ := ((eventually_all.2 fun i ↦ Ioo_mem_nhdsGT (hb₀ i)).and
+    (self_mem_nhdsWithin : Ioi (0 : ℝ) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0)).exists
+  have hout : ∀ᶠ x in atBot, ∀ i, ∀ z : ℍ, z.re = x → z.im = h → (g i • z).im ≤ A i :=
+    eventually_all.2 fun i ↦ hbA i h (hhb i).2.le
+  obtain ⟨X, hX⟩ := eventually_atBot.1 (hcore.and hout)
+  -- the points `x + h i` for `x ≤ X` lie in the bounded truncation, a contradiction
+  refine not_isBounded_of_forall_re_le (S := K \ ⋃ i, {z : ℍ | A i < (g i • z).im}) hh
+    (fun z hzX hzh ↦ ⟨(hX _ hzX).1 z le_rfl, ?_⟩) hb
+  simp only [mem_iUnion, mem_ofPred_eq, not_exists, not_lt]
+  exact fun i ↦ (hX _ hzX).2 i z rfl hzh
+
+end Infinity
+

 /-! ### The faces of an irredundant intersection
 
 Throughout, `K` is the intersection of the closed left half-planes of finitely many geodesic lines
-`L k`, each face `K ∩ L k` is the image of `[a k, b k]` with `a k < b k`, and distinct indices
-have distinct lines. -/
+`L k`, and each line `L k` carries the point `geodesicLine (L k) (u k)` strictly inside all the
+other half-planes. -/
 
 section Faces
 
-variable {κ : Type*} {L : κ → PSL(2, ℝ)} {K : Set ℍ} {a b : κ → ℝ}
+variable {κ : Type*} {L : κ → PSL(2, ℝ)} {K : Set ℍ} {u : κ → ℝ}
 
 /-- A point of `K` lies in each of the closed half-planes. -/
 private theorem mem_closure_leftHalfPlane_of_mem (hK : K = ⋂ j, closure (leftHalfPlane (L j)))
     {z : ℍ} (hz : z ∈ K) (k : κ) : z ∈ closure (leftHalfPlane (L k)) := by
   rw [hK] at hz
   exact mem_iInter.1 hz k
 
-/-- A point of the line of `L k` strictly inside all the other half-planes lies in `K`, and so
-does a point a little further along the line. -/
-private theorem exists_pos_geodesicLine_add_mem [Finite κ]
-    (hK : K = ⋂ j, closure (leftHalfPlane (L j))) {k : κ} {u : ℝ}
-    (hu : ∀ j, j ≠ k → geodesicLine (L k) u ∈ leftHalfPlane (L j)) :
-    geodesicLine (L k) u ∈ K ∧ ∃ ε > 0, geodesicLine (L k) (u + ε) ∈ K := by
+/-- A point of the line of `L k` strictly inside all the other half-planes lies in `K`, together
+with the points of the line near it. -/
+private theorem exists_pos_ball_subset [Finite κ] (hK : K = ⋂ j, closure (leftHalfPlane (L j)))
+    {k : κ} {v : ℝ} (hv : ∀ j, j ≠ k → geodesicLine (L k) v ∈ leftHalfPlane (L j)) :
+    ∃ ε > 0, ∀ τ ∈ Metric.ball v ε, geodesicLine (L k) τ ∈ K := by

+module
+
+public import TauCeti.Analysis.Convex.Sequence.SlopeData
+import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin
+
+/-!
+# Finite slope multisets
+
+The finite slopes of a convex height sequence are the slopes of all of its unit edges,
+counted with multiplicity. This file packages that invariant on `FiniteSlopeData`, the
+canonical presentation of a nonempty convex height sequence with finite domain.
+
+The multiset has cardinality equal to the horizontal length of the polygon. Its sum is the
+difference between the endpoint heights.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `FiniteSlopeData.slopeMultiset`: the multiset of unit slopes.
+* `FiniteSlopeData.count_slopeMultiset`: multiplicities count unit edges of a given slope.
+* `FiniteSlopeData.card_slopeMultiset`: its cardinality is the horizontal length.
+* `FiniteSlopeData.sum_slopeMultiset`: its sum is the total height change.
+
+## References
+
+* N. Koblitz, *p-adic Numbers, p-adic Analysis, and Zeta-Functions*, Chapter IV §3.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open Finset
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+namespace FiniteSlopeData
+
+variable {Γ : Type*} [Preorder Γ]
+
+/-- The multiset of the slopes of the unit edges of finite slope data.
+
+Each `i : Fin length` contributes one copy of `slope i`, so repeated slopes retain their
+multiplicity. In particular, slope data of length zero has the empty slope multiset. -/
+def slopeMultiset (d : FiniteSlopeData Γ) : Multiset Γ :=
+  List.ofFn d.slope
+
+/-- A value occurs in the slope multiset exactly when it is the slope of a unit edge. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem mem_slopeMultiset {d : FiniteSlopeData Γ} {m : Γ} :
+    m ∈ d.slopeMultiset ↔ ∃ i : Fin d.length, d.slope i = m := by
+  simp [slopeMultiset]
+
+/-- The slope multiset is empty exactly when the represented polygon is a singleton. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem slopeMultiset_eq_zero_iff {d : FiniteSlopeData Γ} :
+    d.slopeMultiset = 0 ↔ d.length = 0 := by
+  simp [slopeMultiset]
+
+/-- The number of finite unit slopes is the horizontal length of the polygon. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem card_slopeMultiset (d : FiniteSlopeData Γ) :
+    d.slopeMultiset.card = d.length := by
+  simp [slopeMultiset]
+
+/-- The multiplicity of a value in the slope multiset is the number of unit edges with that
+slope. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem count_slopeMultiset [DecidableEq Γ] (d : FiniteSlopeData Γ) (m : Γ) :
+    d.slopeMultiset.count m = #{i | d.slope i = m} := by
+  rw [slopeMultiset, ← Fin.univ_val_map, Multiset.count_map]
+  simp [eq_comm, Finset.card, Finset.filter_val]
+
+section AddCommMonoid
+
+variable {Γ' : Type*} [Preorder Γ'] [AddCommMonoid Γ] [AddCommMonoid Γ']
+
+/-- The slope multiset of transported slope data is the image of the slope multiset. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem slopeMultiset_map (d : FiniteSlopeData Γ) (f : Γ →+o Γ') :
+    (d.map f).slopeMultiset = d.slopeMultiset.map f := by
+  simp [slopeMultiset, Function.comp_def]
+
+/-- The sum of the finite slopes is the sum over the unit edges. -/
+theorem sum_slopeMultiset_eq_sum (d : FiniteSlopeData Γ) :
+    d.slopeMultiset.sum = ∑ i, d.slope i := by
+  simp [slopeMultiset, List.sum_ofFn]
+
+end AddCommMonoid
+
+section AddCommGroup
+
+variable [AddCommGroup Γ]
+
+/-- The sum of the finite slopes is the difference between the endpoint heights. -/
+theorem sum_slopeMultiset (d : FiniteSlopeData Γ) :
+    d.slopeMultiset.sum =
+      (d.heights (d.start + d.length)).untop₀ - (d.heights d.start).untop₀ := by
+  rw [d.heights_start_add_length, d.heights_start, d.sum_slopeMultiset_eq_sum]
+  simp
+
+end AddCommGroup
+
+end FiniteSlopeData
+
+end TauCeti

+/-!
+# Regularity of supporting values
+
+The real supporting value is concave on the slopes where the supporting value is not
+negative infinity. For a nonempty height sequence, this is its finite-value domain
+and is a lower interval of slopes. No convexity assumption on the heights is needed.
+The real supporting value is continuous on the interior of this slope domain.
+For the empty sequence, the real supporting value is the constant zero function.
+
+For a nonempty finite point set, the supporting value is the minimum of finitely many
+real affine functions on the whole slope line. For a convex height sequence, a finite
+edge `[m, m+1]` gives the finite set of finite-height indices `n ≤ m`, which computes
+every supporting value at slopes strictly below `unitSlope h m`, with no bounded-domain
+assumption. Consequently the real supporting value is continuous there. The same finite
+set works on every compact slope interval below that edge; no assertion is made at a
+limiting terminal-ray slope.
+These finite reductions are useful for identifying active coefficients and for local
+piecewise-affine descriptions of Newton polygons.
+
+## References
+
+* N. Koblitz, *p-adic Numbers, p-adic Analysis, and Zeta-Functions*, second edition,
+  Chapter IV §3.
+* M. Lazard, *Les zéros d'une fonction analytique d'une variable sur un corps valué complet*,
+  Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS 14 (1962), §1.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open Set Finset
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+variable {a h : ℕ → WithTop ℝ}
+
+/-- Slopes with supporting value above negative infinity form a convex set. For a
+nonempty point sequence these are exactly the slopes with finite supporting value. -/
+theorem convex_setOf_supportingValue_ne_bot (a : ℕ → WithTop ℝ) :
+    Convex ℝ {σ | supportingValue a σ ≠ ⊥} := by
+  rw [convex_iff_ordConnected]
+  exact ⟨fun x _ y hy z hz =>
+    ne_bot_of_le_ne_bot hy (supportingValue_antitone a hz.2)⟩
+
+/-- The real supporting value is concave where the supporting value is not negative
+infinity. For a nonempty height sequence this is its finite-value domain; for the empty
+sequence the real supporting value is constant zero. No convexity or admissibility is required. -/
+theorem concaveOn_supportingValue_toReal (a : ℕ → WithTop ℝ) :
+    ConcaveOn ℝ {σ | supportingValue a σ ≠ ⊥}
+      (fun σ => (supportingValue a σ).toReal) := by
+  obtain rfl | ha := eq_or_ne a ⊤
+  · simpa using concaveOn_const (0 : ℝ) (convex_setOf_supportingValue_ne_bot ⊤)
+  have hne : ∃ n, a n ≠ ⊤ := Function.ne_iff.mp ha
+  refine ⟨convex_setOf_supportingValue_ne_bot a, ?_⟩
+  intro x hx y hy u v hu hv huv
+  have htop (σ : ℝ) : supportingValue a σ ≠ ⊤ :=
+    ne_of_lt (supportingValue_lt_top_iff.mpr hne)
+  have hline (σ : ℝ) (hσ : supportingValue a σ ≠ ⊥) :=
+    coe_le_supportingValue_iff_untop₀.mp (EReal.coe_toReal_le hσ)
+  have hxy : supportingValue a (u • x + v • y) ≠ ⊥ :=
+    (convex_setOf_supportingValue_ne_bot a) hx hy hu hv huv
+  apply EReal.coe_le_coe_iff.mp
+  rw [EReal.coe_toReal (htop _) hxy]
+  apply coe_le_supportingValue_iff_untop₀.mpr
+  intro n hn
+  have hx' := hline x hx n hn
+  have hy' := hline y hy n hn
+  simp only [smul_eq_mul]
+  linarith [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hx' hu, mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hy' hv,
+    congrArg (fun t : ℝ => t * (a n).untop₀) huv]
+
+/-- The real supporting value of any height sequence is continuous on the interior
+of the slopes where its supporting value is not negative infinity. -/
+theorem continuousOn_supportingValue_toReal (a : ℕ → WithTop ℝ) :
+    ContinuousOn (fun σ => (supportingValue a σ).toReal)
+      (interior {σ | supportingValue a σ ≠ ⊥}) :=
+  (concaveOn_supportingValue_toReal a).continuousOn_interior

+/-- On a nonempty finite point set, supporting values are the real minimum of the
+finitely many tilted heights. Missing heights do not participate in the minimum. -/
+theorem supportingValue_eq_coe_inf' {I : Finset ℕ} (hI : I.Nonempty)
+    (hdom : ∀ n, a n ≠ ⊤ ↔ n ∈ I) (σ : ℝ) :
+    supportingValue a σ =
+      ((I.inf' hI (fun n => (a n).untop₀ - σ * n) : ℝ) : EReal) := by
+  apply le_antisymm
+  · obtain ⟨n, hn, heq⟩ := I.exists_mem_eq_inf' hI (fun n => (a n).untop₀ - σ * n)
+    rw [heq]
+    convert supportingValue_le a σ n using 1
+    rw [← WithTop.coe_untop₀_of_ne_top ((hdom n).mpr hn), WithTop.toEReal_coe,
+      EReal.coe_sub]
+    simp
+  · apply coe_le_supportingValue_iff_untop₀.mpr
+    intro n hn
+    have := I.inf'_le (fun n => (a n).untop₀ - σ * n) ((hdom n).mp hn)

+
+public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension

+public import TauCeti.Analysis.Normed.Operator.ContinuousLinearEquiv

+/-!
+# The Banach–Mazur distance
+
+The Banach–Mazur distance between two normed spaces `E` and `F` is
+`d(E, F) = inf ‖T‖ ‖T⁻¹‖`, the infimum over continuous linear equivalences `T : E ≃L[𝕜] F`.
+It measures how far `E` and `F` are from being isometric, and is the distance used to compare
+finite-dimensional spaces with Euclidean spaces in the local theory of Banach spaces.
+
+`TauCeti.banachMazurDist 𝕜 E F` is this infimum, as a real number. When `E` and `F` are not
+isomorphic the infimum is over the empty set and its value is the junk value `0`; two
+finite-dimensional spaces over a complete field are isomorphic exactly when they have the same
+dimension (`FiniteDimensional.nonempty_continuousLinearEquiv_iff_finrank_eq`).
+
+## Main results
+
+* `TauCeti.banachMazurDist_comm`: the distance is symmetric.
+* `TauCeti.banachMazurDist_triangle`: the multiplicative triangle inequality
+  `d(E, G) ≤ d(E, F) d(F, G)`.
+* `TauCeti.one_le_banachMazurDist`: between isomorphic nonzero spaces the distance is at least `1`.
+* `LinearIsometryEquiv.banachMazurDist_congr_left` and
+  `LinearIsometryEquiv.banachMazurDist_congr_right`: the distance is invariant under replacing
+  either space by an isometric copy.
+* `TauCeti.exists_norm_mul_norm_symm_eq_banachMazurDist`: over a locally compact field, the
+  infimum is attained when the spaces are finite-dimensional.
+* `TauCeti.banachMazurDist_eq_one_iff`: over `ℝ` or `ℂ`, two nonzero finite-dimensional spaces
+  are at distance one exactly when they are isometric.
+
+Over a general locally compact field the last statement fails, since the norms of scalars need
+not fill out the positive reals: rescaling the norm of a field such as `ℚ_[p]` by a factor that is
+not the norm of a scalar gives a space at distance one from `ℚ_[p]` but not isometric to it.
+
+## References
+
+* F. Albiac and N. J. Kalton, *Topics in Banach Space Theory*, Chapter 12.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open Set
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+variable (𝕜 E F : Type*)
+
+section Definition
+
+variable [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]

+
+/-- The **Banach–Mazur distance** between normed spaces `E` and `F`: the infimum of

+  ⨅ T : E ≃L[𝕜] F, ‖(T : E →L[𝕜] F)‖ * ‖(T.symm : F →L[𝕜] E)‖

+/-- The defining formula of `banachMazurDist`, as an infimum over continuous linear
+equivalences. -/

+    banachMazurDist 𝕜 E F = ⨅ T : E ≃L[𝕜] F, ‖(T : E →L[𝕜] F)‖ * ‖(T.symm : F →L[𝕜] E)‖ :=
+  (rfl)
+

+variable {G : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
+  [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace 𝕜 G]

+/-!
+# The Bishop–Phelps theorem
+
+Let `C` be a closed convex subset of a real or complex Banach space `E`. A *support functional*
+of `C` is a nonzero continuous linear functional `g` whose real part attains its supremum on `C`;
+a point of `C` at which this happens is a *support point*. The **Bishop–Phelps theorem** says
+that there are many of both:
+
+* if `C` is moreover bounded and nonempty and `E` is nonzero, the support functionals of `C` are
+  norm dense in the dual (`Convex.dense_setOf_ne_zero_isMaxOn_re`);
+* the support points of `C` are dense in its boundary
+  (`Convex.frontier_subset_closure_setOf_isMaxOn_re`); conversely every support point lies on the
+  boundary (`StrongDual.mem_frontier_of_isMaxOn_re`);
+* taking for `C` the closed unit ball, the norm-attaining functionals are norm dense in the dual
+  (`TauCeti.dense_setOf_exists_norm_apply_eq_norm`).
+
+The space `E` is assumed complete. Convexity is real convexity, also over `ℂ`.
+
+The proof follows Phelps. Ekeland's variational principle
+(`LowerSemicontinuous.exists_add_mul_dist_le_and_lt_add_mul_dist`), applied to minus the real
+part of a functional `f` on `C`, produces a point `x ∈ C` such that `C` meets the cone
+`x + {w | k * ‖f‖ * ‖w‖ ≤ re (f w)}` only at `x`. Separating `C` from the interior of this cone
+gives a support functional `h` at `x` whose real part is positive on the open cone
+(`Convex.exists_isMaxOn_re_of_bddAbove`), and the *Bishop–Phelps lemma*
+(`StrongDual.exists_pos_norm_sub_ofReal_smul_le`) shows that a positive multiple of `h` lies
+within `k * ‖f‖` of `f`.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `StrongDual.exists_pos_norm_sub_ofReal_smul_le`: the Bishop–Phelps lemma.
+* `StrongDual.convex_setOf_mul_norm_sub_lt_re`: the open Bishop–Phelps cones are convex.
+* `Convex.exists_isMaxOn_re_of_bddAbove`: support functionals at points reached through a cone.
+* `Convex.dense_setOf_ne_zero_isMaxOn_re`: support functionals of a bounded closed convex set are
+  dense.
+* `Convex.frontier_subset_closure_setOf_isMaxOn_re`: support points are dense in the boundary.
+* `TauCeti.dense_setOf_exists_norm_apply_eq_norm`: norm-attaining functionals are dense.
+

+    rw [norm_smul, norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg ha.le, Real.norm_of_nonneg hb.le]

+/-- **Bishop–Phelps support lemma.** Let `C` be a closed convex subset of a Banach space, let `f`

+`z ∈ C` one reaches a point `x ∈ C` with `k * ‖f‖ * ‖x - z‖ ≤ re (f (x - z))` at which `C` has a

+theorem Convex.exists_isMaxOn_re_of_bddAbove (hconv : Convex ℝ C) (hC : IsClosed C)
+    {f : StrongDual 𝕜 E} (hf : f ≠ 0) (hbdd : BddAbove ((fun y ↦ re (f y)) '' C)) {k : ℝ}
+    (hk₀ : 0 < k) (hk₁ : k < 1) {z : E} (hz : z ∈ C) :
+    ∃ x ∈ C, k * ‖f‖ * ‖x - z‖ ≤ re (f (x - z)) ∧ ∃ h : StrongDual 𝕜 E, h ≠ 0 ∧

+  -- Ekeland's principle for `-re ∘ f` on the complete metric space `C`.
+  have : CompleteSpace C := hC.completeSpace_coe

+  have hcont : Continuous fun y : C ↦ -re (f y) :=
+    (continuous_re.comp (f.continuous.comp continuous_subtype_val)).neg
+  obtain ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, hxz, hmin⟩ :=
+    hcont.lowerSemicontinuous.exists_add_mul_dist_le_and_lt_add_mul_dist
+      ⟨-M, by rintro _ ⟨y, rfl⟩; exact neg_le_neg (hM (mem_image_of_mem _ y.2))⟩ hkf ⟨z, hz⟩
+  simp only [Subtype.dist_eq, dist_eq_norm] at hxz hmin
+  refine ⟨x, hx, by simp only [map_sub]; linarith, ?_⟩
+  -- The open cone `s` with vertex `x` is convex, open and disjoint from `C`.
+  set s : Set E := {y | k * ‖f‖ * ‖y - x‖ < re (f (y - x))} with hs
+  have hs_open : IsOpen s := isOpen_lt (by fun_prop)
+    (continuous_re.comp (f.continuous.comp (continuous_id.sub continuous_const)))
+  have hs_conv : Convex ℝ s := f.convex_setOf_mul_norm_sub_lt_re hkf.le x
+  have hdisj : Disjoint s C := by
+    refine disjoint_left.2 fun y hys hyC ↦ ?_
+    simp only [hs, mem_ofPred_eq] at hys
+    by_cases hyx : y = x
+    · subst hyx
+      simp at hys
+    · have := hmin ⟨y, hyC⟩ (by simpa [Subtype.ext_iff] using hyx)
+      simp only [map_sub] at hys
+      linarith
+  obtain ⟨g, u, hgs, hgC⟩ := RCLike.geometric_hahn_banach_open (𝕜 := 𝕜) hs_conv hs_open hconv hdisj
+  -- `x + w` lies in `s` for every `w` in the open cone.
+  have hcone (w : E) (hw : k * ‖f‖ * ‖w‖ < re (f w)) : x + w ∈ s := by
+    simpa [hs] using hw
+  have hneg (w : E) (hw : k * ‖f‖ * ‖w‖ < re (f w)) : re (g w) < 0 := by
+    have := hgs _ (hcone w hw)
+    rw [map_add, map_add] at this
+    linarith [hgC x hx]
+  -- Approaching `x` along a cone direction shows that `re ∘ g` is at most `u` at `x`.
+  obtain ⟨w₀, hw₀⟩ := f.exists_mul_norm_lt_re_apply hkf.le (by nlinarith [norm_pos_iff.2 hf])

+    have hlim : Tendsto (fun t : ℝ ↦ re (g (x + (t : 𝕜) • w₀))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (re (g x))) := by
+      have : Continuous fun t : ℝ ↦ re (g (x + (t : 𝕜) • w₀)) :=
+        continuous_re.comp (g.continuous.comp
+          (continuous_const.add (continuous_ofReal.smul continuous_const)))
+      simpa using (this.tendsto 0).mono_left nhdsWithin_le_nhds
+    refine le_of_tendsto hlim (eventually_nhdsWithin_of_forall fun t (ht : 0 < t) ↦ ?_)
+    refine (hgs _ (hcone _ ?_)).le
+    rw [norm_smul, norm_ofReal, abs_of_pos ht, map_smul, smul_eq_mul, re_ofReal_mul]
+    nlinarith

+  · have := hneg w₀ hw₀
+    rw [neg_eq_zero.1 h0] at this

+      neg_le_neg_iff]

+theorem Convex.dense_setOf_ne_zero_isMaxOn_re [Nontrivial E] (hconv : Convex ℝ C)

+        _ < ε := half_lt_self hε

+      refine ⟨‖f‖ * R, ?_⟩
+      rintro _ ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩
+      exact (re_le_norm _).trans ((f.le_opNorm y).trans (by gcongr; exact hR y hy))
+    obtain ⟨x, hx, -, h, hh, hmax, hpos⟩ :=

+  exact dense_closure.1 ((dense_compl_singleton 0).mono hsub)

+/-- **The Bishop–Phelps theorem for support points.** The support points of a closed convex
+subset `C` of a Banach space, namely the points of `C` at which the real part of some nonzero

+/-!
+# Absolutely summing operators
+
+Let `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞`. A bounded operator `T : E →L[𝕜] F` is *absolutely `p`-summing* if there is a
+constant `C` such that the `Lᵖ` norm of `(T xᵢ)ᵢ`, which is `(∑ ‖T xᵢ‖ᵖ)^(1/p)` for finite `p`,
+is at most `C * weakLpNorm p x` for every finite family `x` in `E`; the least such constant is
+the `p`-summing norm `πₚ(T)`. We record `πₚ(T)` as the extended gauge
+`ContinuousLinearMap.summingENorm p T ∈ [0, ∞]`, the supremum over finite families of the ratio
+of the two sides. It is finite exactly on the absolutely `p`-summing operators, which form the
+submodule `TauCeti.absolutelySummingOperators 𝕜 p E F` of `E →L[𝕜] F`.
+
+The gauge is absolutely homogeneous and subadditive, and satisfies the two-sided ideal inequality
+`πₚ(A ∘ T ∘ B) ≤ ‖A‖ πₚ(T) ‖B‖`. Over real or complex scalars it dominates the operator norm,
+takes the value `‖f‖ ‖y‖` on the rank-one operator `x ↦ f x • y`, and is lower semicontinuous for
+the operator-norm topology, which is the input for completeness of the summing-norm ideal.
+
+## Main declarations
+
+* `ContinuousLinearMap.summingENorm`: the extended `p`-summing gauge `πₚ(T)`.
+* `ContinuousLinearMap.summingENorm_le_ofReal_iff`: `πₚ(T) ≤ C` iff the defining inequality
+  holds with constant `C`.
+* `ContinuousLinearMap.enorm_toLp_le_summingENorm_mul`: the defining inequality with the
+  constant `πₚ(T)`, for families indexed by any finite type.
+* `ContinuousLinearMap.summingENorm_comp_comp_le`: the ideal inequality.
+* `ContinuousLinearMap.enorm_le_summingENorm`: `‖T‖ ≤ πₚ(T)`.
+* `ContinuousLinearMap.summingENorm_smulRight`: the rank-one value.
+* `ContinuousLinearMap.lowerSemicontinuous_summingENorm`: lower semicontinuity.
+* `TauCeti.absolutelySummingOperators`: the submodule of absolutely `p`-summing operators.
+
+## References
+
+* F. Albiac and N. J. Kalton, *Topics in Banach Space Theory*, §8.2.
+* J. Diestel, H. Jarchow and A. Tonge, *Absolutely Summing Operators*, Chapter 2.

+  refine forall₂_congr fun n x ↦ ?_
+  rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_mul hC, ← ofReal_norm,
+    ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff (mul_nonneg hC (apply_nonneg _ _))]
+
+/-- A finite gauge bounds the image of every finite family, whatever its index type. -/
+theorem enorm_toLp_le_summingENorm_mul_of_ne_top {T : E →L[𝕜] F}
+    (hT : T.summingENorm p ≠ ∞) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (x : ι → E) :
+    ‖WithLp.toLp p (fun i ↦ T (x i))‖ₑ ≤
+      T.summingENorm p * ENNReal.ofReal (weakLpNorm (𝕜 := 𝕜) p x) := by
+  let e := Fintype.equivFin ι
+  have h := (summingENorm_le_iff hT).1 le_rfl _ (x ∘ e.symm)
+  have hn : ‖WithLp.toLp p (fun i ↦ T ((x ∘ e.symm) i))‖ₑ =
+      ‖WithLp.toLp p (fun i ↦ T (x i))‖ₑ := by
+    rw [← ofReal_norm, ← ofReal_norm]
+    exact congrArg _ (PiLp.norm_toLp_comp_equiv e.symm fun i ↦ T (x i))
+  rwa [weakLpNorm_comp_equiv, hn] at h
+
+/-- The real form of the defining inequality with constant `πₚ(T)`, for an operator of finite
+gauge. -/
+theorem norm_toLp_le_toReal_summingENorm_mul {T : E →L[𝕜] F}
+    (hT : T.summingENorm p ≠ ∞) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (x : ι → E) :
+    ‖WithLp.toLp p (fun i ↦ T (x i))‖ ≤
+      (T.summingENorm p).toReal * weakLpNorm (𝕜 := 𝕜) p x := by
+  have h := ENNReal.toReal_mono (ENNReal.mul_ne_top hT ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top)
+    (enorm_toLp_le_summingENorm_mul_of_ne_top hT x)
+  rwa [ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (apply_nonneg _ _), toReal_enorm] at h
+
+/-- An operator of zero operator norm has zero gauge. -/
+theorem summingENorm_eq_zero_of_norm_eq_zero {T : E →L[𝕜] F} (hT : ‖T‖ = 0) :
+    T.summingENorm p = 0 := by
+  refine le_antisymm ?_ bot_le
+  rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_zero, summingENorm_le_ofReal_iff le_rfl]
+  intro n x
+  simpa [hT] using PiLp.norm_toLp_comp_le (p := p) (norm_nonneg T) T.le_opNorm x
+
+/-- The zero operator has zero gauge. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem summingENorm_zero : (0 : E →L[𝕜] F).summingENorm p = 0 :=
+  summingENorm_eq_zero_of_norm_eq_zero norm_zero
+
+/-- Absolute homogeneity of the gauge, including its infinite values. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem summingENorm_smul (c : 𝕜) (T : E →L[𝕜] F) :
+    (c • T).summingENorm p = ‖c‖ₑ * T.summingENorm p := by
+  have h (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → E) :
+      ‖WithLp.toLp p (fun i ↦ (c • T) (x i))‖ₑ = ‖c‖ₑ * ‖WithLp.toLp p (fun i ↦ T (x i))‖ₑ := by
+    simp only [smul_apply, ← Pi.smul_def, WithLp.toLp_smul, enorm_smul]
+  simp only [summingENorm_def, h, mul_div_assoc, ENNReal.mul_iSup]
+
+/-- Negation preserves the gauge. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem summingENorm_neg (T : E →L[𝕜] F) : (-T).summingENorm p = T.summingENorm p := by
+  simpa using summingENorm_smul (-1 : 𝕜) T
+
+/-- The gauge is subadditive. -/
+theorem summingENorm_add_le (S T : E →L[𝕜] F) :
+    (S + T).summingENorm p ≤ S.summingENorm p + T.summingENorm p := by
+  refine iSup₂_le fun n x ↦ ?_
+  have hle : ‖WithLp.toLp p (fun i ↦ (S + T) (x i))‖ₑ ≤
+      ‖WithLp.toLp p (fun i ↦ S (x i))‖ₑ + ‖WithLp.toLp p (fun i ↦ T (x i))‖ₑ := by
+    have hadd : WithLp.toLp p (fun i ↦ (S + T) (x i)) =
+        WithLp.toLp p (fun i ↦ S (x i)) + WithLp.toLp p (fun i ↦ T (x i)) := by
+      ext i
+      simp
+    rw [hadd]
+    exact enorm_add_le _ _
+  calc
+    _ ≤ (‖WithLp.toLp p (fun i ↦ S (x i))‖ₑ + ‖WithLp.toLp p (fun i ↦ T (x i))‖ₑ) /
+        ENNReal.ofReal (weakLpNorm (𝕜 := 𝕜) p x) := by gcongr
+    _ = _ := ENNReal.add_div
+    _ ≤ S.summingENorm p + T.summingENorm p :=
+      add_le_add (S.enorm_toLp_div_le_summingENorm x) (T.enorm_toLp_div_le_summingENorm x)
+
+/-- Composing on the left with a bounded operator multiplies the gauge by at most its norm. -/
+theorem summingENorm_comp_left_le (A : F →L[𝕜] G) (T : E →L[𝕜] F) :
+    (A ∘L T).summingENorm p ≤ ‖A‖ₑ * T.summingENorm p := by
+  refine iSup₂_le fun n x ↦ ?_
+  have hle : ‖WithLp.toLp p (fun i ↦ (A ∘L T) (x i))‖ₑ ≤
+      ‖A‖ₑ * ‖WithLp.toLp p (fun i ↦ T (x i))‖ₑ := by
+    rw [← ofReal_norm, ← ofReal_norm, ← ofReal_norm, ← ENNReal.ofReal_mul (norm_nonneg _)]
+    exact ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal
+      (PiLp.norm_toLp_comp_le (norm_nonneg A) A.le_opNorm fun i ↦ T (x i))
+  calc
+    _ ≤ ‖A‖ₑ * ‖WithLp.toLp p (fun i ↦ T (x i))‖ₑ /
+        ENNReal.ofReal (weakLpNorm (𝕜 := 𝕜) p x) := by gcongr
+    _ ≤ ‖A‖ₑ * T.summingENorm p := by
+      rw [mul_div_assoc]
+      gcongr
+      exact T.enorm_toLp_div_le_summingENorm x
+
+/-- Composing on the right with a bounded operator multiplies the gauge by at most its norm. -/
+theorem summingENorm_comp_right_le (T : F →L[𝕜] G) (B : E →L[𝕜] F) :
+    (T ∘L B).summingENorm p ≤ T.summingENorm p * ‖B‖ₑ := by
+  rcases eq_or_ne (T.summingENorm p) ∞ with hT | hT
+  · rcases eq_or_ne ‖B‖ₑ 0 with hB | hB
+    · -- A null right factor makes the composite null, whatever the gauge of `T`.
+      have hB' : ‖B‖ = 0 := by simpa using congrArg ENNReal.toReal hB
+      have hTB : ‖T ∘L B‖ = 0 :=
+        le_antisymm ((opNorm_comp_le T B).trans (by simp [hB'])) (norm_nonneg _)
+      simp [summingENorm_eq_zero_of_norm_eq_zero hTB]
+    · simp [hT, ENNReal.top_mul hB]
+  · rw [summingENorm_le_iff (ENNReal.mul_ne_top hT enorm_ne_top)]
+    intro n x
+    calc
+      _ ≤ T.summingENorm p * ENNReal.ofReal (weakLpNorm (𝕜 := 𝕜) p (B ∘ x)) :=
+        enorm_toLp_le_summingENorm_mul_of_ne_top hT (B ∘ x)
+      _ ≤ T.summingENorm p * (‖B‖ₑ * ENNReal.ofReal (weakLpNorm (𝕜 := 𝕜) p x)) := by
+        rw [← ofReal_norm, ← ENNReal.ofReal_mul (norm_nonneg _)]
+        gcongr
+        exact weakLpNorm_comp_le p B x
+      _ = _ := (mul_assoc _ _ _).symm
+
+/-- The two-sided ideal inequality `πₚ(A ∘ T ∘ B) ≤ ‖A‖ πₚ(T) ‖B‖`. -/
+theorem summingENorm_comp_comp_le (A : G →L[𝕜] H) (T : F →L[𝕜] G) (B : E →L[𝕜] F) :
+    (A ∘L T ∘L B).summingENorm p ≤ ‖A‖ₑ * T.summingENorm p * ‖B‖ₑ :=
+  calc
+    _ ≤ ‖A‖ₑ * (T ∘L B).summingENorm p := summingENorm_comp_left_le A (T ∘L B)
+    _ ≤ ‖A‖ₑ * (T.summingENorm p * ‖B‖ₑ) := by gcongr; exact summingENorm_comp_right_le T B
+    _ = _ := (mul_assoc _ _ _).symm
+
+/-- The rank-one operator `x ↦ f x • y` has gauge at most `‖f‖ ‖y‖`. -/
+theorem summingENorm_smulRight_le (f : StrongDual 𝕜 E) (y : F) :
+    (f.smulRight y).summingENorm p ≤ ‖f‖ₑ * ‖y‖ₑ := by
+  rw [← ofReal_norm, ← ofReal_norm, ← ENNReal.ofReal_mul (norm_nonneg _),
+    summingENorm_le_ofReal_iff (mul_nonneg (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _))]
+  intro n x
+  simp only [smulRight_apply]
+  rw [PiLp.norm_toLp_smul_const]
+  calc
+    _ ≤ weakLpNorm (𝕜 := 𝕜) p x * ‖f‖ * ‖y‖ := by
+      gcongr
+      exact norm_eval_le_weakLpNorm p x f
+    _ = _ := by ring
+
+end NormedField

+section RCLike
+
+variable {𝕜 E F : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜]
+  [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
+  [SeminormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]
+  {p : ℝ≥0∞} [Fact (1 ≤ p)]
+
+/-- A bounded operator maps a family of zero weak norm to a family of zero `Lᵖ` norm. -/
+theorem norm_toLp_eq_zero_of_weakLpNorm_eq_zero (T : E →L[𝕜] F) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
+    {x : ι → E} (hx : weakLpNorm (𝕜 := 𝕜) p x = 0) :
+    ‖WithLp.toLp p (fun i ↦ T (x i))‖ = 0 := by
+  refine le_antisymm ((PiLp.norm_mono (y := (0 : PiLp p fun _ : ι ↦ ℝ)) fun i ↦ ?_).trans
+    (by simp)) (norm_nonneg _)
+  have hxi : ‖x i‖ = 0 := le_antisymm (hx ▸ norm_le_weakLpNorm p x i) (norm_nonneg _)
+  simpa [hxi] using T.le_opNorm (x i)
+
+/-- The defining inequality with the constant `πₚ(T)`, for families indexed by any finite type.
+Over real or complex scalars no finiteness assumption is needed. -/
+theorem enorm_toLp_le_summingENorm_mul (T : E →L[𝕜] F) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (x : ι → E) :
+    ‖WithLp.toLp p (fun i ↦ T (x i))‖ₑ ≤
+      T.summingENorm p * ENNReal.ofReal (weakLpNorm (𝕜 := 𝕜) p x) := by
+  rcases eq_or_ne (T.summingENorm p) ∞ with hT | hT
+  · rcases eq_or_ne (weakLpNorm (𝕜 := 𝕜) p x) 0 with hx | hx
+    · simp [← ofReal_norm, norm_toLp_eq_zero_of_weakLpNorm_eq_zero T hx]
+    · rw [hT, ENNReal.top_mul (ENNReal.ofReal_pos.2 ((apply_nonneg _ _).lt_of_ne' hx)).ne']
+      exact le_top
+  · exact enorm_toLp_le_summingENorm_mul_of_ne_top hT x
+
+/-- The `p`-summing gauge dominates the operator norm. -/
+theorem enorm_le_summingENorm (T : E →L[𝕜] F) : ‖T‖ₑ ≤ T.summingENorm p := by
+  refine T.opENorm_le_bound fun v ↦ ?_
+  have hT : (fun i ↦ T ((Pi.single 0 v : Fin 1 → E) i)) = Pi.single 0 (T v) :=
+    funext fun i ↦ Pi.apply_single (fun _ ↦ ⇑T) (fun _ ↦ map_zero T) 0 v i
+  have h := enorm_toLp_le_summingENorm_mul (p := p) T (Pi.single (0 : Fin 1) v)
+  rwa [hT, weakLpNorm_single, ofReal_norm, PiLp.toLp_single, ← ofReal_norm,
+    PiLp.norm_single, ofReal_norm] at h
+
+/-- The gauge vanishes exactly at zero for maps into a separated normed space. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem summingENorm_eq_zero_iff {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]
+    {T : E →L[𝕜] F} : T.summingENorm p = 0 ↔ T = 0 := by
+  refine ⟨fun h ↦ ?_, fun h ↦ h ▸ summingENorm_zero⟩
+  have hn : ‖T‖ = 0 := by
+    have h0 := congrArg ENNReal.toReal (le_antisymm (h ▸ enorm_le_summingENorm T) bot_le)
+    rw [toReal_enorm] at h0
+    simpa using h0
+  -- Mathlib's `opNorm_zero_iff` requires a normed source; here the source is only seminormed.
+  ext v
+  exact norm_le_zero_iff.mp (by simpa [hn] using T.le_opNorm v)
+
+/-- The rank-one operator `x ↦ f x • y` has gauge `‖f‖ ‖y‖`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem summingENorm_smulRight (f : StrongDual 𝕜 E) (y : F) :
+    (f.smulRight y).summingENorm p = ‖f‖ₑ * ‖y‖ₑ := by
+  refine le_antisymm (summingENorm_smulRight_le f y) ?_
+  calc
+    ‖f‖ₑ * ‖y‖ₑ = ‖f.smulRight y‖ₑ := by
+      rw [← ofReal_norm, ← ofReal_norm, ← ofReal_norm, norm_smulRight_apply,
+        ENNReal.ofReal_mul (norm_nonneg _)]
+    _ ≤ _ := enorm_le_summingENorm _
+
+/-- The `p`-summing gauge is lower semicontinuous for the operator-norm topology. -/
+theorem lowerSemicontinuous_summingENorm :
+    LowerSemicontinuous (summingENorm p : (E →L[𝕜] F) → ℝ≥0∞) := by
+  refine lowerSemicontinuous_iSup fun n ↦ lowerSemicontinuous_iSup fun x ↦ ?_
+  rcases eq_or_ne (weakLpNorm (𝕜 := 𝕜) p x) 0 with hx | hx
+  · -- Every image of a family of zero weak norm is null, so its ratio vanishes identically.
+    have h0 : (fun T : E →L[𝕜] F ↦ ‖WithLp.toLp p (fun i ↦ T (x i))‖ₑ /
+        ENNReal.ofReal (weakLpNorm (𝕜 := 𝕜) p x)) = fun _ ↦ 0 := by
+      funext T
+      simp [← ofReal_norm, norm_toLp_eq_zero_of_weakLpNorm_eq_zero T hx]
+    rw [h0]
+    exact lowerSemicontinuous_const
+  · refine Continuous.lowerSemicontinuous ?_
+    refine (ENNReal.continuous_div_const _
+      (ENNReal.ofReal_pos.2 ((apply_nonneg _ _).lt_of_ne' hx)).ne').comp
+      (continuous_enorm.comp ((PiLp.continuous_toLp p _).comp ?_))
+    exact continuous_pi fun i ↦ continuous_eval_const (x i)
+
+end RCLike
+
+end ContinuousLinearMap

+namespace TauCeti

+variable (𝕜 : Type*) [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] (p : ℝ≥0∞) [Fact (1 ≤ p)]
+  {E F G : Type*}
+  [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
+  [SeminormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]
+  [SeminormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace 𝕜 G]
+
+variable (E F) in
+/-- The absolutely `p`-summing operators from `E` to `F`: the bounded operators of finite
+`p`-summing gauge. -/
+def absolutelySummingOperators : Submodule 𝕜 (E →L[𝕜] F) where
+  carrier := {T | T.summingENorm p < ∞}
+  add_mem' {S T} hS hT :=
+    (S.summingENorm_add_le T).trans_lt (ENNReal.add_lt_top.2 ⟨hS, hT⟩)
+  zero_mem' := by simp
+  smul_mem' c T hT := by
+    simpa [ContinuousLinearMap.summingENorm_smul] using ENNReal.mul_lt_top enorm_lt_top hT
+
+variable {𝕜 p}
+
+/-- Membership in the submodule means finite gauge. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem mem_absolutelySummingOperators {T : E →L[𝕜] F} :
+    T ∈ absolutelySummingOperators 𝕜 p E F ↔ T.summingENorm p < ∞ := Iff.rfl
+
+/-- An operator is absolutely `p`-summing iff for some constant `C` the `Lᵖ` norm of `(T xᵢ)ᵢ` is
+at most `C * weakLpNorm p x` for every finite family `x`. -/
+theorem mem_absolutelySummingOperators_iff {T : E →L[𝕜] F} :
+    T ∈ absolutelySummingOperators 𝕜 p E F ↔ ∃ C, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → E),
+      ‖WithLp.toLp p (fun i ↦ T (x i))‖ ≤ C * weakLpNorm (𝕜 := 𝕜) p x := by
+  rw [mem_absolutelySummingOperators]
+  constructor
+  · intro hT
+    refine ⟨(T.summingENorm p).toReal, ENNReal.toReal_nonneg, ?_⟩
+    rw [← ContinuousLinearMap.summingENorm_le_ofReal_iff ENNReal.toReal_nonneg,
+      ENNReal.ofReal_toReal hT.ne]
+  · rintro ⟨C, hC, h⟩
+    exact ((ContinuousLinearMap.summingENorm_le_ofReal_iff hC).2 h).trans_lt
+      ENNReal.ofReal_lt_top
+
+/-- Absolutely summing operators are stable under composition on the left. -/
+theorem comp_left_mem_absolutelySummingOperators (A : F →L[𝕜] G) {T : E →L[𝕜] F}
+    (hT : T ∈ absolutelySummingOperators 𝕜 p E F) :
+    A ∘L T ∈ absolutelySummingOperators 𝕜 p E G :=
+  (A.summingENorm_comp_left_le T).trans_lt (ENNReal.mul_lt_top enorm_lt_top hT)
+
+/-- Absolutely summing operators are stable under composition on the right. -/
+theorem comp_right_mem_absolutelySummingOperators {T : F →L[𝕜] G}
+    (hT : T ∈ absolutelySummingOperators 𝕜 p F G) (B : E →L[𝕜] F) :
+    T ∘L B ∈ absolutelySummingOperators 𝕜 p E G :=
+  (T.summingENorm_comp_right_le B).trans_lt (ENNReal.mul_lt_top hT enorm_lt_top)
+
+/-- Rank-one operators are absolutely summing. -/
+theorem smulRight_mem_absolutelySummingOperators (f : StrongDual 𝕜 E) (y : F) :
+    f.smulRight y ∈ absolutelySummingOperators 𝕜 p E F :=
+  (ContinuousLinearMap.summingENorm_smulRight_le f y).trans_lt
+    (ENNReal.mul_lt_top enorm_lt_top enorm_lt_top)
+
+end TauCeti

+module

+public import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Operator.NormedSpace
+public import TauCeti.Topology.Algebra.Module.Equiv.SMul
+
+/-!
+# Normalizing continuous linear equivalences
+
+Rescaling a continuous linear equivalence `T` between normed spaces by a nonzero scalar does not
+change `‖T‖ * ‖T⁻¹‖`. Using Mathlib's `rescale_to_shell`, every equivalence from a nonzero space
+can be rescaled to have norm at most `1`, with its inverse then of norm at most
+`‖c‖ * ‖T‖ * ‖T⁻¹‖` for any scalar `c` with `1 < ‖c‖`. This bounds both operators at once, as
+needed in compactness arguments over the set of equivalences.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+namespace ContinuousLinearEquiv
+
+variable {𝕜 E F : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
+  [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]
+
+/-- Given a scalar with `1 < ‖c‖`, every continuous linear equivalence `T` from a nonzero space
+can be rescaled, without changing `‖T‖ * ‖T⁻¹‖`, to have norm at most `1` and inverse of norm at
+most `‖c‖ * ‖T‖ * ‖T⁻¹‖`. -/
+theorem exists_norm_le_one_and_norm_symm_le [Nontrivial E] {c : 𝕜} (hc : 1 < ‖c‖)
+    (T : E ≃L[𝕜] F) :
+    ∃ U : E ≃L[𝕜] F, ‖(U : E →L[𝕜] F)‖ ≤ 1 ∧
+      ‖(U.symm : F →L[𝕜] E)‖ ≤ ‖c‖ * (‖(T : E →L[𝕜] F)‖ * ‖(T.symm : F →L[𝕜] E)‖) ∧
+      ‖(U : E →L[𝕜] F)‖ * ‖(U.symm : F →L[𝕜] E)‖ =
+        ‖(T : E →L[𝕜] F)‖ * ‖(T.symm : F →L[𝕜] E)‖ := by
+  have hT : (T : E →L[𝕜] F) ≠ 0 := fun h ↦ by
+    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := exists_ne (0 : E)
+    exact hx (T.injective (by simpa using congr($h x)))
+  obtain ⟨d, hd, hlt, hge, -⟩ := rescale_to_shell hc one_pos hT
+  obtain ⟨U, hU, hUs⟩ := T.exists_coe_eq_smul hd
+  have hd' : 0 < ‖d‖ := norm_pos_iff.2 hd
+  rw [norm_smul] at hlt hge
+  refine ⟨U, by rw [hU, norm_smul]; exact hlt.le, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · rw [hUs, norm_smul, norm_inv, ← mul_assoc]
+    gcongr
+    rw [inv_le_iff_one_le_mul₀ hd']
+    calc 1 = ‖c‖ * ‖c‖⁻¹ := (mul_inv_cancel₀ (by positivity)).symm
+      _ ≤ ‖c‖ * (‖d‖ * ‖(T : E →L[𝕜] F)‖) := by gcongr; simpa [one_div] using hge
+      _ = _ := by ring
+  · rw [hU, hUs, norm_smul, norm_smul, norm_inv]
+    field_simp
+
+end ContinuousLinearEquiv

+/-!
+# The Banach module and Banach ring of operators over Tate scalars
+
+Let `R` be a seminormed ring admitting a multiplicative pseudo-uniformiser
+(`TauCeti.NormedRing.IsTate R`), and let `E`, `F` be seminormed `R`-modules with contractive
+scalar actions. Over such scalars every continuous linear map has a uniform bound, so the operator
+norm `ContinuousLinearMap.ringOpNorm` of `TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Operator/RingOpNorm.lean`
+satisfies the usual laws. This file installs the resulting structures on `E →L[R] F` as scoped
+instances in the scope `TauCeti.RingOpNorm`:
+
+* `E →L[R] F` is a seminormed group, normed when `F` is, and ultrametric when `F` is;
+* scalar actions on `F` commuting with `R` act contractively on `E →L[R] F`; in particular
+  `E →L[R] F` is an `R`-module with contractive action when `R` is commutative;
+* evaluation `(f, x) ↦ f x` is jointly continuous;
+* `E →L[R] F` is complete when `F` is a complete normed group;
+* the endomorphisms `E →L[R] E` form a seminormed ring, normed when `E` is, with `‖1‖ = 1` as
+  soon as `E` has a vector of nonzero norm.
+
+Mathlib's topology of bounded convergence on continuous linear maps is only defined over normed
+fields, so over other scalar rings these instances introduce no diamond. Over a nontrivially
+normed field the scoped normed group structure equals Mathlib's
+(`TauCeti.RingOpNorm.seminormedAddCommGroup_eq`), but not definitionally, so the scope should not
+be opened there. On the zero module every operator has norm zero (`norm_of_subsingleton`).
+
+For a complete normed `R`-module `E`, the endomorphism ring is a Banach ring, so *Neumann
+inversion* applies: for `‖t‖ < 1` the operator `1 - t` is invertible with inverse the Neumann
+series `∑ tⁿ`. This is packaged as the continuous linear automorphism
+`ContinuousLinearMap.oneSub t ht`. When `E` is ultrametric, `1 - t` and its inverse are
+isometries, so the inverse has operator norm one on a module with a vector of nonzero norm.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `TauCeti.RingOpNorm.seminormedAddCommGroup`, `TauCeti.RingOpNorm.normedAddCommGroup`,
+  `TauCeti.RingOpNorm.seminormedRing`, `TauCeti.RingOpNorm.normedRing`: the scoped operator-norm
+  structures.
+* `ContinuousLinearMap.oneSub t ht`: the automorphism `1 - t` of a complete normed module over
+  Tate scalars, for `‖t‖ < 1`.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `TauCeti.RingOpNorm.completeSpace`: the operator space is complete when the target is.
+* `TauCeti.RingOpNorm.isUltrametricDist`: the operator norm is ultrametric when the target is.
+* `ContinuousLinearMap.coe_oneSub_symm`: the inverse of `1 - t` is `Ring.inverse (1 - t)`,
+  the sum of the Neumann series.
+* `ContinuousLinearMap.norm_oneSub_apply`, `ContinuousLinearMap.norm_oneSub_symm_apply` and
+  `ContinuousLinearMap.ringOpNorm_oneSub_symm`: in the ultrametric case `1 - t` and its inverse
+  preserve norms, and the inverse has operator norm one (the Neumann estimate
+  `TauCeti.norm_inverse_one_sub` in the Banach ring of operators).
+
+## References
+
+* C. Johansson and J. Newton, *Extended eigenvarieties for overconvergent cohomology*,
+  arXiv:1604.07739, §2.1.
+* P. Schneider, *Nonarchimedean Functional Analysis*, Springer, 2002, §3.

+The completeness proof follows Mathlib's `ContinuousLinearMap.ofTendstoOfBoundedRange` and

+`Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Operator/Completeness.lean`.

+/-- Over Tate scalars, continuous linear maps between seminormed modules form a seminormed group
+for the operator norm. -/
+noncomputable scoped instance seminormedAddCommGroup : SeminormedAddCommGroup (E →L[R] F) :=
+  AddGroupSeminorm.toSeminormedAddCommGroup
+    { toFun := norm
+      map_zero' := ringOpNorm_zero
+      add_le' := ringOpNorm_add_le
+      neg' := ringOpNorm_neg }

+  IsUltrametricDist.isUltrametricDist_of_forall_norm_add_le_max_norm ringOpNorm_add_le_max

+commutative `R` this makes `E →L[R] F` an `R`-module with contractive action. -/
+scoped instance isBoundedSMul {S : Type*} [SeminormedAddCommGroup S] [DistribSMul S F]
+    [IsBoundedSMul S F] [SMulCommClass R S F] : IsBoundedSMul S (E →L[R] F) where
+  dist_smul_pair' c f g := by
+    simpa [dist_eq_norm, ← smul_sub] using ringOpNorm_smul_le c (f - g)
+  dist_pair_smul' a b f := by
+    -- Without a right distributive law, bound `a • f - b • f` pointwise through the action on `F`.
+    rw [dist_zero_right, dist_eq_norm]
+    refine ringOpNorm_le_bound _ (by positivity) fun x ↦ ?_
+    calc ‖(a • f - b • f) x‖ = dist (a • f x) (b • f x) := by simp [dist_eq_norm]
+      _ ≤ dist a b * ‖f x‖ := by simpa using dist_pair_smul a b (f x)
+      _ ≤ dist a b * ‖f‖ * ‖x‖ := by
+        rw [mul_assoc]; gcongr; exact le_ringOpNorm f x
+
+/-- Evaluation `(f, x) ↦ f x` is jointly continuous for the operator norm. -/
+scoped instance continuousEval : ContinuousEval (E →L[R] F) E F where
+  continuous_eval := continuous_iff_continuousAt.2 fun ⟨f, x⟩ ↦ by
+    rw [ContinuousAt, tendsto_iff_norm_sub_tendsto_zero]
+    -- `g y - f x = (g - f) y + f (y - x)`, and both terms are controlled by operator norms.
+    refine squeeze_zero (fun _ ↦ norm_nonneg _) (fun p ↦ ?_)
+      (g := fun p : (E →L[R] F) × E ↦ ‖p.1 - f‖ * ‖p.2‖ + ‖f‖ * ‖p.2 - x‖) ?_
+    · calc ‖p.1 p.2 - f x‖ = ‖(p.1 - f) p.2 + f (p.2 - x)‖ := by simp
+        _ ≤ ‖p.1 - f‖ * ‖p.2‖ + ‖f‖ * ‖p.2 - x‖ :=
+          norm_add_le_of_le (le_ringOpNorm _ _) (le_ringOpNorm _ _)
+    · simpa using ((by fun_prop : Continuous fun p : (E →L[R] F) × E ↦
+        ‖p.1 - f‖ * ‖p.2‖ + ‖f‖ * ‖p.2 - x‖).tendsto (f, x))
+
+/-- Over Tate scalars the continuous endomorphisms of a seminormed module form a seminormed ring
+for the operator norm. -/
+noncomputable scoped instance seminormedRing : SeminormedRing (E →L[R] E) :=
+  { seminormedAddCommGroup, ContinuousLinearMap.ring with
+    norm_mul_le := ringOpNorm_comp_le }
+
+/-- The identity has operator norm one on a module with a vector of nonzero norm. -/
+scoped instance normOneClass [NontrivialTopology E] : NormOneClass (E →L[R] E) :=
+  ⟨ringOpNorm_id⟩
+
+end Seminormed
+
+section Normed
+
+variable {R E F : Type*} [SeminormedRing R] [NormedRing.IsTate R]
+  [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [Module R E] [IsBoundedSMul R E]
+  [NormedAddCommGroup F] [Module R F] [IsBoundedSMul R F]
+
+/-- Over Tate scalars, continuous linear maps into a normed module form a normed group for the
+operator norm. -/
+noncomputable scoped instance normedAddCommGroup : NormedAddCommGroup (E →L[R] F) :=
+  NormedAddCommGroup.ofSeparation fun f hf ↦ ContinuousLinearMap.ext fun x ↦
+    norm_le_zero_iff.mp <| by simpa [hf] using le_ringOpNorm f x
+
+/-- Over Tate scalars the continuous endomorphisms of a normed module form a normed ring for the
+operator norm. -/
+noncomputable scoped instance normedRing {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [Module R E]
+    [IsBoundedSMul R E] : NormedRing (E →L[R] E) :=
+  { normedAddCommGroup, seminormedRing with }
+
+/-- **Completeness of the operator space.** Over Tate scalars, continuous linear maps into a
+complete normed module form a complete space for the operator norm. -/
+scoped instance completeSpace [CompleteSpace F] : CompleteSpace (E →L[R] F) := by
+  refine Metric.complete_of_cauchySeq_tendsto fun f hf ↦ ?_
+  -- The sequence is pointwise Cauchy, so it has a pointwise limit `g`.
+  have hfx (x : E) : CauchySeq fun n ↦ f n x := by
+    have : LipschitzWith ‖x‖₊ fun g : E →L[R] F ↦ g x := .of_dist_le_mul fun g h ↦ by
+      simpa [dist_eq_norm, mul_comm] using le_ringOpNorm (g - h) x
+    exact this.uniformContinuous.comp_cauchySeq hf
+  choose g hg using fun x ↦ cauchySeq_tendsto_of_complete (hfx x)
+  -- The pointwise limit is linear, and bounded by a bound on the operator norms of the `f n`.
+  obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := isBounded_iff_forall_norm_le.1 hf.isBounded_range
+  have hglim : Tendsto (fun n x ↦ f n x) atTop (𝓝 g) := tendsto_pi_nhds.2 hg
+  let G : E →L[R] F :=
+    (linearMapOfTendsto g (fun n ↦ (f n : E →ₗ[R] F)) hglim).mkContinuousOfExistsBound

+        le_of_ringOpNorm_le _ (hC _ ⟨n, rfl⟩) x⟩
+  refine ⟨G, ?_⟩

+  obtain ⟨b, hb₀, hfb, hb_lim⟩ := cauchySeq_iff_le_tendsto_0.1 hf
+  refine tendsto_iff_norm_sub_tendsto_zero.2 <| squeeze_zero (fun _ ↦ norm_nonneg _)
+    (fun n ↦ ringOpNorm_le_bound _ (hb₀ n) fun x ↦ ?_) hb_lim
+  refine le_of_tendsto ((tendsto_const_nhds (x := f n x)).sub (hg x)).norm
+    (eventually_atTop.2 ⟨n, fun m hm ↦ ?_⟩)
+  rw [← sub_apply]
+  exact le_of_ringOpNorm_le _ (by simpa [dist_eq_norm] using hfb n m n le_rfl hm) x

+normed group structure on continuous linear maps. -/
+theorem seminormedAddCommGroup_eq {K E F : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField K]
+    [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace K E] [SeminormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace K F] :
+    (seminormedAddCommGroup : SeminormedAddCommGroup (E →L[K] F)) =
+      ContinuousLinearMap.toSeminormedAddCommGroup := by
+  -- Two seminormed group structures with the same norm and group laws agree.

+      a.toNorm = b.toNorm → a.toAddCommGroup = b.toAddCommGroup → a = b from

+    ext x y
+    rw [ha, hb]
+  rfl

+  exact TauCeti.norm_inverse_one_sub ht

+module
+
+public import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function

+/-!
+# The Hopf–Lax formula and its subsolution inequality
+
+For a Lagrangian `L : E → ℝ` and an initial datum `φ : E → ℝ` on a real vector space, the
+*Hopf–Lax formula*
+
+`u (t, x) = inf_y (φ y + t L ((x - y) / t))`
+
+defines, for `t > 0`, the value function of the control problem with running cost `L` and initial
+cost `φ`. For convex `L` it is the candidate solution of the Hamilton–Jacobi equation
+`∂ₜ u + H (∇ₓ u) = 0` with `H` the convex conjugate of `L`. This file proves the inequality that
+makes `u` a subsolution of that equation without any differentiability:
+
+`u (t + h, x + h w) ≤ u (t, x) + h L w` for `t > 0`, `h ≥ 0` and every velocity `w`.
+
+It is the statement that moving at velocity `w` for time `h` costs at most `h L w`. At a point where
+`u` is differentiable it gives `∂ₜ u + ⟨∇ₓ u, w⟩ ≤ L w` for every `w`, that is
+`∂ₜ u + H (∇ₓ u) ≤ 0`, and the inequality survives averaging `u` against a probability kernel in
+space-time. This is the form in which Hopf–Lax functions are tested against solutions of the
+continuity equation to bound transport costs by the kinetic action, as in the lower bound of the
+Benamou–Brenier formula for the cost `L w = ‖w‖ ^ p`.
+
+The infimum is taken in `ℝ`, so the results assume `φ` and `L` bounded below, which makes it finite
+for `t ≥ 0`. At `t = 0` the formula degenerates to the infimum of `φ`; the Hopf–Lax function
+recovers `φ` as a limit `t → 0⁺` only under additional hypotheses. That limit, and times `t ≤ 0`,
+are not studied here.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `TauCeti.hopfLax L φ t x`: the Hopf–Lax value `inf_y (φ y + t L (t⁻¹ (x - y)))`.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `TauCeti.hopfLax_le` and `TauCeti.le_hopfLax_iff`: the Hopf–Lax value is the greatest lower bound
+  of the penalized values.
+* `TauCeti.hopfLax_mono`: the Hopf–Lax value is monotone in the initial datum.
+* `TauCeti.hopfLax_le_add_mul` and `TauCeti.add_mul_le_hopfLax`: the bounds
+  `m + t l ≤ u (t, x) ≤ φ x + t L 0` for lower bounds `m` of `φ` and `l` of `L`.
+* `TauCeti.hopfLax_add_add_smul_le`: the subsolution inequality
+  `u (t + h, x + h w) ≤ u (t, x) + h L w` for convex `L`.
+* `TauCeti.antitoneOn_hopfLax`: for convex `L` with `L 0 ≤ 0`, `u (t, x)` decreases in `t > 0`.
+* `TauCeti.upperSemicontinuousOn_hopfLax`: for continuous `L`, `u` is jointly upper semicontinuous
+  on the open half-space `t > 0`.
+* `TauCeti.hopfLax_norm_rpow` and `TauCeti.hopfLax_norm_rpow_add_add_smul_le`: for the cost
+  `L w = ‖w‖ ^ p`, the formula reads `u (t, x) = inf_y (φ y + ‖x - y‖ ^ p / t ^ (p - 1))`, and the
+  subsolution inequality holds for `1 ≤ p`.
+
+## References
+
+* L. C. Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, 2nd ed., Graduate Studies in Mathematics 19,
+  American Mathematical Society 2010, §3.3.2, on the Hopf–Lax formula.
+* C. Villani, *Optimal Transport: Old and New*, Grundlehren 338, Springer 2009, Chapter 7.
+-/

+public section
+
+noncomputable section
+
+open Set
+
+namespace TauCeti

+section Module
+
+variable {E : Type*} [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E] {L φ : E → ℝ} {t h : ℝ}
+
+/-- The *Hopf–Lax value* `inf_y (φ y + t L (t⁻¹ (x - y)))` of the initial datum `φ` for the
+Lagrangian `L` at time `t` and position `x`. The infimum is taken in `ℝ`; it is the honest infimum
+when `φ` and `L` are bounded below and `t ≥ 0`. -/
+def hopfLax (L φ : E → ℝ) (t : ℝ) (x : E) : ℝ :=
+  ⨅ y, φ y + t * L (t⁻¹ • (x - y))
+
+/-- The defining formula of the Hopf–Lax value. -/
+theorem hopfLax_def (L φ : E → ℝ) (t : ℝ) (x : E) :
+    hopfLax L φ t x = ⨅ y, φ y + t * L (t⁻¹ • (x - y)) :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- At time `1` the Hopf–Lax value is the infimal convolution `inf_y (φ y + L (x - y))`. -/

+module
+
+public import TauCeti.Analysis.Sobolev.LipschitzDomain.Basic

+public import TauCeti.MeasureTheory.Function.AreaFormula.Lipschitz

+/-!
+# Surface measure in a Lipschitz boundary chart
+
+A Lipschitz boundary chart parametrizes the part of the frontier inside its cylinder by
+
+`y ↦ e.symm (normalGraphEmbedding φ y)`.
+
+This file identifies the image of that parametrization and compares tangential Lebesgue measure
+with normalized Euclidean Hausdorff measure on the frontier. It also gives the weighted area
+formula in chart coordinates. These results are the measure-theoretic bridge from local Sobolev
+traces in graph coordinates to traces on the boundary itself.
+
+## Main declarations
+
+* `Set.IsLipschitzChartWith.image_boundaryParametrization`: the chart parametrization covers
+  exactly the frontier inside the chart cylinder.
+* `Set.IsLipschitzChartWith.volume_le_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_frontier_inter`: surface measure
+  dominates tangential volume in a chart.
+* `Set.IsLipschitzChartWith.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_frontier_inter_le`: the converse estimate,
+  with explicit dependence on the Lipschitz constant.
+* `Set.IsLipschitzChartWith.lintegral_frontier_inter_eq`: the weighted area formula in chart
+  coordinates.
+
+## References
+
+* L. C. Evans and R. F. Gariepy, *Measure Theory and Fine Properties of Functions*, revised ed.,
+  §3.3 (the area formula and Lipschitz graphs).
+* W. McLean, *Strongly Elliptic Systems and Boundary Integral Equations*, §3.1.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+noncomputable section
+
+open MeasureTheory Module Set
+open scoped ENNReal NNReal
+
+namespace Set.IsLipschitzChartWith
+
+variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
+  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
+
+section NormedTarget
+
+variable {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
+  [MeasurableSpace F] [BorelSpace F]
+  {Omega : Set F} {L : ℝ≥0} {e : F ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] WithLp 2 (ℝ × E)} {phi : E → ℝ} {a b : ℝ}
+
+omit [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace F] [BorelSpace F] in
+/-- The tangential parameters whose graph points lie in the cylinder of a boundary chart form
+an open, hence measurable, set. -/
+theorem measurableSet_normalGraphEmbedding_preimage_normalCylinder
+    (h : Omega.IsLipschitzChartWith L e phi a b) :
+    MeasurableSet (TauCeti.normalGraphEmbedding phi ⁻¹' TauCeti.normalCylinder a b) :=
+  ((TauCeti.isOpen_normalCylinder a b).preimage
+    h.lipschitzWith.normalGraphEmbedding.continuous).measurableSet
+
+omit [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
+  [MeasurableSpace F] [BorelSpace F] in
+/-- The graph parametrization of a Lipschitz boundary chart is Lipschitz, with the same bound
+as the normal graph parametrization. -/
+theorem lipschitzWith_boundaryParametrization (h : Omega.IsLipschitzChartWith L e phi a b) :
+    LipschitzWith (L + 1) (fun y ↦ e.symm (TauCeti.normalGraphEmbedding phi y)) := by
+  refine LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul fun x y ↦ ?_
+  rw [e.symm.isometry.dist_eq]
+  exact h.lipschitzWith.normalGraphEmbedding.dist_le_mul x y
+
+omit [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
+  [MeasurableSpace F] [BorelSpace F] in
+/-- A Lipschitz chart parametrizes exactly the part of the frontier lying inside its cylinder. -/
+theorem image_boundaryParametrization (h : Omega.IsLipschitzChartWith L e phi a b) :
+    (fun y ↦ e.symm (TauCeti.normalGraphEmbedding phi y)) ''
+        (TauCeti.normalGraphEmbedding phi ⁻¹' TauCeti.normalCylinder a b) =
+      frontier Omega ∩ e ⁻¹' TauCeti.normalCylinder a b := by
+  ext x
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩
+    have hz : TauCeti.normalGraphEmbedding phi y ∈
+        e '' frontier Omega ∩ TauCeti.normalCylinder a b := by
+      rw [h.toIsLipschitzChart.image_frontier_inter_normalCylinder]
+      exact ⟨by simp, hy⟩
+    obtain ⟨z, hzF, hze⟩ := hz.1
+    have hzx : z = e.symm (TauCeti.normalGraphEmbedding phi y) := by
+      rw [← hze, e.symm_apply_apply]
+    have hxF : e.symm (TauCeti.normalGraphEmbedding phi y) ∈ frontier Omega := by
+      rw [← hzx]
+      exact hzF
+    exact ⟨hxF, by simpa using hz.2⟩
+  · rintro ⟨hx, hxC⟩
+    have hz : e x ∈ {z | z.fst = phi z.snd} ∩ TauCeti.normalCylinder a b := by
+      rw [← h.toIsLipschitzChart.image_frontier_inter_normalCylinder]
+      exact ⟨⟨x, hx, rfl⟩, hxC⟩
+    have hgraph : TauCeti.normalGraphEmbedding phi (e x).snd = e x :=
+      (WithLp.ext_iff 2).2 <| Prod.ext (by simpa using hz.1.symm) (by simp)
+    refine ⟨(e x).snd, ?_, ?_⟩
+    · simpa [hgraph] using hz.2
+    · apply e.injective
+      rw [e.apply_symm_apply, hgraph]
+
+/-- In a Lipschitz boundary chart, normalized surface measure dominates tangential Lebesgue
+measure. -/
+theorem volume_le_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_frontier_inter
+    (h : Omega.IsLipschitzChartWith L e phi a b) :
+    volume (TauCeti.normalGraphEmbedding phi ⁻¹' TauCeti.normalCylinder a b) ≤
+      μHE[finrank ℝ E] (frontier Omega ∩ e ⁻¹' TauCeti.normalCylinder a b) := by
+  rw [← h.image_boundaryParametrization]
+  rw [← image_image]
+  rw [e.symm.isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image]
+  exact TauCeti.volume_le_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_normalGraphEmbedding_image phi _
+
+/-- In a Lipschitz boundary chart, normalized surface measure is at most
+`(L + 1) ^ dim E` times tangential Lebesgue measure. -/
+theorem euclideanHausdorffMeasure_frontier_inter_le
+    (h : Omega.IsLipschitzChartWith L e phi a b) :
+    μHE[finrank ℝ E] (frontier Omega ∩ e ⁻¹' TauCeti.normalCylinder a b) ≤
+      ((L + 1 : ℝ≥0) : ℝ≥0∞) ^ finrank ℝ E *
+        volume (TauCeti.normalGraphEmbedding phi ⁻¹' TauCeti.normalCylinder a b) := by
+  rw [← h.image_boundaryParametrization]
+  rw [← image_image]
+  rw [e.symm.isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image]
+  exact h.lipschitzWith.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_normalGraphEmbedding_image_le _
+
+/-- A set of tangential parameters is Lebesgue-null exactly when the corresponding part of the
+boundary chart is null for normalized surface measure. -/
+theorem euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_boundaryParametrization_eq_zero_iff
+    (h : Omega.IsLipschitzChartWith L e phi a b) (s : Set E) :
+    μHE[finrank ℝ E]
+        ((fun y ↦ e.symm (TauCeti.normalGraphEmbedding phi y)) '' s) = 0 ↔
+      volume s = 0 := by
+  rw [← image_image]
+  rw [e.symm.isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image]
+  exact h.lipschitzWith.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_normalGraphEmbedding_image_eq_zero_iff s
+
+/-- The frontier patch in a Lipschitz boundary chart has zero normalized surface measure exactly
+when its set of tangential parameters has zero Lebesgue measure. -/
+theorem euclideanHausdorffMeasure_frontier_inter_eq_zero_iff
+    (h : Omega.IsLipschitzChartWith L e phi a b) :
+    μHE[finrank ℝ E] (frontier Omega ∩ e ⁻¹' TauCeti.normalCylinder a b) = 0 ↔
+      volume (TauCeti.normalGraphEmbedding phi ⁻¹' TauCeti.normalCylinder a b) = 0 := by
+  rw [← h.image_boundaryParametrization]
+  exact h.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_boundaryParametrization_eq_zero_iff _
+
+end NormedTarget
+
+section EuclideanTarget
+
+variable {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace ℝ F]
+  [FiniteDimensional ℝ F] [MeasurableSpace F] [BorelSpace F]
+  {Omega : Set F} {L : ℝ≥0} {e : F ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] WithLp 2 (ℝ × E)} {phi : E → ℝ} {a b : ℝ}
+
+/-- **Weighted area formula in a Lipschitz boundary chart.** Surface integration over the part
+of the frontier inside the chart cylinder is integration over its tangential parameters, weighted
+by the geometric Jacobian of the boundary parametrization. The weight need not be measurable. -/
+theorem lintegral_frontier_inter_eq (h : Omega.IsLipschitzChartWith L e phi a b)
+    (g : F → ℝ≥0∞) :
+    ∫⁻ x in frontier Omega ∩ e ⁻¹' TauCeti.normalCylinder a b, g x ∂μHE[finrank ℝ E] =
+      ∫⁻ y in TauCeti.normalGraphEmbedding phi ⁻¹' TauCeti.normalCylinder a b,
+        ENNReal.ofReal
+            (fderiv ℝ (fun z ↦ e.symm (TauCeti.normalGraphEmbedding phi z)) y).normDet *
+          g (e.symm (TauCeti.normalGraphEmbedding phi y)) := by
+  rw [← h.image_boundaryParametrization]
+  exact (h.lipschitzWith_boundaryParametrization.lintegral_image_eq_lintegral_normDet_fderiv_mul
+    h.measurableSet_normalGraphEmbedding_preimage_normalCylinder
+      (e.symm.injective.comp (TauCeti.injective_normalGraphEmbedding phi)).injOn g)
+
+end EuclideanTarget
+
+end Set.IsLipschitzChartWith

+        ((hf (e.symm z) (hcl z hzC hz)).comp e.symm.continuous.continuousWithinAt
+          fun w hw => hcl w hw.2 hw.1)
+    · have hzero : G =ᶠ[𝓝 z] fun _ => 0 := by
+        filter_upwards [((isClosed_tsupport ψ).isOpen_compl.preimage e.symm.continuous).mem_nhds
+          hzs] with w hw

+      (normalEpigraph ⟨φ, h.lipschitzWith.continuous⟩ : Set (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E)))] G := by

+module
