+public import TauCeti.Analysis.Sobolev.LipschitzDomain.SurfaceMeasure
+public import TauCeti.Analysis.Sobolev.LipschitzDomain.Trace.Basic
+
+/-!
+# Local Sobolev traces and surface measure
+
+The localized Sobolev trace in a Lipschitz boundary chart is constructed as an `L²` function on
+the tangential parameter space. Surface measure on the chart graph and tangential Lebesgue measure
+have the same null sets. Consequently, the chart trace can also be read almost everywhere on the
+frontier by evaluating it at the tangential coordinate of each boundary point.
+
+For a Sobolev function represented by a function continuous up to the boundary, this
+surface-measure interpretation agrees almost everywhere with the classical boundary value of the
+localized function. This is the compatibility needed to patch the local chart traces into a global
+trace on the frontier.
+
+## Main declaration
+
+* `TauCeti.W1p.lipschitzChartTrace_comp_snd_ae_of_continuousOn`: the localized chart trace of a
+  continuous Sobolev representative agrees with its classical value almost everywhere for
+  normalized Euclidean Hausdorff measure on the frontier patch.
+
+## References
+
+* L. C. Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, 2nd ed., §5.5, Theorem 1.
+* J. Nečas, *Direct Methods in the Theory of Elliptic Equations*, Chapter 2.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+noncomputable section
+
+open MeasureTheory Module Set TopologicalSpace
+open scoped ENNReal NNReal ContDiff Gradient
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
+  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
+  {Omega : Opens (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))} {L : ℝ≥0}
+  {e : WithLp 2 (ℝ × E) ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] WithLp 2 (ℝ × E)} {phi : E → ℝ} {a b : ℝ}
+  {psi : WithLp 2 (ℝ × E) → ℝ} {M : ℝ}
+
+/-- **The local trace agrees with classical boundary values in surface measure.** If
+`u ∈ H¹(Ω)` agrees almost everywhere with a function `f` continuous on `closure Ω`, then the
+localized trace through a Lipschitz boundary chart, read at the tangential coordinate of a
+boundary point, equals `ψ * f` almost everywhere on the part of the frontier in that chart. -/
+theorem W1p.lipschitzChartTrace_comp_snd_ae_of_continuousOn
+    (h : (Omega : Set (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))).IsLipschitzChartWith L e phi a b)
+    (hpsi : ContDiff ℝ ∞ psi) (hM : 0 ≤ M)
+    (hpsiM : ∀ x ∈ Omega, |psi x| ≤ M) (hgM : ∀ x ∈ Omega, ‖∇ psi x‖ ≤ M)
+    (hs : tsupport psi ⊆ e ⁻¹' normalCylinder a b) {u : W1p volume Omega 2}
+    {f : WithLp 2 (ℝ × E) → ℝ}
+    (hf : ContinuousOn f (closure (Omega : Set (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E)))))
+    (hu : W1p.value u =ᵐ[volume.restrict (Omega : Set (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E)))] f) :
+    ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[finrank ℝ E] : Measure (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))).restrict
+        (frontier (Omega : Set (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))) ∩ e ⁻¹' normalCylinder a b),
+      W1p.lipschitzChartTrace h psi hpsi hM hpsiM hgM hs u (e x).snd = psi x * f x := by
+  let bad : Set E := {y |
+    W1p.lipschitzChartTrace h psi hpsi hM hpsiM hgM hs u y ≠
+      psi (e.symm (normalGraphEmbedding phi y)) * f (e.symm (normalGraphEmbedding phi y))}
+  have hparameter : volume bad = 0 := by
+    rw [← ae_iff]
+    simpa only [bad, mem_ofPred_eq, not_not] using
+      W1p.lipschitzChartTrace_apply_ae_of_continuousOn h hpsi hM hpsiM hgM hs hf hu
+  have hsurface :
+      μHE[finrank ℝ E]
+          ((fun y ↦ e.symm (normalGraphEmbedding phi y)) '' bad) = 0 :=
+    (h.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_boundaryParametrization_eq_zero_iff bad).2 hparameter
+  have hpatch : MeasurableSet
+      (frontier (Omega : Set (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))) ∩ e ⁻¹' normalCylinder a b) :=
+    isClosed_frontier.measurableSet.inter
+      ((isOpen_normalCylinder a b).preimage e.continuous).measurableSet
+  refine (ae_restrict_iff' hpatch).2 ?_
+  rw [ae_iff]
+  apply measure_mono_null ?_ hsurface
+  intro x hx
+  simp only [mem_ofPred_eq, not_imp] at hx
+  have hximage : x ∈ (fun y ↦ e.symm (normalGraphEmbedding phi y)) ''
+      (normalGraphEmbedding phi ⁻¹' normalCylinder a b) := by
+    rw [h.image_boundaryParametrization]
+    exact hx.1
+  obtain ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩ := hximage
+  refine ⟨y, ?_, rfl⟩
+  simpa only [bad, mem_ofPred_eq, e.apply_symm_apply, normalGraphEmbedding_snd] using hx.2
+
+end TauCeti

+module
+
+public import TauCeti.Analysis.Sobolev.Trace.Multiplication
+public import TauCeti.Analysis.Sobolev.Trace.Epigraph.Basic
+import TauCeti.Analysis.Sobolev.W1p.Mollification
+import TauCeti.Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.Cutoff
+import TauCeti.MeasureTheory.Measure.Haar.InnerProductSpace
+import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.Convolution
+import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.ConvergenceInMeasure
+
+/-!
+# Traces of continuous Sobolev functions
+
+The flat, half-space and graph traces of `H¹` functions are defined abstractly, as continuous
+extensions of restriction from test functions. This file proves that they are the classical
+boundary values whenever the function is continuous up to the boundary.
+
+* `TauCeti.W1p.hyperplaneTrace_apply_ae_of_continuous`: if `u ∈ H¹(ℝ × E)` has a continuous
+  representative `f`, its trace on `{a} × E` is `y ↦ f (a, y)` almost everywhere.
+* `TauCeti.W1p.halfSpaceTrace_apply_ae_of_continuousOn`: if `u ∈ H¹` of the half-space
+  `{a < t}` agrees almost everywhere with a function continuous on the closed half-space
+  `{a ≤ t}`, its trace is the restriction of that function to `{a} × E`.
+* `TauCeti.W1p.normalEpigraphTrace_apply_ae_of_continuousOn`: if `u ∈ H¹` of the region above
+  the graph of a Lipschitz function `φ` agrees almost everywhere with a function `f` continuous
+  on the closed region `{φ y ≤ t}`, its graph trace is `y ↦ f (φ y, y)`.
+
+For a compactly supported continuous representative, mollification produces test functions
+converging to `u` in `H¹` and to `f` pointwise; their traces are their restrictions and
+converge in `L²`, so a subsequence converges almost everywhere and the two limits agree. The
+general whole-space case follows by multiplying with cutoffs, using that the trace commutes
+with smooth multipliers. On the half-space, the even reflection extension of a function
+continuous up to the boundary is continuous; on a graph domain, flattening is a homeomorphism
+of the closed regions.
+
+Together with density of functions smooth up to the boundary, this identification is what
+makes traces taken in overlapping boundary charts agree.
+
+## References
+
+* L. C. Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, 2nd ed., §5.5, Theorem 1 (the trace of a
+  function continuous up to the boundary is its restriction).
+* H. Brezis, *Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and Partial Differential Equations*, §9.3.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+noncomputable section
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+open MeasureTheory Set TopologicalSpace Filter Topology
+open scoped Convolution Distributions ENNReal Gradient
+
+variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
+  [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
+
+/-! ### The flat trace -/
+
+/-- The whole-space restriction of volume is an additive Haar measure. -/
+local instance :
+    ((volume : Measure (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))).restrict
+      ((⊤ : Opens (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))) : Set (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E)))).IsAddHaarMeasure := by
+  rw [Opens.coe_top, Measure.restrict_univ]
+  infer_instance
+
+/-- The flat trace of a whole-space `H¹` function with a continuous compactly supported
+representative is its restriction. Mollifications are test functions whose traces are their
+restrictions; they converge to `u` in `H¹` and to `f` pointwise. -/
+private theorem hyperplaneTrace_apply_ae_of_hasCompactSupport (a : ℝ)
+    {u : W1p (volume : Measure (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))) ⊤ 2} {f : WithLp 2 (ℝ × E) → ℝ}
+    (hf : Continuous f) (hfc : HasCompactSupport f) (hu : W1p.value u =ᵐ[volume] f) :
+    ∀ᵐ y ∂(volume : Measure E), W1p.hyperplaneTrace a u y = f (WithLp.toLp 2 (a, y)) := by
+  let phi : ℕ → ContDiffBump (0 : WithLp 2 (ℝ × E)) := fun k =>
+    ⟨1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1) / 2, 1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1), by positivity, half_lt_self (by positivity)⟩
+  have hphi : Tendsto (fun k => (phi k).rOut) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
+    tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat
+  let conv : ℕ → WithLp 2 (ℝ × E) → ℝ := fun k =>
+    (phi k).normed volume ⋆[ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ, volume] f
+  -- The jet of `u` vanishes off the support of `f`.
+  have hjet : ∀ᵐ x ∂(volume : Measure (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))).restrict
+      ((⊤ : Opens (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))) : Set (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))),
+      x ∉ tsupport f → (u : Sobolev1JetLp (volume : Measure (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))) ⊤ 2) x = 0 := by
+    let V : Opens (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E)) := ⟨(tsupport f)ᶜ, (isClosed_tsupport f).isOpen_compl⟩
+    have hV : ∀ᵐ x ∂(volume : Measure (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))).restrict (V : Set _),
+        W1p.value u x = 0 := by
+      filter_upwards [ae_restrict_of_ae hu, ae_restrict_mem V.isOpen.measurableSet] with x hx hxV
+      rw [hx]
+      exact image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport hxV
+    exact ae_restrict_of_ae <| (ae_restrict_iff' V.isOpen.measurableSet).1
+      (W1p.coe_ae_eq_zero_of_value_ae_eq_zero (le_top : V ≤ ⊤) hV)
+  choose Φ hΦ using fun k => W1p.normedBumpL_mem_range_of_ae_eq_zero (by norm_num) (phi k)
+    hfc hjet
+  -- Each mollification is the test function `Φ k`, which is the pointwise convolution.
+  have hΦconv (k : ℕ) : (Φ k : WithLp 2 (ℝ × E) → ℝ) = conv k := by
+    have hmem : MemLp f 2 ((volume : Measure (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))).restrict
+        ((⊤ : Opens (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))) : Set (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E)))) := by
+      rw [Opens.coe_top, Measure.restrict_univ]
+      exact hf.memLp_of_hasCompactSupport hfc
+    have hval : W1p.value u = hmem.toLp f := by
+      apply Lp.ext
+      filter_upwards [hmem.coeFn_toLp, ae_restrict_of_ae (s := univ) hu] with x h1 h2
+      rw [h1, h2]
+    have h1 := normedBumpLp_ae_eq_convolution (by norm_num) (phi k) hmem
+    have h2 := W1p.value_ofTestFunctionₗ (mu := volume) (Omega := ⊤) (p := 2) (Φ k)
+    have h3 := testFunctionLp_apply_ae (mu := (volume : Measure (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E)))) 2 (Φ k)
+    rw [hΦ k, W1p.value_normedBumpL, hval] at h2
+    rw [← h2] at h3
+    simp only [Opens.coe_top, Measure.restrict_univ] at h1 h3
+    refine (Continuous.ae_eq_iff_eq volume (Φ k).continuous ?_).1 ?_
+    · exact (phi k).hasCompactSupport_normed.continuous_convolution_left _
+        (phi k).continuous_normed hf.locallyIntegrable
+    · filter_upwards [h1, h3] with x h1 h3
+      rw [← h3, h1]
+  have htend : Tendsto (fun k => W1p.hyperplaneTrace a (W1p.normedBumpL (by norm_num) (phi k) u))
+      atTop (𝓝 (W1p.hyperplaneTrace a u)) :=
+    ((W1p.hyperplaneTrace a).continuous.tendsto u).comp (W1p.tendsto_normedBumpL _ hphi u)
+  obtain ⟨ns, hns, hae⟩ := (tendstoInMeasure_of_tendsto_Lp htend).exists_seq_tendsto_ae
+  have htest : ∀ᵐ y ∂(volume : Measure E), ∀ k,
+      W1p.hyperplaneTrace a (W1p.normedBumpL (by norm_num) (phi k) u) y =
+        conv k (WithLp.toLp 2 (a, y)) := by
+    rw [ae_all_iff]
+    intro k
+    rw [← hΦ k, ← hΦconv k]
+    exact W1p.hyperplaneTrace_ofTestFunction_apply_ae a (Φ k)
+  filter_upwards [hae, htest] with y hy hk
+  refine tendsto_nhds_unique hy ?_
+  simp only [hk]
+  exact (ContDiffBump.convolution_tendsto_right_of_continuous hphi hf _).comp
+    hns.tendsto_atTop
+
+/-- **The flat trace of a continuous Sobolev function is its restriction.** If a whole-space
+`H¹` function `u` is represented almost everywhere by a continuous function `f`, then its trace
+on the hyperplane `{a} × E` is `y ↦ f (a, y)` almost everywhere. -/
+theorem W1p.hyperplaneTrace_apply_ae_of_continuous (a : ℝ)
+    {u : W1p (volume : Measure (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))) ⊤ 2} {f : WithLp 2 (ℝ × E) → ℝ}
+    (hf : Continuous f) (hu : W1p.value u =ᵐ[volume] f) :
+    ∀ᵐ y ∂(volume : Measure E), W1p.hyperplaneTrace a u y = f (WithLp.toLp 2 (a, y)) := by
+  have key (n : ℕ) : ∀ᵐ y ∂(volume : Measure E), ‖WithLp.toLp 2 (a, y)‖ < n →
+      W1p.hyperplaneTrace a u y = f (WithLp.toLp 2 (a, y)) := by
+    obtain ⟨ψ, M, hψ, -, hone, hψc, -, hM, hψM, hgM⟩ :=
+      (isCompact_closedBall (0 : WithLp 2 (ℝ × E)) n).exists_contDiff_cutoff_with_bounds
+        isOpen_univ (subset_univ _)
+    have hv := W1p.value_contDiffSMul_ae hψ hM (fun x _ => hψM x) (fun x _ => hgM x) u
+    simp only [Opens.coe_top, Measure.restrict_univ] at hv
+    have hcut := hyperplaneTrace_apply_ae_of_hasCompactSupport a (hψ.continuous.mul hf)
+      hψc.mul_right
+      (by filter_upwards [hv, hu] with x h1 h2; rw [h1, h2, smul_eq_mul, Pi.mul_apply])
+    filter_upwards [hcut, W1p.hyperplaneTrace_contDiffSMul_ae a hψ hψM hgM u] with y h1 h2 hy
+    have hψ1 : ψ (WithLp.toLp 2 (a, y)) = 1 :=
+      interior_subset (hone (mem_closedBall_zero_iff.2 hy.le))
+    rw [h2, hψ1, one_mul] at h1
+    rw [h1, Pi.mul_apply, hψ1, one_mul]
+  filter_upwards [ae_all_iff.2 key] with y hy
+  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := exists_nat_gt ‖WithLp.toLp 2 (a, y)‖
+  exact hy n hn
+
+/-! ### The half-space trace -/
+
+/-- **The half-space trace of a function continuous up to the boundary is its restriction.** If
+`u ∈ H¹` of the half-space `{a < t}` agrees almost everywhere with a function `f` continuous on
+the closed half-space `{a ≤ t}`, then the trace of `u` on `{a} × E` is `y ↦ f (a, y)` almost
+everywhere. -/
+theorem W1p.halfSpaceTrace_apply_ae_of_continuousOn (a : ℝ)
+    {u : W1p (volume : Measure (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))) (normalHalfSpace a) 2}
+    {f : WithLp 2 (ℝ × E) → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f {x | a ≤ x.fst})
+    (hu : W1p.value u =ᵐ[volume.restrict (normalHalfSpace (E := E) a)] f) :
+    ∀ᵐ y ∂(volume : Measure E), W1p.halfSpaceTrace a u y = f (WithLp.toLp 2 (a, y)) := by
+  -- The reflection extension is represented by `f` composed with the fold onto `{a ≤ t}`.
+  let fold : WithLp 2 (ℝ × E) → WithLp 2 (ℝ × E) := fun x =>
+    WithLp.toLp 2 (a + |x.fst - a|, x.snd)
+  have hfold : Continuous fold := by fun_prop
+  have hg : Continuous (f ∘ fold) :=
+    hf.comp_continuous hfold fun x => by simp [fold]
+  have hu' := (ae_restrict_iff' (normalHalfSpace (E := E) a).isOpen.measurableSet).1 hu
+  have hext : W1p.value (W1p.extendByReflectionL a u) =ᵐ[volume] f ∘ fold := by
+    filter_upwards [W1p.value_extendByReflectionL_ae a u, hu',
+      (measurePreserving_normalReflection (E := E) a).quasiMeasurePreserving.ae hu',
+      measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem.1 (Measure.addHaar_setOf_fst_eq (E := E) volume a)] with
+      x hx h1 h2 h3
+    rw [hx]
+    rcases lt_trichotomy a x.fst with hlt | heq | hgt
+    · have hxH : x ∈ (normalHalfSpace (E := E) a : Set (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))) :=
+        (mem_normalHalfSpace a x).2 hlt
+      have hρ : normalReflection E a x ∉ (normalHalfSpace (E := E) a : Set (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))) :=
+        fun h => (lt_asymm hlt) ((normalReflection_mem_normalHalfSpace_iff a x).1 h)
+      rw [indicator_of_mem hxH, indicator_of_notMem hρ, add_zero, h1 hxH, Function.comp_apply]
+      simp only [fold, abs_of_pos (sub_pos.2 hlt), add_sub_cancel]
+      rfl
+    · exact absurd heq.symm h3
+    · have hxH : x ∉ (normalHalfSpace (E := E) a : Set (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))) :=
+        fun h => lt_asymm hgt ((mem_normalHalfSpace a x).1 h)
+      have hρ : normalReflection E a x ∈ (normalHalfSpace (E := E) a : Set (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))) :=
+        (normalReflection_mem_normalHalfSpace_iff a x).2 hgt
+      rw [indicator_of_notMem hxH, indicator_of_mem hρ, zero_add, h2 hρ, Function.comp_apply]
+      congr 1
+      simp only [normalReflection_apply, fold, abs_of_neg (sub_neg.2 hgt)]
+      congr 2
+      ring
+  filter_upwards [W1p.hyperplaneTrace_apply_ae_of_continuous a hg hext] with y hy
+  rw [W1p.halfSpaceTrace_apply, hy]
+  simp [fold]
+
+/-! ### The trace on a Lipschitz graph -/
+
+/-- **The graph trace of a function continuous up to the graph is its restriction.** Let `φ` be
+Lipschitz. If `u ∈ H¹` of the region `{φ y < t}` above the graph agrees almost everywhere with a
+function `f` continuous on the closed region `{φ y ≤ t}`, then the trace of `u` is
+`y ↦ f (φ y, y)` almost everywhere. -/
+theorem W1p.normalEpigraphTrace_apply_ae_of_continuousOn {φ : C(E, ℝ)} {K : NNReal}
+    (hφ : LipschitzWith K φ) {u : W1p (volume : Measure (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E))) (normalEpigraph φ) 2}
+    {f : WithLp 2 (ℝ × E) → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f {x | φ x.snd ≤ x.fst})
+    (hu : W1p.value u =ᵐ[volume.restrict (normalEpigraph φ)] f) :
+    ∀ᵐ y ∂(volume : Measure E),
+      W1p.normalEpigraphTrace hφ u y = f (normalGraphEmbedding φ y) := by
+  set Φ := graphFlattening φ φ.continuous
+  have hg : ContinuousOn (f ∘ Φ.symm) {x | (0 : ℝ) ≤ x.fst} :=
+    hf.comp Φ.symm.continuous.continuousOn fun x hx => by
+      simpa [Φ] using hx
+  have hu' := (measurePreserving_graphFlattening_symm φ φ.continuous).quasiMeasurePreserving.ae
+    ((ae_restrict_iff' (normalEpigraph φ).isOpen.measurableSet).1 hu)
+  have hv : W1p.value (W1p.normalEpigraphEquivL hφ u) =ᵐ[volume.restrict
+      (normalHalfSpace (E := E) 0 : Set (WithLp 2 (ℝ × E)))] f ∘ Φ.symm := by
+    filter_upwards [W1p.value_normalEpigraphEquivL_ae hφ u, ae_restrict_of_ae hu',
+      ae_restrict_mem (normalHalfSpace (E := E) 0).isOpen.measurableSet] with x h1 h2 hx
+    rw [h1, Function.comp_apply]
+    refine h2 ?_
+    simpa [Φ] using hx
+  filter_upwards [W1p.halfSpaceTrace_apply_ae_of_continuousOn 0 hg hv] with y hy
+  have hγ : normalGraphEmbedding φ y = WithLp.toLp 2 (φ y, y) :=
+    (WithLp.ext_iff 2).2 (Prod.ext (normalGraphEmbedding_fst φ y) (normalGraphEmbedding_snd φ y))
+  rw [W1p.normalEpigraphTrace_apply, hy, hγ]
+  simp [Φ]
+
+end TauCeti

+public import TauCeti.CategoryTheory.DG.Functor.Basic
+public import TauCeti.CategoryTheory.DG.HomComplexData

+/-!
+# Twisted objects of a differential graded category
+
+A **twisted object** of a differential graded category `C` is an object `X` together with a
+degree-one endomorphism `δ` satisfying the Maurer–Cartan equation.  In Mathlib's enriched factor
+order, where `dgComp f g` is `f` followed by `g`, that equation reads
+
+`d δ = dgComp δ δ`.
+
+In Keller's order, `δ ∘ δ = (-1)^(1 * 1) • dgComp δ δ = -dgComp δ δ`, so it is the familiar
+`d δ + δ ∘ δ = 0`
+(`TauCeti.DGTwistedObject.dgDifferential_twist_add_negOnePow_smul_dgComp_eq_zero`).
+
+The twisted objects form a differential graded category `TauCeti.DGTwistedObject R C`.  A morphism
+`(X, δ_X) ⟶ (Y, δ_Y)` of degree `n` is a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of degree `n` in `C`, composition
+and identities are those of `C`, and the differential is twisted:
+
+`D f = d f + (-1)^n • dgComp f δ_Y - dgComp δ_X f`.
+
+In Keller's order this is `D f = d f + δ_Y ∘ f - (-1)^n • f ∘ δ_X`.  The twisted differential
+squares to zero exactly because of the Maurer–Cartan equations of `δ_X` and `δ_Y`: expanding
+`D (D f)` with the Leibniz rule and associativity leaves
+`dgComp f (d δ_Y - dgComp δ_Y δ_Y) - dgComp (d δ_X - dgComp δ_X δ_X) f`.  The Leibniz rule for `D`
+holds for arbitrary degree-one endomorphisms, by associativity alone.
+
+Twisted objects are the formal analogue of perturbing the differential of a complex by a
+degree-one endomorphism.  Applied to the additive
+closure of the shift closure of `C`, whose objects are formal sums `⊕ᵢ Xᵢ[rᵢ]`, the twisted
+objects with strictly upper-triangular twisting matrix are the one-sided twisted complexes of
+Bondal and Kapranov, which form the pretriangulated envelope of `C`.
+
+Every object `X` of `C` is a twisted object with zero twist, and `X ↦ (X, 0)` is a DG functor
+`TauCeti.DGTwistedObject.embedding` which is an isomorphism on Hom complexes.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `TauCeti.DGTwistedObject`: an object with a degree-one endomorphism satisfying the
+  Maurer–Cartan equation.
+* `TauCeti.DGTwistedObject.homComplexData`: the explicit Hom-complex data of twisted objects,
+  with the twisted differential.
+* `TauCeti.DGTwistedObject.dgHomEquiv`: degree-`n` morphisms of twisted objects are degree-`n`
+  morphisms of the underlying objects.
+* `TauCeti.DGTwistedObject.embedding`: the DG functor `X ↦ (X, 0)`.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `TauCeti.DGTwistedObject.dgHomEquiv_dgDifferential`: the differential is the twisted
+  differential `d f + (-1)^n • dgComp f δ_Y - dgComp δ_X f`.
+* `TauCeti.DGTwistedObject.dgHomEquiv_dgComp` and `TauCeti.DGTwistedObject.dgHomEquiv_dgId`:
+  composition and identities are those of `C`.
+* `TauCeti.DGTwistedObject.isIso_embedding_map`: the embedding is an isomorphism on Hom
+  complexes.
+
+## References
+
+* A. I. Bondal and M. M. Kapranov, *Enhanced triangulated categories*, Section 1.
+* V. Drinfeld, *DG quotients of DG categories*, Section 2.4.
+* B. Keller, *Introduction to A-infinity algebras and modules*, Section 7.6, for the twisting
+  equation `d δ + δ ∘ δ = 0` in Keller's order.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open CategoryTheory HomologicalComplex
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+universe v u
+
+/-- A **twisted object** of a differential graded category: an object `obj` with a degree-one
+endomorphism `twist` satisfying the Maurer–Cartan equation `d δ = dgComp δ δ`, which in Keller's
+order is `d δ + δ ∘ δ = 0`.  The twisted objects form a differential graded category whose Hom
+complexes carry the twisted differential; see `TauCeti.DGTwistedObject.homComplexData`. -/
+structure DGTwistedObject (R : Type v) [CommRing R] (C : Type u) [DGCategory R C] where
+  /-- The underlying object. -/
+  obj : C
+  /-- The twisting endomorphism `δ`, of degree one. -/
+  twist : DGHom R 1 obj obj
+  /-- The Maurer–Cartan equation `d δ = dgComp δ δ`, in Mathlib's enriched factor order. -/
+  dgDifferential_twist : dgDifferential R 1 twist = dgComp R twist twist rfl
+
+namespace DGTwistedObject
+
+attribute [simp] dgDifferential_twist
+
+variable (R : Type v) [CommRing R] {C : Type u} [DGCategory R C]
+
+/-- **The Maurer–Cartan equation in Keller's order**: `d δ + δ ∘ δ = 0`, where the
+Keller-ordered composite is `δ ∘ δ = (-1)^(1 * 1) • dgComp δ δ`. -/
+theorem dgDifferential_twist_add_negOnePow_smul_dgComp_eq_zero (X : DGTwistedObject R C) :
+    dgDifferential R 1 X.twist + ((1 : ℤ) * 1).negOnePow • dgComp R X.twist X.twist rfl = 0 := by
+  rw [dgDifferential_twist]
+  simp
+
+/-! ### The twisted differential -/
+
+/-- The twisted differential `D f = d f + (-1)^n • dgComp f δ_Y - dgComp δ_X f` on morphisms
+`X ⟶ Y` of degree `n`. -/
+private noncomputable def twistedDifferential (X Y : DGTwistedObject R C) (n : ℤ) :
+    DGHom R n X.obj Y.obj →ₗ[R] DGHom R (n + 1) X.obj Y.obj where
+  toFun f := dgDifferential R n f + n.negOnePow • dgComp R f Y.twist rfl -
+    dgComp R X.twist f (add_comm 1 n)
+  map_add' f g := by
+    simp only [map_add, add_dgComp, dgComp_add, smul_add]
+    abel
+  map_smul' r f := by
+    simp only [map_smul, smul_dgComp, dgComp_smul, smul_sub, smul_add, RingHom.id_apply]
+    rw [smul_comm]
+
+private theorem twistedDifferential_apply {X Y : DGTwistedObject R C} (n : ℤ)
+    (f : DGHom R n X.obj Y.obj) :
+    twistedDifferential R X Y n f = dgDifferential R n f +
+      n.negOnePow • dgComp R f Y.twist rfl - dgComp R X.twist f (add_comm 1 n) :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- The twisted differential squares to zero: after the Leibniz rule and associativity, what
+remains is the Maurer–Cartan defect `d δ - dgComp δ δ` of the two twists, composed with `f`. -/
+private theorem twistedDifferential_twistedDifferential {X Y : DGTwistedObject R C} (n : ℤ)
+    (f : DGHom R n X.obj Y.obj) :
+    twistedDifferential R X Y (n + 1) (twistedDifferential R X Y n f) = 0 := by
+  simp only [twistedDifferential_apply, sub_eq_add_neg, map_add, map_neg, map_zsmul_unit,
+    dgDifferential_dgComp, dgDifferential_dgDifferential, dgDifferential_twist]
+  rw [dgComp_assoc R f Y.twist Y.twist rfl rfl rfl,
+    ← dgComp_assoc R X.twist X.twist f rfl (add_comm 1 n) (by omega),
+    ← dgComp_assoc R X.twist f Y.twist (add_comm 1 n) rfl (by omega)]
+  simp only [Int.negOnePow_succ, Int.negOnePow_one, Units.neg_smul, smul_add, smul_neg, smul_smul,
+    Int.units_mul_self, one_smul]
+  abel
+
+/-- The Leibniz rule for the twisted differential, which holds by associativity alone. -/
+private theorem twistedDifferential_dgComp {X Y Z : DGTwistedObject R C} {p q n : ℤ}
+    (h : p + q = n) (f : DGHom R p X.obj Y.obj) (g : DGHom R q Y.obj Z.obj) :
+    twistedDifferential R X Z n (dgComp R f g h) =
+      dgComp R (twistedDifferential R X Y p f) g (by omega) +
+        p.negOnePow • dgComp R f (twistedDifferential R Y Z q g) (by omega) := by
+  subst h
+  simp only [twistedDifferential_apply, sub_eq_add_neg, add_dgComp, neg_dgComp, units_smul_dgComp,
+    dgComp_add, dgComp_neg, dgComp_units_smul, dgDifferential_dgComp]
+  rw [dgComp_assoc R f g Z.twist rfl rfl (by omega), dgComp_assoc R X.twist f g (add_comm 1 p) rfl
+      (by omega), dgComp_assoc R f Y.twist g rfl (add_comm 1 q) (by omega)]
+  simp only [smul_add, smul_neg, smul_smul, ← Int.negOnePow_add]
+  abel
+
+/-! ### The Hom-complex data -/
+
+/-- The Hom complex `Hom((X, δ_X), (Y, δ_Y))`: the graded module of morphisms `X ⟶ Y` of `C`,
+with the twisted differential. -/
+private noncomputable def homComplex (X Y : DGTwistedObject R C) :
+    CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ :=
+  CochainComplex.of (fun n ↦ (dgHomComplex R X.obj Y.obj).X n)
+    (fun n ↦ ModuleCat.ofHom (twistedDifferential R X Y n))
+    (fun n ↦ by
+      ext f
+      exact twistedDifferential_twistedDifferential R n f)
+
+private theorem homComplex_d (X Y : DGTwistedObject R C) (n : ℤ) :
+    ((homComplex R X Y).d n (n + 1)).hom = twistedDifferential R X Y n := by
+  simp only [homComplex, CochainComplex.of_d, ModuleCat.hom_ofHom]
+  -- The two sides differ only in writing the degree components as `ModuleCat.of R _`.
+  rfl
+
+/-- Composition of twisted objects: the composition of `C` on the underlying morphisms. -/
+private noncomputable def comp {X Y Z : DGTwistedObject R C} (p q n : ℤ) (h : p + q = n) :
+    (homComplex R X Y).X p →ₗ[R] (homComplex R Y Z).X q →ₗ[R] (homComplex R X Z).X n :=
+  (dgCategoryData R C).comp (X := X.obj) (Y := Y.obj) (Z := Z.obj) p q n h
+
+private theorem comp_apply {X Y Z : DGTwistedObject R C} (p q n : ℤ) (h : p + q = n)
+    (f : (homComplex R X Y).X p) (g : (homComplex R Y Z).X q) :
+    comp R p q n h f g = dgComp R (X := X.obj) (Y := Y.obj) (Z := Z.obj) f g h :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- The **explicit Hom-complex data of twisted objects**: the morphisms of `C` with the twisted
+differential `d f + (-1)^n • dgComp f δ_Y - dgComp δ_X f`, and the composition and identities of
+`C`. -/
+noncomputable def homComplexData : DGCategoryData R (DGTwistedObject R C) where
+  hom := homComplex R
+  comp := comp R
+  id X := dgId R X.obj
+  d_comp {X Y Z p q n} h f g := by
+    simp only [homComplex_d, comp_apply]
+    exact twistedDifferential_dgComp R h f g
+  comp_assoc hpq hqr h f g k := by
+    simp only [comp_apply]
+    exact dgComp_assoc R f g k hpq hqr h
+  id_comp g := (comp_apply R _ _ _ _ _ g).trans (dgId_dgComp R g)
+  comp_id f := (comp_apply R _ _ _ _ f _).trans (dgComp_dgId R f)
+
+/-- The differential graded category of **twisted objects** of a differential graded category,
+with the twisted differential on Hom complexes. -/
+noncomputable instance : DGCategory R (DGTwistedObject R C) :=
+  (homComplexData R).toDGCategory
+
+/-! ### Morphisms, differential, composition and identity -/
+
+/-- A morphism `(X, δ_X) ⟶ (Y, δ_Y)` of degree `n` of twisted objects is a morphism `X ⟶ Y` of
+degree `n` in `C`. -/
+noncomputable def dgHomEquiv (X Y : DGTwistedObject R C) (n : ℤ) :
+    DGHom R n X Y ≃ₗ[R] DGHom R n X.obj Y.obj :=
+  LinearEquiv.refl R _
+
+/-- **The twisted differential**: the differential of a degree-`n` morphism of twisted objects
+is `d f + (-1)^n • dgComp f δ_Y - dgComp δ_X f`. -/
+@[simp↓]
+theorem dgHomEquiv_dgDifferential {X Y : DGTwistedObject R C} (n : ℤ) (f : DGHom R n X Y) :
+    dgHomEquiv R X Y (n + 1) (dgDifferential R n f) =
+      dgDifferential R n (dgHomEquiv R X Y n f) +
+        n.negOnePow • dgComp R (dgHomEquiv R X Y n f) Y.twist rfl -
+          dgComp R X.twist (dgHomEquiv R X Y n f) (add_comm 1 n) :=
+  ((homComplexData R).dgDifferential_toDGCategory n f).trans
+    (LinearMap.congr_fun (homComplex_d R X Y n) f)
+
+/-- Composition of twisted objects is the composition of `C`. -/
+@[simp↓]
+theorem dgHomEquiv_dgComp {X Y Z : DGTwistedObject R C} {p q n : ℤ} (f : DGHom R p X Y)
+    (g : DGHom R q Y Z) (h : p + q = n) :
+    dgHomEquiv R X Z n (dgComp R f g h) =
+      dgComp R (dgHomEquiv R X Y p f) (dgHomEquiv R Y Z q g) h :=
+  ((homComplexData R).dgComp_toDGCategory f g h).trans (comp_apply R p q n h f g)
+
+/-- The identity of a twisted object is the identity of its underlying object. -/
+@[simp↓]
+theorem dgHomEquiv_dgId (X : DGTwistedObject R C) : dgHomEquiv R X X 0 (dgId R X) = dgId R X.obj :=
+  (homComplexData R).dgId_toDGCategory X
+
+/-! ### The embedding `X ↦ (X, 0)` -/
+
+/-- An object of `C` with the zero twist, which satisfies the Maurer–Cartan equation since both
+sides vanish. -/
+-- This is reducible so that `(ofObj R X).obj` is reducibly `X`: the morphisms of the embedding
+-- `X ↦ (X, 0)` are then literally the morphisms of `C`.
+abbrev ofObj (X : C) : DGTwistedObject R C where
+  obj := X
+  twist := 0
+  dgDifferential_twist := by simp
+
+/-- The action of the embedding on morphisms of degree `n`: a degree-`n` morphism `X ⟶ Y` of `C`
+is a degree-`n` morphism `(X, 0) ⟶ (Y, 0)` of twisted objects. -/
+noncomputable def embeddingHomEquiv (X Y : C) (n : ℤ) :
+    DGHom R n X Y ≃ₗ[R] DGHom R n (ofObj R X) (ofObj R Y) :=
+  (dgHomEquiv R (ofObj R X) (ofObj R Y) n).symm
+
+/-- The embedding does not change the underlying morphism. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem dgHomEquiv_embeddingHomEquiv {X Y : C} {n : ℤ} (f : DGHom R n X Y) :
+    dgHomEquiv R (ofObj R X) (ofObj R Y) n (embeddingHomEquiv R X Y n f) = f :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- With zero twists, the twisted differential is the differential of `C`. -/
+theorem embeddingHomEquiv_dgDifferential {X Y : C} (n : ℤ) (f : DGHom R n X Y) :
+    embeddingHomEquiv R X Y (n + 1) (dgDifferential R n f) =
+      dgDifferential R n (embeddingHomEquiv R X Y n f) :=
+  (dgHomEquiv R _ _ (n + 1)).injective <| by
+    rw [dgHomEquiv_dgDifferential, dgHomEquiv_embeddingHomEquiv, dgHomEquiv_embeddingHomEquiv]
+    simp
+
+/-- The DG functor from a differential graded category to its twisted objects sending `X` to the
+twisted object `(X, 0)`. -/
+-- The body is exposed so that `(embedding R).obj X` is definitionally `ofObj R X`, as for
+-- `CategoryTheory.EnrichedFunctor.ofDGMap`.
+@[expose]
+noncomputable def embedding :
+    EnrichedFunctor (CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ) C (DGTwistedObject R C) :=
+  EnrichedFunctor.ofDGMap (ofObj R) (fun {X Y} n ↦ (embeddingHomEquiv R X Y n).toLinearMap)
+    (fun n f ↦ embeddingHomEquiv_dgDifferential R n f)
+    (fun X ↦ (dgHomEquiv R _ _ 0).injective <| by
+      rw [LinearEquiv.coe_coe, dgHomEquiv_embeddingHomEquiv, dgHomEquiv_dgId])
+    (fun {X Y Z p q n} f g h ↦ (dgHomEquiv R _ _ n).injective <| by
+      rw [LinearEquiv.coe_coe, LinearEquiv.coe_coe, LinearEquiv.coe_coe, dgHomEquiv_dgComp,
+        dgHomEquiv_embeddingHomEquiv, dgHomEquiv_embeddingHomEquiv, dgHomEquiv_embeddingHomEquiv])
+
+/-- The embedding sends `X` to the twisted object `(X, 0)`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem embedding_obj (X : C) : (embedding R).obj X = ofObj R X :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- The embedding acts on morphisms by `TauCeti.DGTwistedObject.embeddingHomEquiv`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem dgMap_embedding {X Y : C} {n : ℤ} (f : DGHom R n X Y) :
+    (embedding R).dgMap n f = embeddingHomEquiv R X Y n f :=
+  (EnrichedFunctor.dgMap_apply _ f).trans rfl
+
+/-- The embedding is an isomorphism on Hom complexes: `C` is a full DG subcategory of its twisted
+objects. -/
+instance isIso_embedding_map (X Y : C) : IsIso ((embedding R).map X Y) :=
+  have (n : ℤ) : IsIso (((embedding R).map X Y).f n) :=
+    (embeddingHomEquiv R X Y n).toModuleIso.isIso_hom
+  HomologicalComplex.Hom.isIso_of_components _
+
+end DGTwistedObject
+
+end TauCeti

+/-!
+# Triangulated opposite stable categories
+
+For a Frobenius exact category `C`, the additive equivalence from the stable category of `Cᵒᵖ`
+to the opposite of the stable category of `C` is a triangle equivalence. Here the source carries
+Happel's triangulation for the opposite Frobenius exact structure `E.op`, while the target carries
+Mathlib's opposite triangulation `CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.Opposite`, whose shift by `n` is
+the opposite of shift by `-n` and whose distinguished triangles are the opposites of
+distinguished triangles in the stable category of `C` without additional signs.
+
+For a conflation `S` in `C`, the standard triangle of `S.op` in the stable category of `Cᵒᵖ`
+maps under `projectiveStableOpFunctor` to a triangle in `(E.ProjectiveStableCategory)ᵒᵖ` whose
+unopposite under `triangleOpEquivalence` is canonically isomorphic to the standard triangle of `S`.
+The third-arrow compatibility combines the degree-one formula for
+`projectiveStableOpFunctorCommShift`, the transpose connecting-map formula `stableConnectingMapOp`,
+and the suspension-loop relation `stableSuspension_map_stableConnectingMapOp`.
+
+Consequently `projectiveStableOpFunctor` and both directions of `projectiveStableOpEquivalence`
+are triangulated, and a triangle in `E.op.ProjectiveStableCategory` is distinguished if and only
+if its opposite-stable image corresponds under `triangleOpEquivalence` to a distinguished triangle
+in `E.ProjectiveStableCategory`.
+
+## References
+
+* Dieter Happel, *Triangulated Categories in the Representation Theory of Finite Dimensional
+  Algebras*, Chapter I, Section 2.
+* `TauCeti.ExactStructure.IsFrobenius.stableSuspension_map_stableConnectingMapOp`: the
+  suspension-loop compatibility for the transpose of the opposite connecting map.
+* `TauCeti.ExactStructure.IsFrobenius.projectiveStableOpFunctorCommShift`: the coherent integral
+  shift compatibility of the opposite stable comparison functor.
+* `CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.triangleOpEquivalence`: Mathlib's opposite triangulation.
+-/

+

+/-!
+# Spherical categories
+
+A pivotal category is *spherical* when the left and right traces of every endomorphism agree.
+In a spherical category the common value `trace f = leftTrace f = rightTrace f` is the
+categorical trace, and the *quantum dimension* `quantumDim X = trace (𝟙 X)` is the common value
+of the left and right dimensions of `X`.
+
+The trace inherits the properties of both one-sided traces: it is cyclic, additive, linear in a
+linear monoidal category, the identity on scalars, additive on biproducts, and invariant under
+the right adjoint mate, so that `quantumDim Xᘁ = quantumDim X`. Since the left trace lets a
+scalar act on the right of a loop and the right trace lets one act on the left, a scalar acting
+on either side factors out of the trace. Combined with the nested-loop formula for the trace of
+a tensor product, this makes the trace **multiplicative** in every spherical category:
+`trace (f ⊗ₘ g) = trace f ≫ trace g`, and so
+`quantumDim (X ⊗ Y) = quantumDim X ≫ quantumDim Y`.
+No braiding is needed. For the one-sided traces of a merely pivotal category, multiplicativity
+is only available when the relevant scalar acts on an object in the same way from both sides,
+for instance in a braided category.
+
+## Main declarations
+
+* `TauCeti.SphericalCategory`: a pivotal category whose left and right traces agree;
+* `TauCeti.trace` and `TauCeti.quantumDim`: the trace of an endomorphism and the quantum
+  dimension of an object in a spherical category;
+* `TauCeti.trace_comm`: cyclicity of the trace;
+* `TauCeti.trace_rightAdjointMate` and `TauCeti.quantumDim_rightDual`: invariance under duality;
+* `TauCeti.trace_scalar_whiskerRight_comp` and `TauCeti.trace_comp_whiskerLeft_scalar`: a scalar
+  acting on either side factors out of the trace;
+* `TauCeti.trace_tensorHom` and `TauCeti.quantumDim_tensor`: multiplicativity of the trace and
+  of the quantum dimension;
+* `TauCeti.trace_biproduct` and `TauCeti.quantumDim_biproduct`: additivity on finite
+  biproducts.
+
+## References
+
+* A. Henriques, D. Penneys, J. Tener, *Categorified trace for module tensor categories over
+  braided tensor categories*, [arXiv:1509.02937](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.02937), §2.1
+* [P. Etingof, S. Gelaki, D. Nikshych, V. Ostrik, *Tensor categories*][egno15], §4.7
+* [leanprover-community/mathlib4#42191](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/42191),
+  for the names `SphericalCategory`, `leftTrace_eq_rightTrace`, `trace`, `trace_eq_leftTrace`
+  and `trace_eq_rightTrace`

+public section
+
+open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits MonoidalCategory
+open scoped ZeroObject
+
+universe v u
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [MonoidalCategory C] [RigidCategory C] [PivotalCategory C]
+
+variable (C) in
+/-- A pivotal category is *spherical* when the left and right traces of every endomorphism
+agree. -/
+class SphericalCategory : Prop where
+  /-- The left and right traces of every endomorphism agree. -/
+  leftTrace_eq_rightTrace {X : C} (f : X ⟶ X) : leftTrace f = rightTrace f
+
+/-- The *trace* of an endomorphism in a spherical category: the common value of its left and
+right traces. The sphericity hypothesis is not needed to write down the formula, but it is
+carried so that `trace` is only available where it does not depend on the side. -/
+noncomputable def trace [_hC : SphericalCategory C] {X : C} (f : X ⟶ X) : 𝟙_ C ⟶ 𝟙_ C :=
+  leftTrace f
+
+variable [SphericalCategory C]
+
+/-- The *quantum dimension* of an object of a spherical category: the trace of its identity. -/
+noncomputable def quantumDim (X : C) : 𝟙_ C ⟶ 𝟙_ C :=
+  trace (𝟙 X)
+
+/-- The trace is the left trace. -/
+theorem trace_eq_leftTrace {X : C} (f : X ⟶ X) : trace f = leftTrace f :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- The trace is the right trace. -/
+theorem trace_eq_rightTrace {X : C} (f : X ⟶ X) : trace f = rightTrace f :=
+  SphericalCategory.leftTrace_eq_rightTrace f
+
+/-- The trace of an identity is the quantum dimension. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem trace_id (X : C) : trace (𝟙 X) = quantumDim X :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- In a spherical category the left and right dimensions agree. -/
+theorem leftDim_eq_rightDim (X : C) : leftDim X = rightDim X := by
+  rw [← leftTrace_id, ← rightTrace_id, SphericalCategory.leftTrace_eq_rightTrace]
+
+/-- The quantum dimension is the left dimension. -/
+theorem quantumDim_eq_leftDim (X : C) : quantumDim X = leftDim X := by
+  rw [← trace_id, trace_eq_leftTrace, leftTrace_id]
+
+/-- The quantum dimension is the right dimension. -/
+theorem quantumDim_eq_rightDim (X : C) : quantumDim X = rightDim X := by
+  rw [quantumDim_eq_leftDim, leftDim_eq_rightDim]
+
+/-- **Cyclicity of the trace**: `trace (f ≫ g) = trace (g ≫ f)`. -/
+theorem trace_comm {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ X) : trace (f ≫ g) = trace (g ≫ f) := by
+  rw [trace_eq_leftTrace, trace_eq_leftTrace, leftTrace_comm]
+
+/-- The trace is invariant under conjugation by an isomorphism. -/
+theorem trace_conj {X Y : C} (i : X ≅ Y) (f : X ⟶ X) :
+    trace (i.inv ≫ f ≫ i.hom) = trace f := by
+  rw [trace_eq_leftTrace, trace_eq_leftTrace, leftTrace_conj]
+
+/-- Isomorphic objects have the same quantum dimension. -/
+theorem quantumDim_congr {X Y : C} (i : X ≅ Y) : quantumDim X = quantumDim Y := by
+  rw [quantumDim_eq_leftDim, quantumDim_eq_leftDim, leftDim_congr i]
+
+/-- The trace of the right adjoint mate `fᘁ` is the trace of `f`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem trace_rightAdjointMate {X : C} (f : X ⟶ X) : trace (fᘁ) = trace f := by
+  rw [trace_eq_leftTrace, leftTrace_rightAdjointMate, trace_eq_rightTrace]
+
+/-- An object and its right dual have the same quantum dimension. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem quantumDim_rightDual (X : C) : quantumDim Xᘁ = quantumDim X := by
+  rw [← trace_id, ← rightAdjointMate_id, trace_rightAdjointMate, trace_id]
+
+/-- **The trace of a scalar is itself**: for `a : 𝟙_ C ⟶ 𝟙_ C`, `trace a = a`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem trace_unit (a : 𝟙_ C ⟶ 𝟙_ C) : trace a = a := by
+  rw [trace_eq_leftTrace, leftTrace_unit]
+
+/-- The quantum dimension of the unit is `𝟙`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem quantumDim_unit : quantumDim (𝟙_ C) = 𝟙 (𝟙_ C) := by
+  rw [quantumDim_eq_leftDim, leftDim_unit]
+
+/-- A scalar acting on `X` from the left factors out of the trace. -/
+theorem trace_scalar_whiskerRight_comp {X : C} (a : 𝟙_ C ⟶ 𝟙_ C) (f : X ⟶ X) :
+    trace ((λ_ X).inv ≫ a ▷ X ≫ (λ_ X).hom ≫ f) = a ≫ trace f := by
+  rw [trace_eq_rightTrace, trace_eq_rightTrace, rightTrace_scalar_whiskerRight_comp]
+
+/-- A scalar acting on `X` from the right factors out of the trace. -/
+theorem trace_comp_whiskerLeft_scalar {X : C} (f : X ⟶ X) (a : 𝟙_ C ⟶ 𝟙_ C) :
+    trace (f ≫ (ρ_ X).inv ≫ X ◁ a ≫ (ρ_ X).hom) = trace f ≫ a := by
+  rw [trace_eq_leftTrace, trace_eq_leftTrace, leftTrace_comp_whiskerLeft_scalar]
+
+/-- **Multiplicativity of the trace**: in a spherical category,
+`trace (f ⊗ₘ g) = trace f ≫ trace g`, with no braiding required. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem trace_tensorHom {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ X) (g : Y ⟶ Y) :
+    trace (f ⊗ₘ g) = trace f ≫ trace g := by
+  -- The left trace of `f` acts on `Y` from the left inside the loop of `g`; sphericity lets us
+  -- close that loop on the other side, where a scalar acting from the left factors out.
+  rw [trace_eq_leftTrace, leftTrace_tensorHom, ← trace_eq_leftTrace,
+    trace_scalar_whiskerRight_comp, trace_eq_leftTrace f]
+
+/-- **Multiplicativity of the quantum dimension**:
+`quantumDim (X ⊗ Y) = quantumDim X ≫ quantumDim Y`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem quantumDim_tensor (X Y : C) : quantumDim (X ⊗ Y) = quantumDim X ≫ quantumDim Y := by
+  rw [← trace_id, ← trace_id, ← trace_id, ← id_tensorHom_id, trace_tensorHom]
+
+section Linear
+
+variable [Preadditive C] [MonoidalPreadditive C]
+
+/-- The trace is additive. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem trace_add {X : C} (f g : X ⟶ X) : trace (f + g) = trace f + trace g := by
+  simp only [trace_eq_leftTrace, leftTrace_add]
+
+/-- The trace of zero is zero. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem trace_zero (X : C) : trace (0 : X ⟶ X) = 0 := by
+  rw [trace_eq_leftTrace, leftTrace_zero]
+
+/-- The zero object has quantum dimension zero. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem quantumDim_zero [HasZeroObject C] : quantumDim (0 : C) = 0 := by
+  rw [quantumDim_eq_leftDim, leftDim_zero]
+
+/-- The trace commutes with finite sums. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem trace_sum {ι : Type*} {X : C} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → (X ⟶ X)) :
+    trace (∑ i ∈ s, f i) = ∑ i ∈ s, trace (f i) := by
+  simp only [trace_eq_leftTrace, leftTrace_sum]
+
+/-- The trace commutes with negation. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem trace_neg {X : C} (f : X ⟶ X) : trace (-f) = -trace f := by
+  simp only [trace_eq_leftTrace, leftTrace_neg]
+
+/-- The trace commutes with subtraction. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem trace_sub {X : C} (f g : X ⟶ X) : trace (f - g) = trace f - trace g := by
+  simp only [trace_eq_leftTrace, leftTrace_sub]
+
+/-- The trace is `R`-linear in an `R`-linear monoidal category. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem trace_smul {R : Type*} [Semiring R] [Linear R C] [MonoidalLinear R C] {X : C} (r : R)
+    (f : X ⟶ X) : trace (r • f) = r • trace f := by
+  simp only [trace_eq_leftTrace, leftTrace_smul]
+
+section Finite
+
+variable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {X : ι → C} [HasBiproduct X]
+
+/-- The trace of an endomorphism of a finite biproduct is the sum of the traces of its diagonal
+components. -/
+theorem trace_biproduct (f : ⨁ X ⟶ ⨁ X) :
+    trace f = ∑ i, trace (biproduct.ι X i ≫ f ≫ biproduct.π X i) := by
+  simp only [trace_eq_leftTrace, leftTrace_biproduct f]
+
+/-- The trace of a block-diagonal morphism is the sum of its block traces. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem trace_biproduct_map (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ X i) :
+    trace (biproduct.map f) = ∑ i, trace (f i) := by
+  simp only [trace_eq_leftTrace, leftTrace_biproduct_map]
+
+/-- The quantum dimension is additive on finite biproducts. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem quantumDim_biproduct : quantumDim (⨁ X) = ∑ i, quantumDim (X i) := by
+  simp only [quantumDim_eq_leftDim, leftDim_biproduct]
+
+end Finite
+
+section Binary
+
+variable {X Y : C} [HasBinaryBiproduct X Y]
+
+/-- The trace of an endomorphism of a binary biproduct is the sum of the traces of its two
+diagonal components. -/
+theorem trace_biprod (f : X ⊞ Y ⟶ X ⊞ Y) :
+    trace f =

+  simp only [trace_eq_leftTrace, leftTrace_biprod f]
+
+/-- The trace of a binary block-diagonal morphism is the sum of its block traces. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem trace_biprod_map (f : X ⟶ X) (g : Y ⟶ Y) :
+    trace (biprod.map f g) = trace f + trace g := by
+  simp only [trace_eq_leftTrace, leftTrace_biprod_map]
+
+/-- The quantum dimension is additive on binary biproducts. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem quantumDim_biprod : quantumDim (X ⊞ Y) = quantumDim X + quantumDim Y := by
+  simp only [quantumDim_eq_leftDim, leftDim_biprod]
+
+end Binary
+

+module
+
+public import TauCeti.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Pivotal.Trace
+
+/-!
+# Pivotal traces and dimensions of tensor products
+
+In a pivotal category, the pivotal pairing `pivotalExactPairing (X ⊗ Y)` is the tensor product of
+the pivotal pairings of `Y` and of `X`, transported along the comparison
+`rightDualTensorIso X Y : (X ⊗ Y)ᘁ ≅ Yᘁ ⊗ Xᘁ`. This is where the monoidality of the pivotal
+structure enters. Consequently the trace of a tensor product `f ⊗ₘ g` is computed by two nested
+loops.
+
+For the left trace the loop of `f` lies inside the loop of `g`, so the scalar `leftTrace f` acts
+on `Y` from the left:
+`leftTrace (f ⊗ₘ g) = leftTrace ((λ_ Y).inv ≫ leftTrace f ▷ Y ≫ (λ_ Y).hom ≫ g)`. A scalar acting
+on `Y` from the right can be moved out of the left trace, so whenever the left and right actions
+of `leftTrace f` on `Y` agree, the left trace is multiplicative:
+`leftTrace (f ⊗ₘ g) = leftTrace f ≫ leftTrace g`. Symmetrically, the right trace is
+multiplicative whenever `rightTrace g` acts on `X` in the same way from both sides.
+
+The two actions of a scalar need not agree in a general monoidal category, so the hypothesis
+cannot be dropped in general. The actions do agree in a braided category, where the left and right
+traces and dimensions are therefore multiplicative without further hypotheses.
+
+## Main declarations
+
+* `TauCeti.pivotalExactPairing_tensor_evaluation` and
+  `TauCeti.pivotalExactPairing_tensor_coevaluation`: the pivotal pairing of `X ⊗ Y` is the tensor
+  product of the pivotal pairings, up to `rightDualTensorIso X Y`;
+* `TauCeti.leftTrace_tensorHom` and `TauCeti.rightTrace_tensorHom`: the traces of `f ⊗ₘ g` as
+  nested loops;
+* `TauCeti.leftTrace_tensorHom_eq_comp`, `TauCeti.rightTrace_tensorHom_eq_comp`,
+  `TauCeti.leftDim_tensor_eq_comp` and `TauCeti.rightDim_tensor_eq_comp`: multiplicativity of the
+  traces and dimensions when the relevant scalar acts in the same way from both sides;
+* `TauCeti.leftTrace_tensorHom_eq_comp_of_braided` and its companions: multiplicativity in a
+  braided pivotal category.
+
+## References
+
+* A. Henriques, D. Penneys, J. Tener, *Categorified trace for module tensor categories over
+  braided tensor categories*, [arXiv:1509.02937](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.02937), §2.1
+* [P. Etingof, S. Gelaki, D. Nikshych, V. Ostrik, *Tensor categories*][egno15], §4.7
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open CategoryTheory MonoidalCategory ExactPairing
+
+universe v u
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [MonoidalCategory C] [RigidCategory C] [PivotalCategory C]
+
+/-- The evaluation of the pivotal pairing of `X ⊗ Y` is that of the tensor product of the pivotal
+pairings of `Y` and of `X`, after the comparison `rightDualTensorIso X Y : (X ⊗ Y)ᘁ ≅ Yᘁ ⊗ Xᘁ`. -/
+theorem pivotalExactPairing_tensor_evaluation (X Y : C) :
+    @evaluation C _ _ (X ⊗ Y)ᘁ (X ⊗ Y) (pivotalExactPairing (X ⊗ Y)) =
+      (X ⊗ Y) ◁ (rightDualTensorIso X Y).hom ≫
+        @evaluation C _ _ (Yᘁ ⊗ Xᘁ) (X ⊗ Y)
+          (@tensor C _ _ Yᘁ Xᘁ Y X (pivotalExactPairing Y) (pivotalExactPairing X)) := by
+  -- Monoidality of the pivotal structure, with the tensor comparison of the double right dual
+  -- functor unfolded. The two sides differ only in how the target `(X ⊗ Y)ᘁᘁ` is written.
+  have hφ : (pivotalIsoApp (X ⊗ Y)).hom = ((pivotalIsoApp X).hom ⊗ₘ (pivotalIsoApp Y).hom) ≫
+      (rightDualTensorIso Yᘁ Xᘁ).inv ≫ ((rightDualTensorIso X Y).hom)ᘁ := by
+    rw [pivotalIsoApp_tensor_hom, doubleRightDualFunctor_μ]
+    rfl
+  -- The evaluation of the tensor product of the pivotal pairings, written with the canonical
+  -- pairing of `Yᘁ ⊗ Xᘁ`: transporting along `rightDualTensorIso Yᘁ Xᘁ` gives the tensor product
+  -- of the canonical pairings, and the rest is coherence plus one interchange.

+module
+
+public import TauCeti.Combinatorics.Hypergraph.Colored.Basic

+/-!
+# Edit discrepancy of colored three-uniform hypergraphs
+
+The edit discrepancy `H.editDiscrepancy3 H'` of two colorings of the triples of `V` is six times
+the number of unordered triples on which they disagree, divided by `|V|³`. Equivalently, it is
+the fraction of all `|V|³` ordered triples of vertices whose entries are distinct and form a
+triple on which the colorings disagree.
+`H.Approximates3 H' ε` says that the edit discrepancy is at most `ε`.
+
+The discrepancy is a pseudometric: it is nonnegative, symmetric, zero on the diagonal, and
+satisfies the triangle inequality, so approximations compose with their errors added. The
+vertex count is `Nat.card V`, so no finiteness hypothesis is needed: on an infinite vertex type
+the denominator vanishes and every discrepancy is `0`.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `TauCeti.Colored3Graph.editDiscrepancy3`: the normalized number of disagreeing triples.
+* `TauCeti.Colored3Graph.Approximates3`: approximation within a given edit discrepancy.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `TauCeti.Colored3Graph.editDiscrepancy3_triangle`: the triangle inequality.
+* `TauCeti.Colored3Graph.Approximates3.trans`: approximations compose, adding their errors.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+namespace Colored3Graph
+
+variable {κ V : Type*}
+
+/-- Six times the number of unordered triples on which `H` and `H'` disagree, normalized by
+`|V|³`. -/
+noncomputable def editDiscrepancy3 (H H' : Colored3Graph κ V) : ℚ :=
+  6 * {s | H.color s ≠ H'.color s}.ncard / (Nat.card V : ℚ) ^ 3
+
+/-- The edit discrepancy counts disagreeing triples, normalized by `|V|³`. -/
+theorem editDiscrepancy3_def (H H' : Colored3Graph κ V) :
+    H.editDiscrepancy3 H' = 6 * {s | H.color s ≠ H'.color s}.ncard / (Nat.card V : ℚ) ^ 3 :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- The edit discrepancy is nonnegative. -/
+theorem editDiscrepancy3_nonneg (H H' : Colored3Graph κ V) : 0 ≤ H.editDiscrepancy3 H' := by
+  rw [editDiscrepancy3_def]
+  positivity
+
+/-- The edit discrepancy is symmetric. -/
+theorem editDiscrepancy3_comm (H H' : Colored3Graph κ V) :
+    H.editDiscrepancy3 H' = H'.editDiscrepancy3 H := by
+  simp only [editDiscrepancy3_def, ne_comm]
+
+/-- A coloring has edit discrepancy `0` from itself. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem editDiscrepancy3_self (H : Colored3Graph κ V) : H.editDiscrepancy3 H = 0 := by
+  simp [editDiscrepancy3_def]
+
+/-- The **triangle inequality** for the edit discrepancy. -/
+theorem editDiscrepancy3_triangle (H₁ H₂ H₃ : Colored3Graph κ V) :
+    H₁.editDiscrepancy3 H₃ ≤ H₁.editDiscrepancy3 H₂ + H₂.editDiscrepancy3 H₃ := by
+  -- On an infinite vertex type every discrepancy has denominator `0`.
+  cases finite_or_infinite V
+  · simp only [editDiscrepancy3_def, ← add_div, ← mul_add]
+    gcongr
+    -- A triple on which `H₁` and `H₃` disagree is one on which `H₂` disagrees with one of them.
+    have hsub : {s | H₁.color s ≠ H₃.color s} ⊆
+        {s | H₁.color s ≠ H₂.color s} ∪ {s | H₂.color s ≠ H₃.color s} := by
+      intro s hs
+      by_contra h
+      simp_all
+    exact_mod_cast (Set.ncard_le_ncard hsub).trans (Set.ncard_union_le _ _)
+  · simp [editDiscrepancy3_def]
+
+/-- `H` approximates `H'` within `ε` when their edit discrepancy is at most `ε`. -/
+def Approximates3 (H H' : Colored3Graph κ V) (ε : ℝ) : Prop :=
+  (H.editDiscrepancy3 H' : ℝ) ≤ ε
+
+/-- Approximation within `ε` means that the edit discrepancy is at most `ε`. -/
+theorem approximates3_iff (H H' : Colored3Graph κ V) (ε : ℝ) :
+    H.Approximates3 H' ε ↔ (H.editDiscrepancy3 H' : ℝ) ≤ ε :=
+  Iff.rfl
+
+/-- A coloring approximates itself within any nonnegative error. -/
+theorem approximates3_self (H : Colored3Graph κ V) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε) :
+    H.Approximates3 H ε := by
+  simpa [approximates3_iff] using hε
+
+namespace Approximates3
+
+variable {H₁ H₂ H₃ : Colored3Graph κ V} {ε δ : ℝ}
+
+/-- Approximation is symmetric. -/
+theorem symm (h : H₁.Approximates3 H₂ ε) : H₂.Approximates3 H₁ ε := by
+  rwa [approximates3_iff, editDiscrepancy3_comm]
+
+/-- Approximation within `ε` implies approximation within any larger error. -/
+theorem mono (h : H₁.Approximates3 H₂ ε) (hεδ : ε ≤ δ) : H₁.Approximates3 H₂ δ :=
+  h.trans hεδ
+
+/-- Approximations compose, with their errors added. -/
+theorem trans (h₁₂ : H₁.Approximates3 H₂ ε) (h₂₃ : H₂.Approximates3 H₃ δ) :
+    H₁.Approximates3 H₃ (ε + δ) := by

+        exact_mod_cast editDiscrepancy3_triangle H₁ H₂ H₃
+    _ ≤ ε + δ := add_le_add h₁₂ h₂₃
+
+end Approximates3
+

+module
+
+public import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Action.Pointwise.Set.Basic
+public import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Subgroup.Ker
+public import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.BigOperators
+public import Mathlib.Tactic.Abel

+/-!
+# Arrow assignments and their excess
+
+A directed network on a vertex type `V` is described by an explicit arrow family
+`Q : V → V → Type*`, where `Q v w` is the type of arrows from `v` to `w`; parallel arrows,
+antiparallel arrows and loops are all allowed. An *arrow assignment* with values in a type `K`
+attaches a value of `K` to every arrow, with no sign or capacity constraint. Flows, pseudoflows,
+bounded assignments and residual updates are all arrow assignments subject to further conditions,
+and they share the additive calculus developed here. Arrow sums only need `K` to be an additive
+commutative monoid, while excess needs an additive commutative group.
+
+The *excess* of an assignment `f` at a vertex `v` is the total value on arrows entering `v` minus
+the total value on arrows leaving `v`. With this sign convention a demand vertex has positive
+excess and a supply vertex negative excess, and the value of an ordinary `s`–`t` flow is its excess
+at the sink `t`. A loop at `v` enters and leaves `v`, so it contributes nothing to the excess.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `TauCeti.Assignment Q K`: arrow assignments of the arrow family `Q` with values in `K`.
+* `TauCeti.arrowSum Q f S T`: the total value of `f` on the arrows from `S` to `T`.
+* `TauCeti.excessAt Q f v`: the excess of `f` at `v`.
+* `TauCeti.excessHom Q`: excess as an additive homomorphism `Assignment Q K →+ (V → K)`.
+* `TauCeti.IsCirculation f`: `f` has zero excess at every vertex.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `TauCeti.sum_excessAt_eq_arrowSum_sub`: the total excess on a vertex set `S` is the value
+  entering `S` minus the value leaving `S`.
+* `TauCeti.sum_excessAt`: the total excess over all vertices vanishes.
+* `TauCeti.excessAt_source_eq_neg_sink`: an assignment conserved away from `s` and `t` has opposite
+  excesses at `s` and `t`.
+* `TauCeti.isCirculation_iff_mem_ker`: circulations form the kernel of `excessHom`, and
+  `TauCeti.setOf_excessAt_eq_eq_vadd_ker` identifies every nonempty prescribed-excess fibre with a
+  translate of that kernel.
+* `TauCeti.map_excessAt` and `TauCeti.excessAt_comp_equiv`: excess commutes with additive maps of
+  coefficients and with transport along an identification of arrow families.
+
+## Implementation notes
+
+The arrow family is an explicit argument rather than a `Quiver` instance, so that several arrow
+families can coexist on one vertex type, and so that instance search finds `Fintype (Q v w)`
+directly. An assignment binds its endpoints strict-implicitly, as `∀ ⦃v w⦄, Q v w → K`: it is
+applied to an arrow as `f e`, while `f` on its own is not specialised to unknown endpoints.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+open Finset Pointwise
+
+universe u u' v v' w
+
+variable {V : Type u} (Q : V → V → Type v) (K : Type w)
+
+/-- An *arrow assignment* of the arrow family `Q` with values in `K`: a value `f e : K` for every
+arrow `e : Q v w`. It carries no sign, capacity or conservation constraint, and inherits the
+pointwise algebraic structure of `K`. -/
+abbrev Assignment := ∀ ⦃v w : V⦄, Q v w → K
+
+variable {Q K}
+
+section AddCommMonoid
+
+variable [AddCommMonoid K] [∀ v w, Fintype (Q v w)]
+
+/-- The total value of the assignment `f` on the arrows from a vertex of `S` to a vertex of `T`.
+Every arrow is counted once, so parallel arrows add; when `S` and `T` meet, loops at their common
+vertices are counted. -/

+  ∑ v ∈ S, ∑ w ∈ T, ∑ e : Q v w, f e
+

+module
+
+import TauCeti.Combinatorics.Hypergraph.Colored.EditDiscrepancy
+import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum
+
+/-!
+# Regression examples for the edit discrepancy of colored three-graphs
+
+These downstream examples check the normalization of the edit discrepancy through the public API:
+hosts with fewer than three vertices, including the empty host, have no triples and hence
+discrepancy `0`, while recoloring the one triple of a three-vertex host gives `6 / 3³ = 2 / 9`,
+not the fraction `1` of disagreeing unordered triples.
+-/
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+open Colored3Graph
+
+-- The empty host has no triples to disagree on.
+example (H H' : Colored3Graph Bool Empty) : H.editDiscrepancy3 H' = 0 := by
+  simp [editDiscrepancy3_def]
+
+-- A two-vertex host has no triples either.
+example (H H' : Colored3Graph Bool (Fin 2)) : H.editDiscrepancy3 H' = 0 := by
+  have : IsEmpty (Set.powersetCard (Fin 2) 3) := by
+    rw [← not_nonempty_iff, Set.powersetCard.nonempty_iff]
+    simp
+  simp [editDiscrepancy3_def, Set.eq_empty_of_isEmpty]
+
+-- Recoloring the single triple of a three-vertex host has discrepancy `6 / 27`.
+example : (const true : Colored3Graph Bool (Fin 3)).editDiscrepancy3 (const false) = 2 / 9 := by
+  have : {s : Set.powersetCard (Fin 3) 3 | true ≠ false} = Set.univ := by simp
+  rw [editDiscrepancy3_def]
+  simp only [color_const]
+  rw [this, Set.ncard_univ, Set.powersetCard.card]
+  norm_num
+
+-- Approximations compose with their errors added.
+example {V : Type*} (H₁ H₂ H₃ : Colored3Graph Bool V) (h₁₂ : H₁.Approximates3 H₂ (1 / 10))
+    (h₃₂ : H₃.Approximates3 H₂ (1 / 5)) : H₁.Approximates3 H₃ (3 / 10) := by
+  exact (h₁₂.trans h₃₂.symm).mono (by norm_num)
+
+end TauCeti

+/-!
+# Regression examples for infinitary equivalence
+
+These downstream examples use the public API. The forward direction of Karp's theorem holds at a
+carrier in a higher universe than both structures, and agreement at `ℕ` transports to every
+encodable carrier. Contrapositively, `(ℕ, ≤)` and `(ℤ, ≤)` are not potentially isomorphic: the
+sentence asserting a least element holds in the first and fails in the second.
+-/
+
+universe u
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language
+
+-- An isomorphism gives agreement on sentences branching over a carrier in any universe.
+example {L : Language} [L.IsRelational] {M N : Type} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N]
+    (e : M ≃[L] N) (κ : Type u) : InfEquivAt (L := L) κ M N :=
+  e.potentialIso.infEquivAt κ
+
+-- Agreement at `ℕ` transports to every encodable carrier.
+example {L : Language} {M N : Type*} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] (κ : Type*) [Encodable κ]
+    (h : InfEquivAt (L := L) ℕ M N) : InfEquivAt (L := L) κ M N :=
+  h.of_reindex (IndexCoding.ofEncodable κ)
+
+-- `(ℕ, ≤)` has a least element and `(ℤ, ≤)` does not, so they are not potentially isomorphic.
+example :
+    letI := Language.orderStructure ℕ
+    letI := Language.orderStructure ℤ
+    ¬ PotentialIso (L := Language.order) ℕ ℤ := by
+  let _ := Language.orderStructure ℕ
+  let _ := Language.orderStructure ℤ
+  intro h
+  -- `∃ x, ∀ y, x ≤ y`, with `x` and `y` the bound variables `0` and `1`.
+  let φ : Language.order.SentenceInf Unit :=
+    (BoundedFormulaInf.rel leSymb ![Term.var (Sum.inr 0), Term.var (Sum.inr 1)]).all.ex
+  have : Language.order.OrderedStructure ℕ := ⟨fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩
+  have : Language.order.OrderedStructure ℤ := ⟨fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩
+  have hφ : (∃ x : ℕ, ∀ y : ℕ, x ≤ y) ↔ ∃ x : ℤ, ∀ y : ℤ, x ≤ y := by
+    simpa [φ, Fin.snoc] using infEquivAt_iff.1 (h.infEquivAt Unit) φ
+  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hφ.1 ⟨0, Nat.zero_le⟩
+  have := hx (x - 1)
+  omega
+
+end TauCeti

+/-!
+# Multiplication by the pencil of a function
+
+For a nonzero function `z`, write `Z` and `D` for its zero and pole divisors.
+The sections `1, z` of `L(D)` have no common zero; for nonconstant `z` they form
+a pencil. If `deg (A - Z) > 2g - 2`, then every element of `L(A + D)` is
+`a + z b` with `a, b ∈ L(A)`. The results also allow constant `z`.
+
+In particular, for `D = (z)∞` and sufficiently large `n`,
+`L((n + 1)D) = L(nD) + z L(nD)`. Iteration expresses all higher sections using
+powers of `z` and a single finite-dimensional space of sections. This is the
+multiplication input for finite generation of the section ring
+`TauCeti.Divisor.sectionRing D` over the subalgebra generated by its two degree-one
+sections `1, z`; for `z` transcendental over `k`, `D` has positive degree and this
+subalgebra is a polynomial algebra in two variables.
+
+The argument is the base-point-free pencil calculation: the intersection of
+`L(A)` and `z L(A)` is `L(A - Z)`, and Riemann–Roch computes the dimension of their
+sum. Multiplication by `z` is the existing equivalence
+`TauCeti.riemannRochSpaceEquivSubPrincipal`.
+
+## References
+
+* Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*, Chapter IV, Section 3, for the
+  base-point-free pencil argument and section rings.
+* Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, second edition,
+  Theorem 1.5.17, for Riemann–Roch in high degree.
+-/

+/-- The pencil `1, z` generates `L(A + (z)∞)` from `L(A)` in high degree.
+The second summand is `z L(A)`, expressed as a Riemann–Roch space via the principal divisor. -/
+theorem riemannRochSpace_add_poles_eq_sup (hF : IsFunctionField k F)
+    (hex : IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F) (z : Fˣ) (A : Divisor k F)
+    (hA : 2 * (genus k F : ℤ) - 1 ≤ Divisor.degree (A - Divisor.zeros hF z)) :
+    riemannRochSpace (A + Divisor.poles hF z) =
+      riemannRochSpace A ⊔ riemannRochSpace (A - Divisor.principal hF z) := by
+  have hZ : 0 ≤ Divisor.zeros hF z := (Divisor.isEffective_zeros hF z).zero_le

+  have hinf : A ⊓ (A - Divisor.principal hF z) = A - Divisor.zeros hF z := by
+    ext P
+    simp only [WeilDivisor.coeff_inf, WeilDivisor.coeff_sub,
+      Divisor.coeff_principal, Divisor.coeff_zeros]
+    omega
+  have hsup : A ⊔ (A - Divisor.principal hF z) = A + Divisor.poles hF z := by
+    ext P
+    simp only [WeilDivisor.coeff_sup, WeilDivisor.coeff_add, WeilDivisor.coeff_sub,
+      Divisor.coeff_principal, Divisor.coeff_poles]
+    omega
+  have hle : riemannRochSpace A ⊔ riemannRochSpace (A - Divisor.principal hF z) ≤
+      riemannRochSpace (A + Divisor.poles hF z) := by
+    rw [← hsup]
+    exact sup_le (riemannRochSpace_mono le_sup_left) (riemannRochSpace_mono le_sup_right)
+  have hlow : A - Divisor.zeros hF z ≤ A := sub_le_self _ hZ
+  have hhigh : A ≤ A + Divisor.poles hF z := le_add_of_nonneg_right hD

+    hF hex hA
+  have hdimA := Divisor.dim_eq_degree_add_one_sub_genus_of_two_mul_genus_sub_one_le_degree
+    hF hex (hA.trans (Divisor.degree_le_of_le hlow))
+  have hdimHigh := Divisor.dim_eq_degree_add_one_sub_genus_of_two_mul_genus_sub_one_le_degree
+    hF hex (hA.trans (Divisor.degree_le_of_le (hlow.trans hhigh)))

+  have := finiteDimensional_riemannRochSpace hF (A - Divisor.principal hF z)
+  have := finiteDimensional_riemannRochSpace hF (A + Divisor.poles hF z)

+    at hdimLow hdimHigh
+  rw [← Divisor.dim_def]
+  omega

+/-- Every section of `A + (z)∞` decomposes as `a + z b` with both terms drawn from `L(A)`,

+    (hex : IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F) (z : Fˣ) (A : Divisor k F)

+      exact congrArg Subtype.val

+  · rintro ⟨a, ha, b, hb, rfl⟩
+    exact Submodule.add_mem_sup ha (mul_mem_riemannRochSpace_sub_principal hF z hb)

+The bound is on the preceding multiple, so all three Riemann–Roch dimensions are in high degree. -/
+theorem mem_riemannRochSpace_succ_nsmul_poles_iff (hF : IsFunctionField k F)
+    (hex : IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F) (z : Fˣ) (n : ℕ)
+    (hn : 2 * (genus k F : ℤ) - 1 ≤ ((n : ℤ) - 1) * Divisor.degree (Divisor.poles hF z)) (f : F) :
+    f ∈ riemannRochSpace ((n + 1) • Divisor.poles hF z) ↔
+      ∃ a ∈ riemannRochSpace (n • Divisor.poles hF z),
+        ∃ b ∈ riemannRochSpace (n • Divisor.poles hF z), f = a + (z : F) * b := by
+  have hbound : 2 * (genus k F : ℤ) - 1 ≤
+      Divisor.degree (n • Divisor.poles hF z - Divisor.zeros hF z) := by
+    rw [Divisor.degree_sub, map_nsmul, nsmul_eq_mul, Divisor.degree_zeros_eq_degree_poles hF z]
+    nlinarith [hn]
+  simpa only [add_nsmul, one_nsmul] using
+    mem_riemannRochSpace_add_poles_iff hF hex z (n • Divisor.poles hF z) hbound f
+
+/-- All higher sections are generated by one space `L(ND)` and bounded powers of `z`,
+where `D = (z)∞`. Thus a basis of `L(ND)` supplies finitely many generators for the
+high-degree part of the section ring as a module over the pencil `1, z`. -/
+theorem riemannRochSpace_add_nsmul_poles_eq_span (hF : IsFunctionField k F)
+    (hex : IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F) (z : Fˣ) (N : ℕ)
+    (hN : 2 * (genus k F : ℤ) - 1 ≤ ((N : ℤ) - 1) * Divisor.degree (Divisor.poles hF z))
+    (m : ℕ) :
+    riemannRochSpace ((N + m) • Divisor.poles hF z) =
+      Submodule.span k {f : F | ∃ i ≤ m, ∃ a ∈ riemannRochSpace (N • Divisor.poles hF z),
+        f = (z : F) ^ i * a} := by
+  have hD : 0 ≤ Divisor.poles hF z := (Divisor.isEffective_poles hF z).zero_le
+  have hdegD : 0 ≤ Divisor.degree (Divisor.poles hF z) := Divisor.degree_nonneg hD
+  induction m with
+  | zero =>
+    apply le_antisymm
+    · intro f hf
+      exact Submodule.subset_span ⟨0, le_refl 0, f, by simpa using hf, by simp⟩
+    · refine Submodule.span_le.mpr ?_
+      rintro f ⟨i, hi, a, ha, rfl⟩
+      have hi0 : i = 0 := by omega
+      simpa [hi0] using ha
+  | succ m ih =>
+    apply le_antisymm
+    · intro f hf
+      have hbound : 2 * (genus k F : ℤ) - 1 ≤
+          (((N + m : ℕ) : ℤ) - 1) * Divisor.degree (Divisor.poles hF z) := by
+        push_cast
+        nlinarith
+      obtain ⟨a, ha, b, hb, rfl⟩ :=
+        (mem_riemannRochSpace_succ_nsmul_poles_iff hF hex z (N + m) hbound f).mp hf
+      clear hf
+      rw [ih] at ha hb
+      refine Submodule.add_mem _ ?_ ?_
+      · exact Submodule.span_mono (by
+          rintro f ⟨i, hi, a, ha, rfl⟩
+          exact ⟨i, by omega, a, ha, rfl⟩) ha
+      · refine Submodule.mapsTo_span (f := LinearMap.mulLeft k (z : F)) ?_ hb
+        rintro f ⟨i, hi, a, ha, rfl⟩
+        exact ⟨i + 1, by omega, a, ha, by simp [pow_succ, mul_assoc, mul_left_comm]⟩
+    · refine Submodule.span_le.mpr ?_
+      rintro f ⟨i, hi, a, ha, rfl⟩
+      have hpow : (z : F) ^ i ∈ riemannRochSpace (i • Divisor.poles hF z) := by
+        simpa using pow_mem_riemannRochSpace_zsmul (mem_riemannRochSpace_poles hF z) i
+      have hmul := mul_mem_riemannRochSpace_add hpow ha
+      rw [← add_nsmul] at hmul
+      exact riemannRochSpace_mono (nsmul_le_nsmul_left hD (by omega)) hmul
+

+/-!
+# The Weyl group of a maximal torus is finite
+
+For a maximal torus `T` of a compact finite-dimensional real Lie group `G`, the Weyl group
+`N(T) / T` is finite. The proof has three steps.
+
+* **The integral lattice spans.** The elements `X ∈ Lie(T)` with `lieExp X = 1` span `Lie(T)`:
+  through the closed-subgroup theorem `T` is itself a compact commutative Lie group with Lie
+  algebra `Lie(T)`, whose exponential kernel is a lattice of full rank.
+* **The normalizer has the Lie algebra of the centralizer.** For `X` in the Lie algebra of the
+  normalizer of a torus `T`, the operators `Ad (lieExp (s • X))` preserve the integral lattice of
+  `Lie(T)`, which is discrete, and depend continuously on `s`; so they fix the lattice pointwise,
+  hence fix `Lie(T)`, and the one-parameter subgroup of `X` centralizes `T`. For a maximal torus
+  of a compact group the centralizer has the Lie algebra of `T`.
+* **Openness.** A closed subgroup `T ≤ K` with `Lie(K) ≤ Lie(T)` is open in `K`, because near the
+  identity `K` is the exponential image of its Lie algebra. So `T` is open in its normalizer,
+  which is compact; the quotient of a compact group by an open subgroup is finite.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `TauCeti.Lie.IsTorus.span_setOf_lieExp_eq_one`: the integral lattice of a torus spans its Lie
+  algebra.
+* `TauCeti.Lie.IsTorus.lieSubalgebraOfSubgroup_normalizer`: the normalizer and the centralizer of
+  a torus have the same Lie algebra.
+* `TauCeti.Lie.IsMaximalTorus.lieSubalgebraOfSubgroup_normalizer`: the normalizer of a maximal
+  torus of a compact Lie group has the Lie algebra of the torus.
+* `TauCeti.Lie.IsMaximalTorus.finite_normalizerQuotient`: **the Weyl group of a maximal torus of a
+  compact Lie group is finite.**
+
+## References
+
+* T. Bröcker and T. tom Dieck, *Representations of Compact Lie Groups*, Springer GTM 98 (1985),
+  Chapter IV, § 1 (Maximal Tori).
+* D. Bump, *Lie Groups*, 2nd ed., Springer GTM 225 (2013), Chapter 15 (Tori).
+-/

+/-!
+# The Levi form on a complex manifold
+
+Let `M` be a complex manifold modelled on `𝓘(ℂ, E)`, and let `f : M → ℝ`. The **Levi form**
+`TauCeti.manifoldLeviForm E f x` of `f` at `x` is the Levi form `TauCeti.leviForm` of the
+coordinate expression of `f` in the preferred chart at `x`. It is a sesquilinear form on the model
+space `E`, which is the tangent space at `x`.
+
+Unlike the real Hessian, the Levi form of a function which is real `C²` at `x` is intrinsic at
+every point: in any chart `e` at `x` of the holomorphic `C²` maximal atlas, the Levi form of the
+coordinate expression `f ∘ e.symm`, evaluated on the images of tangent vectors under the derivative
+of `e`, is `TauCeti.manifoldLeviForm E f x`. This is because the second derivative of a holomorphic
+chart transition is complex bilinear and does not contribute to the Levi form.
+
+The underlying real manifold of `M` is modelled on `𝓘(ℝ, E)`, with the same charts, and its
+holomorphic charts are real `C²` charts (`IsManifold.maximalAtlas_subset_restrictScalars`). Its
+critical Hessian `TauCeti.criticalHessian 𝓘(ℝ, E) f x` is the real second derivative in the
+preferred chart, and the Levi form of `f` is the Levi form of this real bilinear form. In
+particular, for `C²` `f` the diagonal of the Levi form is one quarter of
+`Hess f(v, v) + Hess f(I • v, I • v)`. At a critical point the critical Hessian is intrinsic as
+well, and this diagonal may be computed from the real Hessian in any real `C²` chart.
+Strict plurisubharmonicity and strong `q`-pseudoconvexity of `f` at `x` are positivity conditions
+on `TauCeti.manifoldLeviForm E f x`, so for `f` real `C²` at `x` they may be checked in any
+holomorphic chart. Consequently the index bounds of strongly `q`-pseudoconvex functions hold for
+the manifold Morse index: at a critical point where `f` is strongly `q`-pseudoconvex, the Morse
+index is at most `dim_ℂ E + q`.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `TauCeti.manifoldLeviForm E f x`: the Levi form of `f` at `x`, computed in the preferred chart.
+* `TauCeti.IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt E f x`,
+  `TauCeti.IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt E q f x`: positive definiteness of the Levi form at
+  `x`, on all of `E` or on a complex subspace of codimension at most `q`.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `TauCeti.leviForm_comp_symm_apply_of_mem_maximalAtlas`: for `f` real `C²` at `x`, the Levi
+  form of the coordinate expression in any holomorphic `C²` chart at `x` is the manifold Levi
+  form.
+* `TauCeti.re_manifoldLeviForm_apply`, `TauCeti.im_manifoldLeviForm_apply`: the real and imaginary
+  parts of the Levi form in terms of the real critical Hessian.
+* `TauCeti.manifoldLeviForm_apply_self`: for `C²` `f`, its diagonal is the real number
+  `(Hess f(v, v) + Hess f(I • v, I • v)) / 4`.
+* `TauCeti.manifoldLeviForm_add`, `TauCeti.manifoldLeviForm_neg`,
+  `TauCeti.manifoldLeviForm_mul_apply`, `TauCeti.manifoldLeviForm_scalar_comp_apply`: the sum,
+  negation, product and composition rules.
+* `TauCeti.manifoldLeviForm_comp_apply`: the pullback rule under a complex `C²` map.
+* `TauCeti.le_re_manifoldLeviForm_scalar_comp_apply_self`: post-composition with an increasing
+  convex function preserves positivity of the Levi form.
+* `TauCeti.isManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt_iff_criticalHessian`: strict plurisubharmonicity
+  in terms of the real critical Hessian.
+* `TauCeti.IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt.scalar_comp` and
+  `TauCeti.IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt.scalar_comp`: increasing convex post-composition
+  preserves the corresponding positivity conditions.
+* `TauCeti.IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt.comp` and
+  `TauCeti.IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt.comp`: the positivity conditions restrict along
+  holomorphic immersions.
+* `TauCeti.re_manifoldLeviForm_apply_of_mem_maximalAtlas` and
+  `TauCeti.im_manifoldLeviForm_apply_of_mem_maximalAtlas`: at a critical point, the real and
+  imaginary parts may be computed from the real Hessian in any real `C²` chart.
+* `TauCeti.manifoldLeviForm_apply_self_of_mem_maximalAtlas`: at a critical point the same holds
+  with the real Hessian computed in any real `C²` chart.
+* `TauCeti.isManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt_iff_of_mem_maximalAtlas` and
+  `TauCeti.isManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt_iff_of_mem_maximalAtlas`: for `f` real `C²` at `x`,
+  these positivity conditions may be checked in any holomorphic chart.
+* `TauCeti.IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt.manifoldMorseIndex_le` and
+  `TauCeti.IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt.manifoldMorseIndex_le`: the manifold Morse index
+  bounds `λ ≤ n + q` and `λ ≤ n` at critical points.
+
+## References

+* J. Milnor, *Morse Theory*, Princeton University Press, 1963, Section 7.
+* R. Hain, *Notes on the Morse theory of complex manifolds*, Section 2.

+/-- The **Levi form** of a real function `f` on a complex manifold at `x`: the Levi form of the
+coordinate expression of `f` in the preferred chart at `x`. It is a sesquilinear form on the model
+space `E`, which is the tangent space `TangentSpace 𝓘(ℂ, E) x`. By
+`TauCeti.leviForm_comp_symm_apply_of_mem_maximalAtlas`, when `f` is real `C²` at `x` it may be
+computed in any chart at `x` of the holomorphic `C²` maximal atlas. -/
+def manifoldLeviForm (f : M → ℝ) (x : M) : E →ₗ⋆[ℂ] E →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ :=
+  leviForm (f ∘ (chartAt E x).symm) (chartAt E x x)

+/-- The manifold Levi form is the Levi form of the coordinate expression in the preferred chart. -/
+theorem manifoldLeviForm_def :
+    manifoldLeviForm E f x = leviForm (f ∘ (chartAt E x).symm) (chartAt E x x) :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- The Levi form of a function depends only on its germ. -/
+theorem manifoldLeviForm_congr_of_eventuallyEq {g : M → ℝ} (hfg : f =ᶠ[𝓝 x] g) :

+  have hfg' : f ∘ (chartAt E x).symm =ᶠ[𝓝 (chartAt E x x)] g ∘ (chartAt E x).symm :=
+    (hchart ▸ hfg).comp_tendsto ((chartAt E x).continuousAt_symm (mem_chart_target E x))
+  rw [manifoldLeviForm_def, manifoldLeviForm_def, leviForm_congr_of_eventuallyEq hfg']
