+@[simp]
+theorem manifoldLeviForm_neg (f : M → ℝ) (x : M) :
+    manifoldLeviForm E (-f) x = -manifoldLeviForm E f x :=
+  leviForm_neg (f ∘ (chartAt E x).symm) (chartAt E x x)
+
+/-- **The product rule** for the Levi form on a complex manifold. Writing `∂f` for the
+complex-linear extension `StrongDual.extendRCLike` of the real differential `mvfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) f x`,
+the Levi form of `f g` at `x` is `f(x) L g + g(x) L f + (conj (∂f v) ∂g w + conj (∂g v) ∂f w) / 4`.
+-/
+theorem manifoldLeviForm_mul_apply {g : M → ℝ} (hf : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) 2 f x)
+    (hg : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) 2 g x) (v w : E) :
+    manifoldLeviForm E (f * g) x v w =
+      f x * manifoldLeviForm E g x v w + g x * manifoldLeviForm E f x v w +
+        (4 : ℂ)⁻¹ *
+          (conj ((StrongDual.extendRCLike (F := E) (mvfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) f x) : StrongDual ℂ E) v) *
+              (StrongDual.extendRCLike (F := E) (mvfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) g x) : StrongDual ℂ E) w +
+            conj ((StrongDual.extendRCLike (F := E) (mvfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) g x) : StrongDual ℂ E) v) *
+              (StrongDual.extendRCLike (F := E) (mvfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) f x) : StrongDual ℂ E) w) := by
+  have h := leviForm_mul_apply hf.contDiffAt_comp_chartAt_symm
+    hg.contDiffAt_comp_chartAt_symm v w
+  rwa [(hf.mdifferentiableAt (by norm_num)).fderiv_comp_chartAt_symm,
+    (hg.mdifferentiableAt (by norm_num)).fderiv_comp_chartAt_symm, comp_apply, comp_apply,
+    (chartAt E x).left_inv (mem_chart_source E x)] at h
+
+/-- **The composition rule** for the Levi form on a complex manifold, for post-composition with a
+function of one real variable. Writing `∂f` for the complex-linear extension
+`StrongDual.extendRCLike` of `mvfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) f x`, the Levi form of `φ ∘ f` at `x` is
+`φ'(f x) L f + φ''(f x) conj (∂f v) ∂f w / 4`. -/
+theorem manifoldLeviForm_scalar_comp_apply {φ : ℝ → ℝ} (hφ : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 φ (f x))
+    (hf : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) 2 f x) (v w : E) :
+    manifoldLeviForm E (φ ∘ f) x v w =
+      deriv φ (f x) * manifoldLeviForm E f x v w +
+        iteratedDeriv 2 φ (f x) * ((4 : ℂ)⁻¹ *
+          (conj ((StrongDual.extendRCLike (F := E) (mvfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) f x) : StrongDual ℂ E) v) *
+            (StrongDual.extendRCLike (F := E) (mvfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) f x) : StrongDual ℂ E) w)) := by
+  have hφ' : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 φ ((f ∘ (chartAt E x).symm) (chartAt E x x)) := by
+    rwa [comp_apply, (chartAt E x).left_inv (mem_chart_source E x)]
+  have h := leviForm_scalar_comp_apply hφ' hf.contDiffAt_comp_chartAt_symm v w
+  rwa [(hf.mdifferentiableAt (by norm_num)).fderiv_comp_chartAt_symm, comp_apply,
+    (chartAt E x).left_inv (mem_chart_source E x)] at h
+
+/-- **Post-composition with a convex function** on a complex manifold. If `φ'' ≥ 0` at `f x`, then
+the diagonal of the Levi form of `φ ∘ f` dominates `φ'(f x)` times the diagonal of the Levi form
+of `f`. In particular, if moreover `φ'(f x) > 0`, post-composition with `φ` preserves strict
+positivity of the Levi form at `x`. -/
+theorem le_re_manifoldLeviForm_scalar_comp_apply_self {φ : ℝ → ℝ} (hφ : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 φ (f x))
+    (hf : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) 2 f x) (hφ₂ : 0 ≤ iteratedDeriv 2 φ (f x)) (v : E) :
+    deriv φ (f x) * (manifoldLeviForm E f x v v).re ≤
+      (manifoldLeviForm E (φ ∘ f) x v v).re := by
+  have hfx : (f ∘ (chartAt E x).symm) (chartAt E x x) = f x := by
+    rw [comp_apply, (chartAt E x).left_inv (mem_chart_source E x)]
+  have h := le_re_leviForm_scalar_comp_apply_self (hfx ▸ hφ) hf.contDiffAt_comp_chartAt_symm
+    (hfx ▸ hφ₂) v
+  rwa [hfx] at h
+
+section Pullback
+
+variable {F N : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℂ F] [TopologicalSpace N]
+  [ChartedSpace F N] {g : M → N} {u : N → ℝ}
+
+/-- **The holomorphic pullback rule** for the Levi form on complex manifolds. If `g` is complex
+`C²` at `x` and `u` is real `C²` at `g x`, then the Levi form of `u ∘ g` is the pullback of the
+Levi form of `u` by the complex manifold derivative of `g`. -/
+theorem manifoldLeviForm_comp_apply (hu : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℝ, F) 𝓘(ℝ) 2 u (g x))
+    (hg : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℂ, E) 𝓘(ℂ, F) 2 g x) (v w : E) :
+    manifoldLeviForm E (u ∘ g) x v w =
+      manifoldLeviForm F u (g x) (mfderiv 𝓘(ℂ, E) 𝓘(ℂ, F) g x v)
+        (mfderiv 𝓘(ℂ, E) 𝓘(ℂ, F) g x w) := by
+  let G : E → F := chartAt F (g x) ∘ g ∘ (chartAt E x).symm
+  have hx' : (chartAt E x).symm (chartAt E x x) = x :=
+    (chartAt E x).left_inv (mem_chart_source E x)
+  have hG : ContDiffAt ℂ 2 G (chartAt E x x) := by
+    rw [← contDiffWithinAt_univ]
+    simpa only [G, extChartAt_coe, extChartAt_coe_symm, modelWithCornersSelf_coe,
+      modelWithCornersSelf_coe_symm, id_comp, comp_id, Set.range_id] using
+      (contMDiffAt_iff.mp hg).2
+  have hGx : G (chartAt E x x) = chartAt F (g x) (g x) := by
+    simp only [G, Function.comp_apply, hx']
+  have hD : fderiv ℂ G (chartAt E x x) = mfderiv 𝓘(ℂ, E) 𝓘(ℂ, F) g x := by
+    rw [(hg.mdifferentiableAt (by norm_num)).mfderiv_abuse]
+    have hcoord : writtenInExtChartAt 𝓘(ℂ, E) 𝓘(ℂ, F) x g = G := by
+      ext z
+      rfl
+    have hpoint : extChartAt 𝓘(ℂ, E) x x = chartAt E x x := by rfl
+    rw [hcoord, modelWithCornersSelf_coe, Set.range_id, fderivWithin_univ, hpoint]
+  have hcomp : (u ∘ g) ∘ (chartAt E x).symm =ᶠ[𝓝 (chartAt E x x)]
+      (u ∘ (chartAt F (g x)).symm) ∘ G := by
+    have hcont : Tendsto (g ∘ (chartAt E x).symm) (𝓝 (chartAt E x x)) (𝓝 (g x)) := by
+      simpa only [ContinuousAt, Function.comp_apply, hx'] using hg.continuousAt.comp_of_eq
+        ((chartAt E x).continuousAt_symm (mem_chart_target E x)) hx'
+    have hmem : (g ∘ (chartAt E x).symm) ⁻¹' (chartAt F (g x)).source ∈
+        𝓝 (chartAt E x x) :=
+      hcont ((chartAt F (g x)).open_source.mem_nhds (mem_chart_source F (g x)))
+    filter_upwards [hmem] with z hz
+    simp only [G, Function.comp_apply]
+    have hz' : g ((chartAt E x).symm z) ∈ (chartAt F (g x)).source := hz
+    rw [(chartAt F (g x)).left_inv hz']
+  rw [manifoldLeviForm_def, manifoldLeviForm_def, leviForm_congr_of_eventuallyEq hcomp]
+  rw [TauCeti.leviForm_comp_apply (hGx ▸ hu.contDiffAt_comp_chartAt_symm) hG, hGx, hD]
+  rfl
+
+end Pullback
+
+/-! ### Independence of the holomorphic chart -/
+
+section Chart
+
+variable [IsManifold 𝓘(ℂ, E) 2 M] {e : OpenPartialHomeomorph M E}
+
+/-- **The Levi form in an arbitrary holomorphic chart.** Let `e` be a chart of the `C²` maximal
+atlas of the complex manifold `M`, with `x` in its source, and let `f` be `C²` at `x`. The Levi
+form of the coordinate expression `f ∘ e.symm` at `e x`, evaluated on the images of `v` and `w`
+under the derivative of `e`, is the Levi form of `f` at `x`. Unlike the real Hessian, the Levi form
+thus transforms as a Hermitian form under holomorphic changes of coordinates at every point. -/
+theorem leviForm_comp_symm_apply_of_mem_maximalAtlas
+    (he : e ∈ IsManifold.maximalAtlas 𝓘(ℂ, E) 2 M) (hx : x ∈ e.source)
+    (hf : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) 2 f x) (v w : E) :
+    leviForm (f ∘ e.symm) (e x) (mfderiv 𝓘(ℂ, E) 𝓘(ℂ, E) e x v)
+        (mfderiv 𝓘(ℂ, E) 𝓘(ℂ, E) e x w) =
+      manifoldLeviForm E f x v w := by
+  set y := chartAt E x x
+  have hy : (chartAt E x).symm y = x := (chartAt E x).left_inv (mem_chart_source E x)
+  -- The holomorphic transition map from the preferred chart to `e`.
+  set φ : E → E := e ∘ (chartAt E x).symm
+  have hφy : φ y = e x := by simp only [φ, comp_apply, hy]
+  have hφ : ContDiffAt ℂ 2 φ y := by
+    have h := (contMDiffAt_of_mem_maximalAtlas he hx).comp_of_eq
+      (contMDiffAt_symm_of_mem_maximalAtlas (IsManifold.chart_mem_maximalAtlas x)
+        (mem_chart_target E x)) hy
+    exact contMDiffAt_iff_contDiffAt.mp h
+  have hDφ : fderiv ℂ φ y = mfderiv 𝓘(ℂ, E) 𝓘(ℂ, E) e x := by
+    rw [(mdifferentiableAt_of_mem_maximalAtlas
+      (IsManifold.maximalAtlas_subset_of_le (by norm_num) he) hx).mfderiv_abuse]
+    simp [writtenInExtChartAt, φ, y]
+  -- The coordinate expression in `e` is `C²`, as `e` is a real `C²` chart.
+  have hfe : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 (f ∘ e.symm) (φ y) := by
+    have h := (contMDiffAt_iff_contDiffAt_comp_extend_symm
+      (IsManifold.maximalAtlas_subset_restrictScalars ℝ he) hx).mp hf
+    simpa only [hφy, OpenPartialHomeomorph.extend_coe, OpenPartialHomeomorph.extend_coe_symm,
+      modelWithCornersSelf_coe, modelWithCornersSelf_coe_symm, id_comp, comp_id] using h
+  -- Near `y`, the preferred coordinate expression factors through `φ`.
+  have hfg : f ∘ (chartAt E x).symm =ᶠ[𝓝 y] (f ∘ e.symm) ∘ φ := by
+    have hmem : (chartAt E x).symm ⁻¹' e.source ∈ 𝓝 y :=
+      ((chartAt E x).continuousAt_symm (mem_chart_target E x)).preimage_mem_nhds
+        (by rw [hy]; exact e.open_source.mem_nhds hx)
+    filter_upwards [hmem] with z hz
+    simp only [φ, comp_apply, e.left_inv hz]
+  rw [manifoldLeviForm_def, leviForm_congr_of_eventuallyEq hfg,
+    leviForm_comp_apply (hφy ▸ hfe) hφ, hDφ, hφy]
+  -- The two sides differ only in reading the model space `E` as the tangent spaces of `M`.
+  rfl
+
+end Chart
+
+/-! ### Strict plurisubharmonicity and strong pseudoconvexity -/
+
+section Positivity
+
+variable (E) in
+/-- A real function `f` on a complex manifold is **strictly plurisubharmonic** at `x` if its Levi
+form at `x` is positive definite: `0 < Re (manifoldLeviForm E f x v v)` for every nonzero `v`
+(`TauCeti.isManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt_iff`). As for `TauCeti.manifoldLeviForm`, it is
+defined in the preferred chart at `x`; by
+`TauCeti.isManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt_iff_of_mem_maximalAtlas`, for `f` real `C²` at `x` it
+may be checked in any chart at `x` of the holomorphic `C²` maximal atlas. -/
+def IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt (f : M → ℝ) (x : M) : Prop :=
+  IsStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt (f ∘ (chartAt E x).symm) (chartAt E x x)
+
+variable (E) in
+/-- A real function `f` on a complex manifold modelled on a finite-dimensional space `E` is
+**strongly `q`-pseudoconvex** at `x` if its Levi form at `x` is positive definite on a complex
+subspace `P` of `E` with `dim_ℂ E ≤ dim_ℂ P + q` (`TauCeti.isManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt_iff`).
+As for `TauCeti.manifoldLeviForm`, it is defined in the preferred chart at `x`; by
+`TauCeti.isManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt_iff_of_mem_maximalAtlas`, for `f` real `C²` at `x` it
+may be checked in any chart at `x` of the holomorphic `C²` maximal atlas. -/
+def IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt [FiniteDimensional ℂ E] (q : ℕ) (f : M → ℝ) (x : M) :
+    Prop :=
+  IsStronglyPseudoconvexAt q (f ∘ (chartAt E x).symm) (chartAt E x x)
+
+/-- Strict plurisubharmonicity on a complex manifold is positive definiteness of the Levi form. -/
+theorem isManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt_iff :
+    IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt E f x ↔
+      ∀ v : E, v ≠ 0 → 0 < (manifoldLeviForm E f x v v).re :=
+  isStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt_iff
+
+/-- Strong `q`-pseudoconvexity on a complex manifold is positive definiteness of the Levi form on
+a complex subspace of codimension at most `q`. -/
+theorem isManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt_iff [FiniteDimensional ℂ E] {q : ℕ} :
+    IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt E q f x ↔ ∃ P : Submodule ℂ E,
+      finrank ℂ E ≤ finrank ℂ P + q ∧ ∀ v ∈ P, v ≠ 0 → 0 < (manifoldLeviForm E f x v v).re :=
+  isStronglyPseudoconvexAt_iff
+
+/-- Strict plurisubharmonicity on a complex manifold in terms of the real critical Hessian: `f` is
+strictly plurisubharmonic at `x` exactly when `Hess f(v, v) + Hess f(I • v, I • v) > 0` for every
+`v ≠ 0`. -/
+theorem isManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt_iff_criticalHessian :
+    IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt E f x ↔ ∀ v : E, v ≠ 0 →
+      0 < criticalHessian 𝓘(ℝ, E) f x v v + criticalHessian 𝓘(ℝ, E) f x (I • v) (I • v) := by
+  simp only [isManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt_iff, re_manifoldLeviForm_apply]
+  exact forall₂_congr fun _ _ ↦ div_pos_iff_of_pos_right (by norm_num)
+
+/-- Strong `q`-pseudoconvexity on a complex manifold is weaker for larger `q`. -/
+theorem IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt.mono [FiniteDimensional ℂ E] {q r : ℕ}
+    (h : IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt E q f x) (hqr : q ≤ r) :
+    IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt E r f x := by
+  rw [isManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt_iff] at h ⊢
+  obtain ⟨P, hP, hpos⟩ := h
+  exact ⟨P, by omega, hpos⟩
+
+/-- Strong `0`-pseudoconvexity on a complex manifold is strict plurisubharmonicity. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem isManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt_zero_iff [FiniteDimensional ℂ E] :
+    IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt E 0 f x ↔
+      IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt E f x := by
+  rw [isManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt_iff, isManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt_iff]
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨P, hP, hpos⟩ v hv
+    have hP : P = ⊤ := Submodule.eq_top_of_finrank_eq (le_antisymm P.finrank_le hP)
+    exact hpos v (hP ▸ Submodule.mem_top) hv
+  · exact fun h ↦ ⟨⊤, by simp, fun v _ hv ↦ h v hv⟩
+
+/-- A strictly plurisubharmonic function on a complex manifold is strongly `q`-pseudoconvex for
+every `q`. -/
+theorem IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt.isManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt
+    [FiniteDimensional ℂ E] (h : IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt E f x) (q : ℕ) :
+    IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt E q f x :=
+  IsStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt.isStronglyPseudoconvexAt h q
+
+/-- Post-composition with a function `φ` of one real variable with `φ'(f x) > 0` and
+`φ''(f x) ≥ 0` preserves strict plurisubharmonicity on a complex manifold at `x`. -/
+theorem IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt.scalar_comp {φ : ℝ → ℝ}
+    (h : IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt E f x) (hφ : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 φ (f x))
+    (hf : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) 2 f x) (hφ₁ : 0 < deriv φ (f x))
+    (hφ₂ : 0 ≤ iteratedDeriv 2 φ (f x)) :
+    IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt E (φ ∘ f) x := by
+  rw [isManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt_iff] at h ⊢
+  exact fun v hv ↦ (mul_pos hφ₁ (h v hv)).trans_le
+    (le_re_manifoldLeviForm_scalar_comp_apply_self hφ hf hφ₂ v)
+
+/-- Post-composition with a function `φ` of one real variable with `φ'(f x) > 0` and
+`φ''(f x) ≥ 0` preserves strong `q`-pseudoconvexity on a complex manifold at `x`. -/
+theorem IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt.scalar_comp [FiniteDimensional ℂ E] {q : ℕ}
+    {φ : ℝ → ℝ} (h : IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt E q f x)
+    (hφ : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 φ (f x)) (hf : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) 2 f x)
+    (hφ₁ : 0 < deriv φ (f x)) (hφ₂ : 0 ≤ iteratedDeriv 2 φ (f x)) :
+    IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt E q (φ ∘ f) x := by
+  rw [isManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt_iff] at h ⊢
+  obtain ⟨P, hP, hpos⟩ := h
+  exact ⟨P, hP, fun v hv hv0 ↦ (mul_pos hφ₁ (hpos v hv hv0)).trans_le
+    (le_re_manifoldLeviForm_scalar_comp_apply_self hφ hf hφ₂ v)⟩
+
+/-- Strict plurisubharmonicity on a complex manifold at `x` depends only on the germ of the
+function at `x`. -/
+theorem IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq {g : M → ℝ}
+    (h : IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt E f x) (hfg : g =ᶠ[𝓝 x] f) :
+    IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt E g x := by
+  rw [isManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt_iff, manifoldLeviForm_congr_of_eventuallyEq hfg]
+  exact isManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt_iff.mp h
+
+/-- Strong `q`-pseudoconvexity on a complex manifold at `x` depends only on the germ of the
+function at `x`. -/
+theorem IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq [FiniteDimensional ℂ E] {q : ℕ}
+    {g : M → ℝ} (h : IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt E q f x) (hfg : g =ᶠ[𝓝 x] f) :
+    IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt E q g x := by
+  rw [isManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt_iff, manifoldLeviForm_congr_of_eventuallyEq hfg]
+  exact isManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt_iff.mp h
+
+/-- The sum of two `C²` functions strictly plurisubharmonic at `x` on a complex manifold is
+strictly plurisubharmonic at `x`. -/
+theorem IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt.add {g : M → ℝ}
+    (hf : IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt E f x)
+    (hg : IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt E g x) (hf' : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) 2 f x)
+    (hg' : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) 2 g x) :
+    IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt E (f + g) x := by
+  rw [isManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt_iff] at hf hg ⊢
+  intro v hv
+  rw [manifoldLeviForm_add hf' hg']
+  simpa using add_pos (hf v hv) (hg v hv)
+
+section Pullback
+
+variable {F N : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℂ F] [TopologicalSpace N]
+  [ChartedSpace F N] {g : M → N} {u : N → ℝ}
+
+/-- **Restriction along a holomorphic immersion** of complex manifolds. If `u` is strictly
+plurisubharmonic at `g x` and the complex manifold derivative of the complex `C²` map `g` at `x` is
+injective, then `u ∘ g` is strictly plurisubharmonic at `x`. -/
+theorem IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt.comp
+    (h : IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt F u (g x))
+    (hu : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℝ, F) 𝓘(ℝ) 2 u (g x)) (hg : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℂ, E) 𝓘(ℂ, F) 2 g x)
+    (hg' : Injective (mfderiv 𝓘(ℂ, E) 𝓘(ℂ, F) g x)) :
+    IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt E (u ∘ g) x := by
+  rw [isManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt_iff] at h ⊢
+  intro v hv
+  rw [manifoldLeviForm_comp_apply hu hg]
+  exact h _ ((map_ne_zero_iff _ hg').2 hv)
+
+/-- **Restriction along a holomorphic immersion** of complex manifolds. If `u` is strongly
+`q`-pseudoconvex at `g x` and the complex manifold derivative of the complex `C²` map `g` at `x` is
+injective, then `u ∘ g` is strongly `q`-pseudoconvex at `x`: the preimage of a positive subspace of
+codimension at most `q` is a positive subspace of codimension at most `q`. -/
+theorem IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt.comp [FiniteDimensional ℂ E] [FiniteDimensional ℂ F]
+    {q : ℕ} (h : IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt F q u (g x))
+    (hu : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℝ, F) 𝓘(ℝ) 2 u (g x)) (hg : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℂ, E) 𝓘(ℂ, F) 2 g x)
+    (hg' : Injective (mfderiv 𝓘(ℂ, E) 𝓘(ℂ, F) g x)) :
+    IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt E q (u ∘ g) x := by
+  rw [isManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt_iff] at h ⊢
+  obtain ⟨P, hP, hpos⟩ := h
+  -- The manifold derivative of `g`, typed on the model spaces.
+  let D : E →L[ℂ] F := mfderiv 𝓘(ℂ, E) 𝓘(ℂ, F) g x
+  refine ⟨P.comap (D : E →ₗ[ℂ] F), ?_, fun v hv hv0 ↦ ?_⟩
+  · have := Submodule.finrank_add_finrank_le_finrank_comap_add_finrank (D : E →ₗ[ℂ] F) P
+    omega
+  · rw [manifoldLeviForm_comp_apply hu hg]
+    exact hpos _ hv ((map_ne_zero_iff _ hg').2 hv0)
+
+end Pullback
+
+variable [IsManifold 𝓘(ℂ, E) 2 M] {e : OpenPartialHomeomorph M E}
+
+/-- **Strict plurisubharmonicity in an arbitrary holomorphic chart.** For `f` real `C²` at `x` and
+a chart `e` at `x` of the holomorphic `C²` maximal atlas, `f` is strictly plurisubharmonic at `x`
+if and only if its coordinate expression `f ∘ e.symm` is strictly plurisubharmonic at `e x`. -/
+theorem isManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt_iff_of_mem_maximalAtlas
+    (he : e ∈ IsManifold.maximalAtlas 𝓘(ℂ, E) 2 M) (hx : x ∈ e.source)
+    (hf : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) 2 f x) :
+    IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt E f x ↔
+      IsStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt (f ∘ e.symm) (e x) := by
+  -- The invertible chart derivative, typed on the model space `E`.
+  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ : ∃ D : E ≃L[ℂ] E, (D : E →L[ℂ] E) = mfderiv 𝓘(ℂ, E) 𝓘(ℂ, E) e x :=
+    isInvertible_mfderiv_chart (IsManifold.maximalAtlas_subset_of_le (by norm_num) he) hx
+  have key (v : E) : leviForm (f ∘ e.symm) (e x) (D v) (D v) = manifoldLeviForm E f x v v := by
+    rw [← leviForm_comp_symm_apply_of_mem_maximalAtlas he hx hf, ← hD]
+    -- The two sides differ only in reading `D` as a map between tangent spaces of `M`.
+    rfl
+  rw [isManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt_iff, isStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt_iff]
+  refine ⟨fun h u hu ↦ ?_, fun h v hv ↦ ?_⟩
+  · obtain ⟨v, rfl⟩ := D.surjective u
+    rw [key]
+    exact h v (by simpa using hu)
+  · rw [← key]
+    exact h (D v) (by simpa using hv)
+
+/-- **Strong `q`-pseudoconvexity in an arbitrary holomorphic chart.** For `f` real `C²` at `x` and
+a chart `e` at `x` of the holomorphic `C²` maximal atlas, `f` is strongly `q`-pseudoconvex at `x`
+if and only if its coordinate expression `f ∘ e.symm` is strongly `q`-pseudoconvex at `e x`. -/
+theorem isManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt_iff_of_mem_maximalAtlas [FiniteDimensional ℂ E]
+    {q : ℕ} (he : e ∈ IsManifold.maximalAtlas 𝓘(ℂ, E) 2 M) (hx : x ∈ e.source)
+    (hf : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) 2 f x) :
+    IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt E q f x ↔
+      IsStronglyPseudoconvexAt q (f ∘ e.symm) (e x) := by
+  -- The invertible chart derivative, typed on the model space `E`.
+  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ : ∃ D : E ≃L[ℂ] E, (D : E →L[ℂ] E) = mfderiv 𝓘(ℂ, E) 𝓘(ℂ, E) e x :=
+    isInvertible_mfderiv_chart (IsManifold.maximalAtlas_subset_of_le (by norm_num) he) hx
+  have key (v : E) : leviForm (f ∘ e.symm) (e x) (D v) (D v) = manifoldLeviForm E f x v v := by
+    rw [← leviForm_comp_symm_apply_of_mem_maximalAtlas he hx hf, ← hD]
+    -- The two sides differ only in reading `D` as a map between tangent spaces of `M`.
+    rfl
+  rw [isManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt_iff, isStronglyPseudoconvexAt_iff]
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨P, hP, hpos⟩
+    refine ⟨P.map (D.toLinearEquiv : E →ₗ[ℂ] E), by rwa [LinearEquiv.finrank_map_eq], ?_⟩
+    rintro _ ⟨v, hv, rfl⟩ hv0
+    simp only [LinearEquiv.coe_coe, ContinuousLinearEquiv.coe_toLinearEquiv] at hv0 ⊢
+    rw [key]
+    exact hpos v hv (by simpa using hv0)
+  · rintro ⟨Q, hQ, hpos⟩
+    refine ⟨Q.map (D.symm.toLinearEquiv : E →ₗ[ℂ] E), by rwa [LinearEquiv.finrank_map_eq], ?_⟩
+    rintro _ ⟨u, hu, rfl⟩ hu0
+    simp only [LinearEquiv.coe_coe, ContinuousLinearEquiv.coe_toLinearEquiv] at hu0 ⊢
+    rw [← key, D.apply_symm_apply]
+    exact hpos u hu (by simpa using hu0)
+
+end Positivity
+
+/-! ### Critical points -/
+
+section Critical
+
+variable {e : OpenPartialHomeomorph M E}
+
+/-- **The real part of the Levi form at a critical point, in an arbitrary real chart.** For a
+real `C²` chart `e`, it is the quarter-sum of the real Hessian on the chart derivatives of
+`(v, w)` and `(I • v, I • w)`. -/
+theorem re_manifoldLeviForm_apply_of_mem_maximalAtlas
+    (he : e ∈ IsManifold.maximalAtlas 𝓘(ℝ, E) 2 M) (hx : x ∈ e.source)
+    (hf : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) 2 f x) (hcrit : mvfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) f x = 0) (v w : E) :
+    (manifoldLeviForm E f x v w).re =
+      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ e.symm)) (e x)
+          (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ, E) e x v) (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ, E) e x w) +
+        fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ e.symm)) (e x)
+          (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ, E) e x (I • v))
+          (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ, E) e x (I • w))) / 4 := by
+  have h₁ := criticalHessian_apply_eq_of_mem_maximalAtlas he hx hf hcrit v w
+  have h₂ := criticalHessian_apply_eq_of_mem_maximalAtlas he hx hf hcrit (I • v) (I • w)
+  simp only [OpenPartialHomeomorph.extend_coe, OpenPartialHomeomorph.extend_coe_symm,
+    modelWithCornersSelf_coe, modelWithCornersSelf_coe_symm, id_comp, comp_id] at h₁ h₂
+  rw [re_manifoldLeviForm_apply]
+  -- On the model space `E`, `mvfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) e x` is `mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ, E) e x` by definition.
+  exact congrArg₂ (fun a b : ℝ ↦ (a + b) / 4) h₁ h₂
+
+/-- **The imaginary part of the Levi form at a critical point, in an arbitrary real chart.** For
+a real `C²` chart `e`, it is one quarter of the difference of the two mixed real-Hessian terms on
+the chart derivatives of `(I • v, w)` and `(v, I • w)`. -/
+theorem im_manifoldLeviForm_apply_of_mem_maximalAtlas
+    (he : e ∈ IsManifold.maximalAtlas 𝓘(ℝ, E) 2 M) (hx : x ∈ e.source)
+    (hf : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) 2 f x) (hcrit : mvfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) f x = 0) (v w : E) :
+    (manifoldLeviForm E f x v w).im =
+      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ e.symm)) (e x)
+          (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ, E) e x (I • v))
+          (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ, E) e x w) -
+        fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ e.symm)) (e x)
+          (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ, E) e x v)
+          (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ, E) e x (I • w))) / 4 := by
+  have h₁ := criticalHessian_apply_eq_of_mem_maximalAtlas he hx hf hcrit (I • v) w
+  have h₂ := criticalHessian_apply_eq_of_mem_maximalAtlas he hx hf hcrit v (I • w)
+  simp only [OpenPartialHomeomorph.extend_coe, OpenPartialHomeomorph.extend_coe_symm,
+    modelWithCornersSelf_coe, modelWithCornersSelf_coe_symm, id_comp, comp_id] at h₁ h₂
+  rw [im_manifoldLeviForm_apply]
+  -- On the model space `E`, `mvfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) e x` is `mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ, E) e x` by definition.
+  exact congrArg₂ (fun a b : ℝ ↦ (a - b) / 4) h₁ h₂
+
+/-- **The Levi form at a critical point, from the real Hessian in any chart.** At a critical point
+`x` of a function `f` which is `C²` at `x`, the diagonal value of the Levi form on `v` is
+`(Hess f(v, v) + Hess f(I • v, I • v)) / 4`, where the real Hessian may be computed in any chart
+`e` of the real `C²` maximal atlas, holomorphic or not, after transporting the tangent vectors by
+the derivative of `e`. -/
+theorem manifoldLeviForm_apply_self_of_mem_maximalAtlas
+    (he : e ∈ IsManifold.maximalAtlas 𝓘(ℝ, E) 2 M) (hx : x ∈ e.source)
+    (hf : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) 2 f x) (hcrit : mvfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) f x = 0) (v : E) :
+    manifoldLeviForm E f x v v =
+      ((hessianQuadraticForm (f ∘ e.symm) (e x) (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ, E) e x v) +
+        hessianQuadraticForm (f ∘ e.symm) (e x) (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ, E) e x (I • v))) / 4 :
+          ℝ) := by
+  apply Complex.ext
+  · have h := re_manifoldLeviForm_apply_of_mem_maximalAtlas he hx hf hcrit v v
+    have hq₁ := hessianQuadraticForm_apply (f ∘ e.symm) (e x)
+      (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ, E) e x v)
+    have hq₂ := hessianQuadraticForm_apply (f ∘ e.symm) (e x)
+      (mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ, E) e x (I • v))
+    simp only [Complex.ofReal_re]
+    exact h.trans (congrArg (fun z : ℝ ↦ z / 4) (congrArg₂ (· + ·) hq₁.symm hq₂.symm))
+  · rw [manifoldLeviForm_apply_self hf]
+    simp
+
+variable [FiniteDimensional ℂ E]
+
+/-- **The index bound for strongly `q`-pseudoconvex functions on a complex manifold.** At a
+critical point `x` of a function `f` which is `C²` at `x` and strongly `q`-pseudoconvex at `x`, the
+Morse index of `f` is at most `dim_ℂ E + q`. -/
+theorem IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt.manifoldMorseIndex_le [IsManifold 𝓘(ℂ, E) 2 M] {q : ℕ}
+    (h : IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt E q f x) (hf : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) 2 f x)
+    (hcrit : mvfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) f x = 0) :
+    manifoldMorseIndex 𝓘(ℝ, E) f x ≤ finrank ℂ E + q := by
+  have he : chartAt E x ∈ IsManifold.maximalAtlas 𝓘(ℂ, E) 2 M :=
+    IsManifold.chart_mem_maximalAtlas x
+  rw [manifoldMorseIndex_eq_morseIndex_of_mem_maximalAtlas
+    (IsManifold.maximalAtlas_subset_restrictScalars ℝ he) (mem_chart_source E x) hf hcrit]
+  simpa only [OpenPartialHomeomorph.extend_coe, OpenPartialHomeomorph.extend_coe_symm,
+    modelWithCornersSelf_coe, modelWithCornersSelf_coe_symm, id_comp, comp_id] using
+    IsStronglyPseudoconvexAt.morseIndex_le h
+
+/-- **The index bound for strictly plurisubharmonic functions on a complex manifold.** At a
+critical point `x` of a function `f` which is `C²` at `x` and strictly plurisubharmonic at `x`, the
+Morse index of `f` is at most `dim_ℂ E`. -/
+theorem IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt.manifoldMorseIndex_le [IsManifold 𝓘(ℂ, E) 2 M]
+    (h : IsManifoldStrictlyPlurisubharmonicAt E f x) (hf : ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℝ, E) 𝓘(ℝ) 2 f x)
+    (hcrit : mvfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, E) f x = 0) :
+    manifoldMorseIndex 𝓘(ℝ, E) f x ≤ finrank ℂ E := by
+  simpa using (h.isManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt 0).manifoldMorseIndex_le hf hcrit
+
+end Critical
+
+end TauCeti

+module
+
+public import TauCeti.Geometry.Manifold.Complex.StructureSheaf.Domain
+public import TauCeti.Geometry.Manifold.Complex.StructureSheaf.LocalRing
+public import TauCeti.Geometry.Manifold.Complex.StructureSheaf.Order
+public import Mathlib.RingTheory.DiscreteValuationRing.Basic

+/-!
+# Holomorphic stalks are discrete valuation rings
+
+The stalk of the holomorphic structure sheaf of a complex curve is a discrete valuation
+ring. Every centered local coordinate is a uniformizer. Thus Mathlib's discrete valuation
+and fractional-ideal theory applies to holomorphic germs, providing the local algebra for
+divisor sheaves and their point twists.
+
+The coordinate may be any chart in the maximal differentiable atlas; no compactness,
+connectedness or Hausdorff hypothesis is needed.
+
+## References
+
+* Otto Forster, *Lectures on Riemann Surfaces*, §§1, 6 and 16.
+-/
+
+public noncomputable section
+
+open IsManifold
+open scoped ContDiff Manifold
+open TauCeti TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf
+
+namespace OpenPartialHomeomorph
+
+variable {X : Type} [TopologicalSpace X] [ChartedSpace ℂ X] [IsManifold 𝓘(ℂ) 1 X]
+  (e : OpenPartialHomeomorph X ℂ) (he : e ∈ maximalAtlas 𝓘(ℂ) 1 X) (x : X)
+
+/-- A centered holomorphic coordinate is irreducible in the local ring of germs. -/
+theorem irreducible_holomorphicCoordinateGerm (hx : x ∈ e.source) :
+    Irreducible (holomorphicCoordinateGerm e he x hx) := by
+  apply IsDiscreteValuationRing.irreducible_of_span_eq_maximalIdeal
+    _ (holomorphicCoordinateGerm_ne_zero e he x hx)
+  rw [maximalIdeal_stalk, ker_eval_eq_span_holomorphicCoordinateGerm e he x hx]
+
+end OpenPartialHomeomorph
+
+namespace TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf
+
+variable {X : Type} [TopologicalSpace X] [ChartedSpace ℂ X] [IsManifold 𝓘(ℂ) 1 X]
+
+/-- The stalk of the holomorphic structure sheaf on a complex curve is a discrete valuation
+ring, with any centered local coordinate as uniformizer. -/
+instance instIsDiscreteValuationRingStalk (x : X) :
+    IsDiscreteValuationRing ((holomorphicStructureSheaf 𝓘(ℂ) X).presheaf.stalk x) := by
+  -- The construction uses `OpenPartialHomeomorph.ker_eval_eq_span_holomorphicCoordinateGerm`
+  -- and `TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf.existsUnique_mem_pow_ker_eval_notMem_succ`, then
+  -- Mathlib's `IsDiscreteValuationRing.ofHasUnitMulPowIrreducibleFactorization`.
+  let e := chartAt ℂ x
+  let he := chart_mem_maximalAtlas x (I := 𝓘(ℂ)) (n := 1)
+  let c := e.holomorphicCoordinateGerm he x (mem_chart_source ℂ x)
+  have hc : Irreducible c := e.irreducible_holomorphicCoordinateGerm he x (mem_chart_source ℂ x)
+  apply IsDiscreteValuationRing.ofHasUnitMulPowIrreducibleFactorization
+  refine ⟨c, hc, fun {f} hf => ?_⟩
+  obtain ⟨n, ⟨hn, hnext⟩, -⟩ := existsUnique_mem_pow_ker_eval_notMem_succ x hf
+  rw [e.ker_eval_eq_span_holomorphicCoordinateGerm he x (mem_chart_source ℂ x),
+    Ideal.span_singleton_pow, Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at hn
+  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := hn
+  have hqunit : IsUnit q := by
+    rw [isUnit_stalk_iff]
+    intro hzero
+    have hdiv : c ∣ q :=
+      (e.holomorphicCoordinateGerm_dvd_iff_eval_eq_zero he x (mem_chart_source ℂ x) q).mpr hzero
+    apply hnext
+    rw [e.ker_eval_eq_span_holomorphicCoordinateGerm he x (mem_chart_source ℂ x),
+      Ideal.span_singleton_pow, Ideal.mem_span_singleton]
+    obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := hdiv
+    exact ⟨r, by rw [hq, pow_succ, mul_assoc, ← hr]⟩
+  obtain ⟨u, rfl⟩ := hqunit
+  exact ⟨n, u, hq.symm⟩
+
+end TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf

+module
+
+public import Mathlib.Geometry.Manifold.IntegralCurve.Basic
+import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.MeanValue
+import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Slope
+import TauCeti.Geometry.Manifold.MFDeriv.Curve
+
+/-!
+# Monotonicity of functions along integral curves
+
+Let `γ` be an integral curve of a vector field `v` on a manifold, and `f` a real function,
+differentiable along `γ`, with `df(v) ≤ 0` along `γ`. Then `f` never increases along `γ`. If
+moreover `df(v) < 0` at `γ s`, then `f` drops strictly below `f (γ s)` at every later time, with no
+further sign condition at the later points.
+
+These are the monotonicity statements behind the deformation of sublevels along descending
+vector fields, which are allowed to vanish away from the region being deformed.
+
+## Main declarations
+
+* `IsMIntegralCurve.antitone_comp`: `f` is antitone along `γ`.
+* `IsMIntegralCurve.lt_of_mvfderiv_apply_lt_zero`: `f` strictly decreases along `γ` after a time
+  at which `df(v) < 0`.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open Filter Set
+open scoped Manifold Topology
+
+variable {E H M : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [TopologicalSpace H]
+  {I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M]
+  {v : (x : M) → TangentSpace I x} {γ : ℝ → M} {f : M → ℝ}
+
+namespace IsMIntegralCurve
+
+/-- **Monotonicity along an integral curve.** If `f` is differentiable along an integral curve `γ`
+of `v` and `df(v) ≤ 0` along `γ`, then `f` is antitone along `γ`. -/
+theorem antitone_comp (hγ : IsMIntegralCurve γ v)
+    (hf : ∀ t, MDifferentiableAt I 𝓘(ℝ) f (γ t))
+    (hvf : ∀ t, mvfderiv I f (γ t) (v (γ t)) ≤ 0) : Antitone (f ∘ γ) :=
+  antitone_of_hasDerivAt_nonpos
+    (fun t ↦ TauCeti.Manifold.hasDerivAt_comp_curve (hf t) (hγ t)) hvf
+
+/-- **Strict decrease along an integral curve.** If `f` is differentiable along an integral curve
+`γ` of `v`, `df(v) ≤ 0` along `γ` and `df(v) < 0` at `γ s`, then `f (γ t) < f (γ s)` for every
+`t > s`. -/
+theorem lt_of_mvfderiv_apply_lt_zero (hγ : IsMIntegralCurve γ v)
+    (hf : ∀ t, MDifferentiableAt I 𝓘(ℝ) f (γ t))
+    (hvf : ∀ t, mvfderiv I f (γ t) (v (γ t)) ≤ 0) {s t : ℝ}
+    (hs : mvfderiv I f (γ s) (v (γ s)) < 0) (hst : s < t) : f (γ t) < f (γ s) := by
+  have hd := TauCeti.Manifold.hasDerivAt_comp_curve (hf s) (hγ s)
+  -- Some time `z ∈ (s, t)` has negative slope `(f (γ z) - f (γ s)) / (z - s)`, so
+  -- `f (γ t) ≤ f (γ z) < f (γ s)`.
+  obtain ⟨z, hz, hzt⟩ := ((hd.hasDerivWithinAt.limsup_slope_le' (lt_irrefl s) hs).and
+    (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT hst)).exists
+  rw [slope_def_field, div_neg_iff] at hz
+  have hzs : (f ∘ γ) z < (f ∘ γ) s := by
+    rcases hz with ⟨-, h⟩ | ⟨h, -⟩
+    · linarith [hzt.1]
+    · linarith
+  exact (hγ.antitone_comp hf hvf hzt.2.le).trans_lt hzs
+
+end IsMIntegralCurve

+module
+
+public import Mathlib.Geometry.Manifold.IsManifold.Basic
+
+/-!
+# Restricting the scalars of a manifold modelled on its model space
+
+Let `𝕜'` be a normed algebra over `𝕜` and let `E` be a normed space over both fields, compatibly.
+A map which is `C^n` over `𝕜'` is `C^n` over `𝕜`, so the `C^n` groupoid of the trivial model
+`𝓘(𝕜', E)` is contained in that of `𝓘(𝕜, E)`. Consequently a `C^n` manifold modelled on
+`𝓘(𝕜', E)` is, with the same charts, a `C^n` manifold modelled on `𝓘(𝕜, E)`, and every chart of
+its maximal atlas over `𝕜'` is a chart of its maximal atlas over `𝕜`.
+
+The groupoid comparison is obtained from Mathlib's `ContDiffOn.restrict_scalars`.
+
+The main example is a complex manifold modelled on `𝓘(ℂ, E)`, which is a real manifold modelled on
+`𝓘(ℝ, E)`; its holomorphic charts are real `C^n` charts. This is how real-analytic notions, such as
+the real Hessian at a critical point, are applied to complex manifolds.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `TauCeti.contDiffGroupoid_le_restrictScalars`: the `C^n` groupoid over `𝕜'` is contained in the
+  `C^n` groupoid over `𝕜`.
+* `IsManifold.restrictScalars`: a `C^n` manifold over `𝕜'` is a `C^n` manifold over `𝕜`.
+* `IsManifold.maximalAtlas_subset_restrictScalars`: the maximal atlas over `𝕜'` is contained in
+  the maximal atlas over `𝕜`.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open Set
+open scoped Manifold
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+variable {𝕜 𝕜' : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜']
+  [NormedAlgebra 𝕜 𝕜'] {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [NormedSpace 𝕜' E]
+  [IsScalarTower 𝕜 𝕜' E] {M : Type*} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace E M] {n : WithTop ℕ∞}
+
+/-- The `C^n` groupoid of the trivial model over `𝕜'` is contained in the `C^n` groupoid of the
+trivial model over the smaller field `𝕜`. -/
+theorem contDiffGroupoid_le_restrictScalars :
+    contDiffGroupoid n 𝓘(𝕜', E) ≤ contDiffGroupoid n 𝓘(𝕜, E) := by
+  rw [contDiffGroupoid, contDiffGroupoid]
+  apply groupoid_of_pregroupoid_le
+  intro f s hfs
+  simp only [contDiffPregroupoid, modelWithCornersSelf_coe, modelWithCornersSelf_coe_symm,
+    Function.id_comp, Function.comp_id, preimage_id_eq, id_eq, range_id, inter_univ] at hfs ⊢
+  exact hfs.restrict_scalars 𝕜

+/-!
+# Semialgebraic Thom encodings in monic polynomial families
+
+For a monic polynomial whose coefficients are polynomial functions of parameters, every Tarski
+query of a polynomial family is determined by finitely many signs of polynomial functions of the
+parameters. Consequently any condition on finitely many such queries is semialgebraic.
+
+Applying this to the products of consecutive derivatives in the full BKR moment system gives a
+uniform coefficient-sign description of each realized Thom encoding. This is the fixed-degree
+monic case of the coefficient description of ordered roots. The monic hypothesis ensures that
+polynomial remainder commutes with every coefficient specialization; arbitrary families require
+separate degree strata and denominator clearing.
+
+## Main declarations
+
+* `TauCeti.isSemialgebraic_setOf_tarskiQuery_map_eval_eq_of_monic` describes one query fiber.
+* `TauCeti.isSemialgebraic_setOf_tarskiQuery_map_eval_of_monic` allows an arbitrary condition on
+  a finite family of queries.
+* `TauCeti.isSemialgebraic_setOf_exists_root_derivative_signs_eq_of_monic` describes realization
+  of a prescribed Thom sign word.
+
+## References
+
+S. Basu, R. Pollack, and M.-F. Roy,
+[*Algorithms in Real Algebraic Geometry*](https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-33099-2),
+second edition, Chapters 4 and 10.
+-/

+variable {σ R : Type*} [Field R] [LinearOrder R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R] [IsRealClosed R]

+/-- The parameters at which a Tarski query of two specializations of polynomial families has a
+prescribed value form a semialgebraic set, provided the root family is monic. -/
+theorem isSemialgebraic_setOf_tarskiQuery_map_eval_eq_of_monic
+    (P Q : (MvPolynomial σ R)[X]) (hP : P.Monic) (c : ℤ) :
+    IsSemialgebraic {x : σ → R |
+      tarskiQuery (P.map (MvPolynomial.eval x)) (Q.map (MvPolynomial.eval x)) = c} := by
+  let H : (MvPolynomial σ R)[X] := (P.derivative * Q) %ₘ P
+  let s : ℕ → ℕ → MvPolynomial σ R := fun e =>
+    signedPsc P (H.reductum (e + 1)) P.natDegree e
+  have hH (x : σ → R) : H.map (MvPolynomial.eval x) =
+      ((P.map (MvPolynomial.eval x)).derivative * Q.map (MvPolynomial.eval x)) %
+        P.map (MvPolynomial.eval x) := by
+    dsimp only [H]
+    rw [map_modByMonic _ hP,
+      modByMonic_eq_mod _ (hP.map (MvPolynomial.eval x))]
+    congr 1
+    rw [Polynomial.map_mul, derivative_map]
+  have hquery (x : σ → R) {e : ℕ} (he : (H.map (MvPolynomial.eval x)).natDegree = e) :
+      tarskiQuery (P.map (MvPolynomial.eval x)) (Q.map (MvPolynomial.eval x)) =
+        (((List.range (P.natDegree + 1)).reverse.map (s e)).map
+          (MvPolynomial.eval x)).permanencesMinusVariations := by
+    rw [tarskiQuery_eq_permanencesMinusVariations_signedPsc,
+      hP.natDegree_map, ← hH, he]
+    have hred := map_reductum_natDegree_map_add_one (MvPolynomial.eval x) H
+    rw [he] at hred
+    rw [← hred]
+    have hs : signedPsc (P.map (MvPolynomial.eval x))
+        ((H.reductum (e + 1)).map (MvPolynomial.eval x)) P.natDegree e =
+          fun j => MvPolynomial.eval x (s e j) :=
+      funext fun j => signedPsc_map_map _ _ _ _ _ _
+    rw [hs, List.map_map]
+    rfl
+  have hset : {x : σ → R |
+        tarskiQuery (P.map (MvPolynomial.eval x)) (Q.map (MvPolynomial.eval x)) = c} =
+      ⋃ e ∈ Iic H.natDegree,
+        {x | (H.map (MvPolynomial.eval x)).natDegree = e} ∩
+          {x | (((List.range (P.natDegree + 1)).reverse.map (s e)).map
+            (MvPolynomial.eval x)).permanencesMinusVariations = c} := by
+    ext x
+    simp only [mem_ofPred_eq, mem_iUnion, mem_inter_iff, mem_Iic, exists_prop]
+    constructor
+    · intro hx
+      refine ⟨_, natDegree_map_le, rfl, ?_⟩
+      rwa [← hquery x rfl]
+    · rintro ⟨e, -, he, hc⟩
+      rwa [hquery x he]
+  rw [hset]
+  exact .biUnion (finite_Iic _) fun e _ =>
+    (isSemialgebraic_setOf_natDegree_map_eval_eq H e).inter
+      (isSemialgebraic_setOf_permanencesMinusVariations_eval _ _)
+
+/-- Any condition on finitely many Tarski queries of a monic polynomial family is
+semialgebraic. The queries have a common finite range bounded by the degree of the root
+polynomial, so the condition is a finite union of intersections of query fibers. -/
+theorem isSemialgebraic_setOf_tarskiQuery_map_eval_of_monic
+    {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (P : (MvPolynomial σ R)[X]) (hP : P.Monic)
+    (Q : ι → (MvPolynomial σ R)[X]) (Φ : (ι → ℤ) → Prop) :
+    IsSemialgebraic {x : σ → R |
+      Φ fun i => tarskiQuery (P.map (MvPolynomial.eval x)) (Q i |>.map (MvPolynomial.eval x))} := by
+  let V := Set.Icc (-(P.natDegree : ℤ)) (P.natDegree : ℤ)
+  have hmem (x : σ → R) (i : ι) :
+      tarskiQuery (P.map (MvPolynomial.eval x)) (Q i |>.map (MvPolynomial.eval x)) ∈ V := by
+    simpa only [V, hP.natDegree_map] using
+      Polynomial.tarskiQuery_mem_Icc_natDegree
+        (P.map (MvPolynomial.eval x)) (Q i |>.map (MvPolynomial.eval x))
+  have hset : {x : σ → R |
+        Φ fun i => tarskiQuery (P.map (MvPolynomial.eval x))
+          (Q i |>.map (MvPolynomial.eval x))} =
+      ⋃ v ∈ {v : ι → V | Φ fun i => (v i : ℤ)},
+        ⋂ i, {x | tarskiQuery (P.map (MvPolynomial.eval x))
+          (Q i |>.map (MvPolynomial.eval x)) = v i} := by
+    ext x
+    simp only [mem_ofPred_eq, mem_iUnion, mem_iInter, exists_prop]
+    constructor
+    · intro hx
+      let v : ι → V := fun i => ⟨_, hmem x i⟩
+      exact ⟨v, hx, fun _ => rfl⟩
+    · rintro ⟨v, hv, heq⟩
+      convert hv using 1
+      funext i
+      exact heq i
+  rw [hset]
+  exact .biUnion (toFinite _) fun v _ => .iInter fun i =>
+    isSemialgebraic_setOf_tarskiQuery_map_eval_eq_of_monic P (Q i) hP (v i)

+/-- **Uniform Thom-encoding realization for monic families.** For a prescribed sign word, the
+parameters at which the specialized polynomial has a root with those signs of its consecutive
+derivatives form a semialgebraic set. Monicity makes the formal index type agree with the degree
+of every specialization. -/

+    (P : (MvPolynomial σ R)[X]) (hP : P.Monic)

+        ∀ j : Fin P.natDegree,
+          SignType.sign (((derivative^[j.val + 1] P).map
+            (MvPolynomial.eval x)).eval r) = τ j} := by
+  let Q : (Fin P.natDegree → Fin 3) → (MvPolynomial σ R)[X] := fun e =>
+    ∏ j : Fin P.natDegree, (derivative^[j.val + 1] P) ^ (e j).val
+  have hsemi := isSemialgebraic_setOf_tarskiQuery_map_eval_of_monic P hP Q
+    (fun v => (SignDetermination.fullInverse (Fin P.natDegree) *ᵥ
+      (fun e => (v e : ℚ))) τ = 1)
+  convert hsemi using 1
+  ext x
+  simp only [mem_ofPred_eq]
+  have hderiv (k : ℕ) :
+      (derivative^[k] P).map (MvPolynomial.eval x) =
+        derivative^[k] (P.map (MvPolynomial.eval x)) := by
+    induction k with
+    | zero => rfl
+    | succ k ih =>
+      rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', Function.iterate_succ_apply', ← derivative_map, ih]
+  have hQ (e : Fin P.natDegree → Fin 3) : (Q e).map (MvPolynomial.eval x) =
+      ∏ j : Fin P.natDegree,
+        (derivative^[j.val + 1] (P.map (MvPolynomial.eval x))) ^ (e j).val := by
+    simp only [Q, Polynomial.map_prod]
+    apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
+    intro j _
+    rw [Polynomial.map_pow, hderiv]
+  simp only [hQ]
+  rw [Polynomial.fullInverse_mulVec_tarskiQuery]
+  simp only [hderiv]
+  symm
+  rw [Finset.signCount_eq_occCount, Function.occCount_of_injective]
+  · have hexists :
+        (∃ r : (P.map (MvPolynomial.eval x)).roots.toFinset,
+          (fun j : Fin P.natDegree => SignType.sign
+            ((derivative^[j.val + 1] (P.map (MvPolynomial.eval x))).eval (r : R))) = τ) ↔
+          ∃ r, (P.map (MvPolynomial.eval x)).eval r = 0 ∧
+            ∀ j : Fin P.natDegree, SignType.sign
+              ((derivative^[j.val + 1] (P.map (MvPolynomial.eval x))).eval r) = τ j := by
+        constructor
+        · rintro ⟨r, hr⟩
+          refine ⟨r, (Polynomial.mem_roots (hP.map (MvPolynomial.eval x)).ne_zero).mp
+            (Multiset.mem_toFinset.mp r.property), fun j => congrFun hr j⟩
+        · rintro ⟨r, hr, hs⟩
+          refine ⟨⟨r, Multiset.mem_toFinset.mpr
+            ((Polynomial.mem_roots (hP.map (MvPolynomial.eval x)).ne_zero).mpr hr)⟩, ?_⟩
+          funext j
+          exact hs j
+    simp only [hexists, Nat.cast_ite, Nat.cast_one, Nat.cast_zero, ite_eq_left_iff,
+      zero_ne_one, imp_false, not_not]
+  · intro a b hab
+    apply Subtype.ext
+    apply Polynomial.thomEncoding_injOn (P.map (MvPolynomial.eval x))
+      RealClosure.polynomialRolle_of_isRealClosed (hP.map (MvPolynomial.eval x)).ne_zero
+      (Polynomial.isRoot_of_mem_roots (Multiset.mem_toFinset.mp a.property))
+      (Polynomial.isRoot_of_mem_roots (Multiset.mem_toFinset.mp b.property))
+    funext j
+    have hj := congrFun hab (Fin.cast (hP.natDegree_map (MvPolynomial.eval x)) j)
+    simpa only [Polynomial.thomEncoding_def, Fin.val_cast, hderiv] using hj

+# The dense torus and the torus action of a product fan scheme
+
+The scheme `X_{Φ × Ψ}` of a product fan is the fibre product `X_Φ ×_{Spec ℂ} X_Ψ`, through the
+toric maps of the two fan projections (`TauCeti.Toric.Fan.isPullback_fst_snd_algebraicMap`), and
+the dense torus `T_{N × N'}` of the product lattice is the fibre product `T_N ×_{Spec ℂ} T_{N'}`
+of the dense tori of the factors, through the torus morphisms of the two lattice projections
+(`TauCeti.Toric.isPullback_affineToricSchemeMap_fst_snd_bot`). This file shows that the toric
+structure of `X_{Φ × Ψ}` is the product of the toric structures of `X_Φ` and `X_Ψ`:
+
+* for nonempty fans, the dense-torus inclusion of `X_{Φ × Ψ}` is the product of the dense-torus
+  inclusions of the factors;
+* the domain `T_{N × N'} ×_{Spec ℂ} X_{Φ × Ψ}` of the torus action is the fibre product of the
+  action domains `T_N ×_{Spec ℂ} X_Φ` and `T_{N'} ×_{Spec ℂ} X_Ψ`, through the maps of action
+  domains induced by the fan projections, and under these identifications the action of
+  `T_{N × N'}` on `X_{Φ × Ψ}` is the product of the actions of `T_N` on `X_Φ` and of `T_{N'}` on
+  `X_Ψ`.
+
+No regularity assumption on the fans is needed.
+

+
+* `TauCeti.Toric.Fan.denseTorusι_prod_comp_algebraicProdComparison`: the dense torus of a
+  product fan scheme is the product of the dense tori of the factors.
+* `TauCeti.Toric.Fan.isPullback_algebraicActionMap_fst_snd`: the action domain of a product fan
+  scheme is the fibre product of the action domains of the factors.
+* `TauCeti.Toric.Fan.algebraicRealizationAction_prod_comp_algebraicProdComparison`: the torus
+  action on a product fan scheme is the product of the torus actions on the factors.
+

+
+* W. Fulton, *Introduction to Toric Varieties*, §§1.3--1.4.
+* D. Cox, J. Little and H. Schenck, *Toric Varieties*, §§1.3 and 3.1.

+/-

+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: The Tau Ceti contributors
+-/
+module
+
+public import TauCeti.LinearAlgebra.ExteriorPower.Basic
+
+/-!
+# Plücker coordinates
+
+For a family `x : Fin p → ι → R` of `p` vectors with coordinates in a linearly ordered type `ι`,
+its Plücker coordinates are its maximal minors: for each `p`-element subset `s` of `ι`, the
+determinant of the `p × p` matrix whose rows are the vectors `x i` restricted to the coordinates
+in `s`, listed in increasing order. The subsets are indexed by Mathlib's `Set.powersetCard ι p`,
+the index type of the induced basis of the exterior power.
+
+The coordinates are those of the exterior product `x 0 ∧ ⋯ ∧ x (p - 1)` in the basis of
+`⋀[R]^p (ι → R)` induced by the standard basis. Consequently a change of the family by a square
+matrix multiplies all coordinates by its determinant, and over a field they vanish identically
+exactly when the family is linearly dependent. Plücker coordinates are the coordinates of the
+point in projective space attached to a subspace of `K^ι`, and heights of subspaces are heights
+of these points.
+
+The Cauchy–Binet formula expresses the determinant of the `p × p` product of two such families
+as the sum of products of their Plücker coordinates. Over a commutative star ring, for instance
+`ℂ`, applying it to a family and its conjugate writes the Hermitian Gram determinant of the
+family as the sum of the squared absolute values of its Plücker coordinates.
+
+All results hold over an arbitrary commutative ring except the comparison with linear
+independence, which is over a field. The empty family has a single Plücker coordinate, equal to
+`1`, and a family of more than `#ι` vectors has none.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `TauCeti.plucker x`: the Plücker coordinates of a family `x : Fin p → ι → R`.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `TauCeti.plucker_eq_repr_ιMulti`: the Plücker coordinates are the coordinates of
+  `exteriorPower.ιMulti R p x` in the exterior-power basis induced by `Pi.basisFun R ι`.
+* `TauCeti.plucker_sum_smul`: replacing the family by its product with a square matrix
+  multiplies the Plücker coordinates by the determinant of that matrix.
+* `TauCeti.det_mul_transpose_eq_sum_plucker_mul`: the Cauchy–Binet formula.
+* `TauCeti.det_mul_conjTranspose_eq_sum_plucker_mul_star`: its Hermitian form.
+* `TauCeti.plucker_ne_zero_iff`: over a field, the Plücker coordinates of a family are not all
+  zero exactly when the family is linearly independent.
+
+## References
+
+* E. Bombieri and W. Gubler, *Heights in Diophantine Geometry*, Cambridge University Press
+  (2006), §2.8.
+
+The proofs use Mathlib's exterior-power basis `Module.Basis.exteriorPower` and its coordinate
+formula `exteriorPower.ιMultiDual_apply_ιMulti`, by Sophie Morel and Daniel Morrison.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open Set Set.powersetCard exteriorPower
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+variable {R S ι : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [LinearOrder ι] {p : ℕ}
+
+/-- The Plücker coordinates of a family `x` of `p` vectors in `ι → R`: at a `p`-element subset `s`
+of `ι`, the `p × p` minor of the matrix with rows `x i` on the columns in `s`, taken in increasing
+order. -/
+def plucker (x : Fin p → ι → R) (s : powersetCard ι p) : R :=
+  (Matrix.of fun i j ↦ x i (ofFinEmbEquiv.symm s j)).det
+
+/-- The Plücker coordinate at `s` is the minor on the columns in `s`. -/
+theorem plucker_apply (x : Fin p → ι → R) (s : powersetCard ι p) :
+    plucker x s = (Matrix.of fun i j ↦ x i (ofFinEmbEquiv.symm s j)).det := (rfl)
+
+/-- The empty family has Plücker coordinate `1`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem plucker_of_isEmpty (x : Fin 0 → ι → R) (s : powersetCard ι 0) : plucker x s = 1 :=
+  Matrix.det_isEmpty
+
+/-- Plücker coordinates commute with ring homomorphisms applied to all coordinates. -/
+theorem plucker_map (f : R →+* S) (x : Fin p → ι → R) (s : powersetCard ι p) :
+    plucker (fun i k ↦ f (x i k)) s = f (plucker x s) := by
+  rw [plucker_apply, plucker_apply, f.map_det]
+  refine congrArg Matrix.det (Matrix.ext fun i j ↦ ?_)
+  simp
+
+/-- Replacing a family by its product with a square matrix `A` multiplies its Plücker
+coordinates by `det A`. -/
+theorem plucker_sum_smul (A : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) R) (x : Fin p → ι → R)
+    (s : powersetCard ι p) :
+    plucker (fun i ↦ ∑ k, A i k • x k) s = A.det * plucker x s := by
+  rw [plucker_apply, plucker_apply, ← Matrix.det_mul]
+  congr 1
+  ext i j
+  simp [Matrix.mul_apply]
+
+/-- The Plücker coordinates of `x` are the coordinates of the exterior product of `x` in the basis
+of `⋀[R]^p (ι → R)` induced by the standard basis of `ι → R`. -/
+theorem plucker_eq_repr_ιMulti [Finite ι] (x : Fin p → ι → R) (s : powersetCard ι p) :
+    plucker x s = ((Pi.basisFun R ι).exteriorPower p).repr (ιMulti R p x) s := by
+  rw [basis_repr_apply, ιMultiDual_apply_ιMulti, plucker_apply]
+  simp
+
+/-- The basis vector of `⋀[R]^p (ι → R)` at `s` pairs with the exterior product of `p` linear
+forms to give the minor of their coefficient matrix on the coordinates in `s`. -/
+private theorem pairingDual_ιMulti_exteriorPower_basisFun [Fintype ι]
+    (y : Fin p → ι → R) (s : powersetCard ι p) :
+    pairingDual R (ι → R) p (ιMulti R p fun j ↦ Fintype.linearCombination R (y j))
+        ((Pi.basisFun R ι).exteriorPower p s) = plucker y s := by
+  classical
+  rw [basis_apply, ιMulti_family, pairingDual_ιMulti_ιMulti, plucker_apply,
+    ← Matrix.det_transpose]
+  congr 1
+  ext i j
+  simp [Fintype.linearCombination_apply, Pi.single_apply]
+
+/-- **The Cauchy–Binet formula.** The determinant of the `p × p` matrix of pairwise products
+`∑ₖ x i k * y j k` is the sum over the `p`-element subsets `s` of `ι` of the products of the
+Plücker coordinates of `x` and `y` at `s`. For `p > #ι` both sides vanish. -/
+theorem det_mul_transpose_eq_sum_plucker_mul [Fintype ι] (x y : Fin p → ι → R) :
+    (Matrix.of x * (Matrix.of y).transpose).det = ∑ s, plucker x s * plucker y s := by
+  classical
+  set b := (Pi.basisFun R ι).exteriorPower p
+  set φ := pairingDual R (ι → R) p (ιMulti R p fun j ↦ Fintype.linearCombination R (y j))
+  have h : (Matrix.of x * (Matrix.of y).transpose).det = φ (ιMulti R p x) := by
+    rw [pairingDual_ιMulti_ιMulti]
+    refine congrArg Matrix.det (Matrix.ext fun i j ↦ ?_)
+    simp [Matrix.mul_apply, Fintype.linearCombination_apply]
+  rw [h, ← b.sum_repr (ιMulti R p x), map_sum]
+  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun s _ ↦ ?_
+  rw [map_smul, pairingDual_ιMulti_exteriorPower_basisFun, ← plucker_eq_repr_ιMulti, smul_eq_mul]
+
+/-- **The Cauchy–Binet formula, Hermitian form.** Over a commutative star ring, the determinant
+of the Hermitian Gram matrix `∑ₖ x i k * star (x j k)` of a family is the sum of the products of
+its Plücker coordinates with their conjugates. -/
+theorem det_mul_conjTranspose_eq_sum_plucker_mul_star [StarRing R] [Fintype ι]
+    (x : Fin p → ι → R) :
+    (Matrix.of x * (Matrix.of x).conjTranspose).det = ∑ s, plucker x s * star (plucker x s) := by
+  have hx : (Matrix.of x).conjTranspose =
+      (Matrix.of fun i k ↦ starRingEnd R (x i k)).transpose := by
+    ext
+    simp [starRingEnd_apply]
+  rw [hx, det_mul_transpose_eq_sum_plucker_mul]
+  simp_rw [plucker_map, starRingEnd_apply]
+
+section Field
+
+variable {K : Type*} [Field K]
+
+/-- Over a field, the Plücker coordinates of a family are not all zero exactly when the family is
+linearly independent. -/
+theorem plucker_ne_zero_iff [Finite ι] (x : Fin p → ι → K) :
+    plucker x ≠ 0 ↔ LinearIndependent K x := by
+  rw [← ιMulti_ne_zero_iff, not_iff_not]
+  have h : plucker x = ((Pi.basisFun K ι).exteriorPower p).repr (ιMulti K p x) := by
+    ext s
+    exact plucker_eq_repr_ιMulti x s
+  rw [h, Finsupp.coe_eq_zero, LinearEquiv.map_eq_zero_iff]
+
+end Field
+
+end TauCeti

+module
+
+public import Mathlib.Algebra.GroupWithZero.Subgroup
+public import Mathlib.Data.FunLike.Fintype
+public import TauCeti.LinearAlgebra.FiniteBilinearModule.Quadratic
+public import TauCeti.LinearAlgebra.QuadraticForm.OrthogonalGroup.Basic
+
+/-!
+# Orthogonal groups of finite quadratic modules
+
+The orthogonal group `O(A)` of a finite quadratic module consists of its additive automorphisms
+preserving the quadratic map. This file specializes the general quadratic-map orthogonal group to
+finite quadratic modules and records its action on the underlying module and its isotropic and
+Lagrangian subgroups. The imported generic orthogonal-group API transports this group across
+isometries of finite quadratic modules, and `QuadraticMap.orthogonalGroupEquivIsometryEquiv`
+identifies its underlying type with the type `Isometry A A` of self-isometries of `A`.
+
+These actions are the group-theoretic interface used when discriminant-form automorphisms act on
+gluing data and primitive embeddings.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `TauCeti.FiniteQuadraticModule.orthogonalGroup`: the group `O(A)`.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `TauCeti.FiniteQuadraticModule.finite_orthogonalGroup`: `O(A)` is finite.
+* `TauCeti.FiniteQuadraticModule.isIsotropic_smul_iff` and
+  `TauCeti.FiniteQuadraticModule.isLagrangian_smul_iff`: `O(A)` preserves the two classes of
+  subgroups used in gluing theory.
+
+## References
+
+* V. V. Nikulin, *Integral symmetric bilinear forms and some of their applications*, §1.1.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+namespace TauCeti.FiniteQuadraticModule
+
+open scoped Pointwise
+
+/-- The orthogonal group `O(A)` of a finite quadratic module `A`. -/
+abbrev orthogonalGroup (A : FiniteQuadraticModule) : Subgroup (A ≃ₗ[ℤ] A) :=
+  QuadraticMap.orthogonalGroup A.quadratic
+
+variable {A : FiniteQuadraticModule}
+
+/-- The orthogonal group of a finite quadratic module is finite. -/
+instance finite_orthogonalGroup (A : FiniteQuadraticModule) : Finite (orthogonalGroup A) := by
+  have : Finite (A ≃ₗ[ℤ] A) := FunLike.finite _
+  infer_instance
+
+/-- The action of `O(A)` on `A` preserves the quadratic map. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem quadratic_smul (g : orthogonalGroup A) (x : A) :
+    A.quadratic (g • x) = A.quadratic x :=
+  QuadraticMap.map_app_of_mem_orthogonalGroup g.property x
+
+/-- Pointwise transport of an additive subgroup by an element of `O(A)` is its image under the
+corresponding self-isometry. -/
+theorem smul_eq_map_toAddEquiv (g : orthogonalGroup A) (H : AddSubgroup A) :
+    g • H = H.map (QuadraticMap.orthogonalGroupEquivIsometryEquiv A.quadratic g).toAddEquiv := by
+  calc
+    g • H = H.map (DistribMulAction.toAddMonoidEnd _ _ g) :=
+      AddSubgroup.pointwise_smul_def H
+    _ = H.map (QuadraticMap.orthogonalGroupEquivIsometryEquiv A.quadratic g).toAddEquiv := by
+      congr 1
+      ext x
+      exact (congrFun (QuadraticMap.coe_orthogonalGroupEquivIsometryEquiv A.quadratic g) x).symm
+
+/-- The orthogonal group preserves quadratic-isotropic subgroups. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem isIsotropic_smul_iff (g : orthogonalGroup A) (H : AddSubgroup A) :
+    A.IsIsotropic (g • H) ↔ A.IsIsotropic H := by
+  rw [smul_eq_map_toAddEquiv]
+  exact Isometry.isIsotropic_map_iff A (QuadraticMap.orthogonalGroupEquivIsometryEquiv _ g) H
+
+/-- The orthogonal group preserves quadratic Lagrangian subgroups. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem isLagrangian_smul_iff (g : orthogonalGroup A) (H : AddSubgroup A) :
+    A.IsLagrangian (g • H) ↔ A.IsLagrangian H := by
+  rw [smul_eq_map_toAddEquiv]
+  exact Isometry.isLagrangian_map_iff A (QuadraticMap.orthogonalGroupEquivIsometryEquiv _ g) H
+
+/-- The action of the orthogonal group commutes with taking the orthogonal complement for the
+polar pairing. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem smul_orthogonalComplement (g : orthogonalGroup A) (H : AddSubgroup A) :
+    g • A.toFiniteBilinearModule.orthogonalComplement H =
+      A.toFiniteBilinearModule.orthogonalComplement (g • H) := by
+  let e : Isometry A A := QuadraticMap.orthogonalGroupEquivIsometryEquiv A.quadratic g
+  rw [smul_eq_map_toAddEquiv, smul_eq_map_toAddEquiv, ← e.toFiniteBilinearModule_toAddEquiv]
+  exact e.toFiniteBilinearModule.map_orthogonalComplement (H := H)
+
+end TauCeti.FiniteQuadraticModule
+
+end

+module
+
+public import Mathlib.RingTheory.DiscreteValuationRing.Basic
+public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Ideal.Norm.AbsNorm
+
+/-!
+# The index of the image of an endomorphism of a free module over a PID
+
+Let `R` be a principal ideal domain and `f` an endomorphism of a finite free `R`-module `M` with
+nonzero determinant. Then `M ⧸ range f` has as many elements as `R ⧸ (det f)`. The Smith normal
+form of `range f` inside `M` splits the quotient into the residue rings `R ⧸ (aᵢ)` of the
+diagonal coefficients, whose product is associated to `det f`, and the cardinality of a quotient
+of a Dedekind domain is multiplicative in the ideal.
+
+This is the principal ideal domain form of Mathlib's `Submodule.natAbs_det_equiv` and
+`AddSubgroup.index_eq_natAbs_det`, where `R = ℤ` and `Nat.card (ℤ ⧸ (d)) = |d|`. Over a discrete
+valuation ring, when the determinant is associated to `ϖ ^ k` for a uniformizer `ϖ`, the quotient
+has `q ^ k` elements, where `q` is the cardinality of the residue field: this is the lattice index
+behind the scaling law of Haar measure under linear maps of `Kⁿ` for a non-archimedean local
+field `K`. No finiteness of the residue field is needed; when it is infinite both sides are `0`
+for `k ≠ 0`.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `LinearMap.card_quotient_range_eq_card_quotient_span_det`: for `det f ≠ 0`,
+  `Nat.card (M ⧸ range f) = Nat.card (R ⧸ Ideal.span {det f})`.
+* `Matrix.card_quotient_range_mulVecLin_eq_card_quotient_span_det`: the same for a square matrix
+  acting on `ι → R`.
+* `Matrix.card_quotient_range_mulVecLin_eq_pow`: over a discrete valuation ring, if `det A` is
+  associated to `ϖ ^ k` for a uniformizer `ϖ`, the quotient has `q ^ k` elements.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open Module Submodule
+
+namespace LinearMap
+
+variable {R M : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsPrincipalIdealRing R]
+  [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Free R M] [Module.Finite R M]
+
+/-- **The index of the image of an endomorphism of a finite free module over a principal ideal
+domain** is that of the principal ideal generated by its determinant, provided the determinant is
+nonzero. -/
+theorem card_quotient_range_eq_card_quotient_span_det {f : M →ₗ[R] M} (hf : f.det ≠ 0) :
+    Nat.card (M ⧸ range f) = Nat.card (R ⧸ Ideal.span {f.det}) := by
+  rcases finite_or_infinite R with hR | hR
+  · -- A finite domain is a field, so `f` is invertible and both quotients are trivial.
+    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := (Finite.isField_of_domain R).mul_inv_cancel hf
+    have hu : IsUnit f.det := IsUnit.of_mul_eq_one y hy
+    rw [Ideal.span_singleton_eq_top.mpr hu,
+      range_eq_top.mpr ((Module.End.isUnit_iff f).mp ((isUnit_iff_isUnit_det f).mpr hu)).surjective]
+    simp
+  classical
+  let b := Module.Free.chooseBasis R M
+  have hinj : Function.Injective f :=
+    ker_eq_bot.mp (not_ne_iff.mp (mt det_eq_zero_iff_ker_ne_bot.mpr hf))
+  let e : M ≃ₗ[R] range f := LinearEquiv.ofInjective f hinj
+  have h : finrank R (range f) = finrank R M := e.finrank_eq.symm
+  let a := smithNormalFormCoeffs b h
+  let b' := smithNormalFormTopBasis b h
+  -- In the Smith bases, the inclusion of `range f` is diagonal with entries `a`.
+  let e' : M ≃ₗ[R] range f := b'.equiv (smithNormalFormBotBasis b h) (Equiv.refl _)
+  have hdet : LinearMap.det ((range f).subtype ∘ₗ (e' : M →ₗ[R] range f)) = ∏ i, a i := by
+    rw [← det_toMatrix b', ← Matrix.det_diagonal]
+    congr 1
+    ext i j
+    simp [toMatrix_apply, e', a, b', Matrix.diagonal_apply, Finsupp.single_apply]
+    grind
+  have hassoc : Associated f.det (∏ i, a i) := by
+    rw [← hdet]
+    convert associated_det_comp_equiv (range f).subtype e e' using 2
+    ext x
+    simp [e]
+  -- The cardinality of a quotient of the Dedekind domain `R` is multiplicative in the ideal.
+  let cardQuotHom : Ideal R →* ℕ :=
+    { toFun := cardQuot
+      map_one' := by rw [Ideal.one_eq_top, cardQuot_top]
+      map_mul' := cardQuot_mul }
+  calc Nat.card (M ⧸ range f)
+      = ∏ i, Nat.card (R ⧸ Ideal.span {a i}) := by
+        rw [Nat.card_congr (quotientEquivPiSpan (range f) b h).toEquiv, Nat.card_pi]
+    _ = cardQuot (∏ i, Ideal.span {a i}) := by
+        simp_rw [← cardQuot_apply]
+        exact (map_prod cardQuotHom _ _).symm
+    _ = Nat.card (R ⧸ Ideal.span {f.det}) := by
+        rw [Ideal.prod_span_singleton, ← Ideal.span_singleton_eq_span_singleton.mpr hassoc,
+          cardQuot_apply]
+
+end LinearMap
+
+namespace Matrix
+
+variable {R ι : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+
+/-- **The index of the image lattice of a square matrix** over a principal ideal domain with
+nonzero determinant is that of the principal ideal generated by its determinant. -/
+theorem card_quotient_range_mulVecLin_eq_card_quotient_span_det [IsPrincipalIdealRing R]
+    {A : Matrix ι ι R} (hA : A.det ≠ 0) :
+    Nat.card ((ι → R) ⧸ LinearMap.range A.mulVecLin) = Nat.card (R ⧸ Ideal.span {A.det}) := by
+  have h := LinearMap.card_quotient_range_eq_card_quotient_span_det
+    (f := toLin' A) (by rwa [LinearMap.det_toLin'])
+  rwa [LinearMap.det_toLin', toLin'_apply'] at h
+
+/-- **The index of an image lattice over a discrete valuation ring.** For a square matrix `A`
+over a discrete valuation ring whose determinant is associated to `ϖ ^ k` for a uniformizer `ϖ`,
+the integer box `ι → R` modulo the image of `A` has `q ^ k` elements, where `q` is the
+cardinality of the residue field. -/
+theorem card_quotient_range_mulVecLin_eq_pow [IsDiscreteValuationRing R] {A : Matrix ι ι R}
+    {ϖ : R} (hϖ : Irreducible ϖ) {k : ℕ} (hk : Associated A.det (ϖ ^ k)) :
+    Nat.card ((ι → R) ⧸ LinearMap.range A.mulVecLin) =
+      Nat.card (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R) ^ k := by
+  rw [card_quotient_range_mulVecLin_eq_card_quotient_span_det
+      (hk.ne_zero_iff.mpr (pow_ne_zero k hϖ.ne_zero)),
+    Ideal.span_singleton_eq_span_singleton.mpr hk, ← Ideal.span_singleton_pow,
+    ← hϖ.maximalIdeal_eq, ← cardQuot_apply, cardQuot_pow_of_prime
+      (IsDiscreteValuationRing.not_a_field R), cardQuot_apply]
+  -- `IsLocalRing.ResidueField R` is by definition `R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R`.
+  rfl
+
+end Matrix

+-/
+module
+
+public import TauCeti.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.Transvection
+
+/-!
+# Perfectness of special linear groups
+
+Over a field containing a nonzero element whose square is not one, the special linear group
+on any finite coordinate type is perfect. Conjugation by the determinant-one diagonal matrix
+with entries `a` and `a⁻¹` rescales a transvection by `a²`. Every transvection is consequently
+a commutator, and transvections generate the special linear group. The hypothesis holds over
+every infinite field; it excludes the small-field exceptions in rank two.
+
+The commutator calculation generalizes Mathlib's `Matrix.commutator_diag2_transvection`
+and the perfectness statement generalizes `Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top` to arbitrary finite
+coordinate types. Generation is reused from
+`Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.closure_range_toSpecialLinearGroup_eq_top_of_field`.
+
+## References
+
+* J. S. Milne, *Algebraic Groups* (2017), §6d.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open scoped commutatorElement
+
+namespace Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup
+
+variable {F ι : Type*} [Field F] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {i j : ι}
+
+/-- Conjugation by the determinant-one two-coordinate diagonal matrix rescales a transvection
+by `a²`, so its commutator has parameter `b * (a² - 1)`. -/
+theorem commutatorElement_diag2n_transvection (hij : i ≠ j) (a : F) (ha : a ≠ 0)

+    apply Subtype.ext

+    apply diagonal_eq_one.mpr

+    split_ifs <;> simp_all

+      transvection hij (a ^ 2 * b) := by
+    rw [hinv]
+    apply Subtype.ext
+    simp only [coe_mul, diag2n_coe, transvection_coe]

+theorem commutator_eq_top {a : F} (ha : a ≠ 0) (hasq : a ^ 2 ≠ 1) :

+  apply le_antisymm le_top
+  rw [← closure_range_toSpecialLinearGroup_eq_top_of_field (ι := ι) (K := F),

+  rw [TransvectionStruct.toSpecialLinearGroup_mk]
+  exact transvection_mem_commutator hij ha hasq c

+end Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup

+module
+
+public import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Subgroup.Basic
+public import Mathlib.Data.Matrix.Mul
+public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Pi
+import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
+
+/-!
+# Monomial linear equivalences of coordinate spaces
+
+A monomial equivalence rescales coordinates by units and then relabels them along an
+equivalence of index types. These transformations form the monomial subgroup of the group of
+linear automorphisms. Coordinate permutations form a subgroup, equal to the monomial subgroup
+when the coefficient semiring has only one unit. The construction allows infinite coordinate
+sets; only the dot-product statements require finite coordinates.
+
+The application, composition, inverse and support formulas provide the coordinate description
+used to compare monomial linear automorphisms with monomial matrices. In particular these
+subgroups make sense over small fields where the normalizer of the rational points of a
+diagonal torus need not be the monomial subgroup.
+
+The code-specific invariants and automorphism groups are developed in
+`TauCeti.InformationTheory.Coding.Equivalence`.
+
+## References
+
+* W. C. Huffman and V. Pless, *Fundamentals of Error-Correcting Codes* (2003), §1.6.
+* N. Bourbaki, *Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Chapters 4--6*, Chapter IV, §2, no. 2.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+open Function Matrix
+
+namespace TauCeti
+
+variable {ι κ μ R : Type*}
+
+section Monomial
+
+variable [CommSemiring R]
+
+/-- The monomial equivalence of coordinate spaces attached to a family of units `u : ι → Rˣ`
+and a relabelling `e : ι ≃ κ` of coordinates: it rescales the `i`-th coordinate by `u i` and
+places the result in the coordinate `e i`. -/
+def monomialEquiv (u : ι → Rˣ) (e : ι ≃ κ) : (ι → R) ≃ₗ[R] (κ → R) :=
+  (LinearEquiv.piCongrRight fun i ↦ LinearEquiv.smulOfUnit (M := R) (u i)).trans
+    (LinearEquiv.funCongrLeft R R e.symm)
+
+/-- At a target coordinate, a monomial equivalence multiplies the corresponding source
+coordinate by its assigned unit. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem monomialEquiv_apply (u : ι → Rˣ) (e : ι ≃ κ) (x : ι → R) (j : κ) :
+    monomialEquiv u e x j = u (e.symm j) * x (e.symm j) :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- The inverse monomial equivalence reads the relabelled coordinate and multiplies it by
+the inverse of the source coordinate's unit. -/
+theorem monomialEquiv_symm_apply (u : ι → Rˣ) (e : ι ≃ κ) (y : κ → R) (i : ι) :
+    (monomialEquiv u e).symm y i = ↑(u i)⁻¹ * y (e i) :=
+  (rfl)
+
+/-- With trivial scalars a monomial equivalence is a bare relabelling of coordinates. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem monomialEquiv_one (e : ι ≃ κ) :
+    monomialEquiv (1 : ι → Rˣ) e = LinearEquiv.funCongrLeft R R e.symm :=
+  LinearEquiv.ext fun x ↦ funext fun j ↦ by simp
+
+/-- Composing monomial equivalences multiplies their coordinate units after relabelling
+and composes their coordinate equivalences. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem monomialEquiv_trans (u : ι → Rˣ) (e : ι ≃ κ) (v : κ → Rˣ) (f : κ ≃ μ) :
+    (monomialEquiv u e).trans (monomialEquiv v f) =
+      monomialEquiv (fun i ↦ u i * v (e i)) (e.trans f) := by
+  refine LinearEquiv.ext fun x ↦ funext fun m ↦ ?_
+  simp only [LinearEquiv.trans_apply, monomialEquiv_apply, Equiv.symm_trans_apply,
+    Equiv.apply_symm_apply, Units.val_mul]
+  ring
+
+/-- Inverting a monomial equivalence inverts and relabels its coordinate units and inverts
+its coordinate equivalence. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem monomialEquiv_symm (u : ι → Rˣ) (e : ι ≃ κ) :
+    (monomialEquiv u e).symm = monomialEquiv (fun j ↦ (u (e.symm j))⁻¹) e.symm :=
+  LinearEquiv.ext fun y ↦ funext fun i ↦ by simp [monomialEquiv_symm_apply]
+
+/-- A monomial equivalence transports support along its coordinate equivalence. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem support_monomialEquiv (u : ι → Rˣ) (e : ι ≃ κ) (x : ι → R) :
+    support (monomialEquiv u e x) = e '' support x := by
+  rw [Equiv.image_eq_preimage_symm]
+  ext j
+  simp [Units.mul_right_eq_zero]
+
+/-- A monomial equivalence is coordinatewise rescaling followed by reindexing. -/
+theorem monomialEquiv_apply_eq_comp (u : ι → Rˣ) (e : ι ≃ κ) (x : ι → R) :
+    (monomialEquiv u e x : κ → R) = (fun i ↦ (u i : R) * x i) ∘ e.symm :=
+  funext fun j ↦ by simp
+
+section DotProduct
+
+variable [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ]
+
+/-- A monomial coordinate change preserves the standard dot product exactly when every
+coordinate multiplier has square one. -/
+theorem dotProduct_monomialEquiv_iff (u : ι → Rˣ) (e : ι ≃ κ) :
+    (∀ x y : ι → R, monomialEquiv u e x ⬝ᵥ monomialEquiv u e y = x ⬝ᵥ y) ↔
+      ∀ i, (u i : R) ^ 2 = 1 := by
+  classical
+  have hdot (x y : ι → R) :
+      monomialEquiv u e x ⬝ᵥ monomialEquiv u e y =
+        (fun i ↦ (u i : R) * x i) ⬝ᵥ (fun i ↦ (u i : R) * y i) := by
+    rw [monomialEquiv_apply_eq_comp, monomialEquiv_apply_eq_comp,
+      comp_equiv_dotProduct_comp_equiv]
+  constructor
+  · intro h i
+    have hi := h (Pi.single i 1) (Pi.single i 1)
+    rw [hdot] at hi
+    simpa [dotProduct, Pi.single_apply, pow_two] using hi
+  · intro h x y
+    rw [hdot]
+    simp only [dotProduct]
+    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+    intro i _
+    calc
+      (u i : R) * x i * ((u i : R) * y i) = (u i : R) ^ 2 * (x i * y i) := by ring
+      _ = x i * y i := by rw [h i]; simp
+
+end DotProduct
+
+end Monomial
+
+section Group
+
+/-- The group of monomial transformations of the coordinate space `ι → R`, as a subgroup of its
+group of linear automorphisms. -/
+def monomialGroup (R ι : Type*) [CommSemiring R] : Subgroup ((ι → R) ≃ₗ[R] (ι → R)) where
+  carrier := {f | ∃ (u : ι → Rˣ) (e : Equiv.Perm ι), monomialEquiv u e = f}
+  one_mem' := ⟨1, Equiv.refl ι, by
+    rw [monomialEquiv_one, Equiv.refl_symm, LinearEquiv.funCongrLeft_id,
+      LinearEquiv.one_eq_refl]⟩
+  mul_mem' := by
+    rintro f g ⟨u, e, rfl⟩ ⟨v, d, rfl⟩
+    exact ⟨fun i ↦ v i * u (d i), d.trans e, by
+      rw [← monomialEquiv_trans, LinearEquiv.mul_eq_trans]⟩
+  inv_mem' := by
+    rintro f ⟨u, e, rfl⟩
+    exact ⟨fun j ↦ (u (e.symm j))⁻¹, e.symm, (monomialEquiv_symm u e).symm⟩
+
+variable [CommSemiring R]
+
+/-- The monomial group consists exactly of the monomial transformations of `ι → R`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem mem_monomialGroup {f : (ι → R) ≃ₗ[R] (ι → R)} :
+    f ∈ monomialGroup R ι ↔ ∃ (u : ι → Rˣ) (e : Equiv.Perm ι), monomialEquiv u e = f :=
+  Iff.rfl
+
+/-- A monomial equivalence induced by coordinate units and a coordinate permutation belongs
+to the monomial group. -/
+theorem monomialEquiv_mem_monomialGroup (u : ι → Rˣ) (e : Equiv.Perm ι) :
+    monomialEquiv u e ∈ monomialGroup R ι :=
+  ⟨u, e, rfl⟩
+
+end Group
+
+section PermutationGroup
+
+/-- The group of coordinate permutations of `ι → R`, as a subgroup of its group of linear
+automorphisms. -/
+def permutationGroup (R ι : Type*) [Semiring R] : Subgroup ((ι → R) ≃ₗ[R] (ι → R)) where
+  carrier := {f | ∃ e : Equiv.Perm ι, LinearEquiv.funCongrLeft R R e.symm = f}
+  one_mem' := ⟨Equiv.refl ι, by
+    rw [Equiv.refl_symm, LinearEquiv.funCongrLeft_id, LinearEquiv.one_eq_refl]⟩
+  mul_mem' := by
+    rintro f g ⟨e, rfl⟩ ⟨d, rfl⟩
+    exact ⟨d.trans e, by
+      rw [Equiv.symm_trans, LinearEquiv.funCongrLeft_comp, LinearEquiv.mul_eq_trans]⟩
+  inv_mem' := by
+    rintro f ⟨e, rfl⟩
+    exact ⟨e.symm, by rw [Equiv.symm_symm, ← LinearEquiv.funCongrLeft_symm]; rfl⟩
+
+variable [Semiring R]
+
+/-- The permutation group consists exactly of the coordinate relabellings of `ι → R`. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem mem_permutationGroup {f : (ι → R) ≃ₗ[R] (ι → R)} :
+    f ∈ permutationGroup R ι ↔ ∃ e : Equiv.Perm ι, LinearEquiv.funCongrLeft R R e.symm = f :=
+  Iff.rfl
+
+/-- A coordinate relabelling belongs to the permutation group. -/
+theorem funCongrLeft_mem_permutationGroup (e : Equiv.Perm ι) :
+    LinearEquiv.funCongrLeft R R e.symm ∈ permutationGroup R ι :=
+  ⟨e, rfl⟩
+
+end PermutationGroup
+
+section PermutationLeMonomial
+
+variable [CommSemiring R]
+
+/-- A coordinate permutation is the monomial transformation with all scalars equal to one. -/
+theorem permutationGroup_le_monomialGroup : permutationGroup R ι ≤ monomialGroup R ι := by
+  intro f hf
+  obtain ⟨e, rfl⟩ := mem_permutationGroup.1 hf
+  exact mem_monomialGroup.2 ⟨1, e, monomialEquiv_one e⟩
+
+end PermutationLeMonomial
+
+section TrivialUnits
+
+variable [CommSemiring R] [Subsingleton Rˣ]
+
+/-- When one is the only unit, a monomial transformation is its underlying coordinate
+permutation. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem monomialEquiv_eq_funCongrLeft (u : ι → Rˣ) (e : ι ≃ κ) :
+    monomialEquiv u e = LinearEquiv.funCongrLeft R R e.symm := by
+  rw [Subsingleton.elim u 1, monomialEquiv_one]
+
+/-- When one is the only unit, the monomial group is the coordinate-permutation group. -/
+@[simp]
+theorem monomialGroup_eq_permutationGroup : monomialGroup R ι = permutationGroup R ι := by
+  refine le_antisymm (fun f hf ↦ ?_) permutationGroup_le_monomialGroup
+  obtain ⟨u, e, rfl⟩ := mem_monomialGroup.mp hf
+  exact mem_permutationGroup.mpr ⟨e, (monomialEquiv_eq_funCongrLeft u e).symm⟩
+
+end TrivialUnits
+
+end TauCeti
